p: yī bù zuò ， èr bù xiū
l: Once one thing is done, two things are not stopped
m: Once you have started something wrong or committed to a course of action, you might as well go all the way rather than stop halfway.
s: When someone decides to break a rule once and then figures they might as well break it repeatedly since they've already started. When a person commits to a risky plan and decides to see it through to the end no matter the consequences rather than backing out halfway.

m: People who are equally bad or worthless; individuals of the same ilk who share the same faults or evil nature.
s: When two corrupt officials are caught taking bribes together and they're clearly just as guilty as each other. When you notice that all the members of a dishonest group share the same moral failings and deserve equal blame.

m: Even the tiniest amount or smallest detail; used to describe something insignificant or a minute quantity.
s: When discussing how even small mistakes matter in precision work like surgery or engineering. When someone is being overly concerned about tiny, negligible differences that don't really matter in the big picture.

m: Completely naked or without any clothing whatsoever.
s: When describing someone who is fully nude. When talking about a person who has lost all their clothes or possessions.

l: not careless even in the slightest detail
m: To be extremely careful, thorough, and meticulous in attending to every detail without any negligence.
s: When a surgeon performs an operation with extreme precision, checking every step carefully. When someone proofreads a document multiple times to catch any tiny mistakes. When a craftsman spends hours perfecting a piece of work to ensure absolute quality.

m: accomplish two beneficial goals with a single action or effort.
s: When you exercise and lose weight at the same time, you get two benefits from one activity. When taking a job that both pays well and gives you experience in your desired field. When you clean your house while listening to an audiobook and accomplish household chores and learning simultaneously.

l: Become famous in a single move
m: To achieve sudden fame or recognition through one notable accomplishment or event.
s: When a musician releases one viral song that makes them instantly famous. When an unknown actor gets cast in a major blockbuster film and becomes a household name overnight.

m: Once the main problem is resolved, all related problems are automatically resolved.
s: When you finally pay off your largest debt and suddenly feel like all your financial worries are gone. When a company fires a problematic manager and the entire team's morale improves overnight.

m: to fail to achieve success in anything despite effort or time spent.
s: When someone has been working on a project for years but has nothing to show for it. When a person tries many different careers but never succeeds at any of them. When someone spends all their money on a venture and ends up with nothing.

m: To recount or explain something in complete detail, omitting nothing and following a systematic order from beginning to end.
s: When someone asks you what happened during an event and you explain every single detail in order. When a witness describes everything they saw to the police without leaving anything out.

p: yī rén chuán xū ， wàn rén chuán shí
l: One person spreads falsehood, ten thousand people spread it as truth
m: A false rumor or lie can become accepted as fact when repeated by many people, regardless of its actual truth value.
s: When false information spreads on social media and people believe it just because everyone is sharing it. When a false accusation against someone gets repeated so many times that people start to believe it's true, even without evidence. When gossip becomes accepted as fact in a community simply because many people are talking about it.

p: yī rén dé dào ， jī quǎn shēng tiān
l: One person attains the way, the chickens and dogs ascend to heaven
m: When someone gains power or success, their relatives and associates benefit from their rise, even those who are undeserving.
s: When a friend gets a high-paying job and suddenly all their family members get hired at the same company. When a politician wins an election and appoints all their friends and relatives to cushy government positions regardless of qualifications.

p: yī rén nán rú qiān rén yì
l: One person cannot satisfy a thousand people's wishes
m: It is impossible for one person to please everyone or meet the diverse expectations of many people.
s: When a manager makes a decision that some employees like but others criticize. When a teacher tries to make lessons interesting for students with different learning styles and preferences. When an artist creates work knowing that different people will have conflicting opinions about it.

l: one final determination of male and female
m: to have a final decisive contest to determine who is superior or who will prevail.
s: When two rivals finally agree to settle their dispute once and for all through competition. When competitors meet in a championship match to see who is truly the best.

m: To completely sever a relationship or connection in a clean and decisive manner, leaving no ambiguity or possibility of reconciliation.
s: When a couple decides to break up and wants to end things completely without staying in contact. When someone quits a job and wants to have nothing more to do with the company or former colleagues.

p: yī zé yǐ xǐ ， yī zé yǐ jù
l: one part rejoicing, one part fearing
m: To experience mixed emotions about the same situation, feeling both joy and worry or hope and dread simultaneously.
s: When you get a promotion at work but worry about whether you can handle the new responsibilities. When your child is getting married and you're happy for them but anxious about the changes ahead. When a risky investment pays off but you're still nervous about what could have gone wrong.

l: one moment worth a thousand pieces of gold
m: time is extremely precious and valuable, and every moment should be cherished and used wisely.
s: When someone is in a critical situation where every second matters, like a student cramming for an exam the night before, or a surgeon performing a delicate operation. When you want to remind someone that they shouldn't waste time on trivial things because life is short and opportunities are fleeting.

m: Accomplish something once that solves a problem permanently, requiring no further effort or worry.
s: When someone completes a difficult project that eliminates future problems entirely. When a company invests in a system upgrade that means they won't need to fix issues constantly anymore.

m: A hope or plan that only one person desires, without consideration or agreement from the other party involved.
s: When someone assumes their crush likes them back without any real evidence. When a parent plans their child's entire future career without asking what the child actually wants to do.

m: Once something is lost or gone, it cannot be recovered or brought back.
s: When time passes and you realize you can't get those moments back with someone you care about. When a business closes down and you know it will never reopen in the same way. When someone moves away and you understand that your old friendship dynamic is permanently changed.

m: To behave in a way that is completely contrary to one's normal habits or character.
s: When a quiet person suddenly speaks up loudly at a meeting. When someone who is always late arrives early for the first time. When a person known for being serious suddenly makes jokes and acts silly.

l: one strand holds a thousand pounds
m: A critical situation where everything hangs in the balance and disaster is imminent if the slightest thing goes wrong.
s: When a company is on the brink of bankruptcy and one bad decision could destroy it completely. When a student is barely passing a class and one failed exam would mean they have to repeat the year. When a bridge is structurally compromised and could collapse at any moment.

m: A small sign or detail can indicate a larger trend or change that is about to happen.
s: When you notice one person leaving a company and predict that others will follow soon. When a minor setback in a project makes you realize bigger problems are coming. When one critical comment about a movie hints that it will receive poor reviews overall.

p: yī yè zhàng mù ， bú jiàn tài shān
l: A single leaf obstructs the view and cannot see Mount Tai
m: A minor issue prevents someone from seeing the bigger picture or recognizing something important and obvious.
s: When someone focuses so much on a small problem that they miss the main point. When a person gets so caught up in one detail that they fail to notice the obvious solution or larger truth right in front of them.

m: When one person calls out, hundreds of people respond immediately, indicating great influence, popularity, or widespread support.
s: When a popular leader makes an announcement and everyone immediately supports and follows it. When a famous celebrity posts something on social media and thousands of followers instantly engage with it. When a respected team captain motivates the group and all members enthusiastically rally behind the cause.

m: When one person calls out, many people immediately respond with agreement or obedience, indicating someone has great authority or influence.
s: When a popular leader makes a suggestion and everyone immediately agrees and follows along. When a celebrity announces something and their fans instantly support it without questioning. When a boss gives an order and all the employees quickly comply.

m: To die or pass away, often used to describe someone's death in a final or dramatic way.
s: When someone dies unexpectedly in an accident or illness. When describing a character's death in a story or historical account. When someone passes away after a long struggle with disease.

m: A group of people quickly disperses in chaos or disorder, often suddenly and without coordination.
s: When a crowd suddenly breaks up and runs away in panic, like when people hear a loud noise at a gathering. When a group of friends who were hanging out together suddenly all leave at once without much warning.

m: Two people coordinate perfectly with each other, acting in agreement or complementing each other's actions seamlessly.
s: When two coworkers work together so smoothly that they anticipate each other's needs without speaking. When a comedy duo delivers jokes with perfect timing, with one person setting up and the other delivering the punchline flawlessly.

l: one sings and a hundred respond
m: When one person initiates something, many others quickly follow and support it, showing widespread agreement or enthusiasm.
s: When a popular influencer suggests a new trend and thousands of people immediately adopt it. When one employee speaks up about a workplace problem and suddenly everyone agrees and joins in. When a leader proposes an idea and the team enthusiastically gets behind it without hesitation.

m: A group of people who maintain perfect agreement and goodwill with each other without any conflict or discord.
s: When a team works together so smoothly that there are no arguments or disagreements. When describing a family or group of friends who always get along perfectly and never have any tension between them.

m: A situation where power is divided equally among three authorities, resulting in confusion and lack of clear leadership.
s: When a company has three co-CEOs who can't agree on direction and nothing gets decided. When a family has three adult children all trying to run the household after a parent passes away, causing constant conflict.

m: Everything falls apart or fails completely; a total mess or complete disaster.
s: When a student fails all their classes and gets expelled from school. When a company loses all its major clients and goes bankrupt. When someone's plans completely fall through and nothing works out as intended.

m: Everything is in complete chaos and disorder, with no way to fix or salvage the situation.
s: When a project falls apart and becomes impossible to manage. When someone's life is in complete disarray and falling apart in every way.

p: yī shī zú chéng qiān gǔ hèn
l: One false step becomes eternal regret
m: A single careless mistake or wrong decision can have irreversible consequences that haunt someone for the rest of their life.
s: When someone makes one impulsive choice that ruins their future, like a student cheating on an important exam that gets them expelled. When a person commits one serious error, such as infidelity or a crime, that permanently damages their reputation and relationships.

m: continuing to behave or perform in exactly the same way as before, without any change.
s: When someone maintains their usual habits or behavior despite changing circumstances. When a coworker shows up late to meetings just like they always have. When a friend remains loyal and supportive through the years, exactly as they've always been.

l: the view of a single hole
m: A narrow, limited perspective based on insufficient information or experience.
s: When someone forms an opinion based on only one small piece of information and refuses to consider the bigger picture. When a person criticizes something they've only briefly encountered without understanding the full context.

l: one character worth a thousand pieces of gold
m: Words or writing that are extremely valuable, precious, and worth a great deal because they are eloquent, wise, or influential.
s: When a famous author's brief endorsement causes a product to sell out. When a renowned teacher's single piece of advice transforms a student's life. When a celebrity's short statement becomes widely quoted and has enormous impact on public opinion.

m: A sincere and unwavering devotion or loyalty that remains steadfast despite difficulties or challenges.
s: When someone demonstrates genuine loyalty to a friend or cause even when it becomes inconvenient or costly. When a person shows their true commitment by continuing to support someone through hard times without expecting reward or recognition.

p: yī cùn guāng yīn yī cùn jīn
l: One inch of time is one inch of gold
m: Time is extremely valuable and should not be wasted, as it cannot be recovered once lost.
s: When someone is procrastinating and you want to remind them that they should be studying or working instead. When a student realizes they've spent their entire day scrolling through social media and could have accomplished so much more.

m: To be completely pure, clean, or untainted, either physically or morally.
s: When describing someone with an impeccable reputation who has never done anything wrong. When you see a pristine room or workspace that is perfectly organized and spotless. When talking about someone who maintains high moral standards and refuses to engage in any dishonest behavior.

m: A small error or mishap can escalate into a serious problem or disaster through a chain of unfortunate consequences.
s: When you forget to save a document and then accidentally close the program, losing all your work. When someone misses one deadline and it causes a domino effect of missed appointments and broken commitments.

m: Everything goes smoothly and successfully without any obstacles or difficulties.
s: When someone starts a new job and everything goes perfectly from day one. When a couple gets married and their life together is free from major problems or conflicts.

m: To completely eliminate or remove something without leaving any trace or remainder.
s: When you thoroughly clean your house and get rid of all the clutter and dust. When a company fires all the corrupt officials and removes every trace of their wrongdoing. When someone cuts off all contact with their past and leaves nothing behind.

m: Balance between work and rest, or between tension and relaxation, is necessary for sustainability and effectiveness.
s: When someone works too hard without taking breaks and burns out. When a manager alternates between strict deadlines and relaxed periods to keep the team motivated and productive.

m: Unwavering and profound devotion or love that remains constant and sincere regardless of circumstances.
s: When someone stays loyal to a person or cause despite hardship or rejection. When describing a person who loves deeply and would do anything for the people they care about, no matter what happens.

m: To advance with unwavering determination and resolve, refusing to retreat or be discouraged by obstacles.
s: When someone pursues their goal despite facing many setbacks and challenges. When a team pushes forward with full commitment to win a difficult competition without giving up.

m: A small or isolated success that does not represent one's overall abilities or true character.
s: When someone gets lucky once and thinks they're an expert. When a person has one good day at work but is generally unreliable, and you don't want to overestimate their abilities based on that one time.

m: A modest or humble expression of one's own limited insight or understanding, typically used when offering a simple opinion or suggestion.
s: When you're offering a basic idea to a group of experts and want to be humble about it. When someone politely shares their simple observation while downplaying their own intelligence or expertise.

m: People are united with a single shared purpose and commitment, working together in perfect harmony.
s: When a team comes together to achieve a common goal despite their differences. When a family stands united to overcome a difficult challenge. When colleagues put aside personal interests to focus on what's best for the company.

m: To be completely focused and committed to something with undivided attention and sincere dedication.
s: When someone devotes all their energy to achieving a single goal without distraction. When a person shows unwavering loyalty and commitment to another person or cause. When describing someone who pursues their dreams with complete determination and no divided loyalties.

l: a difference of a single thought
m: A momentary lapse in judgment or a fleeting wrong thought can lead to completely different and often disastrous outcomes.
s: When someone makes a terrible decision on impulse that ruins their life, like quitting a good job without thinking. When a person commits a crime because they had one moment of weakness or temptation. When a split-second wrong choice leads to a major accident or regrettable consequence.

l: while a single breath still remains
m: As long as one is still alive, one should continue to strive or fight, never giving up hope.
s: When someone is determined to keep trying despite being in a difficult situation. When a person refuses to accept defeat and continues fighting for their goal until the very end.

l: persist stubbornly in one's own way
m: To insist on going one's own way without listening to others' advice or opinions, regardless of the consequences.
s: When someone refuses to listen to reasonable advice from friends or family and does exactly what they want anyway. When a person keeps making the same bad decision even after multiple people have warned them it won't work out.

m: Refusing to change or adapt, remaining rigidly the same regardless of circumstances.
s: When a company uses the exact same marketing strategy for decades despite changing customer preferences. When someone insists on doing things exactly the way they've always done them, even when better methods are available.

m: One person alone takes on all the responsibility or work for something that should be shared or delegated.
s: When a manager refuses to delegate tasks and insists on doing all the work themselves. When one family member always takes charge of organizing everything for holidays, events, or family matters without letting others help.

m: A single person wielding so much power that they can control everything and manipulate the truth, as if they could literally block out the sun with one hand.
s: When a corrupt official uses their position to cover up crimes and nobody can stop them. When a powerful CEO suppresses information and controls the entire narrative in their company. When a dictator has absolute authority and no one dares to challenge their version of events.

m: Something is entirely removed, consumed, or depleted so that nothing remains.
s: When all the food at a party is eaten and there's nothing left. When a store sells out of a popular item within hours. When savings are completely spent due to an unexpected expense.

m: A specialized skill or expertise in a particular area that someone has developed and can rely on.
s: When someone is really good at one specific thing like coding, cooking, or playing an instrument. When a person's main strength is in one particular area that sets them apart from others.

m: death and the grave, or the insignificance of human life in the face of mortality
s: When reflecting on how all humans eventually return to dust and die. When someone is reminding another person not to be too attached to material wealth or status since death is inevitable.

m: Two people or groups quickly agree and work together harmoniously with perfect understanding.
s: When you meet someone new and immediately click with them. When two business partners quickly find common ground and decide to start a project together. When friends instantly understand each other's ideas without needing much explanation.

l: accomplish with a single wave of the hand
m: To complete something quickly and effortlessly, especially something creative or skillful, as if it requires minimal effort.
s: When a talented artist sketches a beautiful drawing in just a few minutes without hesitation. When an experienced writer finishes an entire article in one sitting with remarkable ease and speed.

l: one throw of a thousand gold pieces
m: To spend money extravagantly and wastefully without regard for consequences or future need.
s: When someone who just received a large bonus immediately buys expensive luxury items they don't need. When a wealthy person casually spends enormous amounts of money on frivolous things without thinking twice about the cost.

m: To abandon one's former bad habits or ways and make a genuine change for the better.
s: When someone who used to be lazy suddenly starts working hard and getting good results. When a friend who always arrived late to meetings suddenly becomes punctual and reliable.

m: Something is completely worthless and has no value at all.
s: When someone's promise turns out to be meaningless because they never follow through. When a business idea sounds good but has no actual practical value. When a qualification or degree becomes worthless because the field it represents no longer exists.

l: not a single thing can be taken
m: Completely lacking in merit, value, or redeeming qualities; utterly worthless.
s: When you review someone's work and find absolutely nothing good about it. When describing a person who has no positive qualities or skills whatsoever. When something is so poorly done that there's nothing worth salvaging from it.

m: To be in a state of complete poverty or destitution, possessing absolutely nothing of value or worth.
s: When someone loses everything in a disaster and has to start completely from scratch. When a person immigrates to a new country with no money, no possessions, and no connections.

m: To be completely ignorant or have no knowledge whatsoever about something.
s: When someone asks you about a topic and you have absolutely no idea what they're talking about. When you start a new job and don't know anything about the company's procedures or systems yet.

l: having nothing in which to excel
m: To lack any special skills, talents, or areas of expertise.
s: When describing someone who doesn't seem to be good at anything in particular. When a person struggles to find their strengths or what they're good at. When someone has tried many things but hasn't developed any real competence in any of them.

m: completely worthless or useless in every way, with nothing of value to offer.
s: When describing someone who is completely incompetent and can't do anything right. When criticizing a failed plan or product that has no redeeming qualities whatsoever.

l: one day seems like three autumns
m: Time passes extremely slowly when you are separated from someone or something you miss; a single day feels like an eternity when longing for another person.
s: When you're waiting for your partner to return from a long business trip and every day feels unbearably long. When a child misses their parent who is away and counts down the days until they come back, feeling like each day lasts forever.

m: To progress or develop at an extremely rapid pace, advancing with extraordinary speed.
s: When a startup company grows from zero to millions in revenue within a year. When a student's skills improve dramatically after intensive training. When a technology spreads across the entire country in just a few months.

l: one day of exposure to ten days of cold
m: Inconsistent effort and commitment will prevent you from achieving lasting results or progress.
s: When someone practices an instrument enthusiastically for one day then abandons it for weeks. When a student studies hard before an exam but doesn't maintain consistent effort throughout the semester. When someone starts a fitness routine with excitement but quickly gives up and goes months without exercising.

m: A vast expanse that extends so far that the eye cannot see where it ends.
s: Standing on a high mountain looking out at the endless ocean. Walking through a massive desert and seeing nothing but sand stretching to the horizon. Looking across a flat prairie where fields extend as far as you can see.

m: Something is so obvious or clear that you can understand it immediately at a single glance without needing further explanation.
s: When you look at someone's face and can immediately tell they're upset or lying. When a document is written so clearly that you understand its meaning right away without reading it multiple times.

m: Something cannot be accomplished in a short period of time; it requires sustained effort over a longer duration.
s: When a student says they can't master a language in just one day of studying. When someone expects to build a successful business overnight without understanding it takes months or years of hard work.

c: 一朝被蛇咬，十年怕井绳
p: yī zhāo bèi shé yǎo ， shí nián pà jǐng shéng
l: Once bitten by a snake, fear the well rope for ten years
m: A traumatic experience causes someone to remain fearful and overly cautious about similar situations for a long time afterward.
s: When someone has a bad experience with a product and refuses to buy that brand again for years. When a person who was in a car accident becomes extremely anxious every time they get in a vehicle, even though statistically driving is safe.

l: one capital yields ten thousand profits
m: A small initial investment or effort produces enormous returns or gains.
s: When someone invests a small amount of money and it grows into a fortune. When a teacher spends minimal effort creating a lesson plan that benefits thousands of students for years to come.

m: To appear or behave in an extremely serious, formal, and dignified manner, often in a way that seems overly stiff or self-important.
s: When someone is always putting on a very formal and serious face, even in casual situations. When a person acts extremely proper and stern, making it hard for others to relax around them. When someone delivers a joke or absurd statement while maintaining a completely serious expression and tone.

m: To do something in a rigid, measured, and tedious manner without flexibility or spontaneity.
s: When someone follows rules so strictly that they become boring and inefficient. When a teacher explains a concept in such a mechanical, step-by-step way that students lose interest. When a person does their job correctly but in such a dull, monotonous manner that it lacks any creativity or engagement.

m: A brief moment of glory or success that turns out to be merely a dream with no lasting reality.
s: When someone achieves sudden wealth or fame but loses it all just as quickly. When you wake up from a dream where you accomplished something amazing, only to realize it never actually happened. When someone's plans for success fall apart and they realize they were just fantasizing.

l: kill with a single blow of a stick
m: to condemn or reject everything or everyone based on a single fault or incident without considering individual circumstances.
s: When a teacher fails all students in a class because a few didn't do their homework. When someone says they'll never trust any politicians because one was corrupt. When a parent punishes all their children equally for something only one did.

m: To treat all cases or things as identical without making distinctions or considering individual differences.
s: When a teacher grades all students the same way without considering their different abilities or circumstances. When someone says all people from a certain country are the same without recognizing individual differences. When a manager applies one rule to every employee regardless of their unique situations.

m: Two things are completely identical or exactly the same in every way.
s: When you see two twins who look exactly alike and people can't tell them apart. When a counterfeit product is made so well that it's indistinguishable from the original. When two friends wear the same outfit without planning it beforehand.

l: ascend to heaven in a single step
m: To achieve sudden and dramatic success or advancement from a lowly position to an extremely high one.
s: When someone unexpectedly gets promoted from an entry-level job to a top executive position overnight. When a struggling artist suddenly becomes famous and wealthy after one viral performance. When a person from poverty wins the lottery and becomes extremely rich instantly.

m: Extremely stingy and unwilling to part with even the smallest amount of money or possessions.
s: When someone refuses to spend any money or share anything, no matter how small the cost. When a wealthy person is known for being incredibly cheap and never donates or helps others financially.

p: yī bō wèi píng ， yī bō yòu qǐ
l: One wave has not yet settled, another wave rises again
m: As soon as one problem is resolved, another one immediately emerges; troubles come one after another without respite.
s: When you finally finish dealing with a work crisis, but then your car breaks down the same day. When someone recovers from one illness only to catch another one right after. When a company solves one business problem but immediately faces a different challenge.

m: Something spreads, flows, or progresses unstoppably and rapidly without any obstruction or restraint.
s: When a rumor spreads through a whole office in just hours. When a talented athlete's career suddenly takes off and they become wildly successful. When a river overflows its banks and the floodwater rushes across the entire landscape uncontrollably.

m: Something is completely clear and easy to understand with no confusion or ambiguity whatsoever.
s: When you finally understand a complicated math problem after your teacher explains it carefully. When someone shows you evidence that proves exactly what happened in a situation, leaving no doubt at all.

m: A situation or place that is completely lifeless, unchanging, and lacks any vitality, progress, or hope for improvement.
s: When describing a company that hasn't innovated in years and has lost all its talented employees. When a town has become completely depressed with no new businesses or opportunities and everyone wants to leave.

m: Everyone has someone or something that can control or defeat them; there is always a superior force or person that can overcome any other.
s: When someone who seems invincible finally meets their match. When a bully encounters someone tougher than them and backs down. When a stubborn person finally listens to the one person they respect.

m: A group of people who lack unity, organization, or common purpose and therefore cannot work effectively together.
s: When a team has no leader and everyone is doing their own thing instead of working toward a common goal. When a group of people cannot agree on anything and constantly bicker, making it impossible to accomplish anything together.

m: Something is so obvious or clear that you can understand it immediately at a single glance.
s: When a chart or diagram makes the data immediately obvious without needing explanation. When someone's true intentions or feelings are immediately obvious from their behavior or expression. When a situation is so straightforward that there's no need for lengthy discussion or analysis.

p: yī zhe bù shèn ， mǎn pán jiē shū
l: One move not careful, the whole board all lost
m: A single mistake or careless decision can result in complete failure or ruin of an entire endeavor.
s: When someone's one bad decision at work causes an important project to completely fall apart. When a student makes one critical error on a major test that ruins their overall grade. When a business makes one wrong strategic choice that leads to the collapse of the entire company.

l: knowing one part and understanding half
m: Having only superficial or incomplete knowledge about something without truly understanding it deeply.
s: When someone reads one article about a topic and thinks they're an expert on it. When a student memorizes facts for a test but doesn't actually understand the concepts. When a person overhears a conversation and then pretends to know all about the subject.

m: Extremely impoverished with nothing at all, lacking both material resources and cultural foundation.
s: When describing a country that has just emerged from war or colonialism with almost no infrastructure or wealth. When someone loses everything due to bankruptcy or disaster and has to start completely from scratch.

m: To have absolutely no understanding or knowledge of something whatsoever.
s: When someone has never learned a subject and understands nothing about it, like asking a person with no musical training to explain music theory. When your friend admits they don't know anything at all about computers or cooking.

m: To dismiss or ignore something with a smile, treating it as unimportant or not worth taking seriously.
s: When someone makes a rude comment but you just laugh it off instead of getting upset. When your friend tells an obvious joke or makes a silly argument, and you just smile and move on without engaging with it seriously.

l: erase with a single stroke of the brush
m: to completely wipe away all past debts, grievances, or mistakes and start fresh as if they never happened.
s: When two friends have a big argument but decide to forgive each other and pretend it never happened. When a company decides to forgive all of an employee's previous mistakes and give them a fresh start after they apologize.

m: to dismiss, reject, or completely negate something with a single decisive action, leaving no room for nuance or consideration.
s: When a boss fires an employee without considering their years of good work. When someone dismisses an entire person's character based on one mistake. When a critic completely rejects an artist's body of work based on one failure.

m: To be completely at a loss and unable to think of any way to solve a problem or move forward.
s: When you're facing a difficult situation and have tried everything you can think of but nothing works. When someone is stuck on a problem and has run out of ideas about what to do next.

m: To achieve two important goals or desired outcomes with a single action or effort.
s: When you complete a work project that also impresses your boss and gets you a promotion. When you exercise to stay healthy and also lose weight at the same time. When you buy a gift for someone that they really needed anyway.

m: A written agreement or official document that is worthless because it has no real effect or enforcement behind it.
s: When a contract is signed but nobody actually follows it or enforces it. When a government issues a law but doesn't have the resources or will to make people obey it. When someone makes a promise in writing but has no intention of keeping it.

m: To capture or eliminate all members of a group or all instances of a problem at once, leaving none behind.
s: When police raid a criminal operation and arrest all the gang members in one action. When a company fires all underperforming employees in a single round of layoffs. When you finally organize your messy room and deal with every single item at once.

p: yì ér zài ， zài ér sān
l: once and again, again and a third time
m: Something happens repeatedly or multiple times in succession, often suggesting a pattern of recurrence.
s: When someone keeps making the same mistake over and over again. When a friend repeatedly breaks their promises to you. When a coworker continues to be late to meetings despite being warned multiple times.

m: Ideas, traditions, or characteristics pass down through an unbroken line of succession, maintaining continuity and consistency from predecessors.
s: When a company maintains the same business philosophy that its founder established decades ago. When a child displays the same artistic talents and creative approach as their parent, showing a direct continuation of style and ability.

m: to provide help or support, even if it is modest or limited in scope.
s: When a colleague helps you with a project even though they're busy. When someone contributes to a group effort by doing whatever small task they can manage. When you want to acknowledge that someone's contribution, though not huge, still made a meaningful difference.

m: ordinary or average level of knowledge and judgment that most people possess.
s: When someone lacks basic knowledge about a common topic that most people know. When you're explaining why you can't reason with someone who doesn't have fundamental understanding of how things work.

l: fall ten thousand feet in one drop
m: To experience a sudden, dramatic decline in status, fortune, or condition.
s: When a successful business suddenly collapses and loses all its value. When someone who was once respected becomes disgraced and loses their reputation overnight. When a student's grades plummet from excellent to failing in just one semester.

p: yī xiè bù rú yī xiè
l: one crab is not as good as one crab
m: Each successive attempt or generation is worse than the previous one, representing a continuous decline in quality or performance.
s: When a student's test scores keep getting lower with each exam despite studying. When a company's products become progressively worse with each new release. When someone's excuses for being late get more ridiculous each time it happens.

m: Two places that are separated by only a narrow body of water, implying they are very close to each other despite being divided.
s: When talking about two neighboring countries separated by a river or strait, like how close Taiwan is to mainland China. When describing two cities on opposite sides of a narrow channel that are practically neighbors. When emphasizing how two regions are almost touching despite being technically separated by water.

l: one sight as if old acquaintances
m: To feel an immediate and deep sense of familiarity and connection with someone upon first meeting, as though you have known them for a long time.
s: When you meet someone new and instantly feel comfortable with them, like you've known each other forever. When two people click immediately and feel like old friends even though they just met.

l: love is struck at first sight
m: To fall in love with someone immediately upon seeing them for the first time.
s: When you meet someone and instantly feel attracted to them before even knowing anything about their personality. When two people lock eyes across a room and immediately feel a romantic connection.

m: To treat everyone fairly and impartially without discrimination or favoritism.
s: When a teacher grades all students by the same standards regardless of background. When a manager gives the same opportunities and respect to all team members equally. When a judge applies the law consistently to everyone who comes before the court.

m: Everything is completely visible and exposed at a single glance with nothing concealed.
s: When you stand on a high mountain and can see the entire city spread out before you with no obstructions. When someone's true intentions or feelings are so obvious that they cannot hide anything from you.

m: A situation is so tense or volatile that even the slightest provocation will cause an immediate and violent eruption or confrontation.
s: When a workplace is so filled with tension between two employees that any small disagreement could spark a huge argument. When a political situation is so unstable that one wrong move by a leader could trigger a major conflict or crisis.

m: Something that appears to have some substance but is actually extremely fragile and will fall apart with the slightest pressure or opposition.
s: When a company that seems successful is revealed to be built on fraud and quickly goes bankrupt. When someone's confident argument falls apart immediately when questioned by an expert. When a relationship that seemed stable suddenly ends completely after one small conflict.

m: A single promise or statement is enough to seal an agreement; one's word is one's bond.
s: When two friends agree on something and shake hands without needing a written contract. When you trust someone's verbal promise so much that you don't need any other confirmation or paperwork.

l: one word to cover it all
m: to summarize or explain something complex in just a few concise words.
s: When you want to describe a long movie plot in just one sentence. When someone asks you to sum up a lengthy report in a brief phrase.

p: yī yán jì chū ， sì mǎ nán zhuī
l: Once a word is spoken, four horses cannot overtake it
m: Once you have said something, you cannot take it back or undo the consequences, so you must be careful with your words.
s: When someone makes a promise or commitment and realizes they can't back out of it. When you say something hurtful to a friend and wish you could unsay it but know the damage is already done. When a public figure makes a controversial statement and can't simply retract it without consequences.

m: Something is too complex, profound, or lengthy to be fully expressed or explained in just a few words.
s: When someone asks you about a complicated situation and you don't know where to begin because there's so much to explain. When you're trying to describe a deep emotional experience but realize words just aren't enough to capture it all.

m: A single remark cuts through confusion or pretense to reveal the essential truth of a matter.
s: When someone makes a brief comment that suddenly clarifies a confusing situation everyone has been debating. When a friend points out in just a few words what the real problem is that everyone else has been dancing around.

m: A single statement or remark reveals the true nature of something that was previously hidden or misunderstood.
s: When someone makes a brief comment that suddenly explains a confusing situation. When a simple observation from a friend cuts through all the complexity and shows what was really going on.

m: To repeatedly make the same or similar mistakes, compounding errors through failure to correct course.
s: When someone keeps making the same mistake over and over without learning from it. When a person's poor decision leads to another bad decision, making the situation worse. When a company ignores warning signs and continues down the wrong path, causing larger problems.

l: one promise worth a thousand pieces of gold
m: A person's word is extremely valuable and trustworthy; when someone makes a promise, they will absolutely keep it no matter what.
s: When describing someone who always follows through on their commitments and can be relied upon completely. When you want to praise a friend or colleague for their unwavering integrity and honesty in keeping their promises.

l: one defeat smeared across the ground
m: A complete and utter defeat or failure from which there is no recovery.
s: When a company's product launch fails so badly that they lose all their market share and credibility. When a sports team loses so decisively in the championship that their season is completely ruined and they're eliminated from competition.

m: Extremely poor with nothing at all, having been stripped of all possessions and resources.
s: When someone has lost everything due to bankruptcy or disaster and is left with absolutely nothing. When describing someone who is destitute and has no money, food, or belongings to their name.

m: Wishing someone a safe and smooth journey with no accidents or obstacles along the way.
s: When you say goodbye to a friend who is about to take a long trip or drive somewhere far away. When you want to wish someone well before they travel abroad or embark on any kind of journey.

m: To achieve something quickly and easily in one decisive action, without needing gradual steps or multiple attempts.
s: When someone solves a difficult problem immediately on their first try. When a talented athlete wins a competition without any struggle or practice needed. When a company successfully launches a major project right away without delays or revisions.

m: After suffering a major setback or failure, someone loses confidence and momentum, unable to bounce back or regain their former success.
s: When a student fails an important exam and becomes so discouraged they stop trying in school. When a company experiences a major business loss and gradually declines despite efforts to recover. When an athlete gets seriously injured and loses the will to train and compete again.

m: To be extraordinarily brave and fearless, with courage being one's defining characteristic.
s: When someone volunteers to face a dangerous situation without hesitation or shows no fear in the face of threats. When a person demonstrates exceptional bravery by standing up to someone much more powerful or confronting a terrifying challenge head-on.

m: To identify the core issue or problem with direct precision and clarity, cutting through all irrelevant details.
s: When someone asks a simple question that immediately reveals the real problem nobody else noticed. When a doctor quickly diagnoses an illness by asking the right questions. When a critic points out the fundamental flaw in an argument that everyone else missed.

m: Something is completely worthless or has no value at all.
s: When someone's promises or words mean nothing because they never follow through. When a product is so poorly made that it has no practical value despite being sold.

l: when asked one question, unable to answer three things
m: To claim complete ignorance or inability to answer questions about something, suggesting either genuine lack of knowledge or deliberate evasion of responsibility.
s: When you ask your coworker about the project status and they claim to know nothing about it, even though they were supposedly involved. When someone gets caught doing something wrong and suddenly claims they don't know anything about it, about how it happened, or why it matters.

m: A very superficial relationship with someone you have only met once or briefly.
s: When you run into someone at a party who you only met once years ago, and they're basically a stranger to you now. When a coworker from another department transfers away and you realize you barely knew them despite working at the same company.

m: An account or testimony from only one party, which may be biased or incomplete and should not be trusted as the whole truth.
s: When someone tells you their version of a story but you haven't heard the other person's side yet. When a boss makes a decision based only on one employee's complaint without hearing from the other employee involved.

m: A wide open, flat, and unobstructed plain where there are no obstacles or hindrances.
s: When you finally finish a difficult project and the remaining work is smooth sailing. When someone recovers from illness and can easily return to their normal activities. When a business expands into a new market with no competition or barriers to entry.

m: To be the first to take action or lead the way, showing initiative and courage in taking on a challenge or responsibility.
s: When a coworker volunteers to tackle the hardest part of a project before anyone else. When a team captain is the first one to sprint onto the field before their teammates follow.

l: one scale and half a claw
m: Only a tiny, incomplete fragment or glimpse of something much larger, revealing very little of the whole picture.
s: When you only see a small part of a movie trailer and can't tell what the full story is about. When someone shows you just one page from a thick report and you can't understand the complete situation. When you overhear just a few words of a conversation and can only guess what people were really discussing.

m: To achieve sudden fame or success after a long period of obscurity or silence.
s: When an unknown musician releases their first song and it immediately becomes a viral hit. When a quiet employee finally speaks up in a meeting and impresses everyone with brilliant ideas.

m: To accomplish something through sustained momentum and determination without hesitation or delay.
s: When you need to push through a difficult project without stopping to second-guess yourself. When a team needs to stay focused and motivated to finish a challenging task before losing energy or confidence. When someone should take action immediately while they still have the will and enthusiasm to do it.

m: to be in complete agreement or act in perfect coordination with someone, as if sharing a single breath.
s: When two business partners make decisions together without any disagreement or conflict. When a group of friends always supports each other's ideas and acts as a unified team without internal disputes.

m: To be in a state of extreme anxiety, nervousness, or emotional turmoil with one's feelings in complete disarray.
s: When you're waiting for important exam results and can't sit still or focus. When someone is nervous before a big job interview and their emotions are all over the place. When you're worried about a loved one who is late coming home and your heart won't stop racing.

m: Many people talking at the same time, creating a chaotic and noisy environment where it's hard to hear any single voice clearly.
s: When a group of people all start talking over each other at a meeting and nobody can get a word in. When you're in a crowded room and everyone is chattering loudly at once, making it impossible to have a normal conversation.

m: Many people working together in a confused or disorganized manner, with a lot of hustle and bustle.
s: When a group of people all try to help at once and end up getting in each other's way. When coworkers rush to complete a task together but nobody has a clear plan, resulting in chaos and inefficiency.

m: To assemble something by gathering miscellaneous scraps and fragments from various sources without coherent organization or quality.
s: When someone writes an essay by copying random sentences from different sources without properly organizing them. When you throw together a meal using leftover ingredients from your fridge instead of following a real recipe. When a company creates a product by combining cheap parts from multiple suppliers rather than designing it properly.

m: To be extremely angry or furious, with anger so intense it feels as if smoke is coming from every pore of one's body.
s: When someone is so angry they can barely speak or control themselves. When a person has reached the absolute limit of their patience and is about to explode with rage.

m: A diverse collection of miscellaneous things, troubles, or complaints of varying kinds.
s: When someone complains about many different small problems or ailments at once. When you're dealing with all sorts of minor issues and complications in a situation. When describing a collection of random, unrelated problems or faults.

m: Things are scattered, disorganized, or in complete disarray with items strewn about haphazardly.
s: When you walk into a room after your kids have played and toys are scattered everywhere. When someone's notes and papers are all over their desk in a messy, unorganized way. When a group of people who were supposed to meet up end up arriving at different times in small groups instead of together.

m: To fall or stumble repeatedly in a chaotic and disorderly manner, often describing someone who is severely intoxicated, injured, or in complete disarray.
s: When a drunk person staggers down the street, falling over repeatedly. When someone is so tired or sick that they can barely walk straight and keep losing their balance.

m: Everything goes well and successfully without obstacles or difficulties.
s: When someone is wishing you luck before an important interview or exam. When you hope that a friend's new business venture will succeed without any problems. When congratulating someone embarking on a major life change and wanting everything to work out perfectly for them.

p: wàn shì jù bèi ， zhǐ qiàn dōng fēng
l: All things are prepared, only lacking the east wind
m: Everything is ready for success; we only need one final favorable circumstance or opportunity to achieve our goal.
s: When a company has completed all preparations for a product launch but is waiting for market conditions to improve. When a couple has planned their wedding down to every detail but is just waiting for the right date or weather to happen.

m: Everything is going well and fortunately; all matters have been resolved satisfactorily.
s: When a couple finally gets married after a long engagement and all the wedding preparations are complete. When a business project that faced many obstacles finally launches successfully and everything is running smoothly.

l: ten thousand people empty the streets
m: So many people go to see something that the streets become completely deserted, indicating an event of massive public interest and attraction.
s: When a famous celebrity visits a city and everyone rushes to see them, causing the normally busy streets to empty out. When a major sporting event or concert happens and the entire city seems to shut down because everyone is attending or watching it.

l: ten thousand people with one heart
m: People are united with a common purpose and work together as one collective force.
s: When a community comes together to help rebuild after a disaster. When a team puts aside individual differences to achieve a shared goal. When an entire nation supports a cause with unified determination.

m: In an irretrievable state of ruin or damnation from which there is no possibility of recovery or salvation.
s: When someone has made such catastrophic mistakes that their life is completely ruined beyond any hope of redemption. When a person has committed crimes so serious that they can never restore their reputation or return to a normal life. When a company has lost all credibility and trust and will never recover its business.

p: wàn biàn bù lí qí zōng
l: Ten thousand changes do not depart from their origin
m: Despite countless variations or changes in form, the fundamental essence or core principle remains unchanged.
s: When a company rebrands and changes its marketing strategy, but still maintains the same core values and mission. When a musician experiments with different genres over their career, but their distinctive style and artistic vision always shine through. When someone moves to a different country and adopts new customs, yet their fundamental personality and beliefs stay the same.

l: ten thousand ages and a thousand autumns
m: Something that will last forever or endure through all eternity.
s: When describing a monument or legacy that will be remembered forever. When expressing the timeless significance of a great achievement or contribution to humanity.

l: ten thousand ages flow with fragrance
m: One's name and reputation will be remembered and celebrated throughout endless generations.
s: When discussing a historical figure whose achievements continue to inspire people centuries later. When someone accomplishes something so remarkable that people will remember and honor them forever.

m: To exist or last forever, transcending the passage of time and remaining eternal.
s: When talking about how a great work of art or literature will be remembered forever. When describing how someone's legacy or influence will never be forgotten, no matter how much time passes.

m: Something endures forever with lasting vitality and relevance, never fading or becoming obsolete.
s: When describing a classic work of literature that remains beloved across generations. When talking about a timeless brand or company that stays relevant and successful no matter how much time passes.

l: ten thousand households' lamps and fires
m: The warm, peaceful glow of countless homes lit up at night, symbolizing a peaceful society where people live safely and contentedly.
s: When describing the beauty of a city skyline at night with all the windows lit up. When talking about the comfort and safety of a thriving, stable community where families are home together.

m: Wishing for someone to live an infinitely long life or for a reign to last forever without end.
s: When you're expressing a sincere wish for someone's eternal health and happiness, especially an elderly person or a respected leader. When offering blessings for someone to enjoy a long, prosperous life without decline or limitation.

m: A miraculous cure or solution that works for every problem, a universal remedy for all ailments or difficulties.
s: When someone claims they have a single solution that will fix all of a company's problems. When a salesperson tries to convince you that one product can solve every health issue you have.

m: absolutely certain to succeed with no possibility of failure or error.
s: When a surgeon has performed a procedure thousands of times and you're confident they won't make a mistake. When a company has such a robust safety system that there's virtually no chance of an accident occurring. When someone is so skilled and experienced at something that failure is virtually impossible.

l: ten thousand deaths and one life
m: Barely escaping death by the narrowest margin; surviving an extremely dangerous or life-threatening situation against all odds.
s: When someone survives a serious car accident that could have easily been fatal. When a soldier returns home after being in countless life-or-death combat situations.

l: ten thousand waters and thousand mountains
m: Despite great distances and numerous obstacles, one persists in pursuit of a goal or relationship.
s: When someone travels very far to see a loved one or achieve something important. When describing how far apart two people are but still maintain their connection through effort and determination.

m: An action or event that is happening in front of many witnesses where it is impossible to hide or deny what occurred.
s: When a famous person makes a mistake in public during a live broadcast with millions watching. When a student gets caught cheating on an exam in a large classroom full of other students and teachers.

m: A state of complete silence or profound quietness where all sounds have ceased.
s: When you walk into an empty library at night and there's absolutely no noise at all. When everyone stops talking and the room becomes completely silent, like during a moment of respect or awe. When you're alone in nature early in the morning before any birds start singing.

l: ten thousand purples and thousand reds
m: A scene of vibrant, colorful beauty with diverse and abundant varieties of colors, typically describing nature in full bloom.
s: When describing a beautiful garden full of different colored flowers in springtime. When talking about the spectacular sight of a field of wildflowers at their peak. When praising the visual richness and variety of colors in a natural landscape.

c: 万般皆下品，惟有读书高
p: wàn bān jiē xià pǐn ， wéi yǒu dú shū gāo
l: All pursuits are base, only reading and studying are noble
m: Academic study and scholarly pursuits are superior to all other occupations and activities.
s: When someone believes that studying hard and getting a good education is the most important goal in life, more important than business or manual labor. When parents emphasize that their children should focus on their studies above all else because education is the path to success and respect.

m: Everything takes on a fresh, new appearance as if the world has been rejuvenated and transformed.
s: When spring arrives and nature blooms after winter, everything looks brand new. When a company gets new leadership and completely changes its direction and energy. After a major renovation, a run-down building suddenly looks vibrant and modern again.

m: A long and arduous journey or undertaking that requires sustained effort and perseverance over an extended period.
s: When someone is starting a major project that will take years to complete, like building a business from scratch. When describing a student's path to mastery in a difficult field, emphasizing it's a marathon, not a sprint.

m: A scene of massive, dynamic movement and overwhelming force, often used metaphorically to describe great momentum, enthusiasm, or chaos on a grand scale.
s: When a large crowd rushes excitedly toward something, like fans stampeding into a concert venue. When describing a booming economy or industry experiencing rapid growth and widespread activity. When a powerful army or movement is advancing with unstoppable momentum and energy.

m: A pervasive, oppressive silence where no one dares to speak, often caused by fear, oppression, or a heavy atmosphere that stifles expression.
s: When a dictator takes power and people are afraid to voice their opinions or criticisms. When a teacher is so strict and intimidating that students sit in complete silence and never ask questions or participate. When a tragedy or shocking event happens and everyone is too stunned or scared to say anything.

m: People gathered or scattered in small groups or clusters rather than as a large unified crowd.
s: When guests arrive at a party in small groups rather than all at once. When people stand around chatting in little clusters at a social gathering instead of forming one big group.

c: 三个臭皮匠，胜过一个诸葛亮
p: sān gè chòu pí jiàng ， shèng guò yí gè zhū gě liàng
l: Three mediocre cobblers surpass one Zhuge Liang
m: Collective wisdom and effort from ordinary people can exceed the brilliance of a single exceptional individual.
s: When a team of average workers solves a difficult problem that one expert couldn't. When multiple people brainstorming together come up with better ideas than one genius working alone. When a group project succeeds because everyone contributed their perspective, even if no single person was particularly talented.

m: People gather together in small clusters or groups, typically informal gatherings of a few people at a time.
s: When you see people standing around in twos and threes chatting after work. When a group of friends casually hangs out together without formal planning, just people showing up in small groups throughout the day.

p: sān rén xíng bì yǒu wǒ shī
l: Among three people walking together, there must be one who is my teacher
m: Everyone has something to teach you, and you can learn from anyone regardless of their status or abilities.
s: When you realize that even people with less experience or education than you can teach you valuable lessons. When you approach conversations with humility and recognize that wisdom can come from unexpected sources, even from those you might initially underestimate.

m: To give strict and repeated instructions or warnings to ensure that someone pays close attention and follows directions carefully.
s: When a manager keeps reminding employees about an important deadline because they worry people aren't taking it seriously. When a parent repeatedly tells their child the house rules before leaving them alone, emphasizing each rule multiple times to make sure they understand.

m: Three separate elements or entities that function together as a single unified whole.
s: When a company's success depends on sales, marketing, and customer service working seamlessly together. When a sports team's offense, defense, and coaching all need to be equally strong to win championships. When a healthy relationship requires trust, communication, and commitment all operating in harmony.

p: sān shí liù jì ， zǒu wéi shàng cè
l: Of the thirty-six stratagems, walking away is the best strategy
m: When faced with an unwinnable or dangerous situation, retreat or escape is the wisest course of action.
s: When someone realizes they're losing an argument and decides to leave rather than continue fighting. When a business recognizes a market is too competitive and decides to exit instead of struggling on. When a person finds themselves in a dangerous situation and chooses to run away rather than confront it.

p: sān jù huà bù lí běn háng
l: Three sentences of speech never leave one's profession
m: Someone constantly brings conversations back to their own field of expertise or profession, no matter what the topic is.
s: When a doctor keeps steering every conversation back to health and medical topics. When a programmer can't stop talking about coding and technology even at social gatherings unrelated to work.

p: sān tiān dǎ yú ， liǎng tiān shài wǎng
l: fish for three days and dry nets for two days
m: to work inconsistently and lack perseverance, alternating between effort and neglect without sustained commitment.
s: When someone tries to exercise or study but only does it sporadically, then stops for long periods. When a person starts a project with enthusiasm but keeps abandoning it instead of seeing it through to completion.

m: To have superhuman abilities or extraordinary power that exceeds normal human capacity.
s: When someone accomplishes an impossible amount of work in a short time. When you admire someone for being able to handle multiple difficult tasks at once. When describing someone who seems to have supernatural strength or skill beyond what's normally possible.

p: sān cùn bù làn zhī shé
l: a three-inch tongue that does not rot
m: The power of eloquence and persuasive speech to accomplish things that force cannot achieve.
s: When a skilled negotiator talks their way out of a difficult situation. When a charismatic salesperson convinces you to buy something through their persuasive words alone. When a diplomat uses clever arguments to resolve a conflict without violence.

m: To be indecisive and lack commitment, unable to focus on one thing because of conflicting thoughts or loyalties.
s: When someone can't decide between two job offers and keeps changing their mind about which one to take. When a student studies for an exam but keeps getting distracted by other interests and can't concentrate properly.

m: Carefully consider the consequences and implications of your actions before proceeding.
s: When someone is about to make a major decision like quitting their job, you might tell them to think it through carefully first. When a friend wants to spend all their savings on something risky, you might advise them to reconsider multiple times before doing it.

m: To feel extremely fortunate or blessed, as if one's good luck spans multiple lifetimes.
s: When someone meets their idol and feels incredibly lucky. When you get an amazing opportunity that seems almost too good to be true. When you're grateful for meeting someone special who changed your life.

m: Something happens repeatedly or many times over, emphasizing frequency and persistence.
s: When someone keeps asking you the same question over and over again despite your answers. When a coworker repeatedly makes the same mistake even after being corrected multiple times. When a family member brings up the same complaint again and again.

m: To say something in just a few brief words; to express oneself concisely and succinctly.
s: When someone explains a complicated problem in just a couple of sentences. When you want to describe how your boss gave quick, simple instructions without going into detail.

m: A situation where three equally powerful forces or factions maintain a state of equilibrium and balance with none able to dominate the others.
s: When three major companies compete equally in a market and none can overtake the others. When three countries or regions have equal military or political power and maintain a tense balance. When three strong candidates or teams are tied in a competition with no clear winner emerging.

m: An unexpected misfortune, accident, or death that occurs suddenly and without warning.
s: When someone dies unexpectedly or meets with a sudden tragic accident. When referring to any unforeseen calamity or disaster that befalls a person, especially death or serious harm.

l: Three visits to a thatched cottage
m: To persistently seek out someone's help or advice through repeated, respectful visits, showing genuine sincerity and humility.
s: When a company keeps coming back to recruit a talented employee who initially refused their offer. When you need to ask someone for a big favor and you visit them multiple times to show how serious and respectful you are about the request.

m: To engage in dishonest or deceptive practices, particularly by manipulating situations or documents to one's advantage.
s: When a judge accepts bribes and rules unfairly in court cases. When a business manager alters records to hide embezzlement or fraud. When someone uses their position of authority to cheat others through deception.

p: shàng bù zhe tiān ， xià bù zhe dì
l: above does not touch the sky, below does not touch the ground
m: To be in an awkward or precarious situation with no solid support or stability; caught between two extremes without a secure position.
s: When someone is stuck in a job they hate but can't afford to quit, feeling trapped between two bad options. When a student hasn't prepared enough to pass the exam but has studied enough that they can't just wing it completely. When a relationship is neither fully committed nor broken up, leaving both people uncertain and uncomfortable.

p: shàng tiān wú lù ， rù dì wú mén
l: Heaven has no path, earth has no door
m: To be in a hopeless situation with no way out or no means of escape.
s: When someone is trapped in a desperate circumstance with no possible solution or escape route. When a person has exhausted all options and feels completely cornered with nowhere to turn.

c: 上无片瓦，下无插针之地
p: shàng wú piàn wǎ ， xià wú chā zhēn zhī dì
l: above there is not a single tile, below there is no space to insert a needle
m: Someone is in extreme poverty with absolutely nothing to their name, owning neither shelter nor any piece of land.
s: When describing someone who has lost everything and become destitute. When talking about a refugee or displaced person with no home and no possessions. When emphasizing how dire someone's financial situation has become.

p: shàng liáng bù zhèng xià liáng wāi
l: If the upper beam is not straight, the lower beam will be crooked
m: When leaders or those in positions of authority behave improperly, their subordinates and followers will inevitably follow suit and act incorrectly as well.
s: When a manager embezzles company funds and then wonders why employees are stealing office supplies. When a parent tells their child not to lie but is caught lying to their spouse. When a teacher breaks their own classroom rules and the students stop following them too.

l: superiors set the example and subordinates follow it
m: When leaders or those in authority behave in a certain way, their subordinates and followers will naturally imitate that behavior.
s: When a manager is always late to meetings and soon all the employees start arriving late too. When a CEO cuts corners on ethics and the entire company's culture becomes dishonest. When a parent shows respect to others and their children grow up treating people with the same courtesy.

m: To be obsequious and flattering to those of higher status while being arrogant and contemptuous toward those of lower status.
s: When a manager is extremely polite and accommodating to the company executives but treats their own subordinates with contempt and disrespect. When someone behaves differently depending on the social rank of the person they're talking to, showing excessive respect to the wealthy and powerful while being dismissive to ordinary people.

m: To be restless, overactive, or constantly moving about in an agitated or excited manner, often suggesting someone is overly eager, nervous, or unable to stay still.
s: When a child is hyperactive and can't sit down during class. When someone is anxious and keeps pacing back and forth before an important event.

l: do not make it a precedent next time
m: This action is being excused this once, but it must not happen again or become a habit.
s: When a teacher lets a student turn in homework late but warns them it cannot happen again. When a boss overlooks an employee's mistake but makes clear that repeating it will have consequences.

p: xià bǐ qiān yán ， lí tí wàn lǐ
l: Write a thousand words, but deviate ten thousand miles from the topic
m: To write at great length while completely missing or straying far from the main point or intended subject matter.
s: When someone writes a long essay but fails to address the actual question or topic asked. When a speaker talks for a long time but barely touches on what they were supposed to discuss, going off on irrelevant tangents instead.

l: just stepped down from the carriage
m: Immediately upon taking office or arriving at a new position, before having time to settle in or understand the situation.
s: When a new manager arrives at a company and immediately makes sweeping changes without understanding how things work. When someone moves to a new city and right away starts criticizing the local customs and culture.

l: lowly people of the lower villages
m: Something that appeals to ordinary common people rather than the educated elite or refined tastes.
s: When someone prefers popular mainstream entertainment over high art or classical works. When a person enjoys simple, everyday pleasures that most regular people appreciate rather than exclusive or sophisticated things.

m: to slow down and carefully observe things rather than rushing through or skimming the surface.
s: When someone stops to really examine details instead of just glancing at something quickly. When a manager takes time to walk through a department and observe how things actually work rather than just reading reports.

m: There are so many examples or instances that they cannot be enumerated; the situation is too numerous and varied to count.
s: When describing how many different types of problems a company is facing. When listing all the various reasons why people failed an exam. When explaining that there are countless examples of people breaking the rules.

m: A person or thing that is disreputable, questionable, or of dubious character and origin.
s: When someone hangs around with shady people and you're not sure what they're involved in. When a business seems sketchy and you don't trust whether it's legitimate or not.

m: Being in an awkward middle position that is neither satisfactory nor complete, stuck in an unsatisfactory in-between state.
s: When someone gets a job that pays okay but isn't really what they wanted, so they feel stuck. When a student gets a middling grade that isn't good enough to be proud of but not bad enough to motivate them to improve.

m: To exercise restraint and avoid pushing a matter to extremes or causing excessive harm.
s: When someone is angry at their friend but decides not to say cruel things that would be irreversible. When a boss is upset with an employee but chooses to give them a warning rather than firing them immediately.

m: Money or gains obtained through immoral, dishonest, or illegal means.
s: When someone gets rich by cheating or stealing from others. When a business makes profits by exploiting workers or breaking the law. When a person refuses to accept money that was earned dishonestly.

l: there is no lack of such people
m: There are plenty of people who possess a certain quality or are willing to do a particular thing.
s: When you're looking for volunteers and many people step forward to help. When discussing how many people are willing to take risks or make sacrifices for a cause they believe in.

l: unable to finish and thus let it go
m: To let something end inconclusively or indefinitely without proper resolution, often by neglecting or abandoning it.
s: When a project gets abandoned halfway through and nobody ever addresses it again. When a conflict between friends is never actually resolved, and everyone just stops talking about it over time. When a complaint is filed but nothing is ever done about it and the matter is simply forgotten.

m: The one and only correct method or way to achieve a desired outcome; the sole path to success.
s: When someone is explaining the best way to solve a problem that has no alternatives. When a teacher insists there is only one right technique to master a skill. When a coach says their training method is the only way to win.

m: To maintain proper composure and dignity by avoiding both excessive pride and unnecessary self-deprecation.
s: When someone treats a janitor with the same respect they would show a CEO. When a student confidently answers a teacher's question without being cocky or apologetic about their knowledge.

m: Something is extremely enjoyable and brings great delight or satisfaction.
s: When someone is having so much fun doing something they love that they lose track of time. When a person is absorbed in an activity and experiencing pure happiness and contentment.

m: to disagree with or dismiss something as unimportant; to regard something with disapproval or skepticism.
s: When your friend suggests a new restaurant but you don't think it's worth trying and brush off their recommendation. When a colleague dismisses your idea in a meeting without taking it seriously or considering its merit.

m: Something that is neither one thing nor another, lacking clear identity or classification and appearing confused or out of place.
s: When someone wears clothes that don't match any particular style and just looks awkward. When a restaurant tries to mix cuisines in a way that makes no sense and confuses customers. When a piece of furniture is designed in such a strange way that it doesn't fit any room's aesthetic.

m: To neglect one's personal grooming and appearance, often reflecting a careless or slovenly attitude toward one's presentation.
