s: When someone shows up to work with messy hair, wrinkled clothes, and hasn't shaved in weeks. When a person stops caring about how they look and dresses sloppily all the time. When you notice a friend has let themselves go and no longer pays attention to their appearance.

m: To respond or act immediately without any hesitation or deliberation.
s: When someone answers a difficult question instantly without pausing to think. When a skilled musician plays a complex piece from memory without any delay or consideration.

m: To be completely impartial and fair without favoring either side.
s: When a judge makes a decision based purely on the evidence without showing bias toward either party. When a teacher grades all students by the same standards without favoritism. When a mediator helps resolve a conflict by treating both sides equally.

p: bù rù hǔ xué ， yān dé hǔ zi
l: If you do not enter the tiger's den, how can you catch the tiger's cub?
m: You cannot achieve great rewards without taking significant risks or making difficult efforts.
s: When someone hesitates to apply for a competitive job because they fear rejection. When a student is afraid to ask a challenging question in class because they might look foolish. When an entrepreneur wants to start a business but is too scared to invest their savings.

m: An irreconcilable enmity so deep that two parties cannot coexist in the world together.
s: When two people have such a bitter conflict that they refuse to be in the same room or even live in the same town. When rivals or enemies have hurt each other so badly that reconciliation seems absolutely impossible.

m: To treat everyone equally without making distinctions, or to share everything without regard to ownership or personal boundaries.
s: When close friends or family members are so comfortable with each other that they freely borrow each other's belongings without asking. When a group of people work together so harmoniously that no one cares who gets credit for what.

m: To fail to distinguish between right and wrong, or to judge matters without careful consideration of the facts.
s: When a teacher punishes all students equally without investigating who actually caused the problem. When someone believes rumors and spreads them without checking if they're true. When a parent scolds their child without hearing their side of the story.

p: bù dào huáng hé xīn bù sǐ
l: The heart will not die until reaching the Yellow River
m: Someone refuses to give up or accept reality until they experience failure or disaster firsthand, no matter how much they are warned.
s: When a teenager insists on touching a hot stove despite being warned it will burn them. When someone keeps gambling despite losing money repeatedly, convinced they will eventually win big. When a friend refuses to believe a relationship is over until their partner actually leaves them.

m: To neglect one's primary responsibilities or legitimate work in favor of frivolous or improper pursuits.
s: When a student skips classes to play video games instead of studying. When someone quits their job to pursue an unrealistic dream without any real plan. When a person wastes time on unproductive hobbies instead of taking care of their family obligations.

m: To focus on practical accomplishments rather than seeking hollow praise or undeserved fame.
s: When someone refuses to accept credit they didn't earn or turns down an honorary award they don't deserve. When a person focuses on doing real work instead of trying to look good or impress others with their image.

m: To remain calm and composed without showing any emotional reaction or disturbance on one's face.
s: When someone receives bad news but doesn't show any emotion on their face. When a poker player hides their feelings during a game so opponents can't tell if they have a good hand. When a student gets criticized but stays completely unfazed without any visible reaction.

m: To obtain benefits or rewards without putting in any effort or work.
s: When someone expects to get paid for a job they didn't do. When a student wants a good grade without studying or attending class. When a person hopes to become wealthy without working or building a business.

m: maintaining a relationship that is neither intimate nor distant, keeping an ambiguous or reserved middle distance with someone.
s: When two people interact politely but without warmth, like coworkers who are friendly but never truly close. When someone maintains a deliberately non-committal attitude in a relationship, neither fully engaged nor completely withdrawn.

m: willing to do something repeatedly without getting impatient or annoyed, showing genuine care and dedication.
s: When a teacher explains the same concept multiple times to a struggling student without showing frustration. When a parent answers their child's endless questions about how things work with genuine enthusiasm rather than irritation.

m: To explain or describe something with thorough detail and patient effort without becoming weary or bored.
s: When a teacher goes over a difficult concept multiple times, breaking it down into every small step so students fully understand. When someone writes a very detailed instruction manual, carefully explaining each part rather than glossing over anything.

l: cannot be equaled in this world
m: Someone is so arrogant and full of pride that they believe no one else can compare to them or challenge their superiority.
s: When a talented athlete becomes so cocky after winning a few games that they refuse to acknowledge any competitors. When a wealthy person acts like they're better than everyone else and won't listen to anyone's opinions.

m: Something is so far beyond one's ability or circumstances that it is impossible to achieve or obtain.
s: When a young student from a poor family dreams of attending an elite university but feels it's completely out of reach. When you admire a celebrity's wealth and success so much that you believe you could never achieve anything similar in your lifetime.

m: Both things are equally important and neither should be neglected or given less attention than the other.
s: When a student needs to balance both studying and exercise, neglecting neither one. When managing work and family life, you can't prioritize one completely over the other. When learning both theory and practical skills in a subject.

p: bù kě tóng rì ér yǔ
l: cannot be spoken of on the same day
m: Two things are so different in quality or significance that they cannot be compared or mentioned in the same breath.
s: When comparing a professional athlete's performance now versus when they were injured and recovering. When discussing how a company's products have dramatically improved compared to their early inferior versions. When someone's current success is so much greater than their past attempts that they're incomparable.

m: Something that is extremely rare and valuable, making it difficult to find or acquire.
s: When describing a talented person who is hard to find. When talking about a rare opportunity that doesn't come around often. When appreciating something special that you're lucky to have encountered.

m: A situation is so chaotic, busy, or intense that it becomes difficult to manage or resolve.
s: When a company is in the middle of a major crisis and everything is falling apart at once. When a family is preparing for a big wedding and there are so many tasks that nobody can keep up with the workload.

l: cannot be thought and cannot be discussed
m: Something is so extraordinary or beyond comprehension that it defies normal understanding or explanation.
s: When you witness something that seems physically impossible or completely defies logic. When someone accomplishes a feat that nobody thought was achievable. When an event turns out so unexpectedly that it shocks everyone involved.

l: cannot be collected and put in order
m: A situation has become so chaotic, damaged, or out of control that it is impossible to fix or restore to a normal state.
s: When a company's finances have deteriorated so badly that bankruptcy seems inevitable. When a relationship has fallen apart so completely that reconciliation is no longer possible. When a student has missed so many classes and fallen so far behind that they cannot catch up.

m: Someone or something is so bad or damaged that it is beyond repair or help.
s: When a student has failed every class and shows no interest in learning. When a company's business practices are so unethical that no reforms can fix its reputation.

m: Utterly unreasonable and impossible to communicate with or convince through rational discussion.
s: When someone refuses to listen to any logical argument and won't accept facts no matter how you explain them. When dealing with a person who is so stubborn and irrational that no amount of reasoning can change their mind.

l: cannot be worn away or erased
m: Something that is permanent, enduring, and impossible to remove or forget.
s: When someone makes a lasting impression on you that you'll never forget. When an event leaves a permanent mark on history or someone's memory. When you want to describe something that will always remain significant despite the passage of time.

m: Unable to continue or endure; so troubled or anxious that one cannot even get through a single day peacefully.
s: When someone is in such deep distress or fear that they cannot find peace for even a day. When a person is so overwhelmed by worry or guilt that they cannot function normally in their daily life.

l: unable to be counted to completion
m: There are so many of something that it is impossible to count or enumerate them all.
s: When describing a huge crowd at a concert or festival where you can't possibly count everyone. When talking about the countless stars in the sky or the immense number of grains of sand on a beach. When someone has collected so many items over the years that they've lost track of the exact quantity.

l: cannot be spoken of in words
m: Something is so extreme, profound, or overwhelming that it defies description or expression in language.
s: When you experience something so beautiful or terrible that you struggle to find the right words to describe it. When a feeling or situation is so intense that normal language seems inadequate to capture it.

m: A boundary or limit that cannot be surpassed or violated under any circumstances.
s: When there are certain rules or principles that absolutely cannot be broken. When describing a line that should never be crossed in a relationship or professional setting.

m: Something that is inappropriate, outdated, or unsuitable for the current circumstances or era.
s: When someone insists on using old-fashioned methods that nobody does anymore. When a joke or comment offends people because it reflects outdated attitudes that society has moved past.

m: Something is extraordinarily exceptional and stands out far above what is ordinary or typical.
s: When a student produces work that is far superior to what their peers can do. When a new product or innovation is so much better than anything else on the market that it becomes an instant hit.

m: Extremely poor or destitute, having virtually no money or possessions at all.
s: When someone loses their job and all their savings and ends up with almost nothing. When a family falls into extreme poverty and can barely afford food or shelter.

m: To willingly offer advice, instruction, or guidance without hesitation or reluctance.
s: When you ask an experienced coworker for help and they generously share their knowledge. When someone asks an expert for tips and the expert is happy to teach them without making a big deal about it.

m: Something is so easy or insignificant that it is not worth mentioning or discussing.
s: When someone asks if you can handle a task and you confidently say it's no problem at all. When a skilled musician is asked to play a simple piece of music that requires almost no effort.

m: Something is so weak or fragile that it will collapse or fail at the slightest attack or pressure.
s: When a company's business model is so poorly designed that it fails as soon as it faces any real competition. When someone's argument is so weak that one simple counter-point completely destroys it. When a person's confidence is so fragile that one piece of criticism makes them give up entirely.

m: A past experience is so painful or shameful that one cannot bear to recall or remember it.
s: When someone has gone through a traumatic breakup and doesn't want to talk about it. When a person feels deep regret about their behavior in a previous job and finds it painful to think back on that time.

m: The consequences would be so disastrous that it is difficult or impossible to imagine how bad they could be.
s: When discussing what might happen if a critical system fails without backup plans. When warning someone about the terrible outcome if they continue down a dangerous path.

l: unable to be made or fashioned
m: Someone is so fundamentally flawed or obstinate that they cannot be improved or educated no matter what effort is made.
s: When a student refuses to study and shows no willingness to learn despite all your attempts to help them. When someone is so set in their bad habits that coaching or mentoring seems completely useless.

p: bù sāi bù liú ， bù zhǐ bù xíng
l: Without blocking there is no flow, without stopping there is no progress.
m: Sometimes you must remove obstacles or make sacrifices in order to achieve progress and success.
s: When a company needs to cut unprofitable departments to become more efficient and grow. When a student has to give up leisure time and stop procrastinating in order to make academic progress. When a person needs to break old habits and eliminate bad influences from their life to move forward.

m: To do something quietly and without drawing attention or making any fuss.
s: When someone sneaks into a room without anyone noticing. When a coworker completes their work without asking for help or making complaints. When a child quietly cleans their room without being asked or told.

m: A person who lacks education and possesses no useful knowledge or abilities.
s: When someone has never bothered to study or learn anything useful and therefore cannot do anything well. When a person who is ignorant and incompetent tries to accomplish something important but fails because they have no real knowledge or training.

m: This is not the only problem; matters are even worse than that, with additional troubles compounding the situation.
s: When someone is dealing with one crisis and then discovers there are more serious issues underneath. When a person is already stressed about a situation and then realizes the actual problems are far greater than they initially thought.

m: A situation or decision that does not allow for any objection, interference, or further discussion from others.
s: When a boss makes a final decision and doesn't want to hear any opposing opinions from employees. When a parent tells their child to do something and makes it clear there's no room for debate or negotiation.

m: Something is so certain and clear that there is no room for any doubt or questioning.
s: When scientific evidence proves something conclusively and there's no point arguing about it anymore. When your boss makes a final decision and won't accept any further discussion or objections.

m: To feel a chill of fear or dread that makes you shiver, even though it is not due to physical cold.
s: When you hear a scary ghost story and get goosebumps even though the room is warm. When you read about a terrible crime and feel an involuntary shudder run down your spine.

m: To remain steadfast and determined in the face of difficulties, refusing to give up or surrender despite obstacles.
s: When someone persists with their goals despite repeated failures or setbacks. When a person continues fighting for what they believe in even when others doubt them or circumstances are against them.

m: To regard something or someone with such contempt that it is not even worth looking at or considering.
s: When a successful person dismisses criticism from someone they view as inferior. When you're so confident in your decision that you completely ignore what others think about it.

l: If not balanced, then it sounds
m: When people are treated unjustly or wronged, they naturally feel compelled to speak up and protest against it.
s: When an employee has been unfairly passed over for a promotion and finally decides to complain to their manager. When a person witnesses corruption and feels they must report it to authorities rather than staying silent. When someone has endured mistreatment for too long and can no longer hold back their grievances.

m: to be unpopular or fail to win the approval and support of the people.
s: When a new manager implements unpopular policies that nobody agrees with. When a politician makes decisions that anger the public and lose voter support. When a coworker is disliked by everyone because they're rude and unhelpful.

l: unable to obtain the essential point
m: To fail to grasp the main point or essence of something despite effort or explanation.
s: When you read a long article but don't understand what the author is trying to say. When someone explains a concept to you multiple times but you still can't get what they mean.

m: To forgive past offenses and hold no grudge against someone for what they have done before.
s: When someone apologizes sincerely for hurting you in the past and you decide to let it go and move forward. When friends have had conflicts but choose to reconcile by forgiving each other's previous mistakes.

m: A task or matter that is not pressing and can be postponed or handled later without immediate consequences.
s: When you have many things to do but some tasks don't have deadlines, those are matters of no urgency. A company might decide to delay redecorating the office because it's a matter of no urgency compared to meeting their sales targets.

m: A polite way to ask for something while acknowledging that the request is unreasonable or an imposition on the other person.
s: When you need to ask someone for a big favor but you know it's inconvenient for them. When you want to request something from someone but you're embarrassed because it's a lot to ask.

m: Behavior or conduct that is improper, undignified, or fails to meet acceptable social standards.
s: When someone acts in a way that embarrasses themselves or reflects badly on their family or organization. When a professional behaves unprofessionally in public and people criticize them for it. When someone's actions are so inappropriate that they damage their reputation.

p: bù dǎ bù chéng xiāng shí
l: without fighting there is no acquaintance
m: People can become close friends through conflict or disagreement, as shared struggle or competition can create a strong bond.
s: When two rivals who initially clashed end up becoming best friends. When coworkers who had a heated argument later realize they respect each other and develop a genuine friendship. When two athletes who competed fiercely against each other become teammates and close friends.

m: To confess or reveal one's guilt or secrets without being forced or asked to do so.
s: When someone nervously blurts out what they did wrong before anyone even accuses them. When a guilty person starts explaining themselves and gives away evidence they were trying to hide.

m: Something that is genuine, complete, and without any reduction or compromise in quality or authenticity.
s: When describing a product that is exactly what was promised with no corners cut. When someone delivers on their commitments in full without making excuses or partial efforts.

l: not constrained by a single form
m: To be flexible and not rigidly bound by conventional rules or established patterns.
s: When a company hires talented people from unconventional backgrounds instead of only seeking those with traditional credentials. When a teacher encourages students to solve problems in creative ways rather than forcing them to follow one prescribed method.

m: To not be concerned with minor details or trivial etiquette; to focus on what is important rather than getting caught up in small things.
s: When someone doesn't worry about being perfectly dressed or having perfect manners because they care more about getting things done. When a person is easygoing and doesn't get upset over minor mistakes or small inconveniences.

m: To achieve one's goals by any means necessary, without regard for morality or ethics.
s: When someone will lie, cheat, or hurt others to get what they want. When a competitor uses unfair or illegal tactics to win. When a person abandons all principles to achieve success.

m: A false or weak argument or plan collapses on its own without needing to be actively opposed or refuted.
s: When a lie is so obviously false that people see through it without you having to point out the problems. When a poorly thought-out plan fails because of its own internal contradictions, without anyone having to sabotage it.

p: bù gǎn yuè léi chí yī bù
l: dare not overstep the thunder pool by a single step
m: To strictly adhere to rules and boundaries without daring to deviate or break them in any way.
s: When an employee carefully follows company policies and never tries to bend the rules. When someone respects established limits and refuses to push boundaries even slightly, staying well within what is permitted.

m: Something that provides a modest but meaningful contribution or help, even if it's not a major solution.
s: When a small amount of money helps someone get through a difficult week. When a friend gives you a useful tip that saves you time on a project, even though it doesn't solve everything. When you find a discount that doesn't change your life but definitely helps your budget.

m: An unforeseen circumstance or emergency that requires preparation or resources to handle.
s: When someone saves money for emergencies they can't predict. When a company keeps backup supplies in case something goes wrong unexpectedly. When you maintain an emergency fund for sudden medical expenses or job loss.

m: Something is unclear, ambiguous, or mysterious with no clear explanation or understanding.
s: When someone gives you a vague explanation and you still don't understand what actually happened. When a situation is suspicious or confusing because important details are missing or hidden.

m: A statement or argument that is so obviously true and well-founded that it cannot be disputed or refuted.
s: When someone makes a point that is logically sound and impossible to argue against. When a friend states a fact so clearly correct that there's no room for debate.

l: not expected yet it happens anyway
m: Something occurs naturally and inevitably without being planned or anticipated beforehand.
s: When you run into an old friend by complete chance after many years and start talking like no time has passed. When you gradually develop feelings for someone without initially intending to. When a project starts succeeding in ways you never predicted or designed for.

m: To meet or encounter someone or something unexpectedly by chance without any prior arrangement or planning.
s: When you run into an old friend on the street that you haven't seen in years and neither of you planned to be there. When you discover a useful tool or website by accident while browsing online.

m: A gathering or meeting ends unhappily with participants departing in discontent or disappointment.
s: When a family dinner turns into an argument and everyone leaves upset. When a business negotiation fails and both parties walk away angry and frustrated. When friends have a disagreement at a party and decide to leave early without resolving things.

m: A barren, desolate place with no vegetation where nothing can grow or thrive.
s: When describing a desert or wasteland that is completely uninhabitable. When someone moves to a remote, undeveloped area with no resources or infrastructure.

m: To be content with a superficial understanding of something without making effort to grasp it deeply or comprehensively.
s: When someone skims through a textbook without really studying the concepts. When a person watches a tutorial but doesn't practice to truly master the skill. When someone reads only headlines instead of full articles to understand complex issues.

m: A problem or situation that is so severe or deeply rooted that it cannot be fixed or remedied.
s: When a company has such fundamental structural problems that no amount of reorganization will help. When someone has ingrained bad habits or character flaws that seem impossible to change despite many attempts at intervention.

l: not willing to lag behind others
m: Unwilling to fall behind or be inferior to others; determined to keep up or surpass one's peers.
s: When someone is highly competitive and always wants to be at the top of their class or field. When a person refuses to accept being second-best and constantly pushes themselves to match or exceed others' achievements.

m: Refusing to admit defeat or appear inferior; determined to compete equally or prove one's capability.
s: When two colleagues are competing for the same promotion and neither wants to back down. When a student sees their friend get a better grade and immediately works harder to match or exceed that performance. When a team is losing a game but refuses to give up and fights back with full effort.

m: To act without allowing others to speak or explain; to proceed forcefully without listening to objections or explanations.
s: When your boss makes a decision and won't hear any of your reasons or arguments. When someone grabs your arm and drags you somewhere without letting you say anything first. When a parent punishes their child immediately without listening to what actually happened.

l: unable to act of one's own accord
m: To do something involuntarily or without conscious control, as if compelled by an external force or one's own impulses.
s: When you laugh at a joke even though you were trying to stay serious. When your eyes well up with tears during an emotional movie and you can't help it. When you find yourself humming a song that's been stuck in your head all day without meaning to.

m: Something that is superficial, ineffective, or fails to address the real issue or make a meaningful impact.
s: When someone gives you feedback that is so vague it doesn't actually help you improve. When a company makes minor changes to their product but doesn't fix the main problems customers complain about.

p: bù dēng dà yǎ zhī táng
l: unable to enter the halls of great elegance
m: Something is too crude, vulgar, or lowbrow to be considered refined or acceptable in polite society.
s: When someone tells an off-color joke at a formal dinner and it's considered inappropriate. When a trashy reality TV show is dismissed by critics as having no artistic merit. When someone's crude table manners are not acceptable at an upscale restaurant.

l: unjust wrong that cannot be cleared
m: A serious injustice or false accusation that is difficult or impossible to prove innocent of and clear one's name from.
s: When someone is blamed for something they didn't do and no one believes their denial. When a person is falsely convicted of a crime and struggles to prove their innocence despite evidence.

l: not distinguishable as higher or lower
m: Two things are so similar in quality or ability that neither is clearly better than the other.
s: When two students get nearly identical test scores and you can't say one is smarter than the other. When comparing two job candidates who both have equally impressive qualifications and experience. When two athletes compete at such a similar level that it's impossible to declare one definitively superior.

m: To be unconscious or in a state where one is completely unaware of what is happening around them.
s: When someone is knocked out cold and doesn't remember anything that happened. When a person is so deeply asleep or sedated that they cannot be roused or respond to anything around them.

l: not touching the edge or limit
m: To speak or act in a way that is irrelevant, unrealistic, or completely misses the point.
s: When someone gives you advice that has nothing to do with your actual problem. When a person tells wild, exaggerated stories that are completely disconnected from reality. When a coworker suggests a solution that is totally impractical and off-topic during a meeting.

p: bù zhī rén jiān yǒu xiū chǐ shì
l: does not know that shame exists in the human world
m: To be completely shameless and utterly indifferent to social disgrace or moral standards.
s: When someone commits a deeply embarrassing act in public and shows absolutely no regret or embarrassment about it. When a person repeatedly behaves immorally or unethically without any sense of conscience or concern for how others judge them.

m: Something has happened so many times that it is impossible to count or estimate.
s: When someone has made the same excuse countless times and you've lost track of how many times it's happened. When a website has crashed so many times that nobody bothers counting anymore. When your coworker has been late to meetings an uncountable number of times.

p: bù zhī tiān gāo dì hòu
l: not knowing the height of heaven or the thickness of earth
m: To be arrogant and ignorant, lacking awareness of one's own limitations or the vastness of the world around you.
s: When a young person acts overconfident and disrespectful toward their elders, thinking they know everything. When someone takes on a task that is far beyond their ability because they don't realize how difficult it is.

l: does not know good from bad
m: Someone fails to recognize or appreciate kindness, help, or good intentions shown to them, often responding with ingratitude or hostility.
s: When someone does you a favor and they respond with anger or rudeness instead of gratitude. When a person refuses help that could clearly benefit them and acts like you're trying to harm them instead.

l: not knowing what is being said
m: Unable to understand what someone is trying to communicate because their words are unclear, confusing, or meaningless.
s: When someone gives a rambling explanation that goes nowhere and you can't figure out what point they're trying to make. When you read a poorly written document or listen to a confusing speech and have no idea what the main message is supposed to be.

m: to be confused and unable to understand the cause or reason for something that has happened.
s: When someone receives criticism but has no idea what they did wrong. When a person is suddenly fired from their job without explanation and can't figure out why.

m: To be so confused or overwhelmed that you don't know how to respond or what action to take.
s: When you receive unexpected bad news and freeze up, unable to think clearly about what to do next. When someone asks you a question you're completely unprepared for and you just stand there blankly. When you arrive at a place you've never been and don't know which way to go or who to ask for help.

l: does not know how to advance or retreat
m: Unable to recognize when to act and when to stop, lacking the judgment to know the right timing for action or restraint.
s: When someone keeps pushing an argument even though they're clearly losing and should back down. When a business keeps expanding aggressively without knowing when to consolidate or slow down.

l: Without destruction there is no establishment
m: Progress and innovation require dismantling old systems or ideas before new ones can be built in their place.
s: When a company needs to completely overhaul its outdated processes before implementing new technology. When someone must break free from old habits or beliefs before they can adopt better ones.

p: bù guǎn sān qī èr shí yī
l: Not caring about thirty-seven or twenty-one
m: To act recklessly without considering the consequences or following any logic or rules.
s: When someone acts impulsively without thinking things through, like jumping into a decision without gathering all the facts. When a person ignores warnings and does whatever they want regardless of potential problems or the proper way to handle something.

m: People arrive at the same idea, decision, or action without having discussed or agreed with each other beforehand.
s: When multiple friends independently decide to wear the same color to a party without coordinating. When several colleagues all suggest the same solution to a problem without knowing what others were thinking.

p: bù jīng yī shì ， bù zhǎng yī zhì
l: Without experiencing one matter, one does not gain one piece of wisdom
m: You can only gain wisdom and understanding through actual experience and the lessons learned from facing difficulties or mistakes.
s: When someone finally understands why their parents gave them certain advice after going through a similar situation themselves. When a young person makes a mistake, learns from it, and becomes wiser because of that experience. When someone says they now understand a lesson only after living through the hardship themselves.

m: Speech or ideas that are baseless, unreasonable, or lack any factual foundation or serious consideration.
s: When someone makes wild claims without any evidence or experience to back them up. When your friend suggests an absurd plan that has no practical basis whatsoever. When you hear gossip or rumors that are clearly made up and have no truth to them.

m: Something continues to exist but is extremely tenuous, fragile, or barely maintained, as if hanging by the thinnest of threads.

m: To refuse to express a clear opinion or judgment, remaining noncommittal and ambiguous about something.

m: Something disappears mysteriously or suddenly without explanation or trace.

l: not ashamed to ask those below

m: Descendants who bring shame to their family by failing to live up to their ancestors' reputation or moral standards.

m: to be extremely annoyed or impatient because something tedious or bothersome keeps happening repeatedly.

m: There are so many examples or instances that it is impossible to count or list them all.

m: news or information spreads rapidly on its own without anyone deliberately promoting it
s: When a juicy piece of gossip spreads through the office in just a few hours without anyone officially announcing it. When a funny meme suddenly goes viral across social media with no organized promotion.

m: So deeply trapped or absorbed in something that one cannot free oneself from it, no matter how hard one tries.
s: When someone is addicted to gambling and keeps losing money despite promising to quit. When a person is so infatuated with another that they ignore all warnings and can't break free from the relationship.

l: does not make careless remarks or smile

l: not falling into the old nest

m: To be dressed in rags or extremely poor clothing, indicating a state of poverty or destitution.
s: When someone is so poor they can barely afford decent clothes and shoes. When describing a homeless person or someone living in extreme poverty who lacks basic clothing.

p: bù jiàn guān cái bù luò lèi
l: Will not shed tears until seeing the coffin
m: Someone refuses to accept reality or change their ways until they face dire consequences or irreversible loss.

m: Someone or something is obscure, unknown, or has no historical record or reputation.
s: When a small local business suddenly becomes successful despite never being heard of before. When someone accomplishes great things but remains largely unknown to the public.

m: Something is so obvious or clear that it does not need to be explained or stated explicitly.
s: When a situation is so evident that you don't need to point it out to others. When the results of someone's hard work are plain to see without them having to brag about it.

m: There are so many of something that it is impossible to count or enumerate them.
s: When describing a massive crowd at a concert or festival. When talking about how many stars are visible in the night sky. When someone has collected so many items over the years that they've lost track of the total number.

m: To lack awareness of or fail to consider the broader context and the greater good in one's actions or words.
s: When someone makes a decision that benefits themselves but harms the group or organization. When a person speaks carelessly about sensitive matters without thinking about how it affects everyone involved. When an employee prioritizes their own interests over what's best for the company or team.

l: does not recognize the raising up
m: to be ungrateful for someone's kindness, favor, or help, and fail to appreciate their efforts to assist or promote you.

l: not recognizing the times and circumstances

m: Two or more people independently arrive at the same idea, decision, or action without having discussed it beforehand.

m: A position of strength or advantage where one cannot be defeated or is assured of victory.

p: bù fèi chuī huī zhī lì
l: not worth the effort of blowing away dust

s: When a talented musician plays a difficult piece perfectly on their first try without practicing. When someone solves a math problem in seconds that most people would struggle with for minutes.

l: not sufficient to serve as evidence
m: Something is too insubstantial, unreliable, or insufficient to be used as proof or basis for judgment.

l: not sufficient to be considered strange

l: not sufficient to be a lesson

s: When someone's behavior is so flawed that you wouldn't want anyone to imitate it. When a failed approach shouldn't be considered as guidance for how to do something in the future.

l: not worthy of hanging between the teeth

m: Unable to distinguish between different things; lacking basic knowledge or discernment about fundamental matters.

m: Something is merely ordinary or mediocre, not as impressive or important as it might seem.

m: Lacking sympathy, empathy, or understanding of others' feelings; being cold, harsh, or inhumane in one's treatment of people.

l: If you do not advance, you retreat

s: When someone stops studying and their grades drop. When a business stops innovating and loses market share to competitors. When an athlete takes time off training and loses their competitive edge.

m: It is essential to follow the proper seasons for farming activities to ensure a successful harvest and agricultural prosperity.

m: An unexpected visitor who arrives without being invited or announced.

m: To make every possible effort without holding back or leaving anything undone in pursuit of a goal.

m: Something that is neither one thing nor another; failing to fit into any clear category or standard.

m: To completely ignore something or someone and show no interest or concern whatsoever.

m: To conceal one's emotions or thoughts and maintain a calm, expressionless appearance without showing any outward signs of what one is feeling.

When a person is excited about a surprise but acts completely normal around the guest of honor to keep it secret.

m: To maintain a calm, humble, and steady demeanor without being swayed by pride or becoming hasty in one's actions.
s: When someone achieves success but remains grounded and humble about their accomplishments. When a student studies consistently without getting overconfident or rushing through their work. When a person faces criticism gracefully without becoming defensive or frustrated.

l: having no contention with the world

l: bid a long farewell to the world
m: To die or pass away from this world.
s: When someone dies after a long illness and finally passes away. When an elderly person who has lived a full life dies peacefully. When referring respectfully to someone's death in formal or literary contexts.

m: To treat others with kindness, goodwill, and a benevolent attitude in all interactions.
s: When someone chooses to help a neighbor without expecting anything in return. When a person gives someone the benefit of the doubt instead of being judgmental or harsh. When coworkers support each other and maintain a positive, helpful attitude in the workplace.

m: to be noticeably distinct or unique compared to what is ordinary or common.
s: When someone has a completely different style or approach than everyone else around them. When a student comes up with a creative solution that nobody else thought of. When a person refuses to follow trends and does their own thing instead.

m: Something grows or accumulates steadily with the passage of time.
s: When a student's knowledge expands day by day through consistent studying. When a company's profits grow steadily month after month. When someone's anxiety or worries intensify as time goes on.

m: to attempt something that is futile because it goes against the interests of a powerful party who would never agree to it.

l: ugly behavior displayed a hundred times
m: Someone displays shameful, embarrassing, or ridiculous behavior repeatedly and openly.
s: When a drunk person acts foolishly in public and won't stop no matter what. When someone keeps doing embarrassing things at a party despite being told to stop. When a politician keeps making foolish mistakes that damage their reputation.

l: concentrate the mind and direct the will
m: To focus completely and wholeheartedly on a single task or goal without distraction.
s: When a student studies for an exam with complete focus, ignoring their phone and all other distractions. When someone is so absorbed in their work that they don't notice anything happening around them.

m: To abuse authority and act in an arrogant, domineering manner without regard for others.

m: Continuing through many successive generations across a long period of time.

l: Peach blossom source outside the world

l: worldly conditions are warm and cold

m: Excellence and skill are achieved through hard work and persistent effort rather than talent alone.

m: to rush about busily in many directions; to be constantly on the move dealing with multiple urgent matters.

l: rise again from the eastern mountain
m: To make a successful comeback after a period of decline, failure, or retirement.
s: When a former athlete returns to competition after years away and performs well. When a company that went bankrupt manages to restart and becomes profitable again. When someone loses their job but eventually finds success in a new career.

m: to look around in all directions; to gaze about restlessly or with curiosity.
s: When you enter an unfamiliar place and your eyes dart around trying to take everything in. When someone is distracted and keeps looking around instead of paying attention to what's in front of them.

m: To talk in a disorganized, rambling way that jumps from one unrelated topic to another without focus or purpose.
s: When someone tells a story but keeps going off on tangents and bringing up unrelated details. When a person talks for a long time but never actually gets to the main point they were trying to make.

l: piece together from east and west

When a student puts together a project using random materials that don't really fit together well. When someone throws together a meal using whatever leftover ingredients they can find in the kitchen.

m: Attempting to imitate someone admirable but doing so clumsily and unsuccessfully, resulting in something ridiculous or contemptible.

When a student copies their friend's way of speaking or dressing but just ends up looking awkward and out of place.

m: Fragmentary, disconnected pieces of information or understanding that fail to form a complete or coherent whole.
s: When you've only heard bits and pieces of a story and don't understand the full picture. When someone tries to explain a complex topic but only shares random details without connecting them together. When you're reading an old book with missing pages and can only grasp scattered parts of the plot.

l: thread by thread enters the clasp
m: Something is crafted with such meticulous attention to detail and precision that every element fits perfectly together.
s: When a writer constructs a mystery novel where every clue connects perfectly and the plot comes together flawlessly. When a director carefully plans every scene of a film so that the cinematography, dialogue, and music all harmonize beautifully.

l: sacrifice the pawn to save the rook
m: Abandon something of lesser importance to protect something of greater value.
s: When a company closes a small branch to keep the main business afloat. When a student gives up a hobby to focus on their major studies and career prospects.

m: To abandon one's position in a chaotic or humiliating retreat, often used to describe a complete defeat or loss of composure.
s: When a team gets utterly defeated and players walk off the field in disarray. When someone gives up completely during an argument and leaves in a panic rather than standing their ground. When a company collapses so quickly that employees are abandoning their posts without any organization.

m: To achieve a satisfactory outcome that benefits or pleases both parties or sides equally without compromise.
s: When you find a job that pays well and allows you to spend time with family. When a solution makes both your boss and your team happy at the same time.

m: When two parties are equally happy and willing to do something together, based on mutual agreement and genuine desire from both sides.

m: A pure and innocent relationship between two people who have known each other since childhood, untainted by romantic or ulterior motives.

When recalling a time in your youth when friendships were simple and free from romantic complications.

When a parent grounds their child for breaking an important rule with no exceptions or negotiations.

l: a dog that has lost its home

When someone has dealt with a particular software bug repeatedly and can now fix it faster than the technical support team.

m: When you repeatedly do something over a long period of time, it eventually becomes an automatic, natural part of who you are.

When visiting a famous tourist attraction on a busy day and you're surrounded by visitors everywhere you look.

m: To gain advantage by picking up or utilizing things that others have rejected or abandoned.
s: When someone finds value in used items that others no longer want. When a business finds a niche market segment that larger competitors have ignored. When you benefit from opportunities that others have passed up.

m: When someone lacks status or importance, their opinions and suggestions are not taken seriously by others.
s: When a junior employee makes a good suggestion in a meeting but nobody listens because they're new and low-ranking. When a shy person offers advice to their friend group but everyone ignores them because they don't speak up often.

l: people's hearts turn toward and away
m: The rise and fall of a leader's or group's support depends on whether the people's hearts are with them or against them.
s: When a political leader loses popularity because people no longer trust them. When a company faces boycotts because customers feel betrayed by their actions. When a sports team struggles because fans have lost faith in the coach's leadership.

m: The people's hearts and minds are unified in support for or agreement with something, representing universal acclaim or collective will.
s: When a charismatic leader inspires widespread support among the population. When a new policy is so popular that nearly everyone enthusiastically backs it. When a sports team becomes the nation's favorite and receives overwhelming fan support.

p: rén pà chū míng zhū pà féi
l: people fear becoming famous as pigs fear becoming fat
m: Just as a pig fears being fattened up because it leads to slaughter, a person should fear becoming famous because it brings unwanted attention, scrutiny, and trouble.
s: When someone wants to keep a low profile and avoid public attention because fame would complicate their life. When a person prefers to stay anonymous rather than become a public figure who faces constant criticism and pressure.

m: The practical knowledge of how to navigate social relationships, understand human nature, and conduct oneself appropriately in various social situations.
s: When someone new to the workplace doesn't know how to handle office politics or social dynamics with colleagues. When a young person lacks experience in understanding how people actually behave and what motivates them in real-world situations.

m: A place or group where many talented and capable individuals are assembled.
s: When describing a top university with excellent students and professors. When talking about a successful company that has hired many skilled professionals. When praising a team or organization for having many competent members.

m: Outstanding individuals appear one after another in succession, showing a constant supply of capable and gifted people.
s: When a company or organization keeps producing exceptional employees and leaders over time. When a field like sports or academia consistently develops new champions and experts who follow great predecessors.

p: rén wú lián chǐ ， bǎi shì kě wèi
l: A person without integrity and shame can do anything
m: When someone has no sense of shame or moral principles, they will stop at nothing and are capable of committing any wrongdoing.
s: When a politician is caught in a scandal but continues making false excuses without any embarrassment. When a coworker steals credit for your work repeatedly and shows no remorse when confronted.

p: rén wú yuǎn lǜ ， bì yǒu jìn yōu
l: A person without distant foresight must have immediate worries
m: Failing to plan ahead and think about the future will inevitably lead to problems and hardships in the present.
s: When someone doesn't save money for emergencies and then faces financial crisis when unexpected expenses arise. When a student refuses to study throughout the semester and then panics right before the final exam. When a company ignores long-term planning and suddenly discovers they cannot compete in the market.

l: outstanding people and spiritually blessed land
m: A place with exceptional geographical advantages naturally produces talented and exceptional people.
s: When describing why certain regions throughout history have produced many great leaders, artists, or scholars. When explaining how a particular city or region seems to have a special quality that attracts and nurtures brilliant individuals.

m: A scene of great excitement and jubilation with people cheering loudly and horses neighing, representing a lively and celebratory atmosphere.
s: When a festival or celebration is in full swing with crowds of excited people and the energy is infectious. When describing a bustling marketplace or fair where there's lots of noise and commotion from both people and animals.

m: There are too many people relative to the amount of work that needs to be done, resulting in overstaffing and inefficiency.
s: When a company has hired too many employees and there isn't enough work to keep them all busy. When a project team is oversized and people are standing around with nothing productive to do.

l: both the person and the lute have perished
m: When someone of great talent dies, their exceptional gifts and contributions are lost forever, leaving behind only memories and irreplaceable absence.
s: When a brilliant artist passes away and their unique creative voice can never be replicated. When a master craftsman or musician dies and their special skills and artistry are gone forever.

p: rén ér wú xìn ， bù zhī qí kě
l: A person without credibility, I do not know what they can accomplish
m: Without trustworthiness and integrity, a person cannot succeed or be useful to society.
s: When someone constantly breaks their promises and lies, making it impossible to rely on them for anything important. When evaluating whether to do business with someone who has a reputation for dishonesty and cannot be trusted to keep their word.

l: no one dares to poison me
m: No one dares to harm or betray me because of the respect, fear, or loyalty I command.
s: When someone has built such a strong reputation or position that nobody would risk crossing them. When a leader is so respected and powerful that their subordinates would never think of betraying them.

m: Public opinion and gossip can be so damaging and influential that they are something to be genuinely afraid of.
s: When someone's reputation is ruined by rumors spread by others, even if the rumors aren't true. When a person avoids doing something they want to do because they're worried about what people will say about them. When a scandal or negative comments from the public can seriously harm someone's career or relationships.

m: A place or situation of extreme suffering and misery that feels as bad as hell itself.
s: When someone describes their workplace as unbearable due to a terrible boss and impossible conditions. When a person experiences extreme hardship or oppressive living conditions that make life feel unbearable.

m: Someone who appears civilized and kind on the surface but is actually cruel, vicious, or morally corrupt at their core.
s: When someone treats you kindly in public but behaves viciously behind closed doors. When a charismatic leader is revealed to have committed terrible crimes despite their friendly public image.

p: rén zhě jiàn rén ， zhì zhě jiàn zhì
l: The benevolent see benevolence, the wise see wisdom
m: Different people interpret the same thing differently based on their own values, perspectives, and knowledge.
s: When a movie or book is discussed and everyone has a completely different interpretation of what it means. When colleagues look at the same business problem but each person sees a different solution based on their expertise and background. When a piece of art resonates differently with each viewer depending on their personal experiences.

l: benevolence reaches its utmost and righteousness is exhausted
m: One has done everything possible out of kindness and duty, leaving nothing more that could be expected or done.
s: When you've helped a friend repeatedly despite their poor choices, and finally you have to stop because you've given all you can. When a company goes above and beyond for a customer with complaints, offering refunds, replacements, and compensation until there's nothing more reasonable left to offer.

l: today is right, yesterday is wrong
m: The present situation is correct or improved, while the past was mistaken or inferior; things have changed for the better.
s: When someone who used to hold bad opinions finally admits they were wrong and have changed their views. When a company that had poor practices in the past has now reformed and operates ethically. When a person acknowledges that their earlier mistakes were wrong but they are better now.

l: today is not the same as yesterday
m: The present situation is completely different from the past, often implying significant change, progress, or decline.
s: When someone achieves great success after previously struggling, you might say their life is 今非昔比 now. When a once-thriving business has fallen into decline, people might comment that it is 今非昔比 compared to its glory days.

l: Follow goodness like a flowing stream
m: Be quick and willing to adopt good advice and turn toward virtue without hesitation or resistance.
s: When someone immediately accepts constructive criticism and changes their behavior for the better. When a person eagerly listens to wise counsel from others and implements it without delay or argument.

l: proceeding with leisure and without urgency
m: To remain calm, unhurried, and composed even in difficult or pressing situations.
s: When someone handles a stressful deadline at work without panicking and completes everything methodically. When a person stays cool and collected during an argument instead of getting angry or defensive. When someone takes their time to think through a problem carefully rather than rushing into a hasty decision.

m: To face death or a difficult fate with composure and dignity, especially in service of a just cause.
s: When a martyr or freedom fighter accepts their execution without fear or complaint. When someone faces an inevitable difficult outcome with calm acceptance and moral conviction.

m: To carefully consider a matter over time rather than making a hasty decision, taking into account all aspects before taking action.
s: When facing an important decision like changing jobs or buying a house, you might want to take time and not rush into it. When friends are arguing about a serious issue, someone might suggest they sit down and think about it carefully over time rather than reacting emotionally in the moment.

l: Another mountain's stone can polish jade
m: You can learn from other people's mistakes and use that knowledge to improve yourself and avoid making similar errors.
s: When you watch a coworker fail at a project and use their experience to do better on your own similar task. When a friend tells you about a bad relationship they had and you learn what warning signs to avoid in your own dating life.

m: To speak up boldly and righteously about what is right, especially when it requires courage to do so.
s: When someone publicly criticizes an unfair decision even though it might get them in trouble. When a colleague speaks up against unethical behavior in a meeting, risking their job to do what's right.

m: To be righteous and generous, willing to spend money freely to help others and support just causes.
s: When someone donates generously to help those in need or supports a worthy cause with their own money. When a wealthy friend uses their resources to help friends in trouble or support social justice initiatives.

l: rely on power to bully others
m: to use one's power, status, or connections to intimidate or oppress those who are weaker or have less influence.
s: When a wealthy person throws their weight around to get special treatment or to intimidate someone less privileged. When someone in a position of authority abuses their power to push around employees or subordinates who cannot fight back.

m: To destroy something completely by burning it, or to abandon something entirely.
s: When a building catches fire and all the documents inside are destroyed. When someone angrily burns letters or photos from an ex-partner. When a valuable collection is lost in a fire and nothing can be salvaged.

l: consign it to a single laugh
m: to dismiss something as unimportant or ridiculous by laughing it off without taking it seriously.
s: When someone makes an insulting remark but you just laugh it off instead of getting angry. When a friend warns you about a risky decision but you dismiss their concern with a smile and do it anyway.

l: entrust it to the eastern flow
m: Something valuable is wasted, lost, or comes to nothing despite effort or hope.
s: When a student works hard on a project but the computer crashes and loses all files. When a business fails and years of investment and planning go down the drain. When someone's dreams and aspirations never materialize due to circumstances beyond their control.

m: Something is so disgusting or offensive that it makes people feel physically sick or deeply repulsed.
s: When you see something extremely gross or violent that makes you feel sick to your stomach. When someone's cruel or immoral behavior is so offensive that it disgusts everyone around them.

l: cause people's hair to stand on end
m: Something is so outrageous, infuriating, or horrifying that it provokes an intense emotional reaction of anger or disgust.
s: When you hear about someone committing a terrible crime or act of cruelty that makes you furious. When a company engages in deeply unethical behavior that shocks and angers the public.

m: To be so beautiful, impressive, or desirable that it deeply captivates and inspires longing in people.
s: When you see a breathtaking landscape that makes you desperately want to visit it. When someone describes their dream vacation so vividly that everyone listening wishes they could go there too.

l: orders are executed and prohibitions are obeyed
m: Commands are followed strictly and prohibitions are observed without question, indicating perfect discipline and absolute obedience.
s: When describing a well-disciplined military unit or organization where every command is immediately and completely followed. When praising a leader whose authority is so strong that their orders are executed instantly without any hesitation or resistance.

m: One person possessing the strength or skill of ten people; exceptional courage or capability in facing overwhelming odds.
s: When a small team accomplishes what would normally require a much larger group. When one employee is so productive and skilled that they do the work of ten people. When a single soldier or warrior displays extraordinary bravery and strength against many opponents.

l: use one to warn a hundred
m: Punish or make an example of one person so that many others will be warned and avoid the same mistake.
s: When a teacher disciplines one student severely so the rest of the class learns to behave. When a company fires an employee publicly for breaking rules to discourage others from doing the same.

l: use to warn and prevent similar faults
m: Punish someone severely as a warning to others so they will not commit the same wrongdoing.
s: When a company fires an employee publicly for misconduct to discourage others from breaking rules. When a teacher gives a student a harsh penalty as a warning to the rest of the class.

m: To use physical power or military strength to control or dominate others rather than through persuasion or moral authority.
s: When a dictator maintains control over a country through violence and intimidation rather than gaining people's voluntary support. When a bully uses aggression to make others obey instead of earning their respect.

l: use an egg to strike a stone
m: to attempt something that is doomed to fail because you are far too weak or ill-equipped to succeed against a much more powerful opponent or obstacle.
s: When someone tries to fight against a huge corporation or government agency with no resources or support. When a small startup attempts to compete directly against a major industry giant without any realistic chance of winning.

m: to use deception and cunning to deceive others for personal gain or profit.
s: When a con artist tricks people out of their money by pretending to sell them fake investment opportunities. When someone uses flattery and lies to manipulate their way into a position of trust so they can exploit it later.

p: yǐ zi zhī máo ， gōng zi zhī dùn
l: Use his spear to attack his shield
m: Defeat someone by using their own arguments, methods, or weapons against them.
s: When someone makes a contradictory statement and you point out how their earlier claim proves them wrong. When a critic who demands perfection in others is caught making the same mistakes they condemn.

l: use the few to oppose the many
m: To fight against a much larger or more powerful opposing force despite being heavily outnumbered.
s: When a small startup competes against giant corporations in the same industry. When an underdog sports team faces a much stronger opponent with superior resources and talent.

c: 以小人之心，度君子之腹
p: yǐ xiǎo rén zhī xīn ， dù jūn zǐ zhī fù
l: measure the belly of a gentleman with the heart of a petty person
m: to judge others' noble intentions by projecting one's own base motives and suspicions onto them.
s: When someone assumes you have ulterior motives even though you're genuinely trying to help them. When a dishonest person suspects everyone around them of being dishonest too, because that's how they themselves behave.

l: measure others by one's own measure
m: to judge or evaluate others based on one's own standards, values, or experiences rather than understanding their individual circumstances.
s: When you assume someone should handle stress the same way you do because that's what works for you. When a parent expects their child to have the same interests and talents they had growing up. When you criticize a friend for not being ambitious enough, without considering their different life goals and situation.

m: To respond to someone's hostility or wrongdoing with kindness and moral integrity instead of seeking revenge.
s: When someone has treated you badly but you choose to help them anyway out of principle. When a person continues to be nice to someone who has been mean to them, refusing to stoop to their level.

m: To respond to someone's kindness or favor with malice, ingratitude, or betrayal instead of appreciation.
s: When someone helps you out and you later harm them or betray their trust in return. When a person receives a generous gift or favor but then speaks badly about the giver or acts against their interests.

m: to express regret, remorse, or sudden realization by striking one's forehead with one's hand.
s: When you suddenly realize you made a stupid mistake and hit your forehead in frustration. When someone finally understands something they should have known all along and reacts with exasperation at themselves.

m: The best way to protect oneself is to take the offensive and attack first rather than passively defending.
s: When a company faces competition, they launch new products aggressively instead of just defending their market share. In a debate, instead of just responding to criticism, someone counters with strong arguments of their own.

m: To respond to violence with more violence, which only perpetuates conflict rather than resolving it.
s: When two people keep escalating their arguments into physical fights instead of talking things out. When a country responds to an attack by attacking back, creating an endless cycle of retaliation.

m: fight fire with fire by using harmful or extreme measures to counteract a similar threat or problem.
s: When a company uses aggressive marketing tactics to compete against a rival using the same tactics. When someone uses a person's own manipulative tricks against them to expose their behavior. When a doctor prescribes a toxic drug to fight a deadly disease.

m: To convince or win someone over through logical argumentation and rational explanation rather than force or coercion.
s: When you're trying to settle a disagreement with a colleague by presenting facts and evidence instead of getting angry. When a parent explains the rules to a child using logic rather than just demanding obedience.

p: yǐ yǎn huán yǎn ， yǐ yá huán yá
l: repay an eye with an eye and a tooth with a tooth
m: to respond to harm or injury with equivalent retaliation rather than forgiveness or mercy.
s: When someone hurts you and you decide to hurt them back in the same way. When countries engage in tit-for-tat sanctions or attacks against each other. When a person seeks revenge that matches the severity of the wrong done to them.

l: use ears to substitute for eyes
m: To rely on hearsay and rumor instead of observing the truth directly for oneself.
s: When someone makes a judgment about a situation based only on what others told them rather than seeing it themselves. When a manager makes decisions about an employee's performance based entirely on gossip instead of direct observation.

l: measure the ocean with a ladle
m: to make judgments about something vast and complex based on extremely limited knowledge or experience.
s: When someone tries to understand a huge company's potential after only visiting one store. When a person judges an entire country's culture after a brief visit to one city.

m: to seek revenge by inflicting the same harm that was done to you, or to respond to violence with violence in kind.
s: When a family member is killed and relatives seek violent revenge against the perpetrator. When two rival gangs keep attacking each other in an endless cycle of retaliation.

m: Wait and see how things develop before making a judgment or taking further action.
s: When a manager implements a new policy and decides to monitor the outcomes before deciding whether to keep it or change it. When you give someone a chance to improve their behavior and wait to see if they actually follow through before deciding on consequences.

m: False information spreads and becomes accepted as truth as it is repeatedly passed from person to person without verification.
s: When a rumor starts online and people keep sharing it without checking if it's true. When a misunderstanding about someone gets repeated so many times that everyone believes the false version instead of what actually happened.

m: To form opinions about someone based solely on their physical appearance or external presentation rather than their true character or abilities.
s: When you assume someone is unintelligent because they dress casually, or when you think someone is trustworthy just because they look professional. When people make snap judgments about others based on how they look rather than getting to know them first.

l: use one's body as a model
m: To set a good example for others through your own behavior and conduct.
s: When a manager works hard and arrives early, showing their team the work ethic they expect. When a parent practices the same healthy habits they want their children to adopt.

l: sacrifice one's body for one's duty
m: To give up one's life in the line of duty or while fulfilling one's responsibilities.
s: When a firefighter dies while saving people from a burning building. When a soldier loses their life protecting their country in combat. When a doctor contracts a fatal disease while treating patients during an epidemic.

m: strategically withdraw or concede temporarily in order to gain a stronger position or achieve greater success later.
s: When a business lowers prices temporarily to drive out competitors, then raises them once the market consolidates. When someone admits they were wrong about something minor to build trust before making a bigger ask. When a negotiator gives ground on small issues early on to create momentum and goodwill for securing major concessions later.

m: Gain advantage over an opponent by remaining fresh and rested while they exhaust themselves through effort.
s: When a sports team wins by conserving energy in the first half and attacking aggressively in the second half when opponents are tired. When someone waits patiently for the right moment to act while others wear themselves out with fruitless effort.

l: treat one's neighbor as a valley to drain into
m: To solve your own problems by shifting the burden or harm onto your neighbors instead of taking responsibility yourself.
s: When a factory dumps its waste into a river that flows through a neighboring town instead of properly disposing of it. When a company lays off workers to boost profits while executives keep their bonuses. When someone spreads rumors about a rival to make themselves look better in comparison.

l: look up to and live by others' breath
m: To be dependent on others for survival and success, having no autonomy or self-sufficiency.
s: When someone relies entirely on their parents for money and cannot make independent decisions. When an employee must constantly seek approval from their boss for every small action and has no real authority.

m: Something is so valuable that its worth is equivalent to the wealth of an entire city; priceless.
s: When someone possesses something extremely rare and valuable, like a masterpiece painting or an ancient artifact that cannot be bought with money. When describing a person's talent or contribution that is invaluable to society.

m: Something that is both inexpensive and of excellent quality, offering great value for money.
s: When you find a high-quality item at a very affordable price. When recommending a product to a friend because it's cheap but really well-made. When shopping and discovering that the best items don't always have to be the most expensive ones.

l: employ people solely based on kinship
m: To appoint or promote people based on family relationships rather than merit or ability.
s: When a manager hires unqualified family members instead of the most capable candidates. When a company's leadership positions go to relatives of the boss regardless of their qualifications or experience.

l: appoint people based solely on talent
m: Select and promote people exclusively based on their abilities and merit, regardless of personal relationships or other factors.
s: When a company hires the most qualified candidate even though they don't have connections to anyone in the organization. When a manager promotes the best performer for the job rather than their friend who is less capable.

m: To be completely controlled or manipulated by others without any ability to resist or make one's own decisions.
s: When someone has no say in their own life and just does whatever their boss tells them to do. When a person is so dependent on their partner that they have no independence and just go along with whatever the partner wants.

l: allow it to flow by itself
m: To neglect something and let it develop without any guidance, control, or intervention.
s: When a manager ignores problems in their department and lets things fall apart on their own. When parents don't set rules or boundaries for their children and let them do whatever they want without any discipline.

c: 任凭风浪起，稳坐钓鱼船
p: rèn píng fēng làng qǐ ， wěn zuò diào yú chuán
l: Let the wind and waves arise as they will, sit steadily in the fishing boat
m: Remain calm and unmoved by external circumstances or disturbances, maintaining composure and stability regardless of turmoil around you.
s: When someone stays focused on their goals despite criticism or obstacles from others. When a person remains peaceful and doesn't get caught up in drama or chaos happening around them at work or in their social circle.

m: To willingly do any work without complaint or resentment, no matter how difficult or thankless.
s: When someone consistently takes on difficult tasks at work without ever complaining or asking for recognition. When a family member quietly handles all the household chores without making a fuss about how much they're doing.

l: the responsibility is heavy and the road is long
m: One has an important task ahead that will require sustained effort and determination to complete.
s: When someone takes on a major project at work that will require years of dedication. When a student realizes they need to study hard for many years to become a doctor. When a new leader understands the magnitude of problems they need to solve in their organization.

l: rest and recuperate to nurture life
m: To take time away from work and activity to recover one's health, energy, and strength through rest and rejuvenation.
s: When a company has been through a difficult period and needs time to stabilize and recover before growing again. When someone has been working intensely and needs a break to restore their physical and mental wellbeing.

m: To share both good fortune and hardship equally, with fates deeply intertwined and inseparable.
s: When a group of colleagues decides to stick together through both successful projects and difficult times. When family members support each other through both celebrations and crises, treating each other's problems as their own.

l: rest and sorrow are mutually connected
m: The fortunes of people are closely linked together, so that what affects one directly affects the others.
s: When a company's success depends on teamwork, everyone's individual performance impacts the whole group. When family members support each other through both good times and bad times because their wellbeing is intertwined.

p: zhòng rén shí chái huǒ yàn gāo
l: many people gathering firewood makes the flames burn high
m: when many people work together toward a common goal, the result is much greater and more powerful than any individual effort alone
s: When a community comes together to help rebuild after a disaster, the work gets done much faster and more completely. When a team at work collaborates on a big project, they can accomplish something that would be impossible for one person alone.

l: The multitude rebels and the kin depart
m: A person becomes completely isolated when both their supporters and close family members abandon them due to their actions or character.
s: When someone's behavior becomes so terrible that even their own family stops supporting them and leaves them alone. When a leader loses the trust of all their followers and even their closest relatives turn against them.

l: the mouths of many melt gold
m: Repeated criticism and slander from many people can damage even the most solid reputation or truth.
s: When a public figure's reputation is destroyed by constant negative comments on social media from thousands of people. When false rumors spread widely and everyone starts believing them despite the lack of evidence, eventually affecting how people view someone.

l: Many mouths are difficult to satisfy
m: It is impossible to please everyone because people have different tastes and preferences.
s: When you're organizing an event and trying to pick a restaurant that everyone will like, but some people want Italian while others want Chinese. When a manager tries to set a policy that makes all employees happy, but different departments have conflicting needs.

l: the many and the few differ greatly
m: There is a vast disparity in the number or strength of two opposing sides, creating an overwhelming disadvantage for the weaker one.
s: When a small team faces a much larger competitor with more resources and personnel. When discussing how a lone person trying to stand up to a powerful organization is at a huge disadvantage. When analyzing a conflict where one side has far superior numbers or military might.

l: the united will becomes a city wall
m: When people unite with a common purpose and determination, they become an unbreakable force that can overcome any obstacle.
s: When a community comes together to rebuild after a disaster, pooling their efforts and resources. When a team faces a difficult challenge and everyone commits to working toward the same goal without hesitation.

l: the anger of many is difficult to offend against
m: It is dangerous and unwise to provoke the collective anger of a large group of people, as their combined force is overwhelming and difficult to resist.
s: When a company ignores widespread customer complaints and faces a massive boycott. When a politician makes an unpopular decision and faces overwhelming public backlash that forces them to reverse course.

m: Something that is commonly known and accepted by everyone, requiring no explanation or proof.
s: When stating an obvious fact that everyone already knows about. When you're about to explain something so well-established that it hardly needs mentioning, like how the Earth orbits the Sun or that water is essential for life.

l: many people supporting makes it easy to lift
m: When many people work together toward a common goal, even difficult tasks become easy to accomplish.
s: When a group of colleagues bands together to complete a large project quickly. When a community comes together to help rebuild after a disaster and the work gets done much faster than expected.
