m: Someone who is widely expected and desired by the public to take on a leadership role or position of responsibility.
s: When a popular employee finally gets promoted to manager because everyone wanted them to lead. When a respected community member is elected to office because they have overwhelming public support.

m: Something is so obvious and evident that it is clear to everyone without any doubt.
s: When a public figure's corruption is exposed and everyone can see the evidence. When someone's true intentions become impossible to hide because their actions speak louder than words.

m: An action or event that happens in full view of many people, leaving no room for secrecy or denial.
s: When someone does something wrong or embarrassing right in front of a large crowd. When a public figure makes a mistake that thousands of people witness at the same time. When you catch someone cheating in front of the whole class.

l: the target of ten thousand arrows
m: A person or thing that is the focus of widespread criticism, attack, or blame from all sides.
s: When a public figure makes a controversial statement and becomes the subject of intense criticism from everyone. When a company's product fails and the CEO becomes the target of blame from customers, employees, and the media alike.

m: When many people express different and conflicting opinions about the same issue, with no consensus or agreement.
s: When a controversial news story breaks and people on social media have wildly different takes on what happened. When a group of friends can't agree on where to eat for dinner and everyone keeps suggesting different restaurants.

p: zhòng shuō fēn yún ， mò zhōng yī shì
l: Many voices speak in discord, none can reach agreement
m: When many people express different opinions about something, it becomes difficult or impossible to reach a consensus or unified understanding.
s: When a group of people debates a topic and everyone has a conflicting viewpoint, making it hard to decide on anything. When you ask multiple experts for advice and they each give you completely different recommendations, leaving you confused about what to do.

m: To live or act in a relaxed, unhurried manner without worry or stress.
s: When someone is taking their time doing things without any urgency, enjoying life at a slow pace. When your friend is lounging around on a weekend, completely unbothered by responsibilities, just enjoying themselves.

l: gentle and soft with few decisions
m: To be indecisive and hesitant, unable to make firm decisions or commitments.
s: When someone keeps going back and forth between two choices and can't commit to either one. When a person delays making an important decision because they keep second-guessing themselves. When a friend says they want to do something but then changes their mind multiple times.

l: the superior wins and the inferior loses
m: In competition or struggle, the strong and capable succeed while the weak and incompetent fail, following a natural law of selection.
s: When a company with better products and management dominates the market while poorly run competitors go out of business. When athletes with superior training and talent advance to higher levels while others are eliminated. When discussing how nature selects for the fittest organisms in evolution.

m: To commit acts so immoral and unethical that they violate the natural order and basic principles of human decency.
s: When someone commits a heinous crime that shocks the conscience of society. When a person acts with such cruelty and disregard for ethics that it seems to go against human nature itself.

m: To behave in an indecent or immoral way that violates social norms and offends public morality.
s: When someone engages in scandalous behavior that shocks the community and brings shame to their family. When a public figure is caught doing something that the society considers deeply inappropriate or unethical.

l: between the eldest and second eldest brothers
m: Two people or things are so similar in quality or ability that it is difficult to distinguish which one is superior.
s: When two students have nearly identical test scores and you can't say one is clearly better than the other. When comparing two job candidates who both have equally impressive qualifications and experience. When two sports teams are so evenly skilled that either one could win the championship.

m: Having a quick wit and eloquent speech; being articulate and persuasive in conversation.
s: When someone is very good at talking their way out of trouble or convincing others to agree with them. When a person always has a clever comeback or witty response ready in any conversation.

l: appears to be right but is actually wrong
m: Something that seems correct or true on the surface but is actually false or incorrect upon closer examination.
s: When someone presents an argument that sounds convincing at first but doesn't hold up under scrutiny. When you see a product advertisement that looks legitimate but is actually misleading. When a news story seems credible but turns out to contain false information.

m: To behave in an obsequious, servile manner by degrading oneself or acting in an undignified way to please others.
s: When someone constantly flatters their boss or authority figure in an exaggerated way just to get ahead. When a person abandons their dignity and self-respect to win favor from someone they perceive as more powerful or important.

m: To act in an extremely humble, submissive, or obsequious manner, often to an excessive or demeaning degree.
s: When someone is being overly apologetic and self-deprecating in front of a person they fear or respect. When a worker constantly flatters their boss and agrees with everything they say just to avoid conflict.

m: Someone who combines physical strength or imposing appearance with intellectual sophistication and refined thinking.
s: When describing a person who is unexpectedly thoughtful and detail-oriented despite their intimidating physical presence. When someone surprises you by showing deep insight and careful consideration along with their commanding demeanor.

m: One's body is covered with injuries or wounds with hardly any unmarked skin remaining.
s: When someone gets beaten up badly and is covered in bruises and cuts all over. When a person has been through a traumatic physical ordeal and their body is severely damaged. When describing someone who has been criticized or attacked relentlessly from all sides.

l: considerate and entering into the finest details
m: To show exceptional thoughtfulness and care by attending to the smallest details and nuances of another person's needs and feelings.
s: When someone remembers exactly how you like your coffee and has it ready before you ask. When a friend notices you're feeling down and quietly helps with your chores without being asked, showing they really pay attention to your emotional state.

m: there is no reason not to do something that brings happiness or benefits
s: When someone offers you a good opportunity with no downsides, and you wonder why you wouldn't take it. When a friend suggests a fun activity that's free and easy, and there's no good reason to decline.

p: hé qí xiāng sì nǎi ěr
l: How they are so similar like this
m: Two things are remarkably alike or nearly identical in appearance, quality, or nature.
s: When you see two products that look almost exactly the same and you're amazed at how similar they are. When two people have nearly identical personalities, mannerisms, or ways of thinking. When you notice two situations unfolding in almost the exact same way.

l: where to go and where to follow
m: To be uncertain about which direction to take or what course of action to pursue when faced with difficult choices.
s: When someone is undecided about whether to accept a new job offer or stay in their current position. When a student doesn't know whether to pursue medicine or engineering in college. When a company is uncertain whether to expand into a new market or focus on improving existing operations.

l: how is it worth hanging between the teeth
m: Something so trivial or insignificant that it is not worth mentioning or discussing.
s: When someone apologizes for a small mistake and you want to tell them it's no big deal. When a friend thanks you for a tiny favor and you want to say it was nothing worth talking about.

m: One still has energy, ability, or courage left to contribute or be useful in further endeavors.
s: When a retired athlete says they still have the stamina to coach younger players. When an experienced professional offers to help with a new project because they feel they still have much to offer. When someone recovering from illness wants to return to work because they feel their strength has returned.

l: lingering sound winds around the beams
m: A beautiful sound or melody is so captivating that it seems to echo and resonate long after it has ended, leaving a lasting impression.
s: When you hear a beautiful song that stays in your head for days afterward. When someone gives a powerful speech that continues to affect you emotionally long after they've finished speaking. When a piece of music is so moving that you can't stop thinking about it.

l: act as a spectator on the wall
m: To remain neutral and uninvolved while others compete or struggle, watching from the sidelines without taking sides or action.
s: When two of your friends are arguing and you choose not to get involved, just watching to see how it plays out. When a coworker refuses to help resolve a conflict between colleagues and just observes what happens instead.

l: commit treachery and violate the law
m: To engage in evil deeds and break the law; to act wickedly and criminally without regard for rules or morality.
s: When someone is caught repeatedly doing illegal or immoral things and doesn't care about the consequences. When a person is known for consistently breaking rules and engaging in harmful, criminal behavior.

m: to abuse one's power to oppress others and seek personal gain through tyranny and exploitation.
s: When a manager uses their position to bully employees and take credit for their work. When a corrupt official extorts money from citizens while acting above the law. When someone with a little bit of authority acts like a dictator and mistreats those below them.

m: Someone has done many wicked or harmful things, showing a pattern of serious wrongdoing.
s: When a criminal has committed numerous crimes over a long period. When describing someone who has repeatedly hurt others through dishonest or cruel actions. When a corrupt official has engaged in multiple instances of bribery and abuse of power.

l: creating a method that destroys oneself
m: One's own actions or schemes ultimately lead to their own downfall or failure.
s: When someone sets a trap for others but ends up getting caught in it themselves. When a person's dishonest plan backfires and harms them instead of their intended target. When someone creates a rule or policy that unexpectedly hurts their own interests.

l: weave a cocoon and bind oneself
m: To create problems or restrictions for oneself through one's own actions, ultimately becoming trapped by the consequences of one's behavior.
s: When someone's own bad decisions end up harming them more than anyone else. When a person creates unnecessary complications in their life and then complains about being stuck in a difficult situation.

l: acting like a thief with a guilty heart
m: When someone feels guilty or ashamed about something they've done, they become nervous and anxious, often revealing their wrongdoing through their behavior.
s: When a student who cheated on a test acts suspiciously nervous around the teacher. When someone who broke their friend's vase avoids eye contact and stammers when asked about it. When a person who lied keeps over-explaining themselves and seems jittery.

m: A situation where two parties are in irreconcilable conflict and only one can survive or succeed; a zero-sum struggle where the victory of one requires the complete defeat or destruction of the other.
s: When two companies are competing fiercely and there's only room in the market for one of them to survive. When two political opponents view their conflict as an existential struggle where compromise is impossible and only one side can ultimately prevail.

l: you chase me, I chase you
m: People compete fiercely with each other, each trying to outdo the others in a race or contest.
s: When multiple companies are competing intensely to gain market share. When students in a class are all working hard to get the best grades and push each other to do better.

m: To speak in a fluent, confident, and eloquent manner about a topic.
s: When someone gives a well-prepared presentation and talks smoothly without hesitation. When a knowledgeable person discusses their area of expertise with ease and conviction.

m: There is not enough of something available to satisfy the number of people who want it.
s: When a popular product sells out quickly because too many people want to buy it. When a concert has far more people wanting tickets than there are seats available.

m: Extreme reluctance to leave someone or something, showing deep affection and emotional attachment at the moment of separation.
s: When friends or lovers have to say goodbye at an airport and keep hugging each other, unable to let go. When a student graduates and doesn't want to leave their school and teachers behind. When elderly parents struggle to say goodbye to their adult children who are moving far away.

l: draw the gourd following the pattern
m: to imitate something mechanically without understanding or adapting to actual circumstances.
s: When a student copies homework without learning the material. When someone follows instructions rigidly without thinking about whether they actually make sense in their situation.

m: Something remains unchanged and continues to be the same as it was in the past.
s: When years have passed but a friend's personality hasn't changed at all. When a company continues using the same old methods despite new technology being available. When someone returns to their hometown and finds that their childhood neighborhood looks exactly the same.

m: Someone remains unchanged in their behavior, attitude, or character despite the passage of time or external circumstances.
s: When someone keeps making the same mistakes they've always made, refusing to improve or change their ways. When a friend promises to stop procrastinating but continues with the same habits as before. When an old colleague returns to the company but acts exactly like they did years ago, with no personal growth.

l: leaning on both sides equally possible
m: To remain ambiguous or noncommittal, wavering between two positions without taking a clear stance.
s: When a politician gives an answer that could support either side of a debate without actually committing to either position. When your boss says they'll think about your promotion request but gives no clear yes or no answer. When someone refuses to choose between two options and tries to keep both possibilities open.

m: To achieve victory through luck or chance rather than through skill, preparation, or merit.
s: When a sports team wins a game despite playing poorly, relying on lucky breaks and opponent mistakes. When someone passes an exam they didn't study for because the questions happened to cover exactly what they knew.

m: to look at someone with suspicion, disapproval, or resentment, often with eyes averted to the side.
s: When someone does something so outrageous that people give them dirty looks instead of confronting them directly. When a coworker's unethical behavior causes everyone to regard them with disdain and avoid eye contact with them.

m: To act according to what is most convenient or expedient in the moment, prioritizing ease over principle or proper procedure.
s: When a manager cuts corners on safety procedures to finish a project faster. When someone takes shortcuts in their work because it's easier, even though they know it's not the right way to do it.

l: move knees close and talk from the heart
m: To have an intimate, candid conversation with someone in close proximity, sharing one's true feelings and thoughts without reservation.
s: When two friends sit down together in a quiet place to discuss their deepest concerns and feelings honestly. When family members have a serious, private conversation where they open up about what's really bothering them.

m: Something is so vulgar, tacky, or crude that it is unbearable to witness or experience.
s: When you see someone wearing extremely garish, over-the-top clothing that clashes terribly. When a wealthy person decorates their house with so much gold and flashy ornaments that it looks ridiculous and tasteless.

l: speak with a trustworthy mouth like a river
m: To speak carelessly and without regard for truth or consequences, saying whatever comes to mind without thinking.
s: When someone makes up stories or exaggerates without any factual basis. When a person blurts out whatever they're thinking without considering if it's true or will hurt others' feelings. When someone gossips and spreads rumors without verifying the facts first.

l: speak with a wanton tongue using false yellow
m: To speak carelessly and make unfounded claims or accusations without regard for truth or accuracy.
s: When someone spreads rumors about a coworker without any evidence. When a person makes wild accusations or exaggerated stories just to get attention or stir up trouble.

m: To accomplish something with such skill and ease that it requires no conscious effort or preparation.
s: When a talented musician plays a beautiful song without any sheet music or practice. When someone solves a difficult problem instantly because they have so much experience with it.

m: To walk around aimlessly and without purpose, simply enjoying the act of wandering for pleasure and relaxation.
s: When you have a free afternoon and decide to walk through the neighborhood without any specific destination. When someone takes a slow, relaxing walk through a park just to enjoy the scenery and fresh air.

m: A statement or claim is reliable because it is backed by concrete proof and factual evidence.
s: When someone makes a claim and provides solid documentation or witnesses to support it. When a historical account is considered credible because multiple reliable sources confirm it. When you can trust what someone says because their words are consistently supported by their actions and verifiable facts.

m: To make a serious and earnest promise or commitment, often with great confidence or conviction.
s: When someone insists they will definitely keep their word and swears up and down that they won't let you down. When a friend promises very seriously that they will change their behavior or help you no matter what.

m: A system of governance or management is only credible and effective when rewards for good behavior and punishments for wrongdoing are both consistently and fairly administered.
s: When a manager wants to build trust with their team, they need to follow through on both praising good work and disciplining misconduct fairly. In a company, if employees see that some people are rewarded for success while others who fail face no consequences, they lose faith in the fairness of the system. A coach gains respect from players by reliably giving playing time to those who perform well and reducing minutes for those who slack off.

l: trust the horse and let the reins go loose
m: To act without direction or purpose, allowing things to develop naturally without deliberate control or planning.
s: When someone just goes with the flow without a clear plan or destination. When a project proceeds without any real strategy, just seeing where it goes naturally.

l: repair the old and utilize the discarded
m: To fix what is broken and make use of what has been abandoned or discarded, minimizing waste and maximizing efficiency.
s: When someone repairs old furniture instead of buying new ones to save money. When a factory recycles scrap materials into new products. When you find creative ways to reuse old clothes or household items rather than throwing them away.

m: An extremely short period of time; a moment so brief it takes only the time to bow and stand up again.
s: When something happens so quickly you can barely register it. When a situation changes in just an instant, like a car zooming past or a sudden unexpected event that's over before you know it.

l: bowing and looking up are controlled by others
m: One's actions and fate are entirely controlled or determined by other people, leaving no room for independent choice or freedom.
s: When an employee has to follow every instruction from their boss without any autonomy. When someone is so dependent on their parents that they cannot make any decisions for themselves. When a person is in a situation where they must comply with whatever others demand.

l: bending down and picking up is immediately there
m: Something is so abundant and commonplace that you can find it everywhere with minimal effort.
s: When describing how easy it is to find cheap knockoff products in a market. When someone points out that examples of a certain behavior are extremely common and visible all around us.

l: bow the head and listen to commands
m: To submit obediently to authority without resistance or question.
s: When someone completely accepts orders from their boss without arguing or expressing their own opinion. When a person stops resisting and agrees to follow instructions, showing they have given up their independence.

l: bow the head and stick the ear
m: To show complete obedience and submission, listening attentively and obeying without question.
s: When someone becomes completely obedient to another person's authority and never questions their orders. When an employee becomes so submissive to their boss that they never speak up or express their own opinions anymore.

l: turn over and strike with a rake
m: To turn the tables on someone by falsely accusing them of the very thing they accused you of, or to retaliate unfairly against someone who confronted you.
s: When someone caught doing something wrong suddenly blames the person who called them out instead of admitting fault. When a cheating spouse accuses their partner of infidelity to deflect from their own betrayal.

l: reverse the fruit and make it the cause
m: To mistake the effect for the cause, or to get the relationship between cause and effect backwards.
s: When someone blames a symptom instead of the underlying problem. When a person thinks that staying up late causes success, when really success allows them to stay up late working on their passion. When someone thinks that correlation means causation and gets the logical relationship completely reversed.

m: To know something so thoroughly and perfectly that you can recite it fluently even in reverse order, demonstrating complete mastery.
s: When someone has memorized a text so well they can recite it backwards without hesitation. When a student knows their material so thoroughly that they could answer questions about it in any order or direction.

m: Acting in ways that go against natural principles, reason, or moral standards; stubbornly pursuing a course of action that is fundamentally wrong or counterproductive.
s: When a company ignores customer feedback and makes policies that drive away their best clients. When a leader makes decisions that are obviously harmful to their own organization's goals and values.

l: fortuitous thing that comes by chance
m: An unexpected fortune or benefit that arrives without effort or planning, often attributed to luck or fate rather than one's own actions.
s: When you unexpectedly receive an inheritance from a distant relative you never knew. When you find money in an old jacket pocket or win something you didn't enter a contest for. When a great opportunity suddenly presents itself through pure chance or coincidence.

l: Rely on office and flaunt power
m: To bully others by abusing one's official position and using one's power as a weapon.
s: When a government official uses their authority to intimidate or harm ordinary citizens who cannot fight back. When someone in a position of power treats subordinates unfairly because they know those people depend on them for their job.

l: rely on age and sell age
m: An elderly person uses their advanced age as an excuse to behave arrogantly, demand respect, or avoid responsibility.
s: When an older family member refuses to follow safety rules because they say 'I've lived this long, I know what I'm doing.' When a senior coworker dismisses new ideas by saying they've been around longer and therefore their way is always right.

l: borrow a knife to kill someone
m: to accomplish your goal by manipulating someone else into doing your dirty work for you.
s: When someone tricks their rival into fighting with a third party so they can benefit without getting involved. When a manager gets two employees to argue so neither one suspects the manager caused the conflict. When you want someone eliminated but get another person to do it for you while staying clean.

l: borrow the past to satirize the present
m: to use historical examples or references to criticize or mock current events, people, or conditions.
s: When a politician references a historical scandal to criticize a similar situation happening today. When a teacher uses an old cautionary tale to point out mistakes being repeated by modern society. When someone brings up past failures of a company to highlight their current poor decisions.

l: borrow a corpse to return the soul
m: to revive or repurpose something old or defunct by giving it new life or function under different circumstances.
s: When a company buys an old failing business and completely restructures it to make it successful. When someone takes an outdated technology or idea and reimplements it in a modern context to make it relevant again. When a government uses an existing institution for a completely different purpose than it was originally designed for.

l: borrow flowers to offer to Buddha
m: to use something that belongs to someone else or something readily available to present as one's own gift or tribute.
s: When you regift a present someone gave you to another person. When a colleague takes credit for work that was actually done by their team members. When someone compliments a friend on their appearance but the friend is actually wearing borrowed clothes or accessories.

m: to use a minor issue or topic as a pretext to express one's true thoughts or grievances on a larger matter.
s: When someone brings up a small complaint but is actually upset about something much bigger. When a boss criticizes a minor mistake but is really venting frustration about larger performance issues.

m: To be deeply burdened with accumulated debts that have grown to an overwhelming level.
s: When a person has borrowed money from many sources and owes so much that it seems impossible to repay. When a company has taken on so many loans that it's drowning in financial obligations. When someone's credit card debt and other liabilities have accumulated to a critical point.

l: topple the city and topple the country
m: A woman of such extraordinary beauty that she has the power to bring down cities and nations.
s: When describing an exceptionally beautiful woman whose charm and allure seem almost dangerously captivating. When talking about a legendary beauty from history or fiction whose appearance supposedly influenced the fate of kingdoms and empires.

l: overturn the family and dissipate the estate
m: to lose all of one's wealth and possessions, becoming completely impoverished.
s: When someone gambles away their entire fortune and becomes bankrupt. When a business owner makes terrible investments and loses everything they own. When someone spends recklessly until they have nothing left.

l: the entire nest issues forth in offense
m: to commit a massive attack or invasion with all available forces, leaving nothing behind in defense.
s: When an army mobilizes every soldier for an all-out attack. When a company uses all its resources to launch a major offensive against competitors. When a criminal gang commits a large-scale crime using all its members.

m: A sudden, extremely heavy rainfall that falls in large quantities all at once.
s: When you step outside and it's raining so hard you can barely see across the street. When weather forecasts warn of a sudden storm that dumps rain in buckets within minutes.

l: tip over boxes and dump out chests
m: To give everything one has without holding back, or to search through something thoroughly and completely.
s: When someone empties their savings to help a friend in desperate need. When police thoroughly search a suspect's home, looking in every possible hiding place.

l: lower the flags and silence the drums
m: to cease resistance or stop making noise; to give up or withdraw quietly without further struggle.
s: When a competing team admits defeat and stops fighting back in a game. When someone stops arguing or protesting after realizing they won't win. When a company stops its aggressive marketing campaign and quietly closes down operations.

m: To abandon military pursuits and focus on peaceful, cultural, and intellectual development instead.
s: When a country decides to stop investing heavily in military spending and redirects resources toward education and the arts. When a ruler or leader shifts from an aggressive expansionist policy to one that emphasizes cultural achievements and civilian prosperity.

m: To pretend to be kind and virtuous while actually being selfish or deceitful.
s: When someone donates to charity only for publicity and social media praise. When a person acts nice and helpful in front of others but treats people poorly behind closed doors. When a coworker pretends to care about the team's wellbeing but is actually just looking out for themselves.

l: use public matters to benefit private interests
m: To abuse one's public position or authority to gain personal profit or advantage while pretending to serve the public good.
s: When a government official approves a contract for a company owned by their relative, claiming it's the best bid. When a manager allocates company resources to a project that will make them look good for a promotion rather than benefit the organization.

m: To believe something based on only one side of the story without hearing the other perspective or seeking the full truth.
s: When someone makes a judgment about a conflict after only hearing one person's version of events. When you accept gossip or rumors without getting the other person's side of the story. When a manager disciplines an employee based solely on a complaint without investigating what actually happened.

p: zuò yī tiān hé shàng zhuàng yī tiān zhōng
l: Being a monk for a day and ringing the bell for a day
m: To do the bare minimum required to get by without putting in real effort or caring about the results.
s: When someone shows up to work but just goes through the motions without actually trying. When a student only does what's necessary to pass the test without actually learning anything. When someone treats their job as just a way to collect a paycheck rather than caring about doing good work.

m: To remain in a stagnant state without making any progress or improvement.
s: When a company's sales haven't grown for years despite market opportunities. When someone stays in the same job with no career advancement for a long time. When a student's grades plateau and they stop improving no matter how much they study.

l: once in a while do it
m: To do something unusual or uncharacteristic just this one time as an exception or rare indulgence.
s: When someone who normally doesn't drink alcohol decides to have a beer at a celebration. When a strict teacher decides to skip grading papers one evening and watch a movie instead. When a health-conscious person treats themselves to fast food even though they usually eat healthy.

m: To do something in a secretive, sneaky, or furtive manner, trying to avoid being noticed or discovered.
s: When someone sneaks around trying to hide what they're doing, like a child secretly eating snacks before dinner. When someone conducts business or communicates with another person in a way they don't want others to know about.

l: steal the heavens and swap the sun
m: To deceive people through cunning tricks and deception so skillfully that even obvious truths are hidden or reversed.
s: When a company uses misleading marketing to completely change how people perceive their product. When a politician uses rhetoric so cleverly that they make a bad policy seem good to the public.

m: To cut corners by using inferior materials or doing less work than required to save time and money.
s: When a contractor uses cheaper materials than specified in the contract to increase profits. When a manufacturer reduces quality control steps to speed up production. When someone does a rushed, sloppy job instead of putting in proper effort.

l: steal the beams and replace the pillars
m: to make a deceptive substitution by replacing something valuable or essential with something inferior or worthless while disguising the change.
s: When a contractor uses cheap materials in place of quality ones while charging full price. When someone subtly changes the terms of a deal after you've already agreed to it. When a company removes key features from a product but keeps the price the same.

p: tōu jī bù chéng shí bǎ mǐ
l: Attempting to steal a chicken but losing a handful of rice
m: When trying to gain something through dishonest or cunning means, you end up losing what you already had instead.
s: When someone tries to cheat or scheme their way to profit but ends up worse off than before. When a business cuts corners to save money but loses customers and money instead. When someone tries to avoid paying a small bill dishonestly and gets caught, facing much bigger consequences.

m: To engage in petty theft, sneaky behavior, or dishonorable actions that are morally corrupt and base.
s: When someone is caught shoplifting small items repeatedly. When a coworker is suspected of taking things that don't belong to them or engaging in underhanded dealings at work.

m: To rely on others for support or to live in dependence, lacking independence or self-sufficiency.
s: When someone moves in with relatives and has no job or income of their own. When an adult child relies entirely on their parents for money and shelter without trying to become self-reliant.

m: A person who appears stupid or lacking in intelligence and common sense.
s: When someone does something obviously silly without thinking it through. When a coworker asks a question that shows they weren't paying attention at all. When your friend walks into a glass door because they weren't looking where they were going.

m: Family members or close allies engage in internal conflict while presenting a united front to outsiders.
s: When two siblings fight bitterly over inheritance while pretending everything is fine in public. When business partners who are like brothers start competing against each other instead of working together against their rivals.

p: xiōng dì xì yú qiáng ， wài yù qí wǔ
l: Brothers quarrel within the wall, but together resist insult from outside
m: Family members may have internal conflicts, but they unite against external threats or enemies.
s: When siblings argue constantly but immediately band together if someone outside the family criticizes one of them. When a company has internal disagreements but presents a unified front to competitors or the public. When family members fight among themselves but defend each other fiercely against outsiders.

m: To deliberately ignore or refuse to listen to what others are saying.
s: When someone keeps talking to you but you intentionally pretend not to hear them. When a parent gives advice to their child, but the child completely ignores it and acts like they didn't hear anything.

m: Taking the initiative and acting before others gives you a strategic advantage.
s: When you need to apply for a popular job position before other candidates do. When you want to claim a good spot in line by arriving early before the rush. When you make a preemptive move in a negotiation to set favorable terms before the other side makes their demands.

l: first to enter becomes the master
m: First impressions or initial beliefs are difficult to change, and people tend to stick with what they learned or believed first.
s: When someone meets a person and forms a negative opinion right away, it's hard to convince them otherwise later. When you learn something one way and then struggle to accept a different approach because you're used to the first way. When a student gets a bad first impression of a teacher and maintains that view despite evidence they're actually good at teaching.

m: Opinions or judgments formed before having complete information, often preventing objective understanding of something new.
s: When someone refuses to try a new restaurant because they assume it will be bad based on its appearance. When a person won't listen to a different political viewpoint because they've already made up their mind beforehand.

l: the urgent matter that comes first
m: The most pressing priority that needs to be addressed immediately before anything else.
s: When a company is facing financial crisis, stabilizing cash flow becomes the first order of business. When someone is seriously ill, getting them to the hospital is the most urgent priority. When a student is failing a class, studying for the exam should be their foremost concern.

l: strike first to control the opponent
m: Taking the initiative to act first gives you an advantage over your opponent or competitor.
s: In business, launching a new product before your competitors do puts you in a stronger market position. In a conflict, the person who takes action first often has the upper hand. In sports, scoring early in the game can set the momentum in your favor.

m: To gain a psychological or strategic advantage by making a strong initial impression or taking the first decisive action before others can respond.
s: When a debater makes such a compelling opening statement that the audience is already convinced before the opponent speaks. When a company launches a revolutionary product that dominates the market before competitors can react. When someone establishes their authority or confidence right from the start of a negotiation, putting others at a disadvantage.

c: 先天下之忧而忧，后天下之乐而乐
p: xiān tiān xià zhī yōu ér yōu ， hòu tiān xià zhī lè ér lè
l: Worry about the world's troubles before the world worries, and rejoice in the world's happiness after the world rejoices
m: One should prioritize the welfare and concerns of society before pursuing personal happiness, and only enjoy personal success after ensuring the general well-being of all people.
s: When a leader makes sacrifices for their country's benefit before considering their own comfort. When someone dedicates themselves to solving a community problem even though it doesn't directly affect them personally.

m: To be naturally deficient or disadvantaged from birth, lacking inherent strength or capability that cannot be easily overcome.
s: When someone is born with a disability or genetic condition that limits their abilities. When a company starts with poor foundational design that makes it hard to succeed later. When a student struggles because they lack basic knowledge that others learned early on.

m: Take decisive action on your own authority before seeking permission or approval from superiors.
s: When a manager makes an important business decision without consulting their boss, then explains the reasoning afterward. When someone takes the initiative to solve a pressing problem rather than waiting for permission from higher-ups.

m: To have the privilege of seeing or experiencing something before others get the chance, which brings great pleasure and satisfaction.
s: When you get to read a new book before it's officially released to the public. When you're invited to a private preview of an art exhibition before it opens to everyone else.

l: first to know, first to perceive
m: Having the ability to foresee future events or trends before others do; possessing exceptional foresight and insight.
s: When someone predicted the stock market crash before it happened. When a business leader saw a new technology trend coming and adapted their company years ahead of competitors. When your friend warned you about a bad relationship that everyone else thought was fine, and they turned out to be right.

m: Attempt to resolve a matter through polite negotiation and diplomacy before resorting to conflict or coercion.
s: When you try to reason with someone calmly before getting angry or taking drastic action. When a company gives a customer multiple warnings and chances to pay before taking legal action.

m: The ability to foresee or predict future events before they happen; exceptional foresight or prophetic insight.
s: When someone predicted the housing market crash before it happened and avoided major losses. When a business leader saw the potential of e-commerce years before it became mainstream and pivoted their company successfully.

l: restore old things to their former glory
m: To repair or restore something old back to its original condition or former state of excellence.
s: When someone carefully restores an antique piece of furniture to look like new again. When a museum curator expertly repairs a damaged historical artifact so it looks as good as it did centuries ago. When a skilled craftsperson fixes up an old family heirloom to bring back its original beauty.

m: Something happening in broad daylight, openly and obviously, without concealment or secrecy.
s: When someone commits a crime or does something wrong in public where everyone can see it. When a person acts dishonestly or inappropriately right in front of many witnesses without trying to hide it.

l: bring glory and honor to ancestors
m: To achieve success and distinction that reflects well on one's family name and ancestral lineage.
s: When someone from a humble background becomes successful and their achievement makes their family proud and respected in the community. When a child's accomplishments elevate the family's social status and reputation.

m: Something is so brilliant and impressive in appearance that it captures everyone's attention and admiration.
s: When a celebrity walks into a room wearing an absolutely stunning outfit that everyone stares at. When a new luxury car is parked on the street and turns all the heads because of how shiny and beautiful it looks.

m: Bizarre, fantastical, and outlandish things that are strange and difficult to comprehend.
s: When you see something very unusual and hard to believe at first glance. When describing a movie or book full of weird and fantastical creatures or scenery that seems unreal.

m: Acting in a completely open, honest, and legitimate way without any secrecy or deception.
s: When someone conducts their business affairs transparently and doesn't hide anything from others. When a person is honest about their intentions and doesn't try to sneak around or be sneaky about what they're doing.

m: To be honest, transparent, and free from deception or hidden motives in one's actions and character.
s: When someone conducts their business dealings openly without trying to hide anything. When a person's intentions are pure and they have nothing to be ashamed of, so they don't need to hide their actions.

m: Someone or something shines brilliantly and stands out with exceptional talent, success, or potential.
s: When a young athlete suddenly becomes famous and is winning every competition. When a previously unknown actor gets their breakthrough role and everyone starts talking about them. When someone who was struggling finally succeeds and is thriving in their career.

m: Time passes very quickly and cannot be stopped or recovered once it is gone.
s: When you realize a year has gone by and wonder where the time went. When someone reflects on how fast their children have grown up. When you look back and can't believe how quickly a decade has passed.

l: able to be diligent and able to be frugal
m: To be consistently hardworking and economical in managing resources and daily life.
s: When describing someone who works hard and doesn't waste money or resources. When praising a person or family for their disciplined approach to both labor and spending. When talking about the virtues needed to build wealth through honest work and careful saving.

l: restrain oneself and serve the public
m: To suppress one's own desires and selfish interests in order to dedicate oneself to serving the greater good and public welfare.
s: When a government official makes decisions based on what benefits the people rather than personal gain. When someone volunteers their time and energy for a community project without expecting anything in return. When a leader puts the organization's needs ahead of their own advancement or comfort.

l: overcome the enemy and achieve victory
m: To defeat an opponent or adversary through superior strategy, strength, or cunning and win the battle or competition.
s: When a sports team manages to beat a much stronger rival through clever tactics and teamwork. When a business successfully outmaneuvers its competitors and dominates the market. When someone finds the right approach to solve a difficult problem that others couldn't overcome.

p: tù zi bù chī wō biān cǎo
l: the rabbit does not eat the grass by its nest
m: One should not take advantage of or harm people close to one, as it damages one's own immediate environment and relationships.
s: When someone refuses to date coworkers or people in their social circle to avoid complications. When a business owner avoids cheating their regular customers even though they could get away with it. When someone chooses not to gossip about or betray their close friends despite opportunities to do so.

p: tù zi wěi ba zhǎng bù liǎo
l: a rabbit's tail cannot grow long
m: something bad or undesirable cannot last long and will inevitably come to an end.
s: When someone is engaging in dishonest behavior and you know they will eventually get caught. When a friend is in a bad relationship and you're confident it won't work out in the long run. When a company is using unethical practices and you believe their success is temporary.

l: the rabbit dies and the fox grieves
m: One feels sympathy for others in similar circumstances, recognizing that misfortune could befall oneself next.
s: When coworkers are laid off and you worry about your own job security. When a friend goes through a breakup and you empathize because you've experienced similar heartbreak.

l: the rabbit dies and the dog is cooked
m: When someone is no longer useful, they are discarded or abandoned without gratitude, even if they were instrumental in achieving a goal.
s: When a company lays off employees immediately after a major project succeeds. When a political leader abandons their loyal supporters once they gain power. When a friend stops contacting you after you've helped them through a difficult situation.

l: party with the same and attack the different
m: To favor those who share your views while attacking or opposing those who disagree with you, often for factional or selfish reasons rather than principle.
s: When a manager only promotes employees who agree with them while marginalizing anyone who offers different opinions. When a political group dismisses all criticism from the opposing side without considering any valid points they might make. When colleagues form cliques that support each other's ideas blindly while rejecting outsiders' contributions.

l: cautious and diligent in one's work
m: To work with careful attention and unwavering dedication, maintaining a conscientious and responsible attitude in one's duties.
s: When describing a colleague who always shows up on time, pays attention to detail, and takes their responsibilities seriously. When praising an employee who works steadily and reliably without cutting corners or seeking recognition.

m: One's income is insufficient to cover one's expenses, resulting in a deficit.
s: When a family's monthly bills exceed their salary and they keep going into debt. When a small business is spending more money than it's making each month.

l: Entering a locality, follow the local custom
m: When you go to a new place, you should adapt to and follow the customs and practices of that local community.
s: When you move to a new country and start eating local foods and celebrating local holidays. When you visit a friend's house and follow their house rules about removing shoes or being quiet. When you join a new company and learn to dress and communicate the way your coworkers do.

l: Enter a country and inquire about its customs
m: When you go to a new place, you should learn and respect the local customs and traditions of that area.
s: When traveling to a foreign country, you should learn how people there greet each other and what they consider polite behavior. When you move to a new city or join a new community, it's important to understand local traditions and follow their way of doing things rather than imposing your own habits.

l: Enter a territory and ask about its prohibitions
m: When entering a new place or situation, one should first inquire about the local customs, rules, and regulations to avoid offending or breaking them.
s: When you move to a new country or city, you should learn about the local laws and customs before doing anything. When starting a new job, it's important to ask your colleagues about company rules and workplace norms before acting independently.

m: To be both emotionally resonant and logically sound, acting in a way that is fair, reasonable, and deeply understanding of human feelings.
s: When someone gives advice that you can't argue with because it's both practical and shows they truly understand how you feel. When a manager handles a difficult situation in a way that employees accept because the decision is fair and the manager clearly cares about their wellbeing.

l: enter the wood three points deep
m: to have such deep insight or skill that one penetrates to the very essence or core of something.
s: When a teacher explains a complex concept so well that students truly understand it at the deepest level. When a writer or artist captures the true nature of a character so perfectly that readers feel they know them completely. When a critic's analysis of a book or film reveals hidden meanings that no one else had noticed before.

m: A complete and total defeat or failure, with no survivors or successes remaining.
s: When a team loses every single game in a season with no wins at all. When a company's product launch completely fails and they lose all their market share. When someone tries multiple business ventures and every single one goes bankrupt.

l: commit all strength to rush forth
m: To make an all-out effort and dedicate oneself completely to achieving a goal.
s: When a student studies intensively for an important exam by sacrificing sleep and leisure time. When a team works around the clock to meet a critical project deadline. When an athlete trains with maximum dedication to prepare for a championship competition.

m: To devote oneself entirely and sincerely to something without reservation or distraction.
s: When someone is fully committed to helping a friend through a difficult time. When a team member gives their complete dedication to finishing a project, putting aside all other concerns.

l: concentrate all spirit and channel attention
m: To focus one's complete attention and mental energy entirely on something.
s: When a student is studying for an important exam and blocks out all distractions. When a musician is performing and is completely absorbed in the music. When someone is working on a difficult task and nothing else can break their concentration.

p: bā xiān guò hǎi ， gè xiǎn shén tōng
l: The Eight Immortals cross the sea, each displaying their magical powers
m: Each person uses their own unique talents and abilities to accomplish a goal, with everyone contributing in their own way.
s: When a group project succeeds because each team member brought their own special skills to the table. When different people solve the same problem using completely different methods that all work. When a family works together on a big task, with each person doing what they do best.

m: To display an imposing and commanding presence that inspires awe and respect from all directions.
s: When a powerful leader walks into a room and immediately commands everyone's attention through sheer authority and confidence. When someone carries themselves with such dignity and power that people naturally defer to them.

m: The ability to handle all situations smoothly and get along with everyone through clever social skills and tactfulness.
s: When someone is excellent at networking and always knows what to say to make everyone comfortable around them. When a colleague manages to stay on good terms with all different groups at work despite their conflicts with each other.

m: Handle official business strictly according to rules and procedures without personal bias or favoritism.
s: When a manager applies company policies equally to all employees without making exceptions. When a government official refuses to help a friend cut corners or bend regulations, insisting everything must follow proper procedures.

l: use public matters to settle private grievances
m: To abuse one's official position or authority to seek revenge against someone for personal reasons.
s: When a boss fires an employee not because of poor performance, but because of a personal conflict. When a government official uses their power to punish someone who wronged them privately.

m: To prioritize the public good and collective welfare over personal interests and private gains.
s: When a leader makes decisions that benefit the community even though it costs them personally. When someone volunteers their time and skills for a cause without expecting anything in return. When a manager sacrifices their own comfort to ensure their team succeeds.

c: 公说公有理，婆说婆有理
p: gōng shuō gōng yǒu lǐ ， pó shuō pó yǒu lǐ
l: The husband says the husband is right, the wife says the wife is right
m: Each party believes they are correct and refuses to acknowledge the other's perspective, resulting in an unresolvable dispute where both sides stubbornly maintain their own position.
s: When a couple argues about household decisions and neither one will admit the other has a valid point. When two colleagues disagree about how to solve a problem and each insists their own method is the only correct one.

l: make public to those of shared interests
m: To share something you enjoy or are passionate about with others who have similar interests or tastes.
s: When you discover a great book, movie, or hobby and want to share it with friends who would appreciate it. When someone publishes their collection or hobby online to connect with fellow enthusiasts who share the same passion.

l: not recognizing the six relations of kinship
m: To completely disown or refuse to acknowledge even one's closest family members, typically due to rage, betrayal, or moral outrage.
s: When someone is so angry at a family member that they disown them completely. When a parent cuts off all contact with their child due to a serious conflict. When someone prioritizes principle or justice over family loyalty, even if it means turning against their own relatives.

m: To be in a state of panic or extreme confusion where one loses the ability to think clearly or act rationally.
s: When someone receives shocking bad news and doesn't know what to do or say. When a person is so anxious or frightened that they can't focus or make decisions. When someone is overwhelmed by stress and appears completely lost or disoriented.

m: To show meticulous attention to someone's needs and welfare in every possible way.
s: When a parent carefully prepares meals, checks on your health, and remembers every detail about your comfort. When a boss consistently looks after their employees' wellbeing and professional development with genuine consideration.

m: To establish beneficial policies and practices while eliminating harmful ones, especially in governance or management.
s: When a new manager comes in and tries to implement good practices while getting rid of inefficient or harmful procedures. When a government introduces reforms that encourage economic growth while removing corrupt or wasteful systems.

m: All interest or enthusiasm has completely disappeared, leaving one feeling bored and unmotivated.
s: When you start reading a book that seemed exciting but turns out to be boring halfway through. When you go to a party expecting to have fun, but end up feeling completely disengaged and wanting to leave early.

m: To cause mischief, chaos, or disturbance through deceptive or malicious actions.
s: When someone is deliberately causing problems and stirring up trouble in a group or organization. When a person spreads rumors or creates drama to disrupt the peace and harmony of others.

l: raise an army and mobilize the masses
m: To make a big fuss or deploy large resources for something that may not warrant such a large-scale response.
s: When your parents call all the relatives over just to help you move a single box. When a company sends ten people to fix a minor computer problem. When someone organizes an elaborate plan just to accomplish a simple task.

l: raise troops and question the crime
m: to mobilize forces or make a serious confrontation in order to demand an account from someone for their wrongdoing.
s: When a company discovers that a partner has been cheating them and decides to launch a formal investigation and demand compensation. When a parent finds out their child has been lying repeatedly and calls a serious family meeting to address the dishonesty directly.

m: To be in high spirits and full of enthusiasm or excitement about something.
s: When someone arrives at a party eager to have a great time and ready to enjoy every moment. When a child wakes up on their birthday morning full of anticipation and joy for the day ahead.

m: To deliberately stir up trouble, create chaos, or incite conflict for one's own purposes.
s: When a politician makes inflammatory statements to divide people and gain support. When someone spreads rumors or gossip to cause arguments between friends. When an agitator deliberately provokes confrontation to create social unrest.

m: To be in a state of great happiness, excitement, and enthusiasm about something.
s: When someone gets an acceptance letter from their dream school and can't stop smiling all day. When a group of friends is heading to an amusement park and everyone is bouncing with excitement on the way there.

l: soldiers do not tire of deception
m: In military strategy, the use of deception and cunning tactics is not only acceptable but necessary to achieve victory.
s: When a military commander uses clever tactics to mislead the enemy about troop positions. When someone argues that any strategy is fair game in competition or conflict, as long as it achieves the objective.

l: soldiers without blood on their blades
m: to achieve victory or success without any violence, conflict, or loss of life.
s: When a company successfully acquires a competitor through negotiation instead of a hostile takeover. When a leader resolves a dispute between two groups through dialogue and compromise rather than confrontation.

l: soldiers arrive at the city gates
m: An enemy force has reached the gates of a city and is about to attack or has already begun a siege, representing an imminent or critical threat.
s: When a company is on the brink of bankruptcy and creditors are demanding payment immediately. When a student hasn't studied at all and the final exam is starting tomorrow. When a country faces an invasion and enemy troops have already crossed the border.

m: A military force that is powerful, well-equipped, and prepared for battle.
s: When describing a country with a formidable military that is ready for war. When talking about a sports team that has recruited top players and looks unstoppable in the upcoming season.

l: soldiers and weapons confronting each other
m: Two parties resort to armed conflict or warfare to resolve their dispute instead of peaceful negotiation.
s: When two countries have exhausted diplomatic talks and finally declare war on each other. When rival gangs stop talking and start fighting in the streets. When a long-standing political conflict finally escalates into military violence.

m: A time of widespread chaos and upheaval caused by warfare, invasion, or major social disorder.
s: When a country is experiencing war or invasion and everything becomes chaotic and dangerous. When someone describes a period in history when society completely broke down due to military conflict and lawlessness.

l: In military affairs, speed is valued as supernatural
m: In warfare and competition, swift action and quick decision-making are the most critical factors for success.
s: When a company launches a new product before competitors to dominate the market. When a sports team executes a fast-paced strategy to catch opponents off guard. When someone acts quickly to seize an opportunity before others realize it exists.

m: Wars and disasters follow one another in continuous succession, creating an endless cycle of suffering and calamity.
s: When a country experiences prolonged conflict that triggers economic collapse and humanitarian crises. When one major disaster leads to another, creating a domino effect of problems that seem endless.

m: An activity or experience brings endless happiness and enjoyment that cannot be measured or exhausted.
s: When someone is absorbed in a hobby they love and can do it for hours without getting bored. When a group of friends hangs out together and keeps laughing and having fun with no end in sight.

l: its momentum is fierce and violent
m: The situation or force has become extremely threatening and aggressive, advancing with overwhelming power that is difficult to stop.
s: When a competitor launches an aggressive campaign that seems unstoppable. When a storm or natural disaster approaches with terrifying intensity. When an opponent or rival comes at you with overwhelming force and intensity.

m: Something provides endless satisfaction, enjoyment, or interest that never gets old or exhausted.
s: When you keep enjoying a book or movie even after reading or watching it multiple times. When someone finds a hobby or activity so engaging that they never get tired of it, like a musician who practices the same piece thousands of times but still finds new meaning in it.

m: Someone has an unattractive or unremarkable physical appearance that does not inspire admiration or respect.
s: When you meet someone who looks ordinary or plain at first glance, but turns out to be talented or accomplished. When describing someone whose appearance doesn't match their abilities or status.

m: Something that is small in scale but contains all the essential details and characteristics of a larger whole, serving as a perfect miniature representation.
s: When a small village reflects all the characteristics and problems of an entire nation. When a single family dispute exemplifies the complexities of broader social issues.

l: Nurture honor and dwell in comfort
m: To live a life of ease and luxury, enjoying privileged circumstances without hardship or struggle.
s: When someone has grown up wealthy and sheltered, never having to work hard or face difficulties. When a person who was born into privilege seems out of touch with how ordinary people live and struggle.

l: nourish a canker and leave behind trouble
m: By tolerating or ignoring a small problem, you allow it to grow into a much larger and more serious problem.
s: When a manager ignores an employee's minor misconduct, only to have it escalate into major workplace issues later. When parents fail to discipline a child's bad behavior early on, and it develops into serious problems as the child grows older.

m: To conserve one's energy and strength in preparation for a crucial moment or challenge ahead.
s: When an athlete rests and trains carefully before a big competition to be at their best. When a company saves resources and avoids unnecessary spending to be ready for a major business opportunity or market challenge.

l: Nurture a tiger and leave behind trouble
m: By being lenient or generous with someone dangerous, you create serious problems for yourself in the future.
s: When a company keeps an untrustworthy employee around hoping they'll change, only to have that person sabotage the business later. When a parent gives in to a child's every demand without discipline, and the child grows up to be ungrateful and causes harm to the family.

p: jiān tīng zé míng ， piān xìn zé àn
l: Listening to all sides brings clarity, favoring one side brings blindness
m: When you consider multiple perspectives and viewpoints, you gain a clear understanding, but if you only listen to one side, you become ignorant and misjudge the situation.
s: When making a big decision like hiring someone or buying a house, you should gather opinions from different people rather than relying on just one person's advice. When a company only listens to one department's feedback and ignores others, they often make poor strategic decisions.

m: To be inclusive and open-minded by accepting or accommodating diverse ideas, perspectives, or things without discrimination.
s: When a company values employees from all backgrounds and creates a workplace where different viewpoints are welcomed. When a teacher designs a curriculum that incorporates multiple teaching methods and learning styles to support all students.

m: To embrace and integrate diverse ideas, styles, or traditions without discrimination or conflict.
s: When a chef combines techniques from multiple culinary traditions in one dish. When a designer blends classical and contemporary elements into a cohesive style. When a musician incorporates influences from different genres to create something unique.

m: To be in a difficult situation with problems coming from both internal and external sources simultaneously.
s: When a company is struggling with internal conflicts between departments while also facing tough competition from rivals. When a person is dealing with personal health issues at the same time their business is failing due to market conditions.

m: A state of crisis where an organization or country faces serious problems from both internal conflicts and external enemies simultaneously.
s: When a company is dealing with employee strikes while also losing market share to competitors. When a country is experiencing political division while being threatened by hostile neighbors. When a team has internal disagreements between players while also facing a much stronger opponent.

l: again and again and again and again
m: Something is repeated many times; done over and over with great frequency and persistence.
s: When a teacher has to explain the same concept to a student multiple times. When you keep asking someone to do something and they still won't listen. When a boss repeatedly reminds employees about the same rule because they keep breaking it.

m: Continue making progress with renewed effort and determination, refusing to rest on past achievements.
s: When a student does well on one exam and decides to work even harder for the next one. When a sports team wins a game but knows they need to keep improving to win the championship. When someone achieves a goal and immediately sets their sights on the next challenge without becoming complacent.

m: After initial effort or momentum fades, continued decline leads to complete exhaustion and failure.
s: When a sports team loses momentum after their first failed attempt and then keeps losing, getting progressively weaker. When someone tries to pursue a goal, fails once, and then loses all motivation and energy to try again. When a business starts strong but after the first setback, continuously deteriorates until it collapses.

l: assume a false name and take someone's place
m: To fraudulently impersonate someone else or use another person's identity to gain unauthorized benefits or advantages.
s: When someone uses a fake ID to get into a restricted area. When a student submits another person's work as their own to get credit. When someone pretends to be a doctor or professional they are not qualified to be in order to deceive others.

p: mào tiān xià zhī dà bù wěi
l: Risk committing the greatest wrongdoing under heaven
m: To do something extremely wrong or immoral that goes against the principles and conscience of the entire world.
s: When someone commits an act so heinous and universally condemned that it shocks everyone's moral sensibilities. When a leader makes a decision so corrupt and unjust that it violates basic human ethics and angers the general population.

m: Excessive or unnecessary words that add nothing to the meaning and make writing or speech tedious and hard to follow.
s: When someone writes a long email that could have been said in two sentences. When a speaker keeps repeating the same point over and over in different ways instead of getting to the point.

m: Something that appears grand, dignified, and legitimate on the surface but is actually false, deceptive, or used to cover up improper motives.
s: When a company uses flowery language and noble-sounding principles in their marketing while actually engaging in unethical practices. When a politician justifies a self-serving decision with high-minded rhetoric that sounds impressive but doesn't hold up to scrutiny.

m: It is inevitable that enemies or people who dislike each other will encounter one another, often unexpectedly and at inconvenient times.
s: When you run into someone you had a big fight with at the grocery store. When two rival coworkers who hate each other end up on the same project team and have to work together.

m: To think hard and long about something, often with difficulty and exhaustion, while trying to solve a problem or understand something.
s: When you're stuck on a difficult math problem and have been thinking about it for hours without making progress. When someone is trying to remember a name they forgot and keeps concentrating intensely but can't quite recall it.

m: Someone who is willfully ignorant and refuses to understand or accept the truth despite repeated attempts to help them.
s: When someone keeps rejecting good advice and insists on doing things the wrong way. When a person refuses to learn from their mistakes or understand obvious facts that everyone else sees clearly.

p: bīng dòng sān chǐ ， fēi yī rì zhī hán
l: Ice three feet thick does not freeze in a single day of cold
m: Serious problems or negative situations develop gradually over a long time and cannot be solved quickly or easily.
s: When a company's financial troubles didn't happen overnight but accumulated due to years of poor management. When someone's health problems developed slowly over time due to long-term bad habits rather than a sudden illness.

m: An extremely cold environment where everything is covered in ice and snow, often used to describe harsh winter conditions or difficult circumstances.
s: When describing a brutally cold winter day where snow blankets the entire landscape. When someone is enduring difficult hardships or a very tough situation that feels isolating and harsh.

m: When a conflict or tension between people suddenly disappears or resolves completely, often due to a change in circumstances or attitude.
s: When two people who were in a serious argument suddenly become friendly again after talking things out. When a tense situation at work suddenly becomes relaxed after a misunderstanding is cleared up.

m: Two things or people are fundamentally incompatible and cannot exist together peacefully.
s: When two coworkers have completely opposite personalities and values, making it impossible for them to work together effectively. When someone tries to mix two ideologies or systems that are inherently contradictory and destined to conflict.

l: charge forward and break through formations
m: To be the first to advance into battle or to take the lead in a dangerous or difficult undertaking.
s: When a team leader volunteers to tackle the hardest problem first to set an example. When someone rushes in to help during a crisis before anyone else steps up. When an employee takes on the most challenging client or project to support the company.

m: To compete or fight to determine who is superior or who will prevail between two rivals.
s: When two competitors want to have a final match to settle once and for all who is better. When rivals agree to have one decisive battle or contest to determine the ultimate winner.

m: To mock and criticize someone with a combination of cutting remarks and bitter sarcasm, often alternating between subtle jabs and overt contempt.
s: When coworkers constantly make snide comments and sarcastic jokes about someone's work or appearance. When people respond to someone's failure with a mixture of subtle mockery and sharp, cutting remarks rather than genuine help or sympathy.

m: to observe a situation without getting involved or offering help, remaining detached and uninvested in the outcome.
s: When your coworkers are arguing but you decide not to intervene and just watch from a distance. When a friend is making a bad decision and you choose not to say anything, just observing what happens without taking sides.

m: To be extremely unfriendly, distant, or emotionally unresponsive in one's demeanor or attitude toward others.
s: When someone greets you with a completely blank expression and won't smile or engage in conversation. When a person treats you with obvious coldness and keeps their distance because they're upset with you or don't like you.

m: unkind, sarcastic, or dismissive remarks intended to hurt or belittle someone.
s: When a coworker constantly makes snide comments about your work or appearance. When someone responds to your ideas with mocking or contemptuous remarks instead of genuine feedback.

m: A harsh, desolate, and miserable environment or circumstances that cause suffering and despair.
s: When describing someone going through a very difficult period in their life with constant hardship and bad luck. When you want to convey that someone is facing overwhelming adversity and bleakness in their situation.

p: fán shì yù zé lì ， bù yù zé fèi
l: In all matters, those who plan will succeed, those who do not plan will fail.
m: Careful planning and preparation are essential for success in any endeavor, while lack of foresight and planning inevitably leads to failure.
s: When someone wants to start a business but hasn't thought through the details or made any plans. When a student refuses to study or prepare for an important exam and then fails. When a company launches a product without doing market research or considering potential problems.

m: Something extremely rare and precious, occurring so seldom that it is almost impossible to find.
s: When describing a person with extraordinary talent or ability that is almost never seen. When talking about a product or opportunity that is so rare it's almost impossible to obtain. When someone finds an item or person of exceptional quality that surpasses all others.

m: To come back home victoriously after achieving success or winning a battle.
s: When a sports team wins a championship and comes back to their hometown for a celebration parade. When a soldier returns home after successfully completing a military campaign. When someone accomplishes a major goal and returns to show their success to family and friends.

m: A situation is far more likely to end badly than well; the outlook is grim and dangerous.
s: When a sick person's condition is rapidly deteriorating and doctors say recovery is unlikely. When someone gets into serious legal trouble and their lawyer says the case looks very difficult to win. When a risky business venture has encountered multiple major problems in quick succession.

m: Someone's cruel, evil, or malicious true nature becomes completely exposed and undeniable.
s: When a seemingly kind person suddenly acts violently and shows their true aggressive nature. When a politician who portrayed themselves as trustworthy is caught in a major corruption scandal and their real intentions become clear to everyone.

m: Someone who appears extremely fierce, menacing, or evil in appearance and demeanor.
s: When someone has a very intimidating look or aggressive expression that makes others fear them. When describing a person with a scary, angry appearance who seems dangerous or villainous.

m: To behave inappropriately in public and become a laughingstock or source of embarrassment.
s: When someone gets drunk at a formal event and starts acting foolishly in front of important people. When a person tries to show off a skill they don't actually have and fails miserably in front of an audience.

m: To stand out from others and achieve prominence or success that surpasses your peers.
s: When someone works hard and becomes more successful than their classmates or colleagues. When a person distinguishes themselves through their talents and accomplishments, becoming notably better than average.

m: Something happens in a way that is completely unexpected and surprises everyone, going far beyond what people anticipated.
s: When an underdog team suddenly wins the championship against all odds. When a shy person gives an amazing presentation that impresses the whole audience. When a product launches with features that nobody predicted the company would include.

m: To achieve success by doing something surprising or unexpected that catches others off guard.
s: When a sports team wins by executing a completely unexpected strategy that their opponents didn't prepare for. When someone succeeds by taking an unconventional approach that nobody saw coming. When a company gains market advantage by launching a product feature that competitors weren't anticipating.

m: To speak eloquently and fluently, with words flowing naturally in well-organized and polished phrases.
s: When someone gives a speech and everything they say sounds perfectly articulated and well-structured without any hesitation. When a colleague can speak on any topic at length with impressive eloquence and perfect organization.

l: stick out one's head and show one's face
m: to gain public recognition or prominence by stepping into the spotlight and becoming visible to others.
s: When someone finally gets their chance to be noticed after working hard in the background. When a talented person decides to stop hiding their abilities and let others see what they can do. When someone takes on a leadership role or public position after being unknown.

l: use the unusual to achieve victory
