m: Win by employing unexpected or unconventional tactics that take your opponent by surprise.
s: When a sports team wins by using an unusual play that nobody expected. When someone solves a difficult problem by thinking outside the box in a way that catches everyone off guard. When a business succeeds by adopting a unique strategy that competitors didn't anticipate.

m: To say one thing and then do the opposite; to break one's word or promise.
s: When someone agrees to help you with a project but then backs out at the last minute. When a politician makes campaign promises but does the complete opposite once elected. When a friend promises to keep your secret but then tells everyone.

m: Someone or something appears and disappears unpredictably, with no consistent pattern or schedule.
s: When a coworker shows up to the office at random times without any set schedule. When a friend is unreliable about when they'll respond to messages or visit. When a ghost or supernatural phenomenon is said to appear at unpredictable moments.

m: To face extreme danger and risk one's life without hesitation in service of a cause or duty.
s: When a soldier charges into battle knowing they might not return. When a firefighter runs into a burning building to save someone. When someone makes a dangerous sacrifice to protect their country or loved ones.

l: emerge from the divine and enter into transformation
m: To reach such a high level of skill or artistry that one's work appears magical, supernatural, or beyond human capability.
s: When a musician plays so beautifully that listeners are completely mesmerized and forget the world around them. When a chef's cooking is so exquisite that people can't believe a human made it. When an athlete performs with such grace and precision that their movements seem almost otherworldly.

l: emerge from the class and stand out from the crowd
m: To be exceptionally superior and stand out distinctly above others in ability, talent, or achievement.
s: When a student consistently gets the highest grades in their class and is clearly more brilliant than their peers. When an athlete performs at an elite level and is noticeably better than everyone else on the team. When a colleague at work is so skilled and talented that they immediately stand out as exceptional compared to their coworkers.

m: To speak in a rude, disrespectful, or insulting manner without proper courtesy or deference.

s: When someone acts nice to your face but you suspect they have bad intentions behind the scenes. When a coworker seems cooperative but you discover they were secretly undermining your project the whole time.

m: Something that was supposed to happen or exist completely disappears or fails to materialize, often despite effort or expectation.
s: When someone's hard work on a project gets deleted and all their effort vanishes. When plans for a vacation fall through at the last moment and everything you prepared for comes to nothing. When a business investment fails and all the money invested disappears without result.

m: Something is completely destroyed, ruined, or lost beyond recovery.
s: When a house burns down and is completely destroyed. When someone's dreams or hopes are completely shattered and there's nothing left. When a business fails completely and ceases to exist.

m: To break down a large task or problem into smaller, more manageable pieces.
s: When you have a huge project and need to divide it into smaller steps to make progress. When a manager breaks down a company-wide initiative into individual team assignments so everyone knows what to do.

m: To skillfully turn a dangerous or critical situation into a safe and peaceful one through quick thinking or decisive action.
s: When a driver swerves at the last second to avoid a serious accident. When a business leader makes a tough decision that saves the company from bankruptcy. When someone talks their way out of a dangerous confrontation.

m: Something so strange, unusual, or incomprehensible that it defies normal understanding and belief.
s: When someone does something completely bizarre and illogical that you can't explain. When you hear a story so strange and unbelievable that it seems impossible or insane.

l: the courage of a common man
m: Reckless or foolish bravery that lacks wisdom, strategy, or consideration of consequences.
s: When someone charges into a dangerous situation without thinking it through. When a person uses physical force to solve a problem instead of using their brain or getting help from others.

m: Every individual, regardless of their status or position, bears a responsibility to contribute to the welfare of society and the nation.
s: When discussing how ordinary citizens should participate in environmental protection or community service. When encouraging someone to take action on social issues even though they're not in a position of power. When explaining that you don't need to be a leader or official to make a positive difference in the world.

m: To hide oneself completely and move about without being seen or noticed by others.
s: When someone sneaks around trying not to be detected. When a person deliberately avoids attention and keeps to themselves to avoid being recognized or followed.

m: An extremely urgent and critical situation that requires immediate action without any delay.
s: When a hospital patient needs emergency surgery right now. When a company's main server crashes during their biggest sales day and needs to be fixed immediately. When someone's house is on fire and the fire department needs to arrive as fast as possible.

m: Something that is absolutely perfect with no flaws or shortcomings whatsoever.
s: When describing an ideal product or service that exceeds all expectations in every way. When praising someone's performance or accomplishment as flawless and leaving nothing to be desired.

l: nine houses in ten are empty
m: A place or region is severely depopulated and desolate, with most buildings and homes abandoned.
s: When describing a ghost town or abandoned neighborhood where most people have moved away. When talking about how a once-thriving area has become nearly deserted due to economic decline or disaster.

l: ten years of cold study at the window
m: This idiom refers to the long and difficult years of dedicated study required to achieve academic success, particularly in preparation for important exams.
s: When describing a student who has spent many years studying hard to pass a difficult examination like the college entrance exam. When talking about someone who sacrificed comfort and leisure for years to master a skill or achieve their educational goals.

p: shí nián shù mù ， bǎi nián shù rén
l: Ten years grow trees, one hundred years nurture people
m: Educating and developing a person takes much longer and requires far more effort than growing a tree, emphasizing that human development is a long-term endeavor requiring patience and sustained investment.
s: When discussing why education systems need long-term funding and shouldn't expect quick results. When a teacher explains to parents why raising children well takes decades of consistent effort, not just a few years of schooling. When a government official argues for multi-generational plans to improve society rather than quick fixes.

m: A person has committed such heinous and unforgivable crimes that they deserve the severest punishment and have no hope of redemption.
s: When someone has committed extremely serious crimes like murder or treason and people believe they should receive the death penalty. When describing a criminal whose actions are so evil that society considers them beyond any possibility of forgiveness or rehabilitation.

l: ten parts grasped, nine parts stable
m: Something is almost certain to succeed or be achieved with very high confidence.
s: When you're almost guaranteed to win a competition because you're clearly the best candidate. When a deal is practically done and just needs final paperwork. When you're so well-prepared for an exam that you're confident you'll pass.

p: shí mù suǒ shì ， shí shǒu suǒ zhǐ
l: Ten eyes see it, ten hands point at it
m: When someone's actions are exposed to public scrutiny, they become the focus of widespread attention and criticism.
s: When a public figure makes a mistake and suddenly everyone is talking about them and judging them. When someone gets caught doing something wrong and becomes the target of public disapproval and mockery.

l: thousand threads and ten thousand strands
m: To be closely connected or deeply intertwined with someone or something in many subtle and complex ways.
s: When two friends have known each other since childhood and share countless memories and inside jokes that bind them together. When a company's business practices are deeply connected to and dependent on multiple suppliers and partners in intricate ways.

l: a thousand armies and ten thousand horses
m: An enormous, overwhelming military force or a massive, unstoppable power or momentum.
s: When a large crowd of people rushes toward something with great force and energy. When a company launches a massive marketing campaign that reaches millions of people. When describing the overwhelming power of a natural disaster or movement that cannot be stopped.

l: a thousand changes and ten thousand transformations
m: Something that constantly changes and transforms in countless ways, showing great variety and unpredictability.
s: When describing how fashion trends keep evolving every season. When talking about how weather patterns shift dramatically throughout the year. When explaining how a skilled actor can portray completely different characters in different roles.

l: strange tale of a thousand ages
m: An extraordinary or unusual story that is remarkable and talked about throughout history.
s: When someone tells an incredible or bizarre story that seems unbelievable and shocking. When a historical event is so unusual that people still talk about it centuries later.

m: To be the target of widespread public condemnation and scorn from many people.
s: When a public figure does something shameful and everyone criticizes them harshly. When someone's wrongdoing becomes widely known and they face criticism from all sides of society.

l: a thousand heads and ten thousand threads
m: A situation that is extremely complex and chaotic with many interconnected problems or tasks that are difficult to organize or prioritize.
s: When you first take over a messy project with numerous unresolved issues and don't know where to start. When your desk is covered with a pile of unfinished work, urgent emails, and tasks all demanding attention at once.

m: An extremely wide variety of strange, bizarre, or unusual things that are difficult to categorize or predict.
s: When you visit a museum with a collection of unusual artifacts from different cultures and time periods. When browsing the internet and encountering all sorts of weird trends, memes, and subcultures you never knew existed. When describing how diverse and unpredictable human behavior can be in crowded public spaces.

l: a thousand mountains and ten thousand waters
m: Great distance or vast geographical separation, often used to describe the difficulty of traveling or the vastness of the space between two places.
s: When lovers are separated by great distance and find it hard to be together. When describing how far apart two countries or cities are from each other. When someone has to travel through difficult terrain to reach a destination.

m: Things vary greatly and differ widely from one another in many different ways.
s: When describing how different people's tastes in music are from each other. When explaining why there's such a wide variety of architectural styles across different neighborhoods. When noting how students in a class have vastly different learning abilities and interests.

l: a thousand methods and hundred strategies
m: To try every possible means and method, using all available ways to achieve a goal or solve a problem.
s: When someone is determined to find a solution no matter what obstacles they face. When a person uses every trick and technique they can think of to accomplish something difficult. When describing someone who will do whatever it takes to get what they want.

m: Something is absolutely certain and verified beyond any doubt.
s: When you want to convince someone that what you're saying is completely true and not exaggerated. When you've checked something multiple times and can guarantee it's accurate.

l: a thousand autumns ten thousand generations
m: referring to an extremely long period of time spanning countless generations far into the future; eternity or the indefinite future.
s: When someone talks about wanting their family name to be remembered forever. When a leader hopes their accomplishments will be celebrated for all time. When discussing the long-term legacy of a great work or monument.

l: a thousand compositions in one rule
m: Everything is monotonously identical with no variation or originality.
s: When you visit a new shopping mall but all the stores are the same chains you've seen everywhere else. When a student writes essays that sound exactly like every other student's essay, with no original thoughts or unique voice.

l: A thousand worries yield one gain
m: After much deliberation and effort, one finally arrives at a single useful idea or insight worth keeping.
s: When someone spends hours brainstorming and finally comes up with one good suggestion that makes everything click. When a writer struggles through many drafts but eventually discovers one perfect sentence that captures their idea.

l: thousand words and ten thousand speech
m: An overwhelming surge of emotions or thoughts that are difficult to express in words.
s: When you see a loved one after a long time and don't know where to begin expressing how much you missed them. When someone has so many feelings about a situation that they struggle to put it all into words.

m: An extremely rare opportunity or occurrence that may only happen once in a very long time.
s: When you encounter a once-in-a-lifetime chance that you shouldn't miss. When something incredibly rare and valuable appears unexpectedly, like meeting someone famous or getting an amazing job opportunity that won't come around again.

l: A thousand years hard to encounter
m: An extremely rare opportunity or event that may only happen once in a thousand years.
s: When you meet someone famous you've always admired by pure chance. When you finally get the opportunity to travel somewhere you've dreamed about your whole life. When two old friends randomly run into each other after decades of being apart.

l: thousand hardships and ten thousand bitterness
m: Having endured countless hardships and difficulties to achieve something, often suggesting the effort was worthwhile despite the struggle.
s: When someone finally graduates after years of studying while working multiple jobs. When a couple finally saves enough money to buy their first home after years of sacrifice and struggle.

p: qiān lǐ zhī dī ， kuì yú yǐ xué
l: A levee of a thousand leagues collapses from an ant's hole
m: Small, seemingly insignificant problems that are ignored or neglected can eventually lead to catastrophic failure or disaster.
s: When a company ignores minor safety violations and they eventually cause a major accident. When someone doesn't address a small crack in their foundation and it grows into structural damage that makes the house uninhabitable. When a relationship falls apart because neither person addresses small conflicts and resentments that keep building up over time.

p: qiān lǐ zhī xíng ， shǐ yú zú xià
l: A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step
m: Every great accomplishment starts with a small first action; you must begin somewhere to achieve any large goal.
s: When someone is overwhelmed by a big project and doesn't know where to start, you remind them they just need to take the first step. When encouraging a friend to begin learning a new skill or language, even though it seems like a huge task ahead of them.

l: a thousand miles far and distant
m: A great distance away; traveling from very far away.
s: When someone travels a very long way to visit you, and you want to acknowledge the effort and distance they covered. When describing how far apart two places are, emphasizing the difficulty of the journey between them.

l: A goose feather sent from a thousand miles away
m: A small or humble gift given with sincere affection is more valuable than its material worth, emphasizing that the thought and effort behind a gift matter more than the gift itself.
s: When someone gives you a modest present but you know they went out of their way to find it or spent considerable time thinking about you. When a friend sends you a small handmade item from far away and the gesture touches your heart more than an expensive gift from someone nearby would.

m: An extremely heavy burden or responsibility that is almost unbearable to carry.
s: When someone is given so much work or responsibility that they feel completely overwhelmed. When a person is carrying emotional weight from difficult family circumstances that makes every day feel exhausting.

l: a thousand hammers and hundred refinements
m: Something that has been perfected through countless rounds of hard work, practice, and refinement.
s: When describing a musician who has practiced the same piece thousands of times until it's flawless. When talking about how a successful athlete's skills were built through years of relentless training and improvement.

l: a thousand difficulties and ten thousand dangers
m: To face an overwhelming number of severe obstacles, hardships, and life-threatening challenges.
s: When someone overcomes an extremely challenging journey or mission with many life-threatening obstacles. When describing a difficult historical period where a country faced constant warfare, famine, and disaster. When someone perseveres through countless setbacks and dangerous situations to achieve their goal.

l: ascend the hall and enter the chamber
m: to reach a high level of mastery or achievement in a skill or field of study.
s: When someone has practiced an instrument for years and finally performs at a professional level. When a student goes from struggling with a subject to becoming one of the top performers in the class. When an apprentice has trained so long under a master that they can now work independently and produce excellent results.

l: ascend in office and gain wealth
m: To achieve promotion in one's career and accumulate financial fortune, often representing worldly success and prosperity.
s: When someone gets a promotion at work and also receives a significant bonus or pay raise. When a person pursues career advancement specifically because they want to become both powerful and rich. When colleagues gossip about a successful executive who has climbed the corporate ladder and built considerable wealth.

m: To be uncertain and skeptical about something, neither fully believing nor fully disbelieving it.
s: When someone tells you an incredible story and you're not sure whether to trust them or not. When you receive a job offer that sounds too good to be true and you're unsure if it's legitimate. When a friend claims they saw a celebrity but you're not entirely convinced it actually happened.

l: half the territory of the realm
m: A significant portion of power, territory, or resources, typically referring to losing or controlling about half of what one previously possessed.
s: When a business loses half its market share to competitors. When a political party wins only half the seats in parliament that it used to control. When someone's influence or possessions are reduced to roughly half their former extent.

m: to pretend to resist while actually being willing, showing coy or reluctant acceptance despite outward hesitation.
s: When someone says they don't want to go to a party but clearly hopes you'll convince them to come along. When a friend acts like they don't want your help but immediately accepts it anyway. When someone pretends to decline an invitation but their body language shows they really want to accept.

l: half a catty and eight taels
m: Two people or things are equally matched in ability, merit, or fault, with neither being noticeably better or worse than the other.
s: When comparing two mediocre students and they're both equally bad at math. When two coworkers are both making similar mistakes or producing similar quality work.

l: leave home halfway through the journey
m: To take up a profession or skill later in life without proper foundational training or experience in that field.
s: When someone switches careers to become a doctor in their 40s without any medical background. When a person who never studied music suddenly decides to become a professional musician. When someone with no accounting experience gets hired for a finance job because they know the right people.

m: To give up on something before completing it; to fail to see a task through to the end.
s: When someone starts a project with enthusiasm but loses interest and never finishes it. When a student begins studying for an exam but gives up halfway through the material. When someone quits their job without finding another one or completing their responsibilities.

m: Something that appears attractive or impressive on the surface but lacks real value, substance, or practical utility.
s: When a company has fancy marketing and a sleek website but offers poor quality products. When someone dresses very expensively and talks impressively but has no real skills or knowledge to back it up. When a building looks grand and impressive from outside but is poorly constructed inside.

l: bow low and bend the knee
m: To act in an excessively servile or obsequious manner, showing complete submission and loss of dignity to someone in power.
s: When someone constantly flatters their boss and agrees with everything they say just to get ahead. When a person abandons their principles and self-respect to please someone they fear or want something from.

m: Morally corrupt and despicably dishonest in one's actions and character.
s: When someone uses underhanded tricks to win a competition or takes credit for another person's work. When a politician spreads lies and uses dirty tactics to gain power.

l: outstanding and not in a group
m: To be exceptionally superior and distinctly different from others, standing alone in excellence.
s: When someone has clearly superior talents or abilities compared to their peers. When a student consistently outperforms everyone else in the class and stands out from the rest.

m: To achieve significant and effective results through one's efforts or work.
s: When a company's new marketing strategy leads to a substantial increase in sales. When a student's dedicated studying results in a dramatic improvement in their test scores. When a community program produces meaningful and tangible benefits for its participants.

m: to go straight to the point without any preliminaries or beating around the bush.
s: When someone cuts through all the small talk and gets right to the main issue. When a doctor tells you directly what's wrong without explaining everything else first. When your boss skips the pleasantries and immediately tells you why they called the meeting.

m: to act alone without help or support, relying entirely on one's own efforts.
s: When someone starts a new business by themselves without partners or investors. When a person tries to solve a difficult problem without asking anyone for help or assistance.

l: sell the sword and buy the ox
m: To abandon military pursuits and turn to peaceful agricultural life; to exchange warfare for peaceful pursuits.
s: When a soldier retires from the army and becomes a farmer. When someone leaves a violent or aggressive lifestyle to pursue a peaceful, productive career. When a person gives up conflict and chooses to focus on building a stable, peaceful life instead.

l: sell one's body and pledge allegiance
m: To abandon one's principles and independence by submitting to or serving someone powerful, usually for personal gain or survival.
s: When someone compromises their values to gain favor with an influential person or organization. When an employee stays silent about unethical practices at work just to keep their job and paycheck. When a person makes a deal with someone corrupt just to get ahead financially.

m: To engage in constant warfare across many regions, experiencing numerous battles and military campaigns over a wide area.
s: When describing a general or soldier who has fought in many different places and wars throughout their career. When talking about a company that has expanded its operations to many different regions and faced constant challenges everywhere it goes.

l: a dream of the southern branch
m: A pleasant but brief experience or success that turns out to be illusory or temporary, like waking from a dream.
s: When someone gets caught up in an unrealistic fantasy about their future that doesn't come true. When a business opportunity seems promising but suddenly falls through, leaving you wondering if it was ever real. When you look back on a past romance and realize it feels like it never really happened.

m: a mixture of different regional dialects or accents blended together in someone's speech.
s: When someone who grew up moving between different regions speaks with a blend of multiple accents. When a person's speech combines features from both northern and southern Chinese dialects because they lived in both places.

l: heading south while the cart goes north
m: pursuing actions that directly contradict your stated goals or desired outcome.
s: When someone says they want to save money but keeps spending recklessly. When a company claims to prioritize customer service but implements policies that frustrate customers. When a student says they want better grades but refuses to study or attend class.

l: extensively learned in antiquity and thoroughly versed in the present
m: To possess deep and comprehensive knowledge of both ancient history and contemporary affairs.
s: When someone can discuss historical events in detail and also understands current issues well. When a teacher or scholar demonstrates expertise spanning from classical literature to modern science.

m: A person who has extensive knowledge across many fields and possesses multiple skills or talents.
s: When describing someone like a Renaissance person who is knowledgeable in literature, science, and art all at once. When you meet someone who seems to know something about everything and can do many things well.

m: To have wide-ranging knowledge or skills across many areas without developing deep expertise or mastery in any particular one.
s: When someone knows a little bit about everything but isn't really an expert at anything. When a student tries to study too many subjects at once and doesn't master any of them properly.

m: Someone who has broad learning and excellent ability to remember what they have learned.
s: When describing a scholar or academic who seems to know facts about many different subjects and can recall them easily. When praising a colleague who attends one training session and remembers all the details without needing to take notes.

l: sleep on firewood and taste gall
m: To endure hardship and humiliation with patience and determination in order to achieve a long-term goal or seek revenge.
s: When someone goes through years of difficult training or sacrifice to eventually achieve their dreams. When a person humbly accepts a setback but quietly works toward vindication or success later.

l: danger is at dawn and dusk
m: Someone or something is in extreme danger and could be lost at any moment.
s: When a patient's condition is critical and doctors say they may not survive the night. When a company is on the brink of bankruptcy and could collapse any day. When a relationship is so strained that breaking up could happen imminently.

m: A situation is extremely precarious and could collapse or fail at any moment, like a stack of eggs that is one wrong move away from disaster.
s: When a company is on the brink of bankruptcy and could go under any day. When a peace treaty is so fragile that the slightest disagreement could spark war again. When someone's job is so unstable that they could be fired at any time.

l: danger lurks on all four sides
m: Danger and threats are present everywhere, ready to emerge at any moment.
s: When a company is facing multiple serious problems at once and nobody knows which crisis will hit first. When traveling through a war-torn region where threats could come from any direction.

m: To deliberately use exaggerated or shocking language to frighten people and grab their attention, often without factual basis.
s: When a news headline uses extreme language to make a story sound more dramatic than it actually is. When someone spreads scary rumors or predictions just to get attention from others.

m: It would be impolite or disrespectful to decline or reject something that has been offered to you.
s: When someone offers you a gift or invitation and you feel you must accept it even though you might prefer not to, because turning it down would seem rude. When you're presented with an honor or opportunity and feel obligated to accept out of politeness.

c: 却以其人之道，还治其人之身
p: què yǐ qí rén zhī dào ， hái zhì qí rén zhī shēn
l: use that person's own method to return treatment to that person's body
m: to defeat someone by using the same tactics or methods they used against you.
s: When someone tries to trick you but you use their own trick against them to outsmart them. When a bully gets bullied using the same tactics they use on others. When someone spreads rumors and ends up being hurt by the same rumors spread about them.

l: roll up the earth and come again
m: To make a comeback or return to power with renewed strength after a defeat or setback.
s: When a sports team loses badly but trains hard and comes back to win the championship next season. When a company goes bankrupt but the founder starts a new successful business years later. When someone fails an exam but studies intensely and passes with flying colors on the next attempt.

l: unload the millstone and slaughter the donkey
m: To discard or betray someone after they have served their purpose and are no longer useful.
s: When an employer fires a loyal worker immediately after a major project is completed. When a politician abandons their supporters once they've won the election and no longer needs their votes.

m: Memories or images are so clear and vivid that they seem to be right in front of you as if happening in the present moment.
s: When you remember a childhood event so clearly that you can almost see it happening again. When someone recalls a traumatic or joyful experience and can describe every detail as if it just occurred.

l: treat this one thickly and that one thinly
m: To treat one person or group with favoritism while treating another with neglect or indifference.
s: When a parent gives expensive gifts to one child but minimal gifts to another. When a manager praises and rewards one employee's work while ignoring the equally good contributions of another colleague. When a school provides better resources and opportunities to certain students while neglecting others.

m: Complete lack of shame or conscience; acting with brazen audacity and total disregard for propriety or decency.
s: When someone does something obviously wrong and then acts like nothing happened without any embarrassment. When a person lies directly to your face and shows absolutely no remorse or awkwardness about being caught.

m: A dangerous situation that appears stable on the surface but contains hidden threats ready to explode at any moment.
s: When a company has serious internal conflicts that haven't been addressed and could cause a sudden collapse. When a relationship has unresolved resentments building up that could lead to a sudden breakup.

m: In a complete and unaltered form, preserving all original details and characteristics without any changes or omissions.
s: When you want someone to tell you the whole story of what happened without leaving anything out. When you ask a friend to repeat exactly what was said in a conversation, word for word.

m: Something remains completely unchanged or untouched, exactly as it was originally left.
s: When you return a borrowed item in the exact same condition as when you lent it out. When a person refuses to change their opinions or habits despite new information or circumstances. When a sealed package arrives at your door still completely unopened and undamaged.

m: Someone's true nature, bad intentions, or real character is exposed and can no longer be hidden.
s: When a coworker who seemed friendly suddenly shows they were only being nice to get a promotion. When a scammer's tricks are finally discovered and everyone sees what they really are.

l: remove the false and keep the true
m: To distinguish between what is genuine and what is fake, separating truth from falsehood to identify what really matters.
s: When you're reading multiple news sources and need to figure out which information is actually accurate versus what's misinformation. When you're evaluating someone's claims and trying to determine what parts are truthful and what parts are exaggerated or made up.

l: remove the coarse and take the refined
m: To discard what is worthless or inferior and keep what is valuable or superior; to extract the essential from the trivial.
s: When you're reviewing a long document and only keeping the most important points. When a teacher helps students focus on the key concepts from a lot of reading material instead of memorizing everything. When you're sorting through advice from many people and deciding which suggestions are actually useful.

m: Things are of varying quality or condition, lacking uniformity or consistency.
s: When you look at a group of students' test scores and they range from excellent to failing with no pattern. When you're shopping for tomatoes at the market and some are ripe while others are still green and underripe. When a team has some very skilled players and some who are inexperienced, making their overall performance unpredictable.

m: To experience a mixture of surprise and joy at the same time, feeling both shocked and pleased by an unexpected positive development.
s: When you receive an unexpected gift from someone you hadn't heard from in years. When you run into an old friend by complete chance and they tell you great news about their life.

c: 又要马儿跑得好，又要马儿不吃草
p: yòu yào mǎ ér pǎo dé hǎo ， yòu yào mǎ ér bù chī cǎo
l: Want the horse to run well, yet want the horse not to eat grass
m: To expect excellent results while being unwilling to provide the necessary resources or conditions required to achieve them.
s: When a boss demands high productivity from employees but refuses to invest in better tools or training. When a parent wants their child to excel in school but won't provide time or resources for studying.

l: seize the sharp edge and test it
m: to take advantage of a favorable moment or opportunity to make a decisive move or test one's abilities.
s: When a company launches a new product right when market conditions are perfect for success. When an athlete competes at their peak physical condition during an important championship. When you apply for a job immediately after gaining the exact experience the employer is looking for.

m: To pursue two different approaches or strategies simultaneously to achieve better results.
s: When a company advertises both online and on television at the same time to reach more customers. When a student studies both textbooks and practice problems together to learn more effectively.

p: fǎn qí dào ér xíng zhī
l: reverse the path and act accordingly
m: To deliberately do the opposite of what is expected or conventional; to go against established practice or wisdom.
s: When someone ignores good advice and does exactly what they were warned not to do. When a company rejects proven industry standards and takes a completely different approach to solve a problem. When a student studies the opposite material they were supposed to study.

l: return the lip with mutual ridicule
m: To respond to someone's insult or criticism with equally harsh or sarcastic counterattacks.
s: When two people get into an argument and start trading insults back and forth. When someone makes a mean comment about you and you immediately fire back with something equally cutting about them.

m: To frequently change one's mind, decisions, or behavior in an unpredictable and unreliable way.
s: When a manager keeps changing the project requirements every week, making it impossible for the team to make progress. When a friend constantly cancels plans at the last minute or switches between supporting different people without any loyalty.

m: To turn the tables and take control of a situation that was originally someone else's or to usurp authority from those who were supposed to be in charge.
s: When a guest at someone's house starts making decisions and giving orders instead of the host. When an employee gradually takes over the boss's responsibilities and authority. When someone invited to help with a project ends up directing everyone else and taking charge.

l: turn one's spear around and strike back
m: To turn against one's former allies or masters and strike them down using their own methods or weapons.
s: When an employee who learned everything from their boss suddenly leaves and starts a competing business using all that knowledge. When a student uses their teacher's own arguments to prove the teacher wrong in a debate.

m: To launch a fierce counterattack against someone and seek revenge by settling old scores with them.
s: When someone who has been wronged finally stands up and retaliates against their oppressor. When a person who was previously in a weak position gains power and uses it to punish those who mistreated them in the past.

m: When facing problems or conflicts, one should look inward and reflect on one's own faults rather than blaming others.
s: When a relationship is having problems, instead of just criticizing your partner, you should examine what you might have done wrong. When a project fails, a good leader will first ask what mistakes they made before pointing fingers at the team.

m: to reflect inwardly on one's own faults and shortcomings rather than blaming others.
s: When you make a mistake and need to think about what you did wrong instead of making excuses. When someone is having conflicts with others and should consider their own role in the problem rather than just criticizing the other person.

m: To look inward and honestly examine one's own thoughts, actions, and motivations to determine if you are in the wrong.
s: When you've had a conflict with someone and need to think about whether you share any blame. When you're unsure if you've made a mistake and want to honestly assess your own behavior before blaming others.

m: Something that causes people to think deeply and reconsider their beliefs or actions.
s: When a movie or book makes you think about life in a completely different way. When a teacher's lesson really makes you reconsider what you thought you knew. When someone's words strike you so deeply that you can't stop thinking about them for days.

m: To have the authority to give orders and make decisions that others must follow.
s: When a manager starts making all the decisions without consulting the team. When a new leader takes charge and begins directing everyone on what to do. When someone assumes control of a project and starts telling everyone how things should be done.

m: To work hard and earnestly with determination to become stronger or achieve success.
s: When someone decides to stop making excuses and starts working hard to improve themselves. When a student dedicates themselves to studying intensely to pass a difficult exam. When a person commits to rigorous training to reach their goals.

l: exert effort and forget to eat
m: To work or study with such intense dedication and passion that one becomes completely absorbed and neglects even basic needs like eating.
s: When someone is so focused on completing a project that they skip meals without realizing it. When a student is so engrossed in studying for an exam that they forget to have lunch. When an artist or writer becomes so immersed in their work that hours pass without them eating anything.

m: To promote, advance, and bring something valuable to its fullest potential and greatest success.
s: When a company takes a traditional family business and expands it into a thriving national brand. When a teacher inspires students to master and perfect a classical art form that had been dying out. When someone takes their mentor's teachings and builds upon them to achieve even greater accomplishments.

p: qǔ zhī bù jìn ， yòng zhī bù jié
l: Take from it without exhaustion, use it without depletion
m: A resource or supply is so abundant that it can be used endlessly without ever running out.
s: When describing a wealthy person who seems to have unlimited money to spend. When talking about someone's seemingly infinite patience or kindness that never seems to diminish no matter how much others rely on it.

m: to take someone's or something's place by removing them and putting oneself in their position.
s: When a new employee proves more competent and eventually gets promoted to the manager position instead of the long-time worker. When a newer technology completely replaces an older one in the market because it's superior.

l: take the long to supplement the short
m: Learn from others' strengths to overcome your own weaknesses, or combine complementary abilities to achieve better results.
s: When two people work together because one is good at things the other isn't, they can accomplish more. When a company hires people with different skills to fill gaps in their team. When students study together and help each other with subjects they find difficult.

m: To be pleasantly surprised and deeply touched by unexpected kindness or special treatment from someone important.
s: When your boss suddenly praises your work and you're genuinely shocked because you didn't expect it. When a celebrity you admire remembers your name and talks to you, leaving you overwhelmed with joy.

m: To go through a prolonged period of intense pain, difficulty, or misfortune.
s: When someone has experienced years of poverty and struggle. When a refugee has fled their country and faced many challenges in starting over. When a person has survived serious illness or personal tragedy that tested them deeply.

m: Something that changes frequently and unpredictably, lacking consistency or stability.
s: When the weather keeps switching between sunny and rainy without warning. When a person's mood or opinions shift constantly, making them unreliable and hard to predict. When market prices fluctuate wildly and unpredictably.

l: changes and illusions cannot be measured
m: Something is so unpredictable and changeable that it is impossible to anticipate or understand its true nature.
s: When the weather suddenly shifts from sunny to rainy without warning. When a person's mood or behavior is so inconsistent that you never know how they'll react next. When stock market prices fluctuate wildly and nobody can predict which direction they'll move.

l: change the root and increase the severity
m: A bad situation becomes even worse, or someone intensifies their negative behavior to an even greater degree.
s: When someone who was already rude becomes even more aggressive and insulting. When a problem that was already serious gets significantly worse instead of better. When a student who was already struggling starts doing even worse after failing an exam.

l: pile couch upon couch and frame upon frame
m: To add unnecessary layers or complications to something that is already complete, resulting in redundancy and inefficiency.
s: When a company keeps adding more management layers to an already complicated organizational structure. When someone writes an essay with repetitive points stacked on top of each other instead of getting to the main idea. When a process becomes overly complicated because people keep adding new steps without removing the old ones.

m: To repeatedly and insistently claim or assert something verbally, often with emphasis or exaggeration.
s: When someone keeps saying they will do something but never follows through. When a politician makes the same promises over and over in every speech. When your friend loudly claims to be an expert at something but actually knows nothing about it.

p: kǒu huì ér shí bù zhì
l: offers verbal kindness but fails to deliver in reality
m: Someone makes generous promises or offers kind words but fails to follow through with actual help or action.
s: When a person constantly tells you they'll help you move but never shows up. When a boss promises a raise or promotion but it never materializes despite repeated assurances. When someone says they care about you but their actions show complete indifference.

m: Someone's words do not match their true thoughts or intentions; they are being insincere or dishonest.
s: When a friend says they're happy for you but their tone and behavior suggest they're actually jealous or upset. When a colleague claims to support a decision in a meeting but then complains about it privately to others.

m: To speak eloquently, fluently, and at great length with impressive skill and persuasiveness.
s: When a politician gives a passionate speech that captivates the entire audience with their smooth talking. When a salesman convinces you to buy something through his endless stream of persuasive words. When someone can talk their way out of any situation with their exceptional speaking ability.

l: honey in the mouth, dagger in the belly
m: Someone who speaks sweetly and pleasantly to your face but harbors malicious intentions and will betray you behind your back.
s: When a coworker is very friendly and compliments you constantly, but you later discover they've been spreading rumors about you to the boss. When someone acts kind and supportive in front of you but you find out they've been sabotaging your projects when you're not around.

m: To criticize someone severely using both spoken words and written language.
s: When critics harshly attack a public figure through interviews and opinion pieces. When someone writes angry articles and gives passionate speeches against a policy they oppose.

m: Mere words without evidence or documentation cannot be trusted as proof of something.
s: When someone makes a claim but refuses to provide any documentation or evidence to back it up. When you need a written contract rather than just a verbal promise from someone, because spoken words alone aren't enough to rely on.

l: use the ancient for the present
m: To apply the wisdom, knowledge, or methods of the past to solve problems and meet the needs of the present day.
s: When a company revives traditional craftsmanship techniques to create modern products that appeal to contemporary consumers. When a teacher uses classical literature and historical examples to help students understand current social issues and challenges.

l: ancient and modern, Chinese and foreign
m: Referring to all times throughout history and all places across the world, encompassing everything without limitation.
s: When someone says they've read books from ancient and modern times, from both Chinese and Western sources. When describing a museum collection that spans different historical periods and cultures from around the world.

m: Throughout all of human history from the earliest times to the present moment.
s: When discussing how something has always been true across all of history. When talking about a pattern or human behavior that has remained constant since ancient times until now.

m: Having an old-fashioned, antique quality that evokes the aesthetic and charm of ancient times.
s: When you walk into an old traditional house filled with classical furniture and decorations that feel like they belong in a museum. When someone wears vintage clothing or collects antique objects that have that timeless, historical appeal.

m: To have ulterior motives or a hidden agenda beyond what is openly stated or apparent.
s: When a colleague volunteers to help with a project but you suspect they're trying to take credit for your work. When someone is being unusually nice to you and you sense they want something in return that they haven't mentioned yet.

m: To look at someone or something with a new perspective, typically with increased respect or changed opinion.
s: When a coworker does something impressive and you start to respect them more. When someone proves they're capable of something you didn't think they could do, and you change your opinion about them.

m: A polite way to decline help or involvement by suggesting someone else would be better suited to handle the task.
s: When someone asks you for help with something you don't feel qualified to do, you might say this to politely turn them down. When a professional realizes a job is outside their expertise and recommends the client find someone more skilled instead.

m: To begin a completely new enterprise or undertaking independent of previous efforts or associations.
s: When someone leaves their job to start their own business from scratch. When a group breaks away from an organization to form their own separate group. When you decide to abandon a failed project and begin with a fresh approach.

l: only compete for morning and evening
m: Make the most of every moment and work hard without wasting time, as if each day and night are precious opportunities that must not be lost.
s: When someone is motivated to accomplish their goals quickly before time runs out. When a person decides to stop procrastinating and start working immediately on an important project. When time is running out and someone needs to make the most of the remaining hours.

p: zhǐ kě yì huì ， bù kě yán chuán
l: can only be understood in the mind, cannot be conveyed in words
m: Some things are better understood through intuition or experience rather than explained through language, as words fail to fully capture their essence.
s: When you try to explain the feeling of falling in love to someone who has never experienced it, but realize that no description could really do it justice. When a musician tries to describe the emotion they feel when playing a beautiful piece, knowing that words just cannot capture it.

p: zhī cǐ yī jiā ， bié wú fēn diàn
l: Only this one shop, no other branches
m: Something is unique and exclusive, with no other place or person offering the same thing.
s: When a restaurant has become famous for its signature dish and there's only one location where you can get it. When a skilled craftsman is the only one in town who can repair something in a particular way. When a store has a monopoly on a certain product because no competitors exist.

c: 只要功夫深，铁杵磨成针
p: zhǐ yào gōng fu shēn ， tiě chǔ mó chéng zhēn
l: As long as the effort is deep, an iron pestle can be ground into a needle
m: With enough patience, persistence, and hard work, even the most difficult goals can be achieved.
s: When someone finally masters a skill after years of practice and dedication. When a student gradually improves their grades through consistent studying despite initial struggles. When someone achieves a seemingly impossible goal by never giving up and putting in continuous effort.

p: zhǐ jiàn shù mù ， bú jiàn sēn lín
l: Only seeing the trees, not seeing the forest
m: To focus so much on small details that you miss the bigger picture or overall situation.
s: When someone gets caught up arguing about minor points in a contract and loses sight of the main business opportunity. When a student spends hours perfecting one paragraph of an essay but ignores the overall structure and argument. When a manager obsesses over a small budget line item and fails to notice the company's major strategic problems.

c: 只许州官放火，不许百姓点灯
p: zhǐ xǔ zhōu guān fàng huǒ ， bù xǔ bǎi xìng diǎn dēng
l: Only the prefect is allowed to set fires, but the common people are not allowed to light lamps
m: Those in power are permitted to do things that ordinary people are strictly forbidden from doing; rules are applied unfairly based on status or position.
s: When a manager can arrive late to work without consequence, but employees are disciplined for the same behavior. When a politician breaks the law but faces no real punishment, while ordinary citizens are prosecuted severely for similar actions.

l: call out in suffering without stopping
m: To complain bitterly and persistently about difficulties or hardships without relief.
s: When someone is constantly complaining about how hard their life is or how much they're struggling. When a coworker won't stop grieving about their workload and keeps bringing it up in every conversation.

l: cry out bitterness to the heavens
m: To complain incessantly and loudly about one's suffering or misfortune.
s: When someone keeps complaining about how hard their life is without trying to change anything. When a coworker won't stop whining about their workload to anyone who will listen.

l: an opportunity that can be taken advantage of
m: An opportune moment or favorable circumstance that can be exploited to achieve one's goals.
s: When a competitor makes a mistake and you see a chance to overtake them in business. When someone leaves their guard down and you have the perfect moment to make your move.

p: kě wàng ér bù kě jí
l: can be seen but cannot be reached
m: Something that appears attainable or desirable but is actually impossible to obtain or achieve.
s: When you dream of buying a luxury home but it's way too expensive for your budget. When a talented athlete admires a professional sports career that seems impossible to attain due to circumstances.

l: worthy of song and worthy of tears
m: An event or deed is so noble and moving that it inspires both admiration and deep emotion, deserving to be celebrated in song and mourned with tears.
s: When hearing about a soldier's selfless sacrifice to save others. When learning about someone who overcame tremendous hardship through courage and perseverance. When witnessing an act of heroism that is both inspiring and heartbreaking at the same time.

p: kě yù ér bù kě qiú
l: can be encountered but cannot be sought
m: Something valuable or fortunate that can only happen by chance and cannot be obtained through deliberate effort or pursuit.
s: When you unexpectedly meet a good friend after years of losing touch. When someone finds the perfect job opportunity by pure luck rather than through job hunting. When a genuine romantic connection happens spontaneously rather than through intentional dating efforts.

l: scold and rule the wind and clouds
m: To wield great power and influence, dominating a situation or field with commanding authority.
s: When a powerful military general controls multiple regions and commands respect from all sides. When a successful entrepreneur dominates their industry and influences market trends. When a charismatic leader sways public opinion and shapes political events.

m: Something has never happened before in history; it is completely unprecedented and unparalleled.
s: When a company achieves a sales record that has never been reached in the industry before. When a natural disaster occurs that is more severe than any recorded event in the past. When an athlete breaks a world record that stood for decades.

m: Someone claims to love or admire something, but actually fears or dislikes it when confronted with the real thing.
s: When a person says they love horror movies but covers their eyes during scary scenes. When someone claims to want honest feedback but gets defensive and upset when you actually give it to them. When a friend says they love adventure travel but backs out when you actually plan a trip.

l: when leaves fall they return to the root
m: no matter how far one travels or how successful one becomes, one will eventually return to one's hometown or place of origin.
s: When an immigrant who moved abroad for work finally decides to retire and move back to their hometown. When someone who left their small village to seek fortune in the big city eventually comes back to settle down where they grew up.

l: the minister of works finds it commonplace
m: Something that is so frequently seen or experienced that it no longer seems remarkable or noteworthy.
s: When you see the same traffic jam on your commute every morning and don't even notice it anymore. When your coworker is always late to meetings and nobody thinks anything of it.

p: sī mǎ zhāo zhī xīn ， lù rén jiē zhī
l: Sima Zhao's heart is known even to people on the road
m: Someone's true intentions or ambitions are so obvious that everyone can see through them, no matter how hard they try to hide it.
s: When a coworker pretends to be friendly but is clearly just trying to get a promotion by undermining their colleagues. When a politician claims to care about the people but their actions show they only want power and money.

l: sigh in admiration until there is nothing left to observe
m: To be so amazed and impressed by something that you have no words left to express your admiration.
s: When you watch an incredible performance and are left speechless by how impressive it was. When someone shows you their artwork or creation and it's so beautiful that you can only sigh in amazement.

p: chī yī qiàn ， zhǎng yī zhì
l: Eat one moat, gain one wisdom
m: You learn and gain wisdom from experiencing failure or hardship.
s: When someone makes a mistake but learns from it and doesn't repeat it. When a person goes through a difficult experience and comes out more knowledgeable and careful about similar situations in the future.

l: eat, drink, play, and be merry
m: To indulge in pleasures and entertainment without concern for responsibilities or consequences.
s: When someone spends all their money on parties and vacations instead of saving for the future. When a person neglects their work or studies to focus only on having fun and enjoying themselves.

m: Having the willingness and ability to work hard, persevere through difficult conditions, and not complain about hardship.
s: When describing someone who is willing to do physically demanding or unpleasant work without complaining. When you want to praise a colleague or employee who tackles difficult projects with determination and patience. When talking about someone from a poor background who worked their way up through hard work and sacrifice.

m: Someone responds well to gentle persuasion and kindness but resists forceful demands or coercion.
s: When a stubborn child refuses to do homework if you yell at them, but cooperates when you ask nicely. When a difficult colleague becomes cooperative after you approach them with courtesy rather than confrontation.

m: to betray someone's trust while accepting their benefits, acting as a traitor to those who support you.
s: When an employee takes company secrets to a competitor while still collecting a paycheck. When someone accepts help from a friend but secretly works against their interests. When a family member enjoys the household's resources while scheming to harm the family's interests.

m: To overcome difficulties or opponents by tackling them one at a time rather than trying to handle everything simultaneously.
s: When a student breaks down a big project into smaller tasks and completes them one by one. When a company deals with its problems methodically rather than trying to solve everything at once.

c: 各人自扫门前雪，莫管他人瓦上霜
p: gè rén zì sǎo mén qián xuě ， mò guǎn tā rén wǎ shàng shuāng
l: Each person sweeps the snow from their own doorstep, do not care about the frost on others' tiles
m: Everyone should focus on their own problems and responsibilities rather than interfering in or worrying about other people's affairs.
s: When someone is dealing with their own difficulties and doesn't have time to get involved in their friend's drama. When a manager tells employees to focus on their own work instead of criticizing their colleagues' performance.

l: each rushes toward their own future
m: People go their separate ways to pursue their own individual goals and futures.
s: When a group of friends graduates and moves to different cities for their careers. When business partners decide to end their collaboration and start their own separate ventures. When a team disbands and members pursue different opportunities.

m: Everyone finds a position or role that is suitable and appropriate for their abilities and circumstances.
s: When a team is reorganized and everyone ends up in jobs they're good at. When people in a group finally feel satisfied because they're doing what they do best. When a manager successfully assigns tasks so that each person is working in an area where they excel.

l: each holds to one's own words
m: People involved in a dispute each insist their own account is correct and refuse to agree with the other side.
s: When two people have completely different stories about what happened and neither will admit the other might be right. When a couple argues about who forgot to pay the bill, with each person absolutely certain they're correct.

m: Everyone is free to express their own views and opinions without restriction or censorship.
s: In a team meeting where the manager asks everyone to share their ideas about a new project. During a family discussion about weekend plans where everyone gets a chance to say what they want to do.

m: Everyone or everything has their own unique strengths, merits, or special characteristics that make them valuable in their own way.
s: When comparing two different artists and recognizing that they both have distinct talents worth appreciating. When discussing different approaches to solving a problem and acknowledging that each method has its own advantages depending on the situation.

l: each acts as their own government
m: People or groups act independently without coordination or unified leadership, each pursuing their own interests rather than working together.
s: When a company has different departments that don't communicate and each one makes decisions without consulting the others. When a group project fails because team members work on different things without agreeing on a plan first.

m: Everyone acts according to their own beliefs or preferences without coordination or agreement, leading to disorder or lack of unity.
s: When a team is supposed to work together on a project but each member does things their own way instead of following the plan. When family members refuse to cooperate and everyone insists on doing things according to their own ideas.

m: A rare and precious fragment or remnant of something valuable from the past that has largely been lost or destroyed.
s: When archaeologists discover a few intact pieces of ancient pottery from a lost civilization. When you find an old photograph or letter that is one of the few remaining memories of someone who has passed away. When a museum acquires one of only a handful of surviving manuscripts from a historical period.

l: same hatred of the enemy with one heart
m: People unite with a shared sense of anger and determination against a common adversary or threat.
s: When a team comes together to defeat a rival after being humiliated. When citizens band together to resist an injustice or oppression that affects them all. When coworkers put aside their differences to compete against another company that is trying to destroy their business.

p: tóng shēng xiāng yìng ， tóng qì xiāng qiú
l: Same voice responds in unison, same breath seeks each other
m: People with similar interests, values, or goals naturally attract and support each other.
s: When you meet someone who shares your passion for music and you immediately become close friends. When colleagues who all care about environmental issues naturally gravitate toward working together on sustainability projects.

l: drawing blades against each other in the same room
m: Members of the same family or group fighting against each other instead of presenting a united front against external enemies.
s: When siblings argue bitterly and refuse to support each other. When coworkers from the same department undermine each other's work instead of collaborating. When political allies within the same party turn against one another and weaken their collective position.

m: People who appear to be together or aligned are actually pursuing completely different goals or have conflicting intentions.
s: When a married couple stays together but has completely different life plans. When business partners work under the same company but secretly want different things for the future. When teammates pretend to cooperate but each person is really only looking out for themselves.

m: Both parties are destroyed or ruined together as a result of mutual conflict or opposition.
s: When two enemies fight so fiercely that they both end up destroyed. When two companies engage in a price war that bankrupts them both. When two people pursue revenge on each other so intensely that they both lose everything.

m: When people work together with unified purpose and determination, combining their efforts toward a common goal.
s: When a team works together without conflict to complete a difficult project. When family members all contribute their best to help during a crisis. When colleagues put aside personal interests to achieve the company's mission.

m: People are united in purpose and working together with complete harmony and agreement.
s: When a team works together perfectly toward a shared goal without any conflict. When family members stand united and support each other through difficult times. When colleagues collaborate smoothly because they all believe in the same mission.

l: those with the same evil seek each other out
m: People with similar wicked or base intentions naturally attract and associate with one another.
s: When you notice that all your friend's new companions seem to share the same bad habits or negative attitudes. When corrupt officials seem to find and band together with other corrupt people in government.

m: To associate with or become complicit in the wrongdoings and moral corruption of others.
s: When someone starts hanging out with a bad crowd and begins adopting their unethical behavior. When a colleague stays silent and goes along with office dishonesty instead of speaking up against it. When a person compromises their own values by participating in corrupt practices with their friends or colleagues.

l: Share the sweet and endure the bitter together
m: To stand by someone through both good times and bad times, sharing equally in both joy and hardship.
s: When a couple stays together through financial struggles and celebrates successes as a team. When friends remain loyal to each other whether things are going well or poorly. When coworkers support each other through difficult projects and celebrate achievements together.

m: People who share the same misfortune or suffering naturally sympathize with and support each other.
s: When two friends who have both gone through divorce understand each other's pain without needing explanation. When colleagues who have all been laid off from the same company bond together and help one another find new jobs.

l: sharing one boat and helping each other
m: People must work together and support each other in times of difficulty or crisis, just as passengers in the same boat must cooperate to survive.
s: When a team faces a difficult project deadline and everyone needs to pitch in and work together. When a family goes through financial hardship and all members have to cooperate and make sacrifices to get through it. When colleagues from different departments put aside their differences to solve a critical company problem.

m: Something or someone fails to live up to their reputation, appearance, or what is claimed about them.
s: When a restaurant is highly rated but the food is actually mediocre. When someone boasts about their skills but performs poorly when put to the test. When a product is advertised as premium quality but turns out to be cheap and poorly made.

m: Someone or something's reputation is well-deserved and matches reality.
s: When you finally meet a famous chef and their food is absolutely amazing, living up to all the hype. When you visit a highly-rated restaurant and it's just as good as everyone says it is.

l: name listed among the front ranks
m: To rank among the top performers or achievers; to be among the best or most prominent.
s: When a student consistently scores in the top percentile of their class. When a company becomes one of the industry leaders in their field. When an athlete finishes near the top in a competition.

m: To achieve both fame and financial success at the same time.
s: When a successful entrepreneur becomes wealthy while also gaining widespread recognition and respect in their field. When a talented artist achieves commercial success and critical acclaim simultaneously.

m: Someone or something genuinely deserves the reputation or title they have; the reality fully lives up to the name.
s: When a restaurant is famous for great food and you go there and it's actually amazing. When someone is called a genius and their work proves they really are exceptionally talented.

m: To become famous or notorious for a brief period, experiencing sudden widespread renown that does not necessarily last.
s: When a musician releases a viral hit song and becomes instantly famous across social media for a few months. When a celebrity scandal causes someone to become the talk of the town for a while, but people quickly forget about them.

m: To have one's name remembered and honored throughout history for great achievements or virtues.
s: When someone accomplishes something so remarkable that people will remember them for generations. When discussing historical figures whose contributions have made them immortal in people's memory.

m: Something retains its name or outward form but has lost all real substance, function, or value.
s: When a once-famous company still exists officially but no longer produces anything or does business. When an organization keeps its old name and structure but has become completely ineffective and powerless.

m: When one's title or position is justified and legitimate, one can act with proper authority and speak with rightful justification.
s: When someone has an official position or clear responsibility, they can make decisions confidently. When a teacher disciplines a student because it's their legitimate duty. When a new manager implements changes because they have the proper authority to do so.

l: the reins of fame and the locks of profit
m: The constraints and attachments that come from pursuing fame and wealth, which bind people and prevent them from achieving freedom or enlightenment.
s: When someone is so obsessed with their reputation or making money that they can't make their own free choices. When a person stays in an unfulfilling job or relationship because they're afraid of losing status or income.

m: To fail an examination or competition and not make the list of successful candidates.
s: When a student fails an important entrance exam and doesn't get accepted to their desired school. When someone applies for a competitive job position but doesn't make it past the first round of selection.

l: Strike after the opponent has moved
m: By allowing your opponent to act first, you gain the advantage of seeing their strategy and can respond with a decisive counter-attack.
s: In a chess game, a player waits for their opponent to make the first move before formulating their strategy. In a business negotiation, one party lets the other make their initial offer first, then responds with a better counter-offer based on what they've learned.

m: Failure to address a problem now will result in endless suffering and complications in the future.
s: When you skip important maintenance on your car and it eventually breaks down completely. When a company ignores safety concerns and later faces massive lawsuits and damage to its reputation.

m: Someone who starts later can still surpass or outperform those who had a head start through hard work and persistence.
s: When a student who joined the class late ends up getting better grades than classmates who started earlier. When a company entering a market years after competitors becomes the industry leader. When someone picks up a new skill later in life but eventually becomes better at it than people who started much earlier.

l: the rear waves push the front waves
m: The younger generation surpasses and replaces the older generation through progress and innovation.
s: When young people in a company bring fresh ideas that outperform the old methods of their senior colleagues. When a new athlete breaks records that stood for decades, showing that the next generation is stronger and better than the previous one.

l: the young generation is to be feared
m: Young people have great potential and should not be underestimated, as they may surpass their elders.
s: When a young athlete breaks a long-standing record that no one thought could be beaten. When a teenager comes up with an innovative solution that experienced adults hadn't considered. When you realize that the younger generation is quickly becoming more skilled and capable than you are.

m: There is no one qualified or willing to continue a tradition, skill, or position after the current person.
s: When a master craftsman retires but no apprentices have learned the trade well enough to carry it on. When a company's founder is leaving but there's no capable leader ready to take over. When a martial arts master has trained students but none are truly worthy of inheriting the school's legacy.

l: those who come after have capable people
m: There are qualified successors to carry on one's work, legacy, or tradition.
s: When a teacher sees their students excel and surpass them in their field. When a company's founding leader retires knowing the next generation of leaders are well-prepared. When a master craftsman trains apprentices who will continue the trade after they retire.

l: a rising talent that emerges later
m: A talented person who rises to prominence only after others, or a promising newcomer who shows exceptional ability.
s: When a young athlete breaks onto the scene and suddenly becomes competitive with established champions. When a new employee quickly proves themselves to be exceptionally skilled and talented compared to their peers.

m: Worries or anxieties about family or affairs left at home that distract you from focusing on your current task or responsibility.
s: A soldier who cannot concentrate on battle because he is worried about his family back home. An employee hesitating to take a business trip abroad because they are concerned about leaving their elderly parents alone.

l: expel the old and accept the new
m: To discard outdated or useless things and embrace new, better alternatives in order to progress and improve.
s: When a company modernizes its outdated systems and adopts new technology. When someone cleans out their old wardrobe and buys contemporary clothes instead. When an organization replaces old policies with innovative approaches that better serve their goals.

l: facing the wall and fabricating emptiness
m: to invent or fabricate something false without any basis in reality, making things up entirely from imagination.
s: When someone tells a completely made-up story that never happened and has no factual basis. When a writer creates an entirely fictional account and presents it as true fact.

m: To feel excluded, disappointed, or left out while others around you are happy or celebrating.
s: When you're the only one not invited to a party and feel sad about being left out. When everyone else got promoted at work but you didn't, and you feel isolated in your disappointment.

m: to smoke cigarettes or other substances, typically describing the act of inhaling and exhaling smoke.
s: When someone is smoking a cigarette and you see the smoke being inhaled and released. When describing someone's habit of frequently smoking throughout the day.

m: To speak in a hesitant, stammering manner, unable to express oneself clearly or confidently.
s: When someone is nervous during a presentation and keeps stuttering or pausing awkwardly. When a person struggles to get their words out because they're embarrassed or unsure about what they want to say.

l: chant to the wind and play with the moon
m: To indulge in romantic or poetic pursuits and refined aesthetic pleasures rather than dealing with practical matters.
s: When someone spends all their time writing poetry and daydreaming instead of working on their responsibilities. When a person is more interested in artistic expression and romantic ideals than facing reality and getting things done.

l: bark at shadows and bark at sounds
m: To engage in mindless repetition or empty criticism without understanding the true issue, like dogs barking at each other's shadows rather than at any real threat.
s: When people on social media repeat criticism without thinking about whether it's actually valid. When a group of employees complain about a policy just because one person started complaining, without understanding the real situation.

l: Negation reaches extreme, then prosperity arrives
m: When circumstances reach their worst point, improvement and good fortune will inevitably follow.
s: When someone has been struggling for years but finally gets a breakthrough opportunity. When a company has faced continuous losses and setbacks, but suddenly lands a major deal that turns things around. When a person goes through a terrible period of hardship and then their luck suddenly changes for the better.

m: To silently tolerate insults, mistreatment, and shame without complaint or resistance.
s: When someone stays in a bad relationship but doesn't speak up about how poorly they're being treated. When a person accepts constant disrespect from their boss but never stands up for themselves or complains to others.

When describing historical figures who were unknown for decades before becoming famous.

p: dà chù zhuó yǎn ， xiǎo chù zhuó shǒu

l: greatly lose what was hoped for

l: in the great hall and broad public

l: unfurl flags and beat drums loudly

m: Something that brings immense joy and satisfaction to everyone, especially when a long-awaited desire is finally fulfilled or justice is served.

m: To be so shocked or frightened that one's face becomes pale and one loses composure.

m: to make a big fuss over something trivial or to be overly surprised by something that is not remarkable.

m: To be deeply perplexed or utterly bewildered about something that one cannot understand.
