m: To be overly eager to teach or instruct others, often unsolicited, and to enjoy displaying one's knowledge in a condescending way.
s: When someone is always giving unsolicited advice and acting like they know better than everyone else. When a coworker constantly corrects minor mistakes and lectures people about how things should be done. When someone enjoys showing off their knowledge and can't resist telling others what to do.

m: Worthwhile or positive outcomes often require overcoming numerous difficulties and delays before they can be achieved.
s: When a couple has to wait years and face many challenges before finally getting married. When a promising business deal keeps getting delayed by unexpected problems but eventually succeeds. When someone's dream project faces setback after setback but they persist and finally accomplish it.

l: fond of eating and lazy to work
m: Someone who loves to eat well but is unwilling to work or put in effort.
s: When a person spends all their money on fancy food but refuses to get a job. When someone complains about being poor while eating expensive meals and avoiding any responsibilities.

l: fond of big achievements and loves accomplishments
m: To be excessively ambitious and eager for glory, often pursuing grand projects without regard for feasibility or proper planning.
s: When a new manager takes over and immediately wants to launch several massive initiatives without understanding the current situation. When someone constantly brags about their accomplishments and always wants to do bigger and more impressive things than others.

m: A person who avoids conflict by agreeing with everyone and never expressing disagreement or criticism.
s: When someone always says yes to everything even when they disagree, just to avoid upsetting people. When a coworker never stands up for their own ideas in meetings because they're afraid of causing friction.

l: good scenery does not last long
m: Good times and favorable circumstances are temporary and will not endure forever.
s: When a company has a period of rapid growth but you know market conditions will eventually change. When someone enjoys a streak of good luck but realizes it cannot continue indefinitely. When a relationship is going well but you worry about how long the happiness will remain.

p: hǎo hàn bù chī yǎn qián kuī
l: A good man does not eat immediate losses
m: A wise and capable person knows when to yield or retreat temporarily to avoid unnecessary harm, even if it means appearing to back down in the moment.
s: When someone picks a fight with you but you choose to walk away because the situation isn't worth the trouble. When a skilled negotiator accepts unfavorable terms now to avoid a costly conflict later. When you let a rude comment slide instead of arguing back because you know the confrontation would make things worse.

m: To be lazy and prefer comfort over work, avoiding effort and responsibility.
s: When someone refuses to do their chores and would rather relax all day. When a coworker consistently avoids taking on tasks and leaves everything to others.

m: To have ambitions that are unrealistically high and disconnected from one's actual abilities or circumstances.
s: When someone refuses to start with basic tasks and only wants to work on advanced projects they're not ready for. When a student dreams of becoming a world-famous scientist but won't even study their current coursework.

l: as if mourning one's father and mother
m: to grieve or mourn deeply over something, as though it were the loss of one's own parents.
s: When someone is devastated by a setback or loss and shows extreme sorrow. When a person reacts with disproportionate sadness to something that may not warrant such intense grief. When you see someone treating a failure or disappointment as tragically as if they had lost their closest family members.

l: as if facing a great enemy
m: To treat something with extreme caution and seriousness, preparing oneself as though facing a serious threat or formidable opponent.
s: When someone is overly anxious about a minor problem and treats it with excessive preparation. When a student studies for a regular test as intensely as if preparing for the most important exam of their life.

p: rú rù wú rén zhī jìng
l: as if entering a place where no people exist
m: to move or act freely and unobstructed without any resistance or awareness from others, as if one is in a completely empty space.
s: When someone confidently walks into a crowded room and takes charge without anyone stopping them. When a skilled athlete moves through defenders on the court as if they aren't even there, weaving through traffic effortlessly.

l: as if from the same wheel rut
m: Exactly alike or following the same pattern, as if produced by the same mold or source.
s: When two people make identical mistakes or take the same wrong approach. When different companies release products that are suspiciously similar to each other. When siblings or friends have the exact same mannerisms or way of speaking.

l: like sitting on a needle felt mat
m: To feel extremely uncomfortable, anxious, or restless in a situation, unable to relax or sit still.
s: When you're waiting nervously for important exam results and can't focus on anything else. When someone is in an awkward social situation where they don't fit in and feel deeply uneasy.

p: rú duò wǔ lǐ wù zhōng
l: like falling into a five-mile fog
m: To be completely confused and unable to understand what is happening or being said.
s: When someone explains a complex technical concept and you have no idea what they're talking about. When you wake up in the middle of a conversation and can't follow what people are discussing at all.

m: To be extremely cautious and careful because one is in a precarious or dangerous situation where any mistake could have serious consequences.
s: When you're walking on eggshells around an angry boss, afraid that one wrong word will get you fired. When someone is navigating a very delicate relationship or situation where they must be extremely careful about what they say and do.

l: like a shadow following a form
m: To follow someone or something closely and inseparably, as a shadow naturally follows the person or object casting it.
s: When a loyal friend sticks with you through all your ups and downs and never leaves your side. When a disease or health problem persists and constantly affects your daily life no matter what you do.

m: A wishful plan or scheme that ignores reality and is unlikely to succeed as intended.
s: When someone makes elaborate plans without considering practical obstacles or other people's opinions. When a business owner confidently predicts huge profits without accounting for market competition or economic risks. When your friend thinks they can easily win over someone who has already rejected them.

m: One's wishes or desires have been fulfilled as hoped.
s: When someone finally gets the job they've been dreaming about after months of interviews. When a student passes a difficult exam they studied hard for and gets into their preferred university.

l: recounting as if counting family treasures
m: To know something so thoroughly and intimately that you can discuss it with complete familiarity and expertise, as if describing your own most precious possessions.
s: When a sports fan can rattle off all the statistics and history of their favorite team without hesitation. When a collector describes every single item in their collection with perfect knowledge and affection. When someone talks about their hobbies or area of expertise with such detailed confidence that it's clear they know every aspect by heart.

m: At the peak of power, influence, or success; at the height of one's prosperity or glory.
s: When a company is experiencing explosive growth and dominates its industry. When a celebrity or athlete is at the height of their career and extremely popular. When a government or leader has reached maximum power and influence.

l: awakened as if from a dream
m: To suddenly become aware of reality after being confused or deceived, or to abruptly regain clarity about a situation.
s: When someone finally understands that they've been fooled after a long time of being manipulated. When you're in a daze or confused state and suddenly snap back to reality and recognize what's actually happening around you.

m: Something is simply the way it is, nothing more and nothing less, with no further explanation or justification needed.
s: When someone asks why things turned out a certain way and you want to convey that there's no deeper reason—it just happened that way. When you're dismissing unnecessary speculation about a straightforward situation.

l: like scalding broth poured on snow
m: An overwhelming force or solution that easily destroys or resolves a problem with no resistance, like hot water instantly melting snow.
s: When a skilled lawyer presents an airtight case that completely demolishes the opposing argument. When a new technology makes an old industry instantly obsolete. When a powerful military force defeats a much weaker opponent without any real struggle.

l: follow the method and prepare it the same way
m: To copy someone's methods or actions exactly, often implying mechanical imitation without understanding or originality.
s: When a student copies their classmate's study technique without thinking about whether it actually works for them. When a company simply copies a competitor's business strategy without adapting it to their own situation.

m: Something is developing or progressing with great intensity, momentum, and fervor.
s: When a new project at work is gaining rapid popularity and everyone is enthusiastically participating. When a social movement or campaign is spreading quickly and capturing people's passionate attention.

m: Extremely fierce, aggressive, and predatory in behavior or demeanor.
s: When a group of soldiers charges into battle with overwhelming ferocity. When a sports team plays with intense aggression and dominance against their opponents. When a person behaves in a cruel, ruthless manner to take advantage of others.

m: An incompetent or malicious person placed in a position of authority will inevitably harm those under their care.
s: When a corrupt official is put in charge of a department and starts embezzling funds. When someone known for being dishonest is hired to manage company finances and employees' money goes missing.

l: like an arrow on the bowstring
m: A situation is imminent and unavoidable, ready to happen at any moment.
s: When a project deadline is so close that work must begin immediately. When a conflict between two people is about to explode and cannot be delayed any longer.

m: Two people are inseparably close and deeply devoted to each other, sticking together constantly.
s: When a married couple does everything together and cannot bear to be apart. When two best friends are always by each other's side and share everything in their lives.

l: like a flower and resembling jade
m: A woman who is extraordinarily beautiful and graceful, with delicate and refined features.
s: When describing a young woman who is strikingly beautiful and elegant. When someone's appearance is so lovely and precious that it seems almost unreal, like a perfect flower or valuable jade.

l: as if obtaining the greatest treasure
m: To regard something as extremely precious and valuable, treating it with great care and appreciation.
s: When someone receives a gift they've always wanted and treasures it dearly. When a collector finally finds a rare item they've been searching for and handles it with utmost care. When a person gets an opportunity or piece of advice they consider invaluable and holds onto it seriously.

m: To give added power or capability to someone or something that is already strong or formidable.
s: When a successful company hires a brilliant new executive and suddenly becomes unstoppable. When a talented athlete gets access to a world-class coach and training facility and starts dominating their sport.

l: like ants attached to meat fat
m: People are naturally drawn to something attractive or beneficial, just as ants swarm toward food.
s: When a popular celebrity or influencer announces something and everyone rushes to follow them. When a company offers a special deal and crowds of customers immediately flock to buy it.

m: to feel relieved and relaxed after a heavy load of worry or responsibility has been removed.
s: When you finally submit a major project you've been stressed about for weeks and suddenly feel at peace. When someone who has been caring for a sick family member feels a sense of relief after the person recovers or the situation improves.

m: A name or reputation so famous that it is widely known and has reached many people's ears.
s: When you finally meet a celebrity or famous person whose name you've heard many times. When someone's reputation for excellence in their field is so well-known that everyone recognizes them immediately.

m: To desire or pursue something with intense, urgent eagerness and enthusiasm.
s: When someone is desperately eager to learn a new skill and practices constantly. When a person craves knowledge or information about a topic they find fascinating.

m: to find oneself in an ideal environment or situation where one can thrive and function at one's best.
s: When someone gets a new job that perfectly matches their skills and interests, they feel like a fish in water. When a shy person finally joins a group of people with similar hobbies and feels completely comfortable and happy.

l: like a fishbone stuck in the throat
m: Something that causes constant discomfort or distress and cannot be easily dismissed or forgotten.
s: When you have something bothering you that you can't stop thinking about. When a hurtful comment someone made keeps nagging at you and you can't let it go. When an unresolved problem or conflict continues to trouble you emotionally.

m: A group of people quickly disperses in all directions, often in a chaotic or panicked manner when something unexpected happens.
s: When a crowd suddenly breaks up and everyone runs away in different directions after hearing a loud noise. When a group of friends who were hanging out together all leave at once when the party gets broken up by police.

m: To have an exaggerated sense of one's own importance or abilities without a factual basis.
s: When someone who has minimal experience acts like an expert and looks down on others. When a student who did well on one test starts thinking they're smarter than everyone else and stops studying. When a new employee acts arrogant and dismisses advice from experienced colleagues.

m: To underestimate one's own abilities or worth without justification, showing excessive self-deprecation.
s: When someone is talented but constantly says they're not good enough and refuses opportunities. When a person apologizes excessively for minor mistakes or refuses compliments by insisting they're worthless.

m: To spread false or misleading statements that deceive and manipulate large groups of people.
s: When a politician spreads conspiracy theories to gain support from gullible voters. When someone uses emotional manipulation and lies on social media to turn public opinion against an innocent person. When a cult leader uses false prophecies and deceptive teachings to recruit and control followers.

l: demons and monsters, ghosts and ghouls
m: Evil or wicked people, or things that are strange and frightening; used to refer to bad influences or undesirable elements in society.
s: When someone warns you to stay away from bad people or negative influences that could corrupt you. When describing sensational news stories or rumors that spread fear and panic in a community.

m: Something is so excellent, beautiful, or remarkable that it cannot be adequately described in language.
s: When you taste an amazing dish that is so delicious you struggle to explain how good it is. When you see a breathtaking sunset or piece of art that leaves you speechless. When someone experiences something so wonderful they find it impossible to put into words how much they enjoyed it.

m: A skilled doctor or healer can cure serious illnesses and bring patients back to health, as if restoring them to a state of vitality and renewal.
s: When a doctor successfully treats a patient who was thought to be beyond help. When a talented person fixes or improves something that seemed irreparably broken. When someone with expertise revives a struggling business or project back to its former success.

m: Something is full of clever wit, humor, and delightful interest that captivates and entertains people.
s: When you watch a comedy show that keeps making you laugh with clever jokes. When you read a book written in such a witty and engaging way that you can't put it down.

m: A person has lost their family through death, separation, or disaster, leaving them alone and destitute.
s: When someone's family has been torn apart by tragedy or circumstances beyond their control. When describing the devastating consequences of war, poverty, or misfortune that destroys a family unit.

l: from beginning to end without slackening
m: To persist in effort without ever becoming tired, lazy, or giving up throughout an entire endeavor.
s: When someone works on a difficult project for months without losing motivation or energy. When an athlete trains consistently every single day without skipping or taking shortcuts, showing complete dedication from start to finish.

l: from beginning to end without change
m: To remain steadfast and unwavering in one's commitment or belief throughout, never deviating from one's original resolve.
s: When someone stays loyal to their partner through thick and thin, never wavering in their dedication. When a company maintains its core values and principles consistently over many years despite external pressures.

l: from beginning to end as one
m: To remain consistent and unchanging in one's principles, beliefs, or actions over time.
s: When someone has maintained the same values and commitment throughout their entire life despite changing circumstances. When a company has kept the same quality standards and mission since it was founded decades ago. When a friend has always treated you with the same kindness and loyalty from the day you met until now.

m: Listen to something without taking it seriously or believing it completely, treating it as tentative or unverified information.
s: When someone tells you a rumor but you're not sure if it's true, so you just listen without fully believing it. When a friend shares gossip but you decide to hear them out without committing to what they're saying.

m: To speak without careful consideration or to make a tentative remark without claiming it to be authoritative.
s: When someone offers an opinion but acknowledges it might not be well-informed or completely accurate. When a person prefaces their comment by saying 'I'm just guessing, but...' or 'Take this with a grain of salt, but...'

m: Being too lenient or forgiving toward wrongdoing only encourages the wrongdoer to become bolder and more corrupt.
s: When a parent constantly excuses their child's bad behavior instead of disciplining them, the child gets worse. When a manager repeatedly overlooks an employee's misconduct without consequences, that employee becomes increasingly untrustworthy and problematic.

l: bend one's will and seek wholeness
m: to compromise one's principles or endure humiliation in order to preserve harmony or achieve a greater goal.
s: When someone stays quiet about being treated unfairly at work because they need to keep their job. When a person accepts blame for something they didn't do just to avoid conflict with family members.

m: to arrive late or be delayed, often when someone or something was expected earlier.
s: When a friend shows up significantly late to a meeting you arranged. When an important package finally arrives at your door weeks after you ordered it. When a highly anticipated event or announcement takes much longer to happen than people expected.

m: One's authority, credibility, or reputation is completely destroyed or lost.
s: When a leader makes repeated false promises and nobody believes them anymore. When a teacher is caught lying to students and loses all respect from the class. When a company's CEO is involved in a scandal and the organization's credibility is ruined.

m: To remain steadfast and refuse to surrender one's principles or will even when faced with overwhelming power or threats.
s: When someone stands firm against pressure from authority or powerful forces. When a person refuses to compromise their values despite threats or coercion. When someone maintains their dignity and courage in the face of intimidation.

m: Using both intimidation and temptation to pressure someone into doing something against their will.
s: When a boss threatens to fire an employee while also promising a bonus to get them to work overtime. When a criminal uses threats of violence combined with offers of money to coerce someone into illegal activity.

m: Someone displays a commanding presence and impressive dignity that makes others feel respect and slight fear.
s: When a military general walks into a room in full uniform and everyone immediately stands at attention. When a powerful CEO enters a meeting and the atmosphere becomes serious and formal.

m: Someone who has been excessively pampered and indulged from childhood, making them overly sensitive, weak, or unable to handle hardship or criticism.
s: When a child has been given everything they want and never disciplined, they become unable to cope with disappointment. When someone raised with excessive comfort complains about minor inconveniences or lacks resilience. When parents constantly shield their child from any difficulty, preventing them from developing independence and strength.

l: engaging and pleasant to listen to
m: Speech or storytelling that is so engaging, eloquent, and pleasant that it captivates the listener's attention completely.
s: When a teacher explains a difficult concept in such a clear and interesting way that all students are fascinated. When a storyteller describes events so vividly and smoothly that the whole audience is mesmerized and hangs on every word.

l: speak in a graceful and engaging manner
m: To speak in a smooth, eloquent, and captivating way that holds the listener's attention.
s: When a storyteller keeps you engaged with a well-told story. When a speaker presents their ideas in a charming and articulate way that makes you want to listen.

m: To be indecisive, overly cautious, or to dawdle in a fussy and hesitant manner.
s: When someone takes forever to make a simple decision and keeps going back and forth. When a person fusses over small details instead of getting things done efficiently. When someone complains and worries excessively about minor issues.

m: To shift blame or responsibility for one's own wrongdoing onto someone else.
s: When someone gets caught doing something wrong but blames a coworker instead of taking responsibility. When a student submits late work and claims their group member lost the assignment to avoid getting in trouble.

m: A beautiful, charming smile that lights up someone's face, often suggesting grace and allure.
s: When a shy person suddenly smiles beautifully at you. When someone's genuine happiness is expressed through a lovely, bright smile that captures everyone's attention.

m: To act in a frivolous, disrespectful, or mocking manner without taking something seriously.
s: When someone jokes around and grins mockingly instead of apologizing for their mistake. When a person refuses to be serious during an important conversation and keeps smiling in a cheeky way.

m: To be completely alone with no family, friends, or support.
s: When someone has moved to a new city where they don't know anyone and has no family nearby. When an elderly person has outlived all their relatives and friends and has no one left to rely on.

l: scrutinize characters and deliberate on sentences
m: To carefully choose and refine each word and phrase when writing or speaking, paying close attention to precision and appropriateness.
s: When a writer revises their manuscript multiple times to make sure every word is perfect. When a lawyer drafts a contract and carefully considers the exact wording of each clause to avoid ambiguity. When someone is composing an important email and keeps changing individual words to express their thoughts as clearly as possible.

m: To understand the hidden or implied meaning beneath what is explicitly written or stated.
s: When reading a poem, you notice the author's deeper message isn't directly stated but hidden in subtle word choices. When listening to someone's story, you pick up on what they're not saying based on their tone and pauses. When analyzing a text, you look for the author's unstated assumptions and biases.

l: existence or destruction, continuation or severance
m: A critical moment where survival or complete destruction hangs in the balance, often referring to the fate of a nation, organization, or way of life.
s: When a company is on the verge of bankruptcy and one decision will determine whether it survives or collapses. When a country faces an existential threat that will determine its future existence. When a tradition or culture is at a turning point where it will either be preserved or disappear forever.

m: To deliberately avoid commenting on or addressing something by keeping silent about it.
s: When your friend brings up a sensitive topic but you decide not to engage and just stay quiet. When a manager receives feedback they disagree with but chooses not to respond or argue about it.

m: To pursue something with persistent effort and dedication without becoming weary or losing enthusiasm.
s: When someone studies hard every single day without giving up, even though it takes years to master a skill. When a researcher keeps working on a problem with the same passion and energy, never getting discouraged by setbacks.

m: A person who is both dutiful to their parents and virtuous in character, embodying the highest moral standards of filial piety and personal conduct.
s: When describing someone who takes excellent care of their aging parents while also being respected in the community. When praising a young person who honors their family name through both their dedication to family and their ethical behavior.

m: to struggle or fight against difficulties without any support or assistance from others.
s: When someone is trying to complete a difficult project by themselves with no help from their team. When a person is facing opposition from many people and has no allies to back them up.

m: To be completely isolated and without support or companionship, often due to one's own actions or circumstances.
s: When someone has pushed away all their friends through bad behavior and now has no one to turn to. When a leader makes unpopular decisions and finds themselves without allies or supporters.

m: One person alone cannot accomplish something that requires the cooperation or support of others.
s: When someone tries to organize a group project but nobody else participates. When a person wants to start a business but has no partners or investors to help.

l: stake everything on a single throw
m: to risk everything on one final desperate attempt, abandoning all other options and accepting the possibility of total failure.
s: When someone invests all their money into one risky business venture instead of diversifying. When a failing student puts all their hopes on passing a single final exam to graduate. When a struggling company makes one last-ditch effort with a new product, betting the entire company on its success.

m: To be completely isolated and lack any support or help from others.
s: When someone is facing a difficult situation alone with no one willing to help them. When a person has been abandoned by their friends and family during a crisis. When a company loses all its business partners and customers at once.

m: To admire oneself in isolation without seeking recognition from others, often suggesting arrogant self-satisfaction divorced from reality.
s: When someone thinks they are talented or special but refuses to share their work or accept feedback from others. When a person isolates themselves because they believe nobody else can appreciate their worth or abilities.

m: Being completely alone and in a pitiful, helpless state with no one to rely on.
s: When an elderly person has lost all their family and friends and has no one to care for them. When a refugee arrives in a foreign country with nothing and nobody to help them. When someone is abandoned by everyone they trusted and left to fend for themselves.

l: solitary path following one's own opinion
m: To stubbornly insist on one's own views and refuse to listen to others' advice or suggestions.
s: When a colleague refuses to consider anyone else's input on a project and does things their own way. When someone keeps making the same decisions despite repeated warnings from friends and family.

l: solitary and narrow-minded, scarce in hearing
m: To be ignorant and lacking in knowledge due to limited exposure to the world and information.
s: When someone hasn't traveled or read much and doesn't know about current events or common knowledge. When a person makes obviously outdated or uninformed comments because they've been isolated from mainstream society.

l: study in order to achieve application
m: Knowledge is only valuable when it is put into practical use and applied to real situations.
s: When someone learns a new skill in class but never uses it in their actual work. When a student studies hard for an exam but forgets everything because they don't practice what they learned in real life.

m: Learning is a continuous process that never stops, and there is always more knowledge to acquire.
s: When someone pursues education throughout their entire life, never stopping even after retirement. When a person takes up new skills or subjects despite already being knowledgeable in their field.

m: To have an insatiable desire for learning and continuous self-improvement throughout life.
s: When someone is always reading, taking courses, or asking questions no matter how much they already know. When a scholar or student never feels satisfied with their current knowledge and keeps pushing to learn more.

p: nìng wéi yù suì ， bù wéi wǎ quán
l: Rather be jade shattered than tile left whole
m: It is better to die with honor and integrity than to live a shameful or compromised life.
s: When someone chooses to stand up for their principles even though it will cost them dearly. When a person refuses to surrender their values or dignity just to survive or succeed.

p: níng wèi jī kǒu ， wú wéi niú hòu
l: better to be a chicken's mouth than an ox's rear
m: it is preferable to be a leader in a humble position than a subordinate in a prestigious one
s: When someone chooses to start their own small business rather than take a high position at a large company where they would have little authority. When a person decides to be the head of a small department instead of being just another manager at a Fortune 500 company.

m: It is better to die than to compromise one's principles or surrender to humiliation.
s: When someone refuses to give up their beliefs even when facing terrible consequences. When a person would rather face death or ruin than betray their values or accept shameful treatment from others.

m: It is better to have nothing or be without something than to accept something of poor quality or inferior value.
s: When a company refuses to hire someone just to fill a position if that person isn't qualified enough. When someone would rather stay single than settle for a bad relationship. When a manager decides to leave a team understaffed rather than bring on someone who doesn't meet standards.

l: Guard your mouth like a bottle
m: Keep secrets strictly and never reveal confidential information to others.
s: When someone tells you private information and asks you not to tell anyone. When a friend proves they can be trusted with your deepest secrets. When you need to work with classified information and must keep it completely confidential.

l: guard the stump and wait for the hare
m: to passively hope for good fortune without making any effort, based on a single lucky occurrence in the past.
s: When someone quits their job expecting to get rich quick from one lucky investment. When a person does nothing to improve their situation and just hopes that somehow things will magically work out.

l: In safety, do not forget danger
m: During peaceful and stable times, one should remain vigilant and prepared for potential hardships or crises that may arise.
s: When a company is doing well financially but still maintains emergency reserves and contingency plans. When a nation invests in defense capabilities even during a period of international peace and stability.

l: be at peace with it as if it were normal
m: To accept an unfavorable or difficult situation calmly and naturally without complaint or disturbance.
s: When someone loses their job but continues with their daily routine without anxiety or self-pity. When a person faces criticism or setbacks and responds with composure instead of getting upset or defensive. When someone adapts to a major life change like moving to a new city and settles in without dwelling on the disruption.

l: be content with the present state
m: to be satisfied with one's current situation and unwilling to make efforts to improve or change it.
s: When someone has stopped trying to advance in their career and is just coasting. When a student refuses to study harder because they think their current grades are good enough. When a company stops innovating because their existing products are selling well.

l: be content with one's lot and keep to one's duty
m: To stay within proper bounds, follow rules, and not overstep one's station or responsibilities in society.
s: When someone quietly does their job without complaining or causing trouble. When a person accepts their role in life and doesn't try to do things beyond their position or ability. When someone follows the law and social norms without rebellion or ambition beyond their means.

l: content with soil and reluctant to move
m: People are naturally attached to their homeland and unwilling to leave or relocate to unfamiliar places.
s: When an elderly person refuses to move away from their small hometown despite better opportunities in the city. When a community resists relocation even when offered better living conditions elsewhere. When someone is so emotionally tied to their birthplace that they reject any chance to start fresh in a new location.

m: Something is extremely stable, secure, and unshakeable, like the immovable Mount Tai.
s: When a company has such a strong financial position that it will never go bankrupt. When someone feels completely safe and protected in their home or relationship. When a government or institution is so well-established that it cannot be easily toppled or changed.

m: Extremely stable, secure, and unlikely to change or be disturbed.
s: When a company has been in business for decades without any major problems or scandals. When someone's marriage has lasted 50 years without any serious conflict. When a government maintains complete control over a region with no signs of unrest.

l: establish a home and settle down
m: To find a permanent place to live and establish oneself as a resident or member of a community.
s: When someone moves to a new city for work and decides to buy a house there instead of renting. When an immigrant applies for citizenship and plans to live permanently in their new country.

l: dwell in peace and delight in one's occupation
m: To live in a stable, peaceful environment where one is content and satisfied with their work and livelihood.
s: When describing a society where people have stable jobs, affordable housing, and feel secure about their future. When talking about someone who has finally found a good job and a nice home where they can settle down and be happy.

l: walk at ease as if riding in a carriage
m: To proceed leisurely and unhurriedly, taking one's time without concern for speed or efficiency.
s: When someone is taking a very slow, relaxed walk to their destination even though they could hurry. When a person strolls through the park at their own comfortable pace, in no rush to get anywhere.

m: An official announcement or reassurance issued to calm public anxiety and restore confidence during uncertain or turbulent times.
s: When the government issues a statement to reassure citizens after a crisis or disaster. When a company's leadership addresses employees' concerns with a public announcement to restore morale and trust.

m: To be completely safe and uninjured, having come through a dangerous or difficult situation without any damage or loss.
s: When someone survives a car accident without getting hurt. When a building stands intact after a natural disaster. When a person recovers fully from a serious illness.

m: to set up a base of operations or establish a foothold in a new place, whether literally as a military camp or figuratively as a business, organization, or presence.
s: When a new company opens its first office in a city and starts hiring local employees. When a sports team relocates to a new city and begins building their infrastructure and fan base. When someone moves to a new country and starts settling in by finding housing and establishing routines.

l: find a secure place and establish one's livelihood
m: To find a stable place to live and a secure means of making a living, achieving peace of mind and stability in life.
s: When someone finally finds a good job and a home after years of uncertainty. When a refugee or immigrant successfully settles into a new country and builds a stable life. When a person reaches a point in their career where they feel secure and can stop worrying about their future.

m: To return something valuable or precious to its rightful owner in perfect condition, or to accomplish a difficult task successfully and without damage.
s: When you borrow something expensive from a friend and return it in the exact same perfect condition. When a company manages to complete a difficult project without any mistakes or losses, delivering exactly what was promised.

m: Something that is absolutely perfect with no flaws or imperfections whatsoever.
s: When describing a flawless performance or product that has no issues. When someone produces work that is entirely error-free and meets every possible standard. When praising something as being without any weaknesses or problems.

m: Officials or people in power protect each other from accountability and consequences for their wrongdoings.
s: When corrupt government officials cover up each other's crimes instead of enforcing the law fairly. When managers in a company protect their friends from discipline while punishing ordinary employees for the same mistakes. When people in positions of authority refuse to investigate or prosecute members of their own group.

m: Pompous, verbose writing that sounds impressive but lacks substance and real content.
s: When a government report uses fancy language but doesn't actually say anything meaningful. When someone writes a lengthy email full of bureaucratic jargon that could have been said in two sentences. When formal documents are filled with flowery phrases designed to impress rather than communicate clearly.

l: Officials compel the people to rebel
m: When government oppression and corruption become unbearable, the people have no choice but to rise up in rebellion.
s: When a tyrannical ruler imposes increasingly harsh taxes and restrictions until the population finally organizes a revolt. When a company treats its workers so poorly that they eventually strike or unionize despite the risks of retaliation.

m: To base one's understanding and actions on objective reality and verifiable evidence rather than assumptions, ideology, or wishful thinking.
s: When a manager makes decisions based on actual data and results rather than gut feelings. When someone admits they were wrong after looking at the real evidence instead of defending their initial position.

m: Maintaining emotional equanimity and inner peace regardless of whether one receives praise or criticism, fortune or misfortune.
s: When someone stays calm and composed whether they win an award or face public criticism. When a person doesn't get upset by compliments or insults because they have a strong sense of self-worth. When an employee remains focused on their work regardless of whether they receive recognition or blame from their boss.

l: examine the times and measure the situation
m: to carefully assess current circumstances and trends in order to make well-informed decisions and take appropriate action.
s: When a business leader decides to pivot their strategy based on market changes. When someone chooses the right moment to ask for a favor or make an important announcement based on how things are going.

l: a horse that harms the group
m: A person whose bad behavior or negative influence damages the harmony and well-being of the entire group or community.
s: When one troublemaker in a team keeps causing conflicts and bringing down morale. When a dishonest employee engages in unethical behavior that puts the whole company's reputation at risk.

m: Comfort and luxury can be as deadly as poison, gradually destroying one's will and virtue through indulgence.
s: When someone becomes lazy and loses their ambition after gaining wealth and comfort. When a person surrounded by luxury stops working hard and begins to decline morally or mentally.

p: jiā chǒu bù kě wài yáng
l: A family's shame should not be broadcast outside
m: One should not publicize or expose the private problems, scandals, or shameful matters of one's own family to outsiders.
s: When a family member wants to tell everyone about a relative's embarrassing behavior or mistake, but others advise against it. When someone is tempted to share their family's financial troubles or personal conflicts with neighbors or coworkers.

m: Something is so widely known that it is understood by every family and household.
s: When a celebrity becomes so famous that everyone knows who they are, even small children. When a news story spreads so much that practically every person in the country has heard about it. When a product becomes so popular and well-known that it's recognized everywhere.

m: Something that is very ordinary and happens frequently in everyday life.
s: When something is so routine and normal that it barely deserves special attention. When a skilled person does something difficult that they've practiced so many times it seems effortless to them.

l: a house with only four walls
m: to be in extreme poverty with no possessions or furniture in one's home.
s: When someone has lost everything and is left with nothing but the bare necessities to survive. When describing someone who is so poor they cannot afford any furniture or belongings in their home.

m: A family is completely ruined with members dead or scattered, representing total devastation and loss.
s: When a family loses everything due to war, disaster, or tragedy and the household is torn apart. When someone's entire family is wiped out or dispersed, leaving nothing but destruction and grief behind.

m: A household is prosperous and well-provided for, with everyone's material needs met and living in comfort.
s: When a family business becomes successful and everyone in the household enjoys a better standard of living. When economic conditions improve so that a nation's citizens have enough food and shelter to live comfortably.

m: Someone looks exceptionally healthy, happy, and full of vitality, with a bright and glowing appearance.
s: When someone returns from a relaxing vacation and looks refreshed and energetic. When a person falls in love and suddenly appears much more beautiful and confident. When someone recovers from an illness and regains their healthy, youthful appearance.

l: broad and great as one's heart
m: To have a generous, forgiving, and magnanimous heart that is willing to overlook others' faults and mistakes.
s: When someone does something wrong but you decide to forgive them rather than hold a grudge. When a leader chooses to be lenient with an employee who made an honest mistake instead of punishing them harshly.

m: To be magnanimous, forgiving, and generous in spirit, showing tolerance and understanding toward others.
s: When someone forgives a friend who hurt them instead of holding a grudge. When a leader overlooks minor mistakes made by their team members and focuses on the bigger picture. When you choose to let go of anger and treat someone with kindness despite their wrongdoing.

m: To prepare or gather generously in advance, but use economically and selectively according to actual needs.
s: When a company hires many candidates during recruitment but carefully selects only the most qualified ones for the job. When you buy a large variety of groceries but only use what you actually need for cooking. When a teacher creates many practice problems for students but assigns only the most essential ones based on their level.

l: a guest arrives as if returning home
m: to treat guests with such warmth and hospitality that they feel completely comfortable and at ease, as if they were in their own home.
s: When you visit a friend's house and they make you so comfortable that you feel like you're at your own place. When a host is so welcoming and attentive that their guests don't feel like outsiders but like family members.

m: to live in dependence on others, lacking freedom and autonomy in one's own home.
s: When someone has to stay with relatives after losing their job and feels uncomfortable because they're not independent. When a person lives with in-laws and has to follow their rules even though they're adults.

l: eat the grain of the next month during the current month
m: to spend money or resources before earning them, living beyond one's means and mortgaging the future.
s: When someone spends their entire paycheck immediately and has no money left until the next payday. When a business takes on too much debt and uses future revenue to pay for current expenses, putting itself at financial risk.

m: Much preparation or buildup with no concrete results or follow-through.
s: When a company announces a major project but nothing ever gets done. When someone talks a lot about their plans but never actually takes action. When there's a lot of hype and expectation but the actual outcome disappoints.

m: Something that is extremely luxurious, grand, and impressive in appearance.
s: When describing a fancy new building or palace with elaborate decorations and expensive materials. When someone talks about how stunning and opulent a hotel or mansion looks with all its ornate details.

l: enrich the country and strengthen the military
m: A nation achieves prosperity and power by building economic wealth and military strength together.
s: When a government invests in both economic development and defense capabilities to become a strong nation. When discussing how successful countries balance commercial growth with military readiness.

m: A person of strong moral character will not be corrupted or morally compromised by wealth and high status.
s: When someone becomes rich or powerful but maintains their integrity and good values. When a successful person refuses to use their wealth or influence to do something unethical or immoral, showing they have principles that money cannot buy.

m: Time passes naturally and inevitably through the changing seasons, symbolizing the continuous flow of time.
s: When talking about how quickly time flies, noticing how we've gone through many seasonal cycles. When someone reflects on how life continues through its natural rhythms regardless of what happens to us individually.

m: To carefully pay attention to what people say and how they look in order to understand their true feelings or intentions.
s: When you're in a meeting and you notice your boss's facial expression change, so you adjust what you're saying to match their mood. When you're talking to a friend and you can tell by their expression that they're upset even though they say everything is fine, so you know to ask what's wrong.

l: the few cannot overcome the many
m: A small number of people cannot defeat a large number of people in conflict or competition.
s: When a small team is overwhelmed by a much larger opposing force. When one person tries to argue against a group and realizes they're outnumbered and outmatched. When a small company cannot compete against industry giants with more resources and manpower.

l: lacking integrity and rare in shame
m: Completely shameless and devoid of moral integrity, showing no sense of dignity or honor.
s: When someone acts without any embarrassment despite doing something clearly wrong or immoral. When a public figure engages in blatantly corrupt behavior and shows no remorse whatsoever. When a person repeatedly lies and cheats without any sign of guilt or self-awareness.

m: Having limited knowledge and experience due to narrow exposure to the world and lack of learning.
s: When someone makes a naive comment because they haven't traveled or been exposed to different cultures. When a person doesn't understand current events or popular culture because they rarely read or interact with others.

m: There are very few of something; the quantity or number is extremely small and scarce.
s: When only a handful of people show up to an event you organized. When a store has almost no stock left of a popular item. When there are barely any qualified candidates applying for a difficult job position.

l: as sparse as the morning stars
m: Something is extremely rare or scarce, with very few examples remaining.
s: When there are only a handful of tickets left for a popular concert. When you're looking for skilled craftspeople who still practice a traditional art form, but almost none exist anymore.

l: contend for every inch of earth
m: To fight fiercely for every piece of territory or resource, refusing to concede even the smallest amount.
s: When a country refuses to give up any land in a territorial dispute. When two companies are competing intensely in a market and neither wants to lose even a small customer base. When a sports team plays with complete determination and refuses to let the opponent score without a fight.

l: not departing by a single step
m: To stay extremely close to someone or something at all times, never leaving their side even for a moment.
s: When a young child refuses to let their parent out of sight and follows them everywhere around the house. When a bodyguard stays right next to an important person during an event. When someone is so devoted to another person that they are always together and never apart.

m: Unable to make any progress or move forward due to severe obstacles or constraints.
s: When a project is completely blocked by bureaucratic red tape and you can't proceed at all. When someone is so restricted by their circumstances that they cannot take any action forward. When a crowded area is so packed that you literally cannot walk or move anywhere.

l: not a blade of grass remains
m: Everything is completely destroyed or consumed, leaving nothing behind.
s: When invading troops destroy a land so thoroughly that nothing is left. When someone uses up all their resources completely, leaving nothing for the future. When a natural disaster like locusts or fire wipes out an entire area completely.

p: cùn jīn nán mǎi cùn guāng yīn
l: An inch of gold cannot buy an inch of time
m: Time is more valuable than money and cannot be purchased no matter how wealthy you are.
s: When someone is wasting time doing unproductive things instead of working on important goals. When a person realizes that spending money on shortcuts to save time is actually worthwhile because time is irreplaceable.

l: playing the lute to a cow
m: It is futile to try to communicate something valuable or sophisticated to someone who cannot understand or appreciate it.
s: When you try to explain a complex concept to someone who has no interest in learning. When you share your passion for art or music with people who only care about money and don't value such things. When you give thoughtful advice to someone who refuses to listen and won't change their behavior.

l: apply medicine according to the symptoms
m: To address a problem by using a solution that is specifically tailored to its root cause.
s: When a teacher identifies why a student is struggling and adjusts their teaching method to help them learn better. When a manager figures out what's really causing low team morale and takes action to fix that specific issue rather than applying a generic solution.

m: To deliberately look for reasons to cause trouble, conflict, or disputes where none existed before.
s: When someone shows up to a gathering and immediately starts arguments over minor things. When a coworker constantly creates drama by picking fights over trivial matters. When a person seems determined to turn peaceful situations into confrontations.

l: search for the root and investigate the bottom
m: To investigate thoroughly and get to the very root cause or fundamental truth of a matter.
s: When a detective is trying to solve a crime by examining all the evidence and uncovering what really happened. When you keep asking your friend questions about why they're upset until you understand the real reason behind their sadness.

m: To indulge in carefree enjoyment and entertainment without regard for responsibility or consequences.
s: When someone spends all their money on parties and vacations instead of saving for the future. When a person ignores their work duties to go out and have fun constantly.

l: seeking death and looking for life
m: To engage in reckless or dangerous behavior that invites disaster or death upon oneself.
s: When someone keeps doing extremely dangerous things despite warnings, like driving recklessly or taking deadly drugs. When a person deliberately provokes dangerous criminals or puts themselves in life-threatening situations repeatedly.

m: to plagiarize or borrow phrases and passages from existing works without originality or proper attribution.
s: When a student copies passages from Wikipedia and pastes them into their essay without rewriting. When a writer lifts entire phrases from famous books and uses them as their own work without citation.

l: Life as long as the Southern Mountain
m: A wish for someone to have a long and enduring life, comparing their lifespan to the permanence of mountains.
s: When you want to wish someone a long and healthy life, especially at birthday celebrations or retirement parties. When expressing hope that an elderly person will live many more years in good health.

l: Long life ends in the proper bedroom
m: To die of old age peacefully in one's own bed, having lived a full and natural lifespan.
s: When an elderly person passes away naturally after living a long life, without suffering or tragedy. When someone dies at home surrounded by family after reaching an advanced age, rather than dying suddenly or violently.

m: to offer high positions and make generous promises in order to gain support or loyalty, often without genuine intention to fulfill them.
s: When a politician promises people various benefits and positions just to get their votes before an election. When a company recruits someone by offering promotions and raises that never actually materialize after they join.

m: To be uncertain and unable to decide whether to believe something or not, remaining in a state of doubt and skepticism.
s: When you receive news that sounds too good to be true but comes from a usually reliable source, you're not sure whether to trust it. When someone makes a promise but has broken promises before, and you're uncertain whether to believe them this time.

m: To make up for past mistakes or wrongdoings by performing good deeds or achieving positive results.
s: When someone who has made serious errors at work then goes on to complete an important project successfully. When a friend betrays your trust but later does something significant to prove they have changed and want to restore the relationship.

m: To atone for past wrongdoings by performing good deeds or making significant contributions that offset previous mistakes.
s: When someone who made serious errors tries to prove their worth through hard work and positive actions. When a person in trouble attempts to regain trust by doing something valuable to compensate for their past misbehavior.

p: jiāng yù qǔ zhī ， bì xiān yǔ zhī
l: If you want to take it, you must first give it
m: To gain something you desire, you must first make sacrifices or investments; you cannot receive without giving first.
s: When a business owner invests heavily in customer service to build loyalty and eventually increase profits. When someone volunteers their time and skills to build a network, knowing that future opportunities will come from the relationships they cultivate.

l: using the plan as the plan
m: To turn an enemy's own scheme or trick against them by pretending to go along with it.
s: When someone tries to deceive you but you see through their trick and use it to your advantage instead. When a scammer's own con is used to catch them in the act.

l: taking the mistake and continuing with it
m: To accept an error and proceed based on it rather than correcting course, often making the best of a bad situation.
s: When you've made a mistake in a plan but decide to just keep going with it anyway instead of starting over. When someone discovers they've been doing something wrong the whole time but figures they might as well finish it now that they're already committed.

l: revere the teacher and value the Way
m: To respect teachers and value the pursuit of knowledge and moral cultivation.
s: When someone shows great respect for their mentors and takes their teachings seriously. When a student is dedicated to learning and follows the guidance of wise teachers. When a culture emphasizes the importance of education and honoring those who teach.

p: xiǎo bù rěn zé luàn dà móu
l: A little impatience then disrupts a great plan
m: Failure to tolerate minor annoyances or setbacks can jeopardize a major objective or long-term goal.
s: When someone gets angry over a small disagreement with their business partner and quits, ruining a potentially successful venture. When a student gives up on studying for a difficult exam because they're frustrated with one confusing chapter, sabotaging their chances of graduating.

m: Petty villains or insignificant people acting arrogantly and causing trouble, often used to dismiss their actions as merely ridiculous antics.
s: When minor troublemakers or insignificant people are trying to cause chaos but you don't take them seriously because they're not actually powerful. When someone is making a big show of acting tough but everyone knows they're actually unimportant and harmless.

m: A woman of modest or humble background who is delicate, refined, and graceful in manner despite her lower social status.
s: When describing a girl from a poor family who carries herself with elegance and poise. When someone admires a woman for her gentle demeanor and refined taste despite coming from humble circumstances.

m: Something is small in size but elegant, refined, and skillfully made with great attention to detail.
s: When you admire a tiny decorative box or piece of jewelry that is beautifully crafted despite its small size. When someone has a petite figure but moves gracefully and elegantly. When describing a small apartment that is cleverly designed and efficiently organized with every space serving a purpose.

l: a small witch meeting a great witch
m: When compared to something far more impressive or powerful, something seems insignificant or inferior by contrast.
s: When you think your cooking skills are good until you taste a professional chef's food. When a company's small achievement is overshadowed by a competitor's major breakthrough. When someone brags about their car until they see a luxury sports car pull up next to them.

m: To act with extreme caution and careful attention to avoid making mistakes or causing harm.
s: When someone is handling a delicate vase and moves very slowly and carefully so it doesn't break. When a new employee is learning their job and does everything very cautiously to avoid making errors. When someone is walking on thin ice and takes each step very deliberately.

m: Trivial favors or minor benefits that are often given with the intention of gaining favor or loyalty from others.
s: When a politician gives out free gifts to win votes. When a boss occasionally buys lunch for employees to make them work harder without giving real raises or benefits.

m: To act in a timid, hesitant, or overly cautious manner, lacking boldness or confidence in one's actions.
s: When someone is afraid to take risks or make decisions and keeps second-guessing themselves. When a new employee is too nervous and careful, moving slowly and hesitantly instead of being decisive and confident at work.

m: To make a first attempt or modest display of one's abilities to gauge one's competence or see how others respond.
s: When someone does a small project to see if they're good at something before committing to a bigger one. When a new employee takes on a minor task to prove their skills to their boss. When an athlete competes in a local tournament before trying out for a major league.

l: make a small matter into a big production
m: To exaggerate the importance of a minor issue or make an unnecessarily big fuss about something trivial.
s: When your roommate gets upset about a small scratch on a shared cup and demands a replacement. When someone calls an emergency meeting to discuss a tiny administrative detail that could have been handled in an email.

m: Being young and lacking experience or worldly knowledge about how things work.
s: When someone makes a naive decision because they haven't dealt with the world much yet. When a teenager does something foolish because they haven't lived long enough to understand the consequences. When you look back on your younger self and realize how innocent and uninformed you were about life.

c: 少壮不努力，老大徒伤悲
p: shào zhuàng bù nǔ lì ， lǎo dà tú shāng bēi
l: If you do not work hard when young and strong, you will only grieve uselessly when old and weak.
m: Wasting your youth through laziness and lack of effort will inevitably lead to regret and hardship in old age.
s: When a young person squanders their opportunities to study or develop skills, then later realizes they have no prospects. When someone in their prime refuses to work hard and later complains about being poor or unsuccessful in middle age.

m: Something that is incomplete, disorganized, or lacking proper beginning and ending structure.
s: When someone tells a story that jumps around and doesn't make sense because it's missing important details at the start and end. When a project is poorly planned with no clear starting point or conclusion.

m: A young person who behaves with maturity, wisdom, and composure far beyond their years.
s: When a teenager shows remarkable responsibility and good judgment that surprises adults around them. When a child demonstrates thoughtfulness and emotional intelligence that seems unusual for their age.

m: Someone who lacks experience tends to be surprised or amazed by ordinary things that are actually quite common.
s: When a person from a remote village visits a big city and is shocked by simple things like escalators or traffic lights. When someone who has never traveled abroad acts overly impressed by basic foreign customs or everyday items.

l: you deceive me and I deceive you
m: People engage in mutual deception and cunning schemes against each other, each trying to outwit the other for personal gain.
s: When business competitors are constantly trying to trick each other to get ahead. When friends in a group are all being dishonest and manipulative rather than trusting one another. In a workplace where everyone is scheming behind each other's backs instead of working together honestly.

l: sharp and sour, cutting and harsh
m: Being cruel, mean-spirited, and verbally cutting in one's remarks toward others.
s: When someone makes hurtful, sarcastic comments that are designed to wound or demean others. When a person has a reputation for saying cruel things about people's appearance, abilities, or character. When someone responds to criticism with harsh, bitter remarks that attack the other person instead of addressing the actual issue.

l: discuss the matter based on the matter itself
m: To evaluate or discuss something objectively based solely on the facts and merits of that specific situation, without bringing in personal feelings, unrelated issues, or past grievances.
s: When you're trying to have a fair conversation about a work problem and want to focus only on what happened without bringing up old arguments. When someone is being accused of something and you want to judge them based only on that specific incident, not their general reputation.

m: To make use of whatever materials or resources are readily available in the local environment rather than seeking them from elsewhere.
s: When you're camping and build a shelter using branches and leaves found nearby instead of bringing supplies. When a teacher uses everyday classroom objects to demonstrate a science concept instead of waiting for special equipment. When someone repairs their car using tools and parts they happen to have at hand.

l: occupy a position without substance and eat without merit
m: To hold an official position without doing any actual work or contributing anything of value.
s: When a company executive collects a large salary but never shows up to work or makes any decisions. When someone gets promoted based on connections rather than ability and just sits around doing nothing all day.

l: corpses lying sprawled across the wilderness
m: A place where numerous people have died in violence or disaster, leaving many bodies scattered on the ground.
s: When describing a battlefield after a major conflict with many casualties. When talking about the aftermath of a devastating disaster or massacre where bodies cover the ground. When discussing historical tragedies or wars that resulted in massive loss of life.

l: A foot is short while an inch is long
m: Everyone has different strengths and weaknesses; what one person lacks in one area, they may excel in another.
s: When comparing two people's abilities and realizing they're good at different things. When someone is not good at math but is an excellent writer, showing that different skills matter for different people.

p: jìn rén shì ， tīng tiān mìng
l: exhaust human effort, listen to heaven's decree
m: Do everything within your power to accomplish something, and then accept whatever outcome results as beyond your control.
s: When you've prepared thoroughly for an exam and studied hard, but you know the final grade depends on factors you can't control. When a business owner has done all they can to run their company well, but economic conditions or market forces might still determine success or failure.

m: To do your best effort within your ability and circumstances, without necessarily guaranteeing success.
s: When you've tried as hard as you can on a difficult exam but might not get the highest score. When someone works on a project with full dedication even though they don't have all the resources they ideally would want.

m: To achieve the highest degree of perfection by doing everything as well as possible in every aspect.
s: When describing a performance, product, or work that has no flaws and represents the absolute best quality. When someone has put in maximum effort and attention to detail to make something as excellent as it can possibly be. When praising something that meets or exceeds all expectations in every single way.

m: Everything turns out exactly as desired, satisfying everyone completely.
s: When a party goes perfectly and all your guests have a wonderful time. When a project succeeds beyond expectations and makes everyone involved happy. When a vacation goes exactly as planned with no problems or disappointments.

m: To make an all-out effort and do everything possible to accomplish something, holding nothing back.
s: When someone works as hard as they possibly can on a project despite difficulties. When a parent does everything in their power to provide the best for their children. When a team member gives their absolute best effort to help the company succeed.

m: A subordinate part becomes so powerful that the main authority can no longer control it.
s: When a company's branch office grows so large and independent that headquarters can no longer manage it effectively. When a politician's local supporters become so influential that they control the politician instead of the other way around.

m: A state of nervousness and discomfort caused by feeling trapped, restricted, or anxious in a situation.
s: When someone is sitting in a waiting room before an important job interview and keeps fidgeting nervously. When a person feels uncomfortable and tense at a formal dinner where they don't know many people. When someone is stuck in a cramped elevator with strangers and starts to feel anxious and restless.

m: Things of a similar kind appear continuously one after another without end or limit.
s: When new problems keep appearing in a project even after you solve one. When a store keeps introducing new product variations and you can't keep track of them all. When scandals or controversies about a celebrity keep surfacing repeatedly.

m: During times of safety and comfort, one should remain vigilant and prepared for potential future difficulties.
s: When a company is doing well financially but should still plan for economic downturns. When someone is healthy but should maintain good habits to prevent future illness. When a country is at peace but maintains a strong military to deter potential threats.

m: Someone has hidden, malicious intentions that are difficult to discern or predict.
s: When a coworker is being unusually nice to you but you suspect they have ulterior motives. When someone's friendly behavior seems fake and you sense they're plotting something behind the scenes.

m: To occupy a superior or commanding position, either physically or metaphorically, giving oneself an advantage over others.
s: When a company with more resources treats smaller competitors with disdain. When someone with more experience looks down on beginners with contempt rather than helping them learn.

m: To be arrogant and contemptuous of others because of one's superior position or status.
s: When a successful executive looks down on their employees and refuses to listen to their ideas. When a wealthy person treats service workers disrespectfully because they believe their money makes them better than others.

m: To be forced into making a false confession through torture or coercion rather than truthful admission.
s: When someone admits to something they didn't actually do just to make the abuse stop. When a person gives a confession under extreme pressure or threats, even though it's not true. When authorities extract statements from suspects through violent interrogation methods.

m: So few in number that they can be counted on the fingers of one hand; extremely rare or scarce.
s: When describing how few qualified candidates applied for a highly specialized position. When talking about how many times you've seen a particular movie or event happen in your entire life.

m: To greedily consume or indulge in something with excessive enthusiasm and lack of restraint, often used to describe someone savoring empty words or hollow boasts.
s: When someone eagerly believes and spreads exaggerated claims or rumors without questioning their truth. When a person excitedly accepts flattery or compliments that are clearly insincere and over-the-top.

l: repeatedly taught yet does not change
m: Someone persistently refuses to correct their behavior despite being repeatedly instructed, warned, or punished.
s: When a student keeps breaking the same classroom rule even after being scolded multiple times. When a colleague continues to make the same mistake at work despite your corrections. When someone you know keeps doing something wrong no matter how many times you've tried to help them see the error of their ways.

m: Something happens multiple times in succession or over and over again with great frequency.
s: When your child keeps asking for the same toy even after you've said no several times. When a coworker submits the same flawed report multiple times despite your corrections.

m: Something that happens so often that it is no longer novel or noteworthy.
s: When you see the same type of problem occur regularly in your workplace and nobody pays attention anymore. When a celebrity's scandals are so frequent that the news doesn't surprise anyone anymore.

m: Something that has been tried many times and has consistently worked or proven effective every single time.
s: When a recipe you've made dozens of times always turns out perfectly. When a particular strategy in a video game has never let you down, no matter how many times you use it. When a trusted method for solving a problem has succeeded every time you've attempted it.

l: tread peril as if it were level ground
m: To face danger or difficult situations with calm composure and without fear, treating serious threats as though they were insignificant.
s: When a experienced soldier remains unafraid during a dangerous mission because they have trained for years. When a skilled surgeon performs a complex operation without hesitation because they have done it many times before.

m: Describes people or things that are scattered far and wide across distant places, separated by great distances.
s: When friends from college have moved to different cities and rarely see each other anymore. When family members are spread out living in different countries and it's hard to stay connected.

m: A place has stunning natural scenery with picturesque mountains and pristine waters.
s: When describing a tourist destination known for its breathtaking landscape. When someone talks about a remote area they visited that had gorgeous mountains and clear rivers. When praising the natural beauty of a national park or countryside region.

m: An idiom referring to the rarest and most luxurious food delicacies available from both mountainous regions and the sea.
s: When describing an elaborate feast with extremely expensive and hard-to-find ingredients. When someone is bragging about the lavish banquet they attended with all sorts of exotic dishes. When talking about a fancy restaurant that serves only the most exclusive and premium ingredients from around the world.

m: To be in a completely hopeless situation with no way out or no resources left.
s: When a company has run out of money and has no options left to survive. When someone has tried everything they can think of and still cannot solve their problem. When a person feels trapped with no possible escape route from their difficult circumstances.

p: shān yǔ yù lái fēng mǎn lóu
l: The wind fills the tower as the mountain rain is about to come
m: Warning signs and tension precede an impending crisis or major event, like how wind precedes a storm.
s: When you can feel tension building in a relationship before a big argument happens. When there are obvious signs that a company is about to go through major layoffs or changes. When political tensions are rising and you sense a conflict is coming soon.

m: Something that is enduring, timeless, and will last forever, like the eternal nature of mountains and flowing rivers.
s: When you want to express that a friendship or love will last forever. When describing something that has stood the test of time and will continue to do so indefinitely.

l: How can there be such a principle?
