s: When someone makes a comment that seems innocent on the surface but you sense they're really criticizing you indirectly. When a boss compliments your work but you can tell they're actually disappointed by their tone and body language.

l: weak and unable to withstand wind
m: Someone is extremely frail, delicate, or physically weak, appearing as though they could be knocked over by a strong breeze.
s: When describing someone who is very thin and looks like they might blow away in strong wind. When you see a sickly person who appears extremely fragile and vulnerable to illness.

m: Extremely frail and delicate, so physically weak that even light clothing feels burdensome.
s: Describing someone who is gravely ill and has lost so much weight that their clothes hang loosely on them. When someone is so emaciated from disease or starvation that they appear paper-thin and fragile. Describing an elderly or sickly person whose body has become so skeletal that they seem unable to support even the lightest garments.

m: In a competitive world, the strong naturally dominate and consume the weak, following the law of nature.
s: When describing a harsh business environment where only the most powerful companies survive. When explaining why smaller nations struggle against larger, more militarily advanced ones. When someone faces a situation where they must compete fiercely or be eliminated by stronger competitors.

m: An extremely small piece of land or territory, often used to describe a nation or region that is geographically insignificant.
s: When describing a small island nation that has limited land area. When talking about how a tiny country punches above its weight in international affairs despite its small size.

m: People rejoice together and celebrate mutually when someone achieves success or gains an advantageous position.
s: When a group of friends all get promoted around the same time and throw a celebration together. When colleagues are excited because one of them just landed a big client and they know it will benefit the whole team.

l: bullets exhausted and food cut off
m: In a state of complete desperation where all resources and supplies are depleted, leaving no means to continue or survive.
s: When a company has spent all its budget and has no income coming in, leaving them unable to pay employees or operate. When a soldier or army has run out of ammunition and food during a siege or battle, making their situation hopeless. When someone has used up all their savings and has no way to earn more money to support themselves.

p: qiáng zhōng zì yǒu qiáng zhōng shǒu
l: Among the strong there is always someone stronger
m: No matter how skilled or powerful you are, there will always be someone more skilled or powerful than you.
s: When a talented athlete finally meets their match in competition. When a successful businessperson encounters a competitor with even greater abilities. When someone who considers themselves the best in their field discovers someone even more talented.

l: to force the strong to do what is difficult
m: To demand that someone do something beyond their ability or capacity; to make an unreasonable request of someone.
s: When your boss asks you to complete a project in an impossible timeframe when you don't have the resources. When a friend pressures you to help them move on a day you've already told them you're sick and can't.

m: To impose one's own decisions or policies on the people against their wishes and desires.
s: When a government implements unpopular policies that the majority of citizens oppose. When a leader makes important decisions without consulting or listening to what the people actually want.

p: qiáng jiàng shǒu xià wú ruò bīng
l: Under a strong general, there are no weak soldiers
m: A capable leader brings out the best in their team, making even ordinary people perform exceptionally well through their leadership and example.
s: When a skilled manager transforms a struggling department into a high-performing team. When a great coach takes over a losing team and suddenly they start winning because the players are motivated and well-organized.

m: To use forceful or clever arguments to defend an unreasonable position or to twist the truth in your favor.
s: When someone argues loudly and confidently even though they know they are wrong. When a person uses twisted logic or aggressive debate tactics to win an argument they shouldn't win.

m: To have an intense, urgent desire to return home or to a beloved place.
s: When someone has been away on a long business trip and can barely wait to get back to their family. When a traveler is so homesick during vacation that they keep checking flight times to leave early and return home.

l: return to the root and settle the bottom
m: When all is said and done, the fundamental cause or essential truth of a matter is what ultimately matters.
s: When you're analyzing why a project failed and you trace it back to poor planning from the start. When someone keeps blaming external factors for their problems, but ultimately it comes down to their own lack of effort.

m: To fully deserve recognition, praise, or a position based on one's genuine merit and accomplishments.
s: When someone wins an award and everyone agrees they were the most qualified candidate. When a hardworking employee gets promoted and nobody questions the decision because they clearly earned it.

l: when duty calls, do not yield
m: When faced with a responsibility or opportunity to do what is right, one should take it on without hesitation or modesty.
s: When someone sees a problem that needs fixing and steps up to handle it immediately without waiting for others. When a person with the right skills for a job volunteers without false modesty because they know they can do it best.

l: the pressing business of the moment
m: The most urgent and important matter that needs to be dealt with immediately.
s: When you need to focus on the most critical task before anything else. When someone is distracted by minor issues when there's a major problem that needs immediate attention.

l: to lose face on the spot
m: To be embarrassed or humiliated in front of others in the moment.
s: When someone makes a terrible mistake during a presentation in front of their boss and colleagues. When a person trips and falls in front of a large crowd at a public event. When someone says something inappropriate at a dinner party and everyone goes silent.

m: A sudden, harsh reality check or warning that shocks someone into awareness and forces them to change their behavior or perspective.
s: When someone is living in denial and finally gets confronted with the hard truth that makes them wake up. When a person receives unexpected criticism that makes them realize they've been going down the wrong path.

p: dāng jú zhě mí ， páng guān zhě qīng
l: The person involved is confused, the bystander is clear
m: People directly involved in a situation often lack objectivity and clarity, while detached observers can see things more clearly.
s: When you're too emotionally invested in a problem to think straight, but a friend can immediately spot the obvious solution. When someone is caught up in a conflict and can't see their own role in it, but others watching can clearly identify what went wrong.

l: when the opportunity comes, decide immediately
m: When a critical moment arrives, one should make a decisive decision without hesitation or delay.
s: When your boss suddenly offers you a promotion and you need to accept or decline on the spot. When you see a great investment opportunity but only have a few hours to commit your money. When you're negotiating a business deal and need to make a final decision quickly before the other party walks away.

l: treat as wind passing by the ear
m: To ignore or disregard what someone says, treating their words as though they have no importance or effect.
s: When someone gives you advice but you completely ignore it and do whatever you want anyway. When a boss gives instructions but an employee just pretends to listen and doesn't follow through.

m: Circumstances are so difficult or urgent that one is compelled to take action or make difficult decisions.
s: When someone is facing mounting pressure from their job and has no choice but to work harder. When a business must adapt quickly because market conditions are changing rapidly and leaving them behind.

m: To be completely alone and without companionship, often implying a state of loneliness or isolation.
s: When someone has lost all their friends and family and has no one to rely on. When a person is left behind by everyone and feels utterly abandoned and isolated.

m: A wide variety of different types, kinds, or categories of people or things.
s: When describing a diverse group of people with different backgrounds and personalities at a party. When talking about the many different styles and designs of products available in a store.

m: Two people or things are so closely connected that they are always together and cannot be separated.
s: When two best friends do everything together and are never seen apart. When a child clings to their parent and follows them everywhere they go. When a husband and wife are so devoted to each other that they're constantly by each other's side.

l: form and shadow mutually console each other
m: To be so lonely that one's only companion is one's own shadow, expressing profound isolation and desolation.
s: When someone has lost all their friends and spends all their time alone at home with no one to talk to. When an elderly person lives by themselves after their spouse passes away and has no family nearby to visit them.

m: Someone's behavior, manner, or actions appear suspicious and warrant doubt or investigation.
s: When someone is acting strangely and avoiding eye contact, making you wonder what they're hiding. When a person is lurking around a place where they don't belong and their nervous behavior makes them seem guilty.

m: To display refined manners, politeness, and elegant behavior in all interactions.
s: When someone always says please and thank you, maintains good posture, and treats everyone with respect. When describing a person who never raises their voice and always knows the right thing to say in social situations.

m: Something is so obvious and clear that it cannot be denied or hidden from anyone.
s: When someone's talent or skill is so obvious that everyone immediately recognizes it. When the truth about a situation becomes impossible to conceal or dispute, no matter how hard someone tries to hide it.

m: Something that is complete, thorough, and absolute in every aspect from beginning to end.
s: When someone is completely and utterly wrong about something. When a plan fails at every stage without any success whatsoever. When describing someone who is thoroughly honest or dishonest in all their dealings.

p: bǐ yī shí ， cǐ yī shí
l: That time is one time, this time is another time
m: Circumstances change over time, so what was true or relevant in the past may no longer apply to the present.
s: When someone brings up a mistake you made years ago, you might say the situation is different now. When technology or market conditions change so dramatically that old strategies no longer work. When someone argues that a historical event justifies a current decision, but you point out that times have changed.

m: Traveling or working back and forth without achieving any meaningful result or progress.
s: When you keep going back and forth to a government office trying to complete paperwork but nothing gets resolved. When someone spends weeks commuting to interviews but doesn't get the job.

l: proceed directly according to one's feelings
m: To act in a straightforward and direct manner without hesitation or detours, following one's instincts or intentions openly.
s: When someone cuts through all the complicated procedures and goes straight to solving the problem. When a person speaks their mind directly without worrying about social niceties or takes the most efficient path to their goal without overthinking it.

m: The way a person behaves toward others and conducts themselves in social interactions and everyday dealings.
s: When someone has good manners and knows how to interact respectfully with different types of people. When evaluating whether a colleague is professional and courteous in their interactions with clients and coworkers. When describing someone who is tactful and considerate in how they handle social situations and relationships.

l: wait for the price and then sell
m: To hold out for a better offer or higher price rather than accepting the first opportunity that comes along.
s: When someone refuses a job offer because they're waiting for a better position with higher pay. When a homeowner delays selling their house because they believe the market price will increase soon.

m: Effort that is expended without producing any useful result or accomplishment.
s: When you spend hours studying for a test but still fail it. When a company invests millions in a product that nobody wants to buy. When someone tries to convince a stubborn person to change their mind but nothing works.

l: gain does not compensate for loss
m: The benefits obtained are not worth the costs, sacrifices, or negative consequences incurred.
s: When someone spends a huge amount of money on a vacation but gets sick the whole time and doesn't enjoy it. When a student cheats on an exam, gets caught, and gets expelled even though they might have passed honestly with some studying.

m: To be exceptionally blessed with natural advantages, talents, or favorable circumstances that others do not possess.
s: When someone is born with extraordinary abilities or talents that give them an unfair advantage over others. When a place has ideal natural resources or geographical advantages that make it naturally prosperous.

l: gaining an inch, advancing a foot
m: When someone is given a small concession or advantage, they become greedy and demand much more.
s: When you give your child a small treat and they immediately ask for something much bigger. When a coworker is given a flexible work arrangement and starts taking excessive liberties with their schedule.

l: the heart obtains and the hand responds
m: To perform a task with such skill and familiarity that your hands move naturally without conscious thought, achieving perfect coordination between intention and action.
s: When a musician plays a piece they've practiced thousands of times and their fingers move perfectly without thinking. When an experienced cook prepares a familiar dish and everything flows smoothly from preparation to plating.

m: To become so pleased with oneself that one loses composure and behaves inappropriately or arrogantly.
s: When someone wins an award and then starts bragging excessively about their abilities. When a person gets promoted and suddenly becomes rude and dismissive to their former colleagues. When someone succeeds once and acts like they're now an expert in everything.

m: To come back successfully after winning a battle, competition, or difficult challenge.
s: When a sports team wins a championship and comes back home to celebrate with their fans. When someone completes a difficult project successfully and returns to share the good news with their family.

l: obtain and pass, then pass again
m: To get by with minimum effort and accept things as they are without striving for improvement or excellence.
s: When someone does just enough work to not get fired but makes no effort to excel or improve. When a student passes tests with mediocre grades and doesn't care about doing better. When someone maintains a relationship without putting in real emotional effort or investment.

p: dé dào duō zhù ， shī dào guǎ zhù
l: The virtuous gain much help, the vicious gain little help
m: Those who act morally and justly will receive support from many people, while those who act unethically will find themselves isolated and abandoned.
s: When a leader treats their employees fairly and with respect, people are willing to go the extra mile to help them succeed. When a boss is dishonest and exploits their workers, employees will do the bare minimum and won't support them when they face difficulties.

l: Having obtained Long, gaze towards Shu
m: Once you gain something, you immediately desire something else; greed and ambition are never satisfied.
s: When someone gets a promotion and immediately starts complaining about not having the executive position. When a person buys a nice car but soon becomes envious of their neighbor's luxury vehicle. When someone achieves one goal but instantly focuses on a bigger, more ambitious target instead of enjoying their current success.

l: Having caught the fish, forget the net
m: Once you have achieved your goal, you forget or abandon the means that helped you succeed, showing ingratitude toward those who assisted you.
s: When someone gets a promotion with their mentor's help but then stops acknowledging or helping their mentor. When a student passes an exam thanks to a teacher's guidance but later refuses to credit or assist that teacher.

l: follow the name and hold responsible for the reality
m: Judge something or someone by whether their actual substance and performance match their stated title, function, or promise.
s: When you hire someone with impressive credentials but they can't actually do the job. When a company claims to be environmentally friendly but their practices don't match their marketing. When a leader has a grand title but fails to demonstrate the competence that title implies.

m: Progress through a systematic and gradual process, moving step by step in an orderly manner without rushing.
s: When teaching a child to read, you start with simple letters, then move to words, then sentences. When learning a new skill like programming, you begin with basic concepts before tackling complex projects. When recovering from an injury, a doctor recommends gradual exercise rather than intense activity immediately.

m: To guide someone patiently and gently, using kind persuasion to lead them toward the right path or understanding.
s: When a teacher takes time to explain a difficult concept to a struggling student in a calm and encouraging way. When a parent gradually helps a child understand why a certain behavior is wrong, without scolding or forcing them.

l: follow rules and tread established paths
m: To strictly adhere to rules, customs, and established conventions without deviation or innovation.
s: When someone always follows the rules and never takes risks or tries anything new. When an employee always does things exactly as they've been taught and refuses to think creatively. When a student studies only what the teacher says and never explores beyond the curriculum.

m: Something so small or insignificant that it is not worth paying attention to or considering important.
s: When someone dismisses a minor problem as unimportant. When a wealthy person gives a small donation and says it's just a tiny amount. When you make a small mistake but think it doesn't really matter in the big picture.

l: slight to the point of being barely noticeable
m: Something is so small, insignificant, or trivial that it is almost negligible or hardly matters at all.
s: When comparing your savings to the total cost of a house, your current amount seems utterly insignificant. When someone points out a tiny flaw in your work that doesn't affect the overall quality or outcome. When a minor inconvenience happens but it's so small that you decide it's not worth complaining about.

m: A small amount of words or subtle expression contains profound wisdom and deep significance.
s: When a teacher gives a brief piece of advice that completely changes how you see a problem. When a mentor says something short but it makes you think deeply about life. When a famous person's simple quote turns out to have layers of deeper meaning.

m: A person who possesses both moral integrity and professional competence or intelligence.
s: When describing an ideal leader or employee who is not only skilled at their job but also honest and ethical. When praising someone who is both intelligent and has strong character.

m: A person of exceptional moral character who commands great respect and admiration from others.
s: When describing an elderly teacher who has spent decades helping students and is universally respected in the community. When referring to a senior colleague who is known for their integrity and wisdom, and everyone looks up to them for guidance.

m: Your mind is not focused on what you are doing; you are distracted or inattentive.
s: When someone is physically present but clearly thinking about something else and not paying attention. When a student sits in class but their mind is elsewhere and they don't absorb any information. When you're talking to a friend but they keep looking at their phone and missing what you're saying.

l: have a number in one's heart
m: To have a clear understanding or accurate assessment of a situation; to know exactly what to expect or how things stand.
s: When you've done this job many times before and you know exactly how long it will take and what the outcome will be. When a manager reviews the quarterly numbers and already knows which departments performed well and which ones underperformed.

m: One's mind is extremely confused, anxious, and disorganized, unable to think clearly or focus.
s: When you're so stressed about multiple problems that you can't concentrate on anything. When someone is so emotionally overwhelmed that they can't make a decision or remember what they were doing.

m: To be completely drained both physically and mentally from prolonged effort or hardship.
s: When someone has been working on a difficult project for months and is completely burned out, both tired and emotionally drained. When a caregiver has been looking after a sick family member for years and feels utterly depleted in every way.

m: Constant worry and effort without progress leads to physical and mental exhaustion, making things worse instead of better.
s: When someone works themselves to exhaustion trying to solve a problem but their anxiety only makes them more confused and less effective. When a student studies so hard out of stress that they become more tired and forgetful, actually performing worse on the exam.

m: To be sincere and honest, with your words and actions reflecting your true thoughts without deception.
s: When someone is completely trustworthy and says exactly what they mean without pretense. When a person's actions match their words and you never have to worry about them being two-faced.

m: To feel intense emotional pain or deep sorrow, as if one's heart is being slashed by a blade.
s: When someone receives devastating news about losing a loved one and is overwhelmed with grief. When a person realizes they've made a terrible mistake that has hurt someone they care about deeply.

l: heart at peace and reason justified
m: To feel completely at ease and justified in one's actions because one believes they are morally right.
s: When someone does the right thing even though it was difficult, and they feel good about their decision afterward. When a person acts with integrity and has no guilt or regrets about what they did.

l: a broad heart and a fat body
m: When someone is content and free from worries, they tend to gain weight because they eat well and live comfortably without stress.
s: When someone gets married and starts living a comfortable life, they often gain weight because they're happy and well-fed. When a friend stops worrying about their problems and starts enjoying life, you notice they've gained some weight because they're eating better and less stressed.

m: To remain calm, peaceful, and composed in one's mind and emotions regardless of circumstances.
s: When someone stays patient and doesn't get angry during a difficult situation. When a person responds to criticism with understanding instead of getting defensive. When someone maintains their composure even though things aren't going their way.

m: Two people have a deep spiritual connection and understand each other perfectly without needing to speak.
s: When two best friends can communicate just by looking at each other without saying a word. When a couple has been together so long that they instinctively know what the other is thinking or feeling.

m: To feel discontented, resentful, or unhappy about something while keeping those negative feelings inside.
s: When an employee disagrees with their boss's decision but stays quiet instead of speaking up. When someone has been treated unfairly and can't stop feeling bitter about it, even though they don't complain openly.

m: To harbor secret sinister intentions or ulterior motives that one conceals from others.
s: When you suspect someone is being friendly to you only because they want something from you. When a coworker seems overly helpful but you sense they are plotting to take credit for your work.

m: To be extremely anxious, impatient, or worried about something urgent.
s: When you're waiting for important test results from a doctor and can't stop thinking about it. When your child is late coming home and you're pacing back and forth, unable to relax.

m: To be genuinely convinced and willingly obedient from the heart, without any reluctance or reservation.
s: When someone is so impressed by another person's ability or character that they naturally want to follow them. When you finally understand why someone was right all along and you're happy to admit it. When a strict coach earns their team's respect through fair treatment and good results.

m: To feel happy, relaxed, and at ease with a light and pleasant mood.
s: When you finally finish a difficult project and feel relieved and happy. When someone goes on vacation and comes back feeling refreshed and cheerful. When good news arrives and lifts a burden off your shoulders.

m: To be seized with extreme fear or panic, experiencing both emotional and physical signs of terror.
s: When you hear a sudden loud noise late at night and your whole body shakes with fear. When someone gets startled by an unexpected jump scare and their heart races uncontrollably. When a student waits for exam results they're anxious about and feels physically trembling with worry.

m: To be extremely frightened or terrified, experiencing intense fear and anxiety.
s: When you're walking alone at night and hear strange noises behind you. When you're about to give a presentation in front of a large audience and your nerves are completely on edge. When you receive unexpected bad news that shocks and frightens you.

m: Being too kind-hearted and gentle to take firm action, resulting in excessive leniency or inability to be strict when necessary.
s: When a parent cannot discipline their child because they feel too sympathetic. When a manager is reluctant to fire an underperforming employee because they feel bad for them.

m: To be in a state of panic, confusion, and emotional distress where one cannot think clearly or act rationally.
s: When someone is so nervous about an exam that they can't focus or remember anything they studied. When a person receives shocking bad news and becomes so anxious they can't make decisions or speak coherently.

l: the heart has no second use
m: One cannot focus on two things at the same time; complete concentration requires undivided attention.
s: When you're trying to study but keep checking your phone, you can't do both well at the same time. When a driver is texting while driving and nearly causes an accident because their attention is split. When someone is supposed to be listening to an important presentation but is thinking about their lunch plans instead.

m: A state of perfect contentment and joy where one feels completely relaxed, peaceful, and mentally uplifted.
s: When you take a vacation to a beautiful mountain retreat and feel all your stress melt away. When someone sits in nature on a perfect sunny day and feels completely at peace and happy.

m: To suddenly understand something clearly or gain sudden insight and awareness about a situation.
s: When someone finally understands a confusing explanation after you explain it in a different way. When a person realizes the truth about a situation they were previously confused or deceived about.

m: To still feel lingering fear or dread after a frightening or traumatic experience has passed.
s: When someone survives a car accident and feels anxious every time they get back in a car. When a person has recovered from a scary incident but still feels nervous thinking about what could have happened.

p: xīn yǒu yú ér lì bù zú
l: the heart has surplus but strength is insufficient
m: One has the desire and willingness to do something, but lacks the physical ability, resources, or circumstances to accomplish it.
s: When someone wants to help you move but is too injured or tired to do the heavy lifting. When a student is motivated to learn a subject but doesn't have enough time to study because of work commitments.

p: xīn yǒu líng xī yī diǎn tōng
l: hearts have spiritual resonance with a single point of understanding
m: Two people understand each other perfectly without needing to speak, as if their minds are naturally in harmony.
s: When you and a close friend can communicate with just a glance and know exactly what the other is thinking. When two people finish each other's sentences or make the same joke at the exact same moment without planning it.

m: To be completely convinced and willingly accept something, both intellectually and emotionally.
s: When someone finally admits they were wrong after seeing clear evidence. When a person stops arguing and genuinely agrees with you, not just pretending. When a skilled teacher explains a difficult concept so well that students fully understand and accept it.

m: To be completely satisfied and content with one's circumstances or achievements.
s: When someone finally gets what they've been working toward and feels completely happy about it. When a person is no longer striving for more because they're already satisfied with what they have.

m: To feel intense, overwhelming emotions such as excitement, passion, or deep sentiment.
s: When you watch an inspiring movie and feel a rush of emotion washing over you. When you receive life-changing good news and your heart races with joy and anticipation. When listening to a powerful speech that moves you deeply and stirs your innermost feelings.

m: To lose all hope, motivation, and desire to continue; to become completely dispirited and apathetic.
s: When someone has tried so hard for so long without success that they've given up entirely. When a person stops caring about their goals or responsibilities because they feel defeated and see no point in trying anymore.

m: Someone who is both intelligent and manually talented, able to create or make things with great skill and ingenuity.
s: When describing an artist or craftsperson who can create beautiful things with their hands. When someone picks up a new craft or skill very quickly and produces excellent results. When you want to praise someone for being both creative and good at hands-on work.

m: Quick thinking combined with fast physical reflexes, enabling someone to respond promptly and effectively to unexpected situations.
s: When a waiter catches a falling glass before it hits the ground. When someone quickly spots an opportunity and acts on it before anyone else does.

m: A state of mental agitation and emotional disturbance where one cannot focus or find peace due to worry or frustration.
s: When you have so many stressful things happening at once that you can't concentrate on anything. When someone is so anxious about an upcoming exam or important event that they feel restless and irritable. When a person receives bad news and spends the whole day in a state of emotional turmoil, unable to settle down.

m: Two people understand each other perfectly without needing to speak or explain explicitly.
s: When you and a friend exchange a glance and both know exactly what the other is thinking without saying anything. When colleagues work together so well that they anticipate each other's needs without discussion.

m: To be ruthless and merciless in both intention and action, willing to harm others without hesitation or remorse.
s: When someone hurts people without any guilt or compassion to achieve their goals. When a person schemes and acts brutally against others to gain power or advantage, showing no mercy whatsoever.

m: The mind is restless and unfocused, unable to concentrate or settle on one thing.
s: When you're trying to study but keep thinking about other things and can't focus. When someone is supposed to be working but their attention keeps jumping from one distraction to another.

m: To do something willingly and wholeheartedly without any reluctance or complaint.
s: When someone agrees to help you without being asked and seems genuinely happy to do it. When a person accepts a difficult situation or sacrifice because they truly believe it's the right thing to do. When someone willingly takes on extra work because they care about the outcome.

m: To be honest and direct in speech, saying what one thinks without filters or hesitation.
s: When someone always tells you exactly what they're thinking without sugarcoating their words. When a coworker blurts out their opinion in a meeting without worrying about how it might sound to others. When a friend is known for being brutally honest because they can't hold back what's on their mind.

m: To be mentally restless, anxious, or unable to concentrate due to worry or unease.
s: When someone is waiting for important news and can't focus on their work. When a student is stressed about an upcoming exam and keeps worrying instead of studying.

m: To feel anxious, worried, or mentally unsettled and unable to find peace or calm.
s: When you're waiting for important exam results and can't focus on anything else. When someone you care about is in danger and you can't stop thinking about them. When you have a difficult decision to make and keep second-guessing yourself.

m: To be overwhelmed with extreme fear and terror that shakes one to the core.
s: When someone witnesses a terrifying accident and is left trembling with shock. When a person receives devastating news that leaves them emotionally devastated and unable to function normally.

l: a affliction of the heart and belly
m: A serious internal threat or danger that poses a fundamental risk to one's security or well-being.
s: When a trusted employee betrays you and damages your company from within. When internal conflict within a family threatens its stability and harmony. When corruption within an organization undermines its core mission and values.

m: One's heart is filled with intense joy and happiness, expressed through an exuberant emotional outburst.
s: When someone receives news of a major promotion or achievement and can barely contain their excitement. When a student gets accepted to their dream university and celebrates with unrestrained joy. When a person reunites with a loved one after a long separation and radiates pure happiness.

m: A sudden impulse or whim that arises unexpectedly without prior planning or deliberation.
s: When someone suddenly decides to take a spontaneous road trip without telling anyone beforehand. When a person impulsively buys something expensive just because they felt like it in the moment. When a friend randomly suggests going out to eat at midnight because they just had the urge to do so.

m: To understand something without it being explicitly stated, through implicit communication or intuition.
s: When you and a friend exchange a knowing glance and both instantly understand what the other is thinking without saying anything. When someone gives you a subtle hint and you immediately grasp what they mean without needing explanation.

m: To show the utmost respect and reverence; to behave with complete deference and formality.
s: When someone is meeting an important dignitary or authority figure and wants to show them the highest level of respect. When a junior employee is interacting with the company president or a senior mentor they greatly admire.

l: the path that must be traveled
m: An inevitable course of action or necessary path that one must follow to achieve a goal or reach a destination.
s: When someone is pursuing their career goals and realizes they need to get a degree first - it's a necessary step they have to take. When a country needs to go through difficult economic reforms to modernize and develop, even though the process is painful.

l: recall bitterness and think of sweetness
m: By remembering past hardships and suffering, one can better appreciate and cherish the comfort and happiness of the present.
s: When someone who grew up poor looks back on their difficult childhood and feels grateful for their current comfortable life. When older generations tell younger people about the struggles they endured, hoping they will appreciate what they have now instead of taking it for granted.

m: Unable to hold back from laughing or smiling despite trying to remain composed or serious.
s: When someone is trying to stay serious during a formal meeting but can't help smiling at a funny joke. When you're at a funeral and someone says something unintentionally hilarious, and you have to bite your lip to keep from laughing out loud.

l: endure without anything left to endure
m: One has reached the absolute limit of patience and can no longer tolerate a situation.
s: When someone has been treated badly repeatedly and finally decides to stand up for themselves. When a person reaches their breaking point after being disrespected over and over again and decides they won't take it anymore.

l: swallow anger and gulp down voice
m: to silently endure grievances without complaint or protest.

m: To be in such a state of constant worry and fear that one cannot find peace or rest even for a single day.
s: When someone is so stressed about an upcoming exam or presentation that they can't sleep or focus on anything else. When a person is constantly worried about bad news and can't enjoy their daily life because of ongoing anxiety.

m: To deliberately cause problems, conflicts, or trouble for others through one's actions or words.
s: When someone starts drama or gossip at work and it creates conflict between coworkers. When a person deliberately insults others online just to get a reaction and start arguments.

m: to bring disaster upon oneself through one's own reckless or provocative actions.
s: When someone deliberately antagonizes a dangerous person and ends up getting hurt as a result. When a company ignores safety warnings and then suffers a major accident. When someone keeps lying to their boss and finally gets fired.

m: To put on a false, insincere display of emotion or concern in order to deceive others.
s: When someone cries dramatically at a movie they've seen before, pretending to be deeply moved when they're really not. When a coworker suddenly acts concerned about a project only after the boss walks by, even though they've ignored it all week.

m: People of similar talent, character, or understanding naturally respect and appreciate each other deeply.
s: When two artists meet and immediately bond over their shared creative vision. When two talented individuals recognize each other's abilities and develop a special respect and friendship.

m: To have a visibly sad, worried, or distressed expression that shows one's inner emotional pain.
s: When someone arrives at a gathering looking clearly upset or troubled by what's happened to them. When you see a friend at work with a noticeably gloomy expression after receiving bad news.

m: Someone is persistently sad, anxious, or troubled, with their distress clearly visible on their face.
s: When someone looks visibly upset or stressed and you can see the worry lines on their forehead. When a friend has been dealing with a difficult situation and hasn't smiled in days, their sadness showing plainly in their expression.

m: To have a sad, distressed, or unhappy facial expression that shows one is troubled or suffering.
s: When someone comes home looking sad and upset because they failed an exam. When a friend shows up to a gathering clearly worried about a problem they're dealing with and their unhappy mood is written all over their face.

l: the meaning is beyond the words
m: The true intention or message lies in what is implied rather than explicitly stated.
s: When someone makes a comment that seems innocent on the surface but you realize they're actually criticizing you indirectly. When a poet writes something beautiful that seems to have a deeper message you need to think about to fully understand.

l: Let passion and temperament handle affairs
m: To act based on emotion and impulse rather than reason, allowing anger or pride to drive decisions.
s: When someone makes a major decision in anger without thinking it through. When a person quits their job in a fit of rage over a small disagreement with their boss. When friends get into a heated argument and say things they don't really mean because they're too emotional to think clearly.

m: Two people have compatible temperaments and similar values, making them naturally drawn to each other as kindred spirits.
s: When you meet someone new and immediately feel like you've known them forever because you think the same way. When two friends bond quickly because they share the same interests, sense of humor, and outlook on life.

m: To be in high spirits and full of confidence and enthusiasm, displaying a bold and triumphant demeanor.
s: When a young athlete wins their first major competition and feels invincible. When someone just got promoted at work and walks in with confidence radiating from them. When a team wins a big game and the players are celebrating with unbridled enthusiasm and pride.

l: The foolish old man moves the mountains
m: Persistent effort and determination can overcome even the most seemingly impossible obstacles through perseverance over time.
s: When someone tackles a huge, overwhelming project by breaking it into small steps and working at it consistently. When a person refuses to give up on a difficult goal despite others saying it's impossible, and eventually succeeds through sheer determination and hard work.

m: A state of being deeply ignorant, lacking education or understanding, and unable to perceive or comprehend basic facts or reasoning.
s: When someone believes obviously false information and refuses to listen to facts. When a person makes decisions based on superstition rather than evidence or common sense. When someone lacks basic education and understanding about how the world works.

p: yú zhě qiān lǜ ， bì yǒu yī dé
l: A fool's thousand thoughts must have one gain
m: Even someone of limited intelligence can occasionally stumble upon a correct idea or solution through sheer quantity of effort or attempts.
s: When someone keeps trying random approaches to a problem and finally gets lucky with one that works. When a person with poor judgment manages to make one good decision despite their usual mistakes. When someone makes many unsuccessful attempts but eventually achieves one success by chance.

m: To deeply touch someone's emotions or heart, moving them profoundly.
s: When a movie or story makes you cry and feel deeply moved. When someone's selfless act or sacrifice touches your heart so much that you can't help but be emotional about it.

l: feeling the same as if experiencing it in one's own body
m: To deeply empathize with someone's experience as if you were going through it yourself.
s: When your friend tells you about their heartbreak and you feel their pain so intensely that you almost cry. When you read a story about someone's struggle and it feels like your own struggle because you've been through something similar. When a parent watches their child suffer and feels every bit of that suffering as keenly as if it were happening to them.

m: To be deeply grateful and appreciative, feeling indebted to someone for their kindness or help.
s: When someone does you a huge favor and you want to express how much you appreciate it. When you feel genuinely thankful to a person who has made a significant positive impact on your life or helped you through a difficult time.

m: To make decisions based on feelings rather than reason or logic.
s: When someone quits their job in anger without thinking about the consequences. When a person makes a major life decision because they're upset rather than considering all the facts. When a friend invests money in a business just because they like the owner, ignoring red flags.

m: To be so deeply grateful that one cannot help but shed tears of emotion.
s: When someone does something incredibly kind for you and you become emotional. When you receive help during your darkest moment and feel overwhelmed by the kindness of others.

l: indignant at the world, jealous of corruption
m: to feel bitter resentment and scornful disdain toward society and human nature due to perceived injustice and moral decay.
s: When someone has become so disillusioned by corruption and unfairness in the world that they view everyone with cynicism and contempt. When a person constantly criticizes society and expresses disgust toward human behavior, believing the whole system is rotten.

m: To act or speak in a slow, deliberate, and unhurried manner without any sense of urgency.
s: When someone is taking their time to complete a task despite pressure to hurry. When a person speaks very slowly and carefully, choosing each word with deliberation. When someone remains calm and composed while others around them are rushed and frantic.

m: To face death willingly and courageously for a noble cause or principle, sacrificing oneself heroically.
s: When someone volunteers for a dangerous mission knowing it might cost them their life for the greater good. When a person stands up against injustice despite knowing they will face severe consequences or execution for their beliefs.

m: To speak or act with passionate intensity, fervent enthusiasm, and righteous indignation about something one feels strongly about.
s: When someone gives a rousing speech about injustice that moves everyone in the room. When a person argues passionately about a cause they believe in, speaking with great emotion and conviction.

m: To willingly and generously give money or financial help to others in need.
s: When a wealthy person donates a large sum to charity without hesitation. When your friend immediately offers to pay for everyone's meal even though it's expensive. When someone opens their wallet to help a family member through financial hardship.

p: chéng shì bù zú ， bài shì yǒu yú
l: Insufficient in accomplishing matters, excessive in ruining matters
m: Someone who is incompetent at constructive work but remarkably skilled at causing damage and failure.
s: When a coworker can't complete their assigned tasks properly but somehow always manages to create problems for the whole team. When someone on a project contributes nothing positive but consistently makes things worse through their interference.

m: To help others achieve their desires or goals; to contribute to someone else's happiness or success.
s: When a friend wants to pursue their dream and you offer to help them get there. When you support someone's relationship by introducing them to a potential partner. When you assist a colleague in getting a promotion they've been working hard for.

m: To willingly sacrifice one's life for a righteous cause or moral principle.
s: When someone chooses to stand up for what is right even though it costs them dearly. When a person is willing to die rather than compromise their principles or values.

m: An extremely large number or quantity; countless or innumerable amounts.
s: When describing a massive crowd at a concert or festival. When talking about how many stars are visible in the night sky. When discussing the huge number of social media followers a celebrity has.

l: become famous and become a master
m: To achieve both widespread recognition and high professional mastery in one's field.
s: When someone works hard for years and finally becomes well-known and respected in their profession. When a musician or artist reaches a level where they are both celebrated and considered an expert in their craft.

l: establish a family and build a career
m: to get married and become established in one's profession or business, achieving adult success and stability.
s: When someone gets married and starts their own business or gets a good job. When you're talking about a young person reaching important life milestones like finding a spouse and becoming financially independent.

l: success and failure, sharp and dull
m: All possible outcomes of an endeavor, whether victorious or defeated, are ultimately determined by circumstances beyond one's complete control.
s: When someone is reflecting on how their business venture could succeed or fail based on market conditions. When a coach is reminding their team that winning or losing depends on many factors including luck and opponent strength, not just effort.

m: A perfect pairing where two things complement each other so well that they form a harmonious and complete whole.
s: When a couple is so well-suited to each other that they seem made for one another. When two business partners work together seamlessly with complementary skills that create something greater than the sum of their parts.

l: I act according to my own nature
m: Someone stubbornly insists on doing things their own way regardless of others' opinions or advice.
s: When a coworker refuses to follow the team's process and keeps doing things their own way. When your friend ignores everyone's suggestions and makes the same poor decision repeatedly. When someone won't adapt to new rules or expectations and continues with their old habits.

l: guard against pride and guard against impetuousness
m: One should remain humble and calm, avoiding arrogance and rash behavior in order to maintain steady progress and good judgment.
s: When someone wins a competition and you want to remind them not to get overconfident. When a young employee gets promoted and you advise them to stay level-headed and not let success go to their head.

m: to struggle fiercely against all obstacles and adverse circumstances without fear or hesitation.
s: When someone is determined to overcome every challenge in their path, no matter how difficult. When a person shows unwavering resolve to pursue their goals despite facing seemingly impossible odds from nature or circumstances.

m: To act with extreme caution and anxiety due to fear or nervousness.
s: When someone is giving their first public speech and is visibly shaking and nervous. When an employee is called into the boss's office and walks in very anxiously, worried about what they might have done wrong.

p: zhàn wú bù shèng ， gōng wú bù kè
l: In battle there is no defeat, in attack there is no fortress that cannot be taken
m: To be completely invincible and capable of overcoming any obstacle or opponent through superior strength, skill, or strategy.
s: When describing a sports team that wins every game and never loses. When talking about a company that dominates its market and easily outcompetes all rivals. When someone is so skilled at something that they never fail, no matter what challenge they face.

m: Completely opposite or fundamentally different in nature, with no similarity between the two things being compared.
s: When two siblings have completely opposite personalities and interests. When a person's behavior before and after a major life event is drastically different. When two products that seem similar on the surface actually work in completely different ways.

l: cut off toes to fit the shoe
m: to destroy something valuable or harm oneself in order to force a fit with an unsuitable standard or requirement.
s: When a company cuts important features from their product just to meet an arbitrary deadline. When someone changes their core values or beliefs to fit in with a group that doesn't accept them as they are.

l: cut the long to mend the short
m: To balance inequalities by taking from those with excess and giving to those with insufficiency.
s: When a company redistributes resources from profitable departments to struggling ones. When a teacher uses a high-performing student's work to help improve a struggling student's skills. When a wealthy family member helps support a relative who is struggling financially.

m: People working together with complete unity of purpose and effort to achieve a common goal.
s: When a team faces a difficult challenge and everyone puts aside their differences to work toward the same objective. When a family comes together during a crisis, with each member contributing their best effort without conflict or hesitation.

m: to atone for past wrongdoings by performing good deeds or making contributions in the present.
s: When someone who made serious mistakes is given a chance to prove themselves through hard work and positive actions. When a company that caused harm tries to rebuild trust by doing charitable work and improving their practices.

l: the threshold is worn through by many feet
m: A place or person becomes extremely popular or receives many visitors, resulting in constant traffic and activity.
s: When a new restaurant opens and becomes so popular that customers keep coming in and out all day long. When someone's house becomes a gathering spot that friends visit so frequently the entranceway gets worn down from all the foot traffic.

l: all that it encounters crumbles away
m: To be unstoppable and overcome all obstacles or enemies with overwhelming force.
s: When a successful sports team wins every game and dominates their opponents. When a new product takes over the market and defeats all competitors. When a powerful military force advances without any real resistance.

m: To be invincible and unstoppable in all directions, facing no opposition or defeat.
s: When describing a sports team that wins every game decisively. When talking about a powerful army or nation that conquers all opposition. When someone is so skilled at something that no one can beat them.

p: biǎn dàn méi zhā ， liǎng tóu dǎ tā
l: A carrying pole unfastened at both ends collapses on both sides
m: Attempting to handle multiple things without proper preparation or commitment results in failure on all fronts.
s: When someone tries to work two jobs simultaneously without proper planning and ends up performing poorly at both. When a student tries to study for multiple exams without a proper schedule and fails them all. When a business tries to enter multiple markets without adequate resources and fails in each one.

m: Someone is so devoted to reading that they rarely put books down, indicating a deep love of learning and scholarship.
s: When describing someone who is constantly reading and always carries a book with them. When you notice a friend or colleague spends nearly all their free time with their nose in a book, unable to put it down even during meals or breaks.

m: A skilled doctor or healer can cure illness immediately with just a touch or simple treatment.
s: When a doctor quickly diagnoses and treats your problem effectively. When someone is so skilled at their job that they solve difficult problems almost instantly, like a mechanic who fixes your car on the first try.

m: To be in a state of panic or confusion where one is rushing around frantically and disorganized, unable to cope with a situation.
s: When someone is overwhelmed by multiple urgent tasks at once and doesn't know where to start. When a waiter drops several plates during a busy dinner rush and scrambles to clean up while managing other customers.

m: To be quick-witted and physically agile, able to react swiftly to opportunities or dangers with both sharp perception and rapid action.
s: When a waiter skillfully catches a falling glass before it hits the ground. When someone spots a good deal at a market and quickly grabs it before others notice. When a goalkeeper reacts instantly to a sudden shot coming at them.

l: hands without even an inch of iron
m: to be completely defenseless or unarmed, having no weapons or means of self-defense.
s: When someone gets into a dangerous situation without any way to protect themselves. When a person faces a powerful opponent but has no tools or resources to fight back.

p: shǒu wú fù jī zhī lì
l: hands lack the strength to bind a chicken
m: Someone is extremely weak and physically powerless, lacking even the basic strength to accomplish simple tasks.
s: When describing someone who is very frail or sickly and cannot do physical work. When someone is so exhausted they can barely lift their own belongings. When referring to an intellectually gifted person who is completely helpless when it comes to practical physical matters.

m: To dance and jump around with unrestrained joy and excitement.
s: When someone is so happy they can't help but move their body and dance around. When a child gets excited at a party and starts jumping and waving their arms in celebration.

m: To be so confused or panicked that you don't know what to do with yourself or how to respond to a situation.
s: When someone is caught completely off guard and freezes up, not knowing how to react. When a person is so overwhelmed by a crisis that they can't think clearly or take any action. When you're in an awkward or unexpected situation and feel totally lost and helpless.

m: A perfect romantic pairing of an intelligent, accomplished man with a beautiful, refined woman, often used to describe an ideal couple or romantic match.
s: When two people seem perfectly suited for each other, combining intelligence with beauty and charm. When describing a couple that appears to be a fairy-tale match where both partners are accomplished and attractive.

l: talent and wit overflow in all directions
m: Someone possesses exceptional talent and intelligence that is so abundant it manifests prominently in everything they do.
s: When describing a brilliant student who excels in every subject and impresses everyone with their creativity and insight. When talking about a talented artist, writer, or musician whose exceptional abilities are obvious to anyone who encounters their work.

m: One possesses limited natural ability and insufficient knowledge or education.
s: When someone apologizes for not being able to help with a difficult problem because they lack the expertise or education needed. When a person humbly acknowledges they don't have the skills or knowledge to tackle a complex task.

m: Someone possesses exceptional intelligence and talent far beyond ordinary people.
s: When describing a brilliant student who excels in every subject and learns things effortlessly. When someone demonstrates remarkable creative or intellectual abilities that make them stand out from their peers.

m: A situation that is extremely confusing and difficult to understand because of its complex and mysterious nature.
s: When you're trying to figure out what really happened in a complicated situation but the facts keep changing and nothing makes sense. When a mystery novel has so many twists and clues that you can't tell what's real anymore.

m: To completely neglect or abandon someone or something, leaving them in a state of isolation and disregard.
s: When a company stops supporting an old product and leaves it to die without updates. When someone you were close to suddenly ignores you and treats you like you don't exist anymore. When a once-popular employee is sidelined and given no meaningful work to do.

l: break into homes and rob houses
m: to commit robbery and burglary; to plunder and despoil homes and travelers.
s: When describing a region plagued by bandits or criminals who steal from people's homes and travelers on the road. When talking about organized crime groups that rob houses and assault people for their belongings.

p: dǎ kāi tiān chuāng shuō liàng huà
l: open the skylight and speak bright words
m: To speak frankly and honestly without beating around the bush or hiding the truth.
s: When you need someone to stop making excuses and just tell you what's really going on. When a friend is being evasive about a problem and you want them to be direct and truthful with you.

l: beat until the fire is hot
m: To describe two people or groups who are getting along extremely well and are very close or intimate with each other.
s: When two people have just started dating and are constantly together, showing a lot of affection. When colleagues or friends are collaborating so enthusiastically on a project that they seem inseparable and deeply connected.

m: People from different backgrounds or groups come together harmoniously and become unified as if they were one.
s: When a new team member quickly becomes friends with everyone and feels like part of the group. When people from different departments work together so well that all barriers disappear and they feel like one team.

m: To stand up and fight against injustice on behalf of someone who has been wronged.
s: When you see someone being treated unfairly and you speak up or take action to help them. When a friend is being bullied and you intervene to defend them. When you witness workplace discrimination and you report it to management.

p: dǎ pò shā guō wèn dào dǐ
l: break the clay pot and ask to the bottom
m: to persistently pursue the truth of a matter by asking questions until you get a complete and thorough answer.
s: When a child keeps asking 'why' over and over again about something they don't understand. When someone refuses to accept a vague explanation and demands specific details and complete information. When a detective or investigator keeps digging deeper into a case until all the facts are uncovered.

p: dǎ zhǒng liǎn chōng pàng zi
l: hit your face swollen to pretend to be fat
m: To pretend to have wealth, status, or ability that you do not actually possess by living beyond your means or putting on a false appearance.
s: When someone buys expensive clothes they can't afford just to impress others at a party. When a friend takes out loans to buy a luxury car to look rich in front of their colleagues.

l: beat the grass and startle the snake
m: An action intended to achieve one thing inadvertently alerts an enemy or reveals a secret, causing them to become defensive or flee.
s: When you try to investigate something quietly but your actions tip off the person you're investigating. When a manager asks too many questions about a problem and accidentally warns the employee who caused it to cover their tracks.

l: strike a dog in the water
m: to ruthlessly attack or exploit someone who is already in a weakened or defeated position.
s: When a company aggressively pursues a competitor that's already struggling financially. When someone keeps bullying a person who is already down and defenseless. When a politician continues to attack an opponent who has already lost credibility.

m: To back out of a commitment or abandon an undertaking when faced with difficulty or opposition.
s: When someone agrees to help with a project but suddenly quits when things get tough. When a business partner withdraws from a deal at the last minute because they got cold feet.

m: To make an incorrect calculation or miscalculation that leads to an unexpected or undesired outcome.
s: When someone's plan fails because they didn't account for all the costs and ran out of money halfway through. When a business owner thought they would make a profit but discovered they actually lost money due to poor accounting.

l: strike the heartstrings of the heart
m: To deeply move or emotionally captivate someone; to stir someone's feelings profoundly.
s: When you watch a movie scene that makes you cry unexpectedly. When a musician's performance is so beautiful that it moves everyone in the audience to tears. When someone tells a story that resonates deeply with your own experiences and emotions.

l: stubbornly persist in delusion without awakening
m: To stubbornly cling to false beliefs or mistaken ideas despite evidence or warnings, refusing to recognize one's error.
s: When someone keeps investing money in an obvious scam despite multiple people warning them. When a person refuses to admit they were wrong about a relationship or business decision, no matter how much evidence shows they made a mistake.

m: to examine one's own conscience and motivations honestly, asking oneself difficult questions about whether one's actions are truly right or justified.
s: When you need to decide if you were really in the right during an argument with someone. When you're questioning whether your reasons for doing something were actually honest or if you were just making excuses. When reflecting on whether you treated someone fairly or if you let your biases influence your judgment.

m: To be completely ruined, destroyed, or stripped of all dignity and honor.
s: When someone's reputation is completely destroyed by a scandal. When a person loses everything they worked for and is left with nothing but shame.

l: ladle the boiling water to stop it from boiling
m: attempting to solve a problem with superficial measures that address only the symptoms rather than the root cause.
s: When a company keeps giving employees small raises to address turnover without fixing the underlying management problems. When someone tries to cool down their house by opening windows instead of fixing the broken air conditioning unit.

m: To feel proud, relieved, and vindicated after a long period of being wronged, humiliated, or underestimated.
s: When someone finally gets recognition after years of hard work and nobody believing in them. When a person proves wrong all the critics who doubted their abilities. When someone overcomes a difficult situation and can finally hold their head high with pride.

m: To leave proudly or triumphantly, often in a haughty manner after achieving success or making a point.
s: When someone wins an argument and then walks away with their head held high, acting superior. When a person leaves a situation feeling victorious or satisfied, making sure everyone knows they got the better outcome.

l: support the endangered and relieve the distressed
m: To help those in dangerous or difficult situations and provide assistance to people in need.
s: When a charity organization provides food and shelter to homeless people during winter. When a wealthy person donates money to help families affected by a natural disaster. When community members volunteer to assist elderly neighbors who are struggling financially.

l: support the weak and restrain the strong
m: To help those in disadvantaged positions while limiting the power of the dominant, creating a more balanced and fair society.
s: When a government implements policies to protect small businesses from being crushed by large corporations. When a teacher gives extra help to struggling students while challenging advanced ones to prevent any single group from dominating the class.

l: rise straight up on a whirlwind
m: To rise rapidly and achieve sudden success or advancement.
s: When a young entrepreneur's startup suddenly becomes very successful and grows rapidly. When someone gets promoted multiple times in quick succession at their job.

l: support the elderly and lead the young
m: To care for and bring together people of all ages, from the very old to the very young, in a family or community.
s: When describing a family outing where grandparents, parents, and children all go together. When talking about a community event that welcomes people of every generation, from babies to seniors.

l: carry forward the past and open up the future
m: To inherit and preserve the achievements of predecessors while simultaneously creating new possibilities and progress for future generations.
s: When a leader takes over a successful company and both maintains its core values while innovating for growth. When a teacher passes down traditional knowledge to students who will then advance the field further. When a generation preserves their cultural heritage while adapting it for the next generation's context.

m: A rhythmic pattern with varied intonation and pacing that creates an engaging and pleasant flow in speech or music.
s: When a skilled speaker delivers a presentation with dramatic pauses and changes in emphasis, making it captivating. When a singer performs with expressive dynamics, alternating between soft and loud passages to create emotional impact.

m: To be anxious, frustrated, or agitated, showing visible signs of distress or impatience.
s: When someone is stuck on a difficult problem and doesn't know what to do. When a person is waiting for important news and can't sit still because they're nervous. When someone is deeply worried or troubled about something.

m: to cater to someone's preferences or interests in order to please them or win their favor.
s: When a salesman learns a customer loves golf and starts showing him golf equipment. When a manager gives an employee projects they're passionate about to keep them happy. When you buy a gift based on exactly what you know someone enjoys rather than what you think they should have.

l: invest for opportunity and resell for profit
m: To engage in illegal or unethical buying and selling, typically by hoarding goods and reselling them at inflated prices for personal gain.
s: When someone buys up all the hand sanitizer during a pandemic and sells it at three times the price. When a scalper buys concert tickets in bulk and resells them illegally at huge markups. When a merchant hoards essential supplies and sells them at exorbitant prices during a shortage.

m: to use dishonest or cunning methods to gain an unfair advantage rather than working through proper channels or honest effort.
s: When a student cheats on an exam instead of studying. When a businessman cuts corners and uses underhanded tactics to undercut competitors. When someone tries to exploit loopholes in rules to get ahead without doing the real work.

l: offer a peach and return a plum
m: To reciprocate kindness or generosity with similar gestures, showing mutual goodwill and exchange of favors.
s: When someone gives you a gift and you want to give them something equally nice in return. When a friend does you a favor and you want to repay them with a similar act of kindness.

l: cast aside the pen to take up the sword
m: to abandon a peaceful civilian life, typically scholarly or literary pursuits, in order to join the military or take up arms for a cause.
s: When a writer decides to leave their career to enlist in the army. When someone gives up their comfortable job to fight for their country or beliefs.

l: cast a whip to sever the flow
m: to possess such overwhelming military force that even a symbolic gesture could change the course of events, representing invincible power and dominance.
s: When describing an army so massive and powerful that it seems capable of accomplishing anything. When referring to a leader or organization with such dominant strength that they can reshape circumstances at will. When someone has accumulated so much power or resources that they can bend situations to their advantage.

l: throw at the rat but fear the vessel
m: Refrain from taking action against someone or something because you're afraid of harming something else of value in the process.
s: When a manager hesitates to fire a problematic employee because they worry it will upset an important client. When a parent avoids punishing their child too harshly because they're concerned it might damage their relationship with them.

l: clash and resolve at the wine cup and dining table
m: to settle disputes and achieve diplomatic victories through skillful negotiation and clever rhetoric in social settings rather than through military force.
s: When a skilled diplomat manages to resolve a tense international conflict through a well-orchestrated state dinner and careful conversation. When someone uses charm and wit at a social gathering to turn a potential enemy into an ally or convince others to support their position.

l: caress the present and pursue the past
m: To reflect on the past while contemplating the present, often with a sense of nostalgia or melancholy about how things have changed.
s: When you visit your hometown after many years and feel emotional comparing how it was before to how it is now. When someone looks at old photos and thinks about how much their life has changed since then.

m: To appear in public or take on a visible, prominent role where one's identity becomes known.
s: When someone overcomes their shyness and performs on stage for the first time. When a private person decides to run for political office and must campaign publicly. When a reclusive artist finally agrees to hold an exhibition and meet their audience in person.

l: toss a brick to attract jade
m: to offer something of little value as a way to invite others to contribute something more valuable or worthwhile in return.
s: When you share a rough draft of your idea hoping others will improve it with their better suggestions. When a host serves a simple appetizer at a party to encourage guests to bring more elaborate dishes. When someone makes a modest first offer in hopes of getting more substantial responses from others.

l: take revenge and wash away resentment
m: To seek vengeance and resolve deep grievances, typically after suffering a serious wrong or humiliation.
s: When someone has been wronged or humiliated and finally gets an opportunity to get back at the person who hurt them. When a team that lost badly wants to play their rival again to prove themselves and settle the score.

l: wearing stars and capping the moon
m: To work or travel through the night and early morning, suggesting exhaustion from long hours of labor or journeying.
s: When someone works very early in the morning before sunrise and stays late into the night, going through their day in darkness. When a delivery driver or traveling salesman is always on the road, leaving before dawn and returning after dusk every day.

l: spread out sand and pick gold
m: To carefully select the valuable or essential elements from a large amount of material, separating the worthwhile from the worthless.
s: When you're reading through hundreds of job applications to find the best candidates. When you're scrolling through a huge pile of research papers to find the few that are actually relevant to your project.

l: bare the liver and drip the gallbladder
m: To show absolute sincerity and loyalty by revealing one's innermost heart and dedicating oneself completely to someone or something.
s: When someone sacrifices their own interests to help a friend in need, giving everything they have. When a person works tirelessly for a cause they believe in, showing complete dedication and honesty without any hidden agenda.

m: To overcome difficulties and obstacles through hard work and determination to achieve one's goals.
s: When someone is working through a difficult project with many challenges and keeps pushing forward. When a business founder faces many setbacks but persists in building their company. When a student struggles through a difficult subject but doesn't give up studying.

l: clutching head and scurrying like rats
m: To flee in panic and humiliation, running away desperately without dignity or composure.
s: When someone is caught doing something wrong and runs away in shame and fear. When a person is defeated in an argument or confrontation and bolts away rather than facing consequences. When a criminal or wrongdoer is chased and escapes in a frantic, undignified manner.

l: embrace regret until the end of days
m: To carry deep regret or sorrow for the rest of one's life, unable to resolve it before death.

m: attempting to solve a problem by using methods that actually make it worse.

m: To leave in an angry, indignant, or disdainful manner, typically as a gesture of protest or rejection.

m: To bravely step forward and take action or responsibility, especially in a difficult or dangerous situation.

s: When you look at a city map and see countless small shops and restaurants spread throughout different neighborhoods. When hiking through the countryside and noticing many small villages dotted across the valleys and hillsides.

m: Each person or thing has their own unique qualities and strengths that shine in their proper time and circumstances.
s: When different people excel in different situations or seasons of life. When you're comparing two people who are both talented but in completely different ways, so it's unfair to judge them by the same standard. When explaining why someone who was successful in one era might not succeed in another era.

m: Subtle and gentle influence that naturally inspires growth and positive change, like how spring rain nourishes plants without force.
s: When a teacher quietly inspires students through patient guidance rather than strict discipline. When someone gradually changes their behavior because of a friend's kind example, not because they were forced to.

m: Something is so obvious and apparent that it cannot be hidden or denied by anyone.
s: When someone's true intentions become completely obvious to everyone despite their attempts to conceal them. When the truth about a situation becomes undeniably clear to all observers.

l: affirm the ancient and deny the present
m: To blindly praise the past while dismissing or criticizing the present and modern ways.
s: When an older person insists that everything was better in their youth and refuses to accept any modern improvements. When someone rejects new technology or methods simply because they prefer how things used to be done.

p: shì kě rěn ， shú bù kě rěn
l: If this can be tolerated, what then cannot be tolerated?
m: There is a limit to what one should endure; if you tolerate something this egregious, there is nothing you won't accept.
s: When someone has finally reached their breaking point after being disrespected repeatedly. When a person decides they must draw the line and stop accepting mistreatment, because allowing it would mean accepting anything.

l: right and wrong, straight and crooked
m: The distinction between what is right and what is wrong, or between justice and injustice in a situation.
s: When you need to judge a dispute fairly and understand both sides to see who is actually in the right. When someone refuses to acknowledge the clear right and wrong in a disagreement, insisting everything is ambiguous.

p: shì fēi zì yǒu gōng lùn
l: right and wrong naturally have public opinion
m: The truth will eventually be recognized and judged fairly by the general public, regardless of current circumstances or opinions.
s: When someone is being falsely accused but you're confident that eventually people will see through the lies and understand what really happened. When a company tries to cover up wrongdoing but you believe the public will eventually learn the truth and judge them fairly.

m: Something is so obvious and clear that it requires no explanation or proof.
