s: When the solution to a problem is obvious to everyone. When someone's guilt or innocence is apparent to all who look at the facts. When the benefits of a decision are plain for anyone to understand.

m: To be confused, disoriented, or overwhelmed by a situation or information overload.
s: When you're so stressed at work that you can't think clearly anymore. When someone bombards you with too many questions at once and you feel completely bewildered. After watching a confusing movie with a complicated plot, you walk out feeling dazed and disoriented.

m: The whole world celebrates together in joy and harmony over an auspicious or significant event.
s: When a country wins an Olympic medal and people across all regions and social classes celebrate together. When a national holiday brings the entire population into festive celebration regardless of their background or location.

m: A sudden, unexpected disaster or shocking news that strikes without warning, leaving someone completely unprepared.
s: When you receive suddenly devastating news like losing your job unexpectedly or hearing that a loved one has passed away. When something terrible happens that you had absolutely no way of seeing coming beforehand.

m: A person who possesses both intelligence and bravery, able to think strategically while also having the courage to act decisively.
s: When describing a leader who can make wise decisions under pressure and isn't afraid to take risks. When praising someone who outsmarts their opponents while also standing up to them fearlessly.

p: zhì zhě qiān lǜ ， bì yǒu yī shī
l: The wise person in a thousand considerations must have one failure
m: Even the most intelligent and prudent people are bound to make mistakes occasionally, no matter how carefully they think things through.
s: When a brilliant colleague makes an unexpected error despite their usual excellence. When you realize that even the most experienced expert in a field can overlook something or make a wrong decision sometimes.

m: To try to find a way forward without clear guidance, information, or understanding of the situation.
s: When you're trying to solve a problem but don't have enough information to know where to start. When someone is learning a new skill without proper instruction and has to figure things out through trial and error.

l: secretly advance through Chen Cang while openly elsewhere
m: to accomplish one's true objective through deception by creating a distraction or false appearance of doing something else.
s: When a company announces a major public project to distract attention while quietly acquiring a competitor behind the scenes. When a person pretends to be interested in one thing but is actually working toward a completely different goal without anyone noticing.

m: A situation is so oppressive, hopeless, or miserable that it feels like there is no light or relief in sight.
s: When someone is living under a tyrannical ruler with no freedom or hope for improvement. When a person is trapped in a job or relationship that is so unbearable and bleak that they see no way out.

m: Someone harms you through secret, underhanded means that you cannot see coming or defend against.
s: When a coworker spreads rumors about you behind your back instead of confronting you directly. When someone sabotages your project in ways you can't immediately detect or prove.

m: To make subtle, flirtatious glances or signals at someone to show romantic interest or attraction.
s: When two people across a crowded room keep making eye contact and smiling at each other, suggesting hidden attraction. When someone keeps giving meaningful looks to their crush when they think nobody is watching.

m: A pervasive sense of decline, gloom, and lack of vitality, as if everything is aging and losing its vigor.
s: When you walk into an old, neglected building where everything feels dark and lifeless. When describing a company or organization that has lost its energy and seems to be slowly dying. When someone describes the mood of a dying era or a fading historical period.

m: A reminder to stay vigilant and disciplined, or the passage of time marked by regular routine practices.
s: When you need to remind someone to stay on track with their responsibilities every day. When describing the rhythmic passage of days in a monastery or structured institution where routines repeat without fail.

m: To act with cruel brutality and unrestrained tyranny, showing complete disregard for others' rights and suffering.
s: When a powerful leader abuses their authority to harm innocent people without any consequences or accountability. When someone in a position of power acts viciously and does whatever they want regardless of how it affects those around them.

m: Recklessly wasting valuable natural resources or materials that should be cherished and preserved.
s: When someone throws away perfectly good food or clothes without any consideration. When a company destroys excess inventory instead of donating it to those in need. When a person carelessly damages something precious or beautiful that took nature or craftspeople a long time to create.

l: wrestle a tiger and ford a river
m: to act recklessly and courageously without adequate preparation or protection, showing bravery but lacking wisdom.
s: When someone rushes into a dangerous situation without proper planning or equipment. When a person confronts a powerful enemy or obstacle with only courage and no real strategy. When someone attempts something extremely difficult or risky without the necessary skills or resources.

m: To be extremely angry and lose control of one's emotions, showing one's rage through violent physical movements.
s: When someone finds out they've been betrayed and starts yelling and stomping around in fury. When a parent discovers their child has lied to them repeatedly and explodes in anger. When someone receives terrible news at work and can't contain their rage anymore.

m: Something is completely revealed or exposed with nothing hidden or concealed.
s: When someone's true intentions or secret flaws become completely obvious to everyone. When a lie or deception is fully uncovered and there's no way to hide it anymore.

m: A sudden, fierce, and overwhelming attack, assault, or criticism that comes with great force and intensity.
s: When a boss suddenly launches into a harsh criticism of an employee's work in front of everyone. When a group of people suddenly gangs up on someone with aggressive complaints and accusations.

m: To perform or create something with such skill and artistry that every nuance and subtlety is perfectly expressed, leaving nothing more to be achieved.
s: When a musician plays a piece so beautifully that every note seems perfectly placed and emotionally resonant. When an artist executes their work with such mastery that the audience is completely moved by how well they've captured every detail.

l: distort one's intentions to please others
m: To abandon one's own principles and values in order to ingratiate oneself with others through flattery and compliance.
s: When an employee pretends to agree with their boss's bad ideas just to avoid conflict. When someone changes their opinions constantly depending on who they're talking to in order to win favor.

l: bend the chimney and move the firewood
m: To prevent a disaster by taking precautionary measures before the problem occurs, rather than trying to fix it after it happens.
s: When someone fixes a potential safety hazard in their home before an accident occurs. When a company updates their security systems to prevent data breaches rather than waiting for one to happen. When you back up your important files regularly to avoid losing data in a computer crash.

m: Sophisticated or refined work appeals to only a small audience because most people lack the understanding or taste to appreciate it.
s: When an avant-garde film festival screening has very few attendees because the experimental movies are too complex for mainstream audiences. When a classical composer creates intricate symphonies that only trained musicians and serious enthusiasts truly appreciate, while the general public finds them boring or inaccessible.

m: To reach a higher level of achievement, skill, or success beyond what has already been accomplished.
s: When someone improves their performance and does better than before. When a student goes from getting B's to getting A's. When a business expands and becomes even more successful than it already was.

m: A time late at night when everything is peaceful, quiet, and most people are asleep.
s: When you're awake alone in the middle of the night and everything around you is completely silent. When you want to describe that calm, undisturbed feeling of very late night when the world has gone to sleep.

m: referring to a time not long ago that now seems distant or feels like it has passed very quickly.
s: When you realize how quickly your child has grown up. When you reflect on how recent events feel like they happened long ago. When someone mentions something that happened just months ago but feels nostalgic.

m: The divine matchmaker who brings people together in romantic relationships and destined marriages.
s: When two people meet and fall in love unexpectedly, you might say the Old Man Under the Moon brought them together. When someone believes their romantic fate is predetermined, they might credit the Old Man Under the Moon for deciding their destiny.

p: yǒu yī lì bì yǒu yī bì
l: Where there is one advantage, there must be one disadvantage
m: Every benefit or advantage inherently comes with some corresponding drawback or disadvantage.
s: When you get a higher-paying job but have to work longer hours. When a new technology makes work easier but creates new problems to solve. When someone buys a bigger house but has higher costs and more maintenance.

p: yǒu qí fù ， bì yǒu qí zi
l: If there is such a father, there must be such a son
m: Children tend to resemble and inherit the characteristics, behaviors, or qualities of their parents.
s: When you notice a child behaving exactly like their parent in mannerisms or personality. When someone's talents or flaws clearly come from their family background.

p: yǒu zé gǎi zhī ， wú zé jiā miǎn
l: If there are faults, correct them; if there are none, redouble your efforts.
m: When receiving criticism, correct any faults found and use the feedback as motivation to continue improving if no faults are found.
s: When your boss gives you feedback on your work, you should fix any mistakes and keep working hard if everything was good. When a teacher points out errors in your essay, you correct them, but if there are no errors, you should still strive to write even better next time.

m: Something continues to grow or increase without any end or limit.
s: When a company keeps adding new features to their product with no plan to stop. When someone's workload keeps piling up day after day with no relief in sight.

m: Being brave and daring but without the intelligence or planning to use that courage effectively, often leading to reckless or foolish actions.
s: When someone rushes into a dangerous situation without thinking it through. When a person is willing to fight but has no plan for how to actually win or solve the problem. When someone's enthusiasm and boldness outweigh their common sense and tactical thinking.

l: having a mouth but no heart
m: Speaking thoughtlessly without intending to cause harm; saying something hurtful by accident rather than out of malice.
s: When someone makes an insensitive comment without realizing how it might hurt you. When a friend blurts out something rude but immediately apologizes because they didn't mean it that way.

l: Everyone has a monument in their mouth
m: Someone or something is so widely praised and admired that everyone speaks favorably about it.
s: When a restaurant becomes so popular that every customer raves about it to their friends. When a new movie gets amazing reviews and everyone you talk to recommends it. When a coworker is so helpful and kind that everyone in the office has only good things to say about them.

l: having a mouth but difficulty explaining
m: Unable to explain oneself clearly or defend oneself against misunderstandings, even though one has much to say.
s: When you're accused of something unfair but can't find the right words to defend yourself. When you try to explain a complicated situation but people keep misunderstanding what you're trying to say.

l: having a mouth but difficult to speak
m: Unable to express one's thoughts or feelings due to embarrassment, fear, or complicated circumstances that make it hard to explain.
s: When you know the truth about something but can't tell anyone because it would hurt them or cause trouble. When someone asks you a personal question but you're too ashamed or conflicted to answer honestly.

l: having a name but lacking substance
m: Something appears to have a particular title, status, or reputation but does not actually possess the real qualities, abilities, or value that the name suggests.
s: When a company claims to be eco-friendly but doesn't actually follow sustainable practices. When someone has an impressive job title but does minimal actual work. When a product is advertised as premium quality but is actually made cheaply.

m: Something is presented in a vivid, lively, and engaging manner that captures attention through both its form and expression.
s: When a teacher explains a lesson in such an animated and interesting way that the whole class is captivated. When someone tells a story with expressive gestures and tone so that listeners are completely drawn in. When a performance, presentation, or event is executed with energy and skill so that it comes alive for the audience.

l: with preparation there is no trouble
m: Being well-prepared in advance prevents problems and difficulties from arising.
s: When you study hard before an exam so you won't fail. When a company stocks up on supplies before a natural disaster to ensure they can continue operating. When you keep an emergency fund so unexpected expenses don't cause financial crisis.

l: having a head but no tail
m: to start something with enthusiasm but fail to finish it or see it through to completion.
s: When someone begins a project with great energy but abandons it halfway through. When a person makes promises or grand plans but never actually follows through with them.

m: People will attach themselves to and serve whoever provides them with benefits or sustenance, regardless of loyalty or true relationships.
s: When someone switches their allegiance to whoever gives them money or advantages. When a person abandons their friends as soon as they find someone wealthier or more powerful to benefit from. When an employee is only loyal to the boss who pays them the most, not out of principle but pure self-interest.

l: having a beginning but no ending
m: To start something with enthusiasm but fail to complete it or see it through to the end.
s: When someone starts a new hobby or project with great excitement but abandons it after a few weeks. When a person makes big promises about what they'll accomplish but never follows through. When you begin reading a book with determination but never finish it.

m: To see something through from start to finish with consistency and commitment.
s: When someone completes a project they started months ago without giving up halfway. When a student follows through on their study plan all the way to graduation. When a friend commits to a fitness routine and sticks with it for the whole year.

m: People who have strong determination and noble aspirations to achieve something meaningful or virtuous.
s: When describing someone who is driven to make a positive difference in society despite obstacles. When talking about people who volunteer for important causes or pursue noble goals with passion and dedication.

p: yǒu zhì zhě shì jìng chéng
l: Those with ambition will eventually accomplish their goals
m: Determined people can overcome obstacles and achieve their goals through perseverance and effort.
s: When someone works hard toward their dream despite facing many setbacks and finally succeeds. When you encourage a friend who is struggling with a difficult task by reminding them that commitment and persistence will pay off.

m: Acting recklessly or boldly because one has something or someone to rely on for protection or support.
s: When a student cheats on a test because their parent is friends with the principal and they think they won't get caught. When someone drives recklessly because they know their wealthy father will bail them out of any legal trouble.

m: A good teacher or leader provides education and guidance to everyone regardless of their background, social status, or circumstances.
s: When a mentor welcomes students from all walks of life and teaches them equally well. When someone in a position of knowledge chooses not to discriminate and makes their expertise available to anyone willing to learn.

l: there is a morning one day
m: Someday in the future, a particular moment or opportunity will arrive.
s: When you're waiting for something to happen eventually, like hoping that one day you'll have enough money to travel. When someone believes that their hard work will finally pay off at some point in the future.

m: There is an opportunity or opening that can be exploited for one's purposes.
s: When a competitor makes a mistake and you can capitalize on their weakness. When someone leaves their door unlocked and a thief sees a chance to break in. When a company's market leader drops the ball and smaller competitors see an opening to gain market share.

m: To be well-organized, methodical, and systematic in one's actions or approach.
s: When describing someone who plans their work carefully and executes it step by step without any mistakes. When a company has clear processes and procedures that everyone follows precisely. When praising how someone manages their time and tasks in an organized and efficient manner.

m: Things are organized in a systematic and orderly manner with clear logic and structure.
s: When you see someone's workspace perfectly organized with everything in its place. When a project plan is well-structured with clear steps and procedures that make sense. When someone explains a complex topic in a way that's easy to follow because it flows logically from one point to the next.

m: Something is done in an orderly, methodical, and well-organized manner with proper rhythm or structure.
s: When someone performs a task with clear steps and precision, following a well-defined pattern. When a teacher explains a lesson in a structured way that's easy to follow, or when a musician plays with good timing and coordination.

l: have records that can be verified
m: Something is verifiable because there are written records or documented evidence of it.
s: When you need to prove something happened in the past by showing official documents or historical records. When someone questions a historical fact but you can point to reliable written sources that confirm it.

m: To be physically weak, exhausted, or lacking energy and vigor.
s: When someone is so tired after work that they can barely move or speak. When a sick person is recovering but still feels completely drained and can only move slowly. When someone speaks in a weak, quiet voice because they have no energy left.

m: To always agree to requests and fulfill whatever others ask for without refusal.
s: When someone is so accommodating that they say yes to everything people ask of them, even unreasonable requests. When a parent gives their child anything they want without ever saying no. When a friend is so generous and willing that everyone takes advantage of their kindness.

m: To take action with a clear purpose or goal, aiming efforts precisely at what needs to be addressed.
s: When a teacher designs lessons specifically for their students' weak areas instead of generic instruction. When a company tailors its marketing campaign to target its ideal customer rather than advertising broadly to everyone.

m: Something is so obvious and clear that everyone can see it without any doubt.
s: When a student's improvement in grades is so obvious that all the teachers notice it. When someone's talent is so evident that everyone recognizes it immediately without needing explanation.

m: Something is so excellent or beautiful that everyone who sees it recognizes and appreciates its value.
s: When a piece of art or performance is so good that critics and audiences alike give it praise. When a new product design is so elegant that people from all walks of life find it appealing and attractive.

p: yǒu yǎn bù shí tài shān
l: Having eyes yet not recognizing Mount Tai
m: To fail to recognize someone's importance, talent, or greatness despite being in their presence; to be blind to obvious merit or status.
s: When you don't realize someone famous or important is standing right in front of you until someone tells you. When a manager overlooks a very capable employee's talents and contributions. When you misjudge someone as ordinary and later discover they are actually highly respected or skilled.

l: having eyes but not seeing pearls
m: lacking the ability to recognize or appreciate value, talent, or beauty; being blind to what is obvious or important.
s: When someone fails to recognize a talented person's abilities and dismisses them. When a person overlooks an obvious opportunity or doesn't appreciate something valuable right in front of them.

p: yǒu fú tóng xiǎng ， yǒu huò tóng dāng
l: Share fortune together, share disaster together
m: True friends stand by each other through both good times and bad, sharing equally in success and hardship.
s: When a group of friends decides to split both their winnings and their losses fairly. When teammates commit to supporting each other whether they win or lose the game. When family members promise to help each other financially regardless of whether times are prosperous or difficult.

m: Describes something that is vivid, lifelike, and full of substance with genuine emotional depth and character.
s: When a writer creates a character that feels real and relatable rather than flat and one-dimensional. When someone tells a story with rich details and emotional authenticity that makes you feel connected to it.

m: Something was agreed upon or stated beforehand, so one is just following through on what was previously established.
s: When someone reminds you of a prior agreement you both made. When a friend says 'I told you this would happen' because they had warned you earlier about the consequences.

m: People who are knowledgeable, wise, and able to see things clearly and make good judgments.
s: When you're looking for advice from someone smart and experienced. When a company hires an expert consultant who truly understands their industry. When a historical figure is praised for having insight that others lacked at the time.

p: yǒu guò zhī ér wú bù jí
l: has surpassed it and has not fallen short
m: To be even more extreme or excessive than something else; to go beyond or exceed in a negative or exaggerated way.
s: When someone's behavior is not just as bad as another person's, but actually worse. When a situation gets escalated beyond what was already problematic, making it even more difficult or severe than before.

m: To indiscriminately record or accept all information without critical evaluation or verification.
s: When someone believes every rumor or piece of gossip they hear without questioning its accuracy. When a journalist publishes unverified claims just because they heard them from someone.

m: When people band together with bad intentions to commit wrongdoing or fraud through mutual collusion and conspiracy.
s: When a group of corrupt officials work together to embezzle public funds. When business partners secretly conspire to defraud their investors or customers. When friends gang up together to bully or harm someone else.

l: gaze at dust and cannot reach it
m: To fall far behind someone in ability or achievement, unable to catch up or even come close to their level.
s: When a student's grades are nowhere near as good as their classmate who always gets top marks. When a new employee's skills are far inferior to a senior colleague who has decades of experience. When a local athlete cannot compete at the level of an Olympic champion.

l: look at text and generate meaning
m: To interpret something based solely on its surface appearance or literal wording without understanding its true context or deeper meaning.
s: When someone misunderstands a technical term by only reading its literal definition without grasping how it's actually used in practice. When a person takes a figure of speech or idiom completely literally instead of understanding what it really means. When you judge a book by its title without reading it first.

l: gaze at plums to quench thirst
m: to comfort oneself with false hopes or imaginary solutions instead of addressing real problems.
s: When someone keeps saying they'll feel better once they get a promotion, but doesn't actually try to improve their skills or work harder. When a person talks about all the great things they'll do someday instead of taking any real action today.

l: gaze upon the ocean and heave a sigh
m: To feel helpless and despairing when facing something too vast or difficult to overcome.
s: When you stand before a huge problem that seems impossible to solve. When someone realizes they lack the ability or resources to achieve their ambitious goal.

l: gaze until eyes are about to break through
m: To look forward to something so intensely and for so long that one's eyes seem ready to burst from the strain of waiting and watching.
s: When you've been waiting at the airport for hours for a loved one's arrival and keep scanning the crowd desperately. When someone stares out the window all day waiting for news from someone they care about.

l: gaze and then retreat in steps
m: To hesitate and back away from something due to fear or intimidation before even attempting it.
s: When you see a difficult task and feel so overwhelmed that you don't even try to start. When someone looks at a steep mountain trail and decides to turn back without attempting the climb because it seems too challenging.

m: To inspire such dread or intimidation in others merely by one's appearance or presence that they are afraid to approach or challenge you.
s: When a strict teacher walks into a noisy classroom and everyone immediately goes silent just from seeing them. When a powerful leader's reputation is so fearsome that people tremble in their presence without them saying anything.

l: seeing the wind and scattering like wheat chaff
m: Forces or resistance collapse and scatter immediately upon the mere appearance or approach of a powerful opponent or authority.
s: When an army flees without putting up a fight at the rumor of an enemy's approach. When protesters quickly disperse the moment police arrive at the scene. When a bully's group of friends abandons him immediately when confronted by someone stronger.

m: to flee in panic at the slightest sign of danger or trouble, without even waiting to confirm the threat
s: When someone runs away from a situation based only on rumors or slight hints of trouble, without checking if the danger is real. When a group of people scatter and run the moment they hear a rumor that authorities are coming, even before anyone actually arrives.

m: Someone who is fickle and changes their mind constantly without any real reason or principle.
s: When your boss keeps changing the project requirements every few days without explanation. When a friend constantly switches between different career plans or romantic partners without committing to anything.

m: Life is so uncertain and precarious that you cannot be sure you will survive from morning until evening.
s: When a company is on the brink of bankruptcy and might collapse at any moment. When someone is seriously ill and their survival from day to day is uncertain. When a refugee or homeless person has no stable shelter and doesn't know where they'll be tomorrow.

l: morning does not plan for evening
m: To live in such poverty or uncertainty that one cannot plan beyond the immediate present and must focus solely on meeting today's basic needs.
s: When someone is so poor they don't know where their next meal will come from. When a person is in such a precarious financial situation that they can only think about surviving today without worrying about tomorrow.

m: A leader frequently changes their decisions or policies, making it impossible for others to follow consistent direction.
s: When a boss constantly reverses their decisions, making employees confused about what to do. When a government keeps changing its rules or regulations so often that people don't know what the current policy is.

l: depart at dawn and arrive at dusk
m: a journey that is short enough to be completed within a single day from morning to evening.
s: When describing a quick business trip where you leave early in the morning and return the same evening. When someone travels to a nearby city for a day visit, leaving at sunrise and coming back before sunset.

m: Full of youthful energy, vitality, and enthusiasm; displaying a vibrant and optimistic spirit characteristic of youth.
s: When describing a young team that approaches their work with infectious enthusiasm and optimism. When you see a group of students or young professionals who are eager, energetic, and positive about their goals and future.

m: Someone who frequently changes their allegiance, loyalty, or opinions depending on circumstances or who they are with.
s: When a politician supports different parties depending on which way the wind is blowing politically. When a friend agrees with whoever they're talking to at the moment, never sticking to their own principles. When a business partner keeps switching sides between competing companies based on profit opportunities.

m: To speak in a halting, stammering manner with frequent pauses and hesitations.
s: When someone is nervous during a presentation and keeps stuttering and losing their train of thought. When a person struggles to articulate their words clearly because they are anxious or unsure of what to say.

l: The wood has already become a boat
m: What is done is done and cannot be undone; it is too late to change the course of events.
s: When a major decision has already been made and implemented, and there's no point in complaining about it anymore. When someone has already committed to a plan and there's no turning back, even if others now have objections.

m: Attend to the fundamental or original source of something rather than being distracted by superficial matters.
s: When someone is focused on solving the root cause of a problem instead of just treating symptoms. When a leader reminds their team to remember the original mission and values that the organization was founded on, rather than getting lost in daily details.

m: To know or predict something before it happens, as if possessing prophetic or clairvoyant abilities.
s: When someone accurately predicts an outcome that hasn't happened yet, like a friend who guessed the plot twist before watching the movie. When a manager anticipates a problem and takes action to prevent it before it occurs.

l: not yet to be heavily blamed
m: An action or behavior, while not ideal, is understandable under the circumstances and does not deserve harsh criticism.
s: When someone makes a mistake but had good intentions or was in a difficult situation. When you want to defend someone's questionable choice by acknowledging that their reasoning was reasonable even if the outcome wasn't perfect.

m: to decline in health, vigor, or vitality prematurely, appearing or becoming old before one's actual age.
s: When someone works so hard that they look much older than they actually are. When a person's health deteriorates rapidly due to stress or illness, making them seem elderly when they're still relatively young. When someone wastes away their youth through poor lifestyle choices and ends up frail and tired.

m: Unable to escape from following common customs or behaving like everyone else, despite perhaps wanting to be different or above such things.
s: When someone tries to maintain high principles but eventually gives in to peer pressure or social expectations like everyone else. When a person who prides themselves on being unique ends up doing the same thing as the crowd anyway.

m: Take precautionary measures in advance before problems or difficulties arise.
s: When someone saves money for emergencies before they happen. When a company invests in new technology before their competitors catch up. When you study hard before an exam instead of waiting until the last minute.

l: Original nature is difficult to change
m: A person's fundamental nature or character is deeply ingrained and cannot be easily altered or reformed.
s: When someone reverts to their old bad habits despite promising to change. When you realize that no matter how hard someone tries, their core personality remains the same. When someone who was always selfish continues to act selfishly even after years of trying to be more generous.

l: the root and branch inverted and placed
m: To confuse priorities by treating what is secondary as primary and what is fundamental as unimportant.
s: When a student spends all their time on decoration and presentation but neglects actually learning the material. When a company focuses so much on fancy marketing that it ignores product quality and customer service.

m: The true nature or real appearance of something that has been hidden, disguised, or misunderstood.
s: When a dishonest person is finally caught and exposed. When you finally understand what someone's real intentions are after they've been pretending. When a complicated situation is finally explained clearly and you see what was really going on.

c: 朱门酒肉臭，路有冻死骨
p: zhū mén jiǔ ròu chòu ， lù yǒu dòng sǐ gǔ
l: Behind vermilion gates the smell of wine and meat is foul, on the road there are bones of the frozen dead
m: There is a stark contrast between the extravagant waste of the wealthy and the desperate poverty and suffering of common people.
s: When you see wealthy people throwing away expensive food while homeless people go hungry on the streets. When a luxury brand destroys unsold merchandise while families cannot afford basic necessities. When you notice extreme inequality in a city with mansions next to slums.

p: jī bù kě shī ， shí bù zài lái
l: The opportunity cannot be missed, time will not come again.
m: You must seize favorable opportunities immediately because they rarely come around twice and will not wait for you.
s: When a job offer with a great company comes along but you're hesitant to leave your current position. When you have a chance to invest in something promising but keep delaying the decision. When someone finally reaches out to reconnect after years but you keep putting off meeting up.

m: Some people are so incorrigible or hopeless that no amount of effort, teaching, or improvement can help them.
s: When someone refuses to change their bad behavior no matter how much you try to help them. When you're frustrated because a person has wasted their potential and won't make any effort to improve themselves.

m: A person who is completely worthless and beyond redemption, or something so fundamentally corrupt that it cannot be improved.
s: When describing someone who is lazy, immoral, and refuses to change their ways no matter what opportunities they're given. When talking about a project or organization that is so deeply flawed and corrupt that it's impossible to fix it.

l: kill one to warn a hundred
m: Punish one person severely as a warning to deter others from committing the same offense.
s: When a company fires an employee publicly for rule-breaking to discourage others from doing the same. When a teacher gives a student a harsh punishment as a warning to the rest of the class.

l: kill people without blinking an eye
m: To commit terrible acts of violence or cruelty without any hesitation, remorse, or emotional reaction.
s: When describing a ruthless dictator or criminal who commits heinous acts without showing any guilt or conscience. When someone is so hardened by violence that they can harm others casually and without any visible distress or regret.

m: to harm someone severely through indirect, cunning, or psychological means without leaving obvious evidence of wrongdoing.
s: When a coworker undermines you in meetings and spreads rumors to damage your reputation without directly confronting you. When someone uses manipulation or legal tactics to ruin another person's life or career while maintaining a clean public image.

m: To kill people indiscriminately and in great numbers, showing extreme cruelty and disregard for human life.
s: When describing a ruthless dictator or warlord who committed mass atrocities against the population. When talking about a violent conflict where one side committed horrific massacres without mercy.

l: kill people and destroy the mouth
m: to murder someone to prevent them from revealing a secret or testifying against you.
s: When a criminal kills a witness to prevent them from going to the police. When someone tries to silence someone else through violence or threats to keep them from exposing wrongdoing.

m: To commit serious crimes including killing people and stealing their possessions, representing the worst criminal behavior.
s: When describing a gang that not only steals from people but also commits violent acts against them. When discussing historical bandits or criminals who engaged in both violence and theft as part of their reign of terror.

l: kill with a return horse spear
m: To make a sudden unexpected counterattack or comeback after appearing to retreat or withdraw.
s: When a losing team scores multiple points in quick succession to catch up and take the lead. When someone who seemed defeated comes back with a surprising move to turn the tables on their opponent.

m: To display intense anger, hostility, or a threatening demeanor that suggests one is ready for violence or confrontation.
s: When someone storms into a room with an aggressive expression and clenched fists, clearly furious about something. When a rival team's players enter the field with an intimidating, aggressive attitude ready for a fierce confrontation.

l: Sacrifice one's body to achieve humaneness
m: To willingly die or make the ultimate sacrifice in order to uphold moral principles and righteousness.
s: When someone chooses to suffer greatly or even die rather than compromise their ethical beliefs. When a person stands firm on their principles despite facing severe consequences or threats to their life.

l: kill the chicken to get the egg
m: to destroy a valuable resource for short-term gain, resulting in the loss of future benefits.
s: When a company cuts corners on quality to save money in the short term, but loses customers and reputation in the long run. When someone harvests all the crops immediately instead of saving seeds for next year's planting. When a parent forces their child to study constantly without rest, burning them out and destroying their love of learning.

p: shā jī yān yòng niú dāo
l: Why use a ox knife to kill a chicken
m: It is unnecessary and wasteful to use something far too powerful or elaborate for a simple, minor task.
s: When someone brings professional equipment or tools to handle a trivial problem. When a skilled expert is called in to do basic work that anyone could do. When you're using an expensive, sophisticated solution for something that requires only simple effort.

l: kill the chicken to warn the monkeys
m: punish someone as an example to deter others from making the same mistake.
s: When a manager fires an underperforming employee to send a message to the rest of the team. When a teacher gives one student a harsh penalty so other students will behave better in class.

m: Something is chaotic, disorganized, and lacks any clear structure or system.
s: When you walk into someone's room and everything is scattered everywhere with no organization. When a company's files and documents are all mixed up and impossible to find what you need.

l: expedient measure of power and convenience
m: A temporary or makeshift solution adopted for immediate practical advantage rather than as a permanent or ideal resolution.
s: When a company hires temporary contractors just to meet an urgent deadline instead of hiring permanent staff. When someone uses a quick fix to solve a problem, knowing it's not the best long-term solution but it works for now.

m: To carefully consider and compare the relative importance or severity of different factors before making a decision.
s: When deciding between two job offers, you need to weigh the lightness and heaviness of salary versus work-life balance. A parent must weigh the lightness and heaviness of strict discipline versus allowing their child freedom to grow.

l: the plum tree dies in place of the peach tree
m: One person sacrifices themselves or suffers in place of another, often unknowingly or unwillingly.
s: When someone takes the blame for another person's mistake to protect them. When an innocent person is punished instead of the actual guilty party. When someone bears the consequences of another's actions without knowing it.

l: person from Qi worries about the sky
m: To worry excessively about imaginary or unlikely disasters that are beyond one's control.
s: When someone constantly catastrophizes about things that will probably never happen. When a friend is anxious about worst-case scenarios that have almost no chance of occurring, like worrying that the sky will fall on their head.

l: Bundle it and place it on a high shelf
m: To abandon or neglect something, leaving it unused and forgotten.
s: When you buy a book but never read it and it sits on your shelf for years. When a company develops a good idea but decides not to implement it and just forgets about it. When someone receives advice but ignores it and never acts on it.

m: To surrender without resistance or to accept defeat passively without putting up a fight.
s: When someone gives up easily without even trying to defend themselves or their position. When a person accepts an unjust situation without any attempt to resist or protest.

l: bind hands and wait for death
m: To passively accept an inevitable defeat or disaster without making any effort to resist or escape.
s: When someone faces a serious problem but does nothing to solve it, just waiting for things to get worse. When a company knows it's about to fail but refuses to take action to save itself. When a person gives up and stops trying to improve their situation.

m: To be completely helpless and unable to find any way to solve a problem.
s: When you face a difficult situation and have no idea what to do about it. When someone is stuck and has exhausted all possible solutions but nothing works.

m: To be severely restricted or constrained in one's ability to act freely and effectively.
s: When a manager has so many rules and regulations that they can't make decisions quickly. When a company is so afraid of legal issues that it can't innovate or take any risks.

l: separate by threads and analyze by strands
m: To analyze something in meticulous detail, breaking it down into its smallest components to understand it thoroughly.
s: When a lawyer carefully examines every detail of a contract before signing. When a teacher breaks down a complex math problem step by step to help students understand each part clearly. When someone investigates a problem at work by examining each factor and cause systematically.

l: The days that come are long
m: There is plenty of time ahead, so there is no need to rush or worry about things that can be done later.
s: When your friend is stressed about a deadline but you want to remind them they have plenty of opportunities in the future. When someone is reluctant to do something now because they feel pressured, and you're trying to assure them there will be other chances.

p: lái zhě bù shàn ， shàn zhě bù lái
l: Those who come are not kind, and those who are kind do not come.
m: When someone unexpectedly arrives or contacts you, it usually signals trouble or bad intentions; conversely, people with good intentions typically don't show up unannounced.
s: When a stranger suddenly appears at your door demanding something, you might think their arrival suggests bad news. When an old rival from school suddenly reaches out to you after years, you might be suspicious of their true motives. When someone you've been avoiding suddenly makes contact, it often means they want something from you rather than coming to help.

l: those who come are not refused
m: to welcome and accept anyone who arrives or seeks to join without rejection or discrimination
s: When a restaurant serves all customers regardless of their background or appearance. When a club or organization accepts every person who wants to join without turning anyone away. When someone is friendly and hospitable to all visitors who come to their home.

p: lái ér bù wǎng fēi lǐ yě
l: To receive without reciprocating is not courteous
m: It is impolite and disrespectful to accept someone's hospitality, gifts, or kindness without returning the favor or showing appreciation in kind.
s: When someone invites you to dinner and you should invite them back sometime. When a friend gives you a gift and you feel obligated to give them something in return to show respect and maintain the relationship.

m: The complete record or evidence of someone's movements, whereabouts, and activities, including where they came from and where they went.
s: When a detective is trying to track a suspect's movements and figure out everywhere they've been. When you're curious about someone's background and want to know their full history of where they've lived and traveled.

m: The complete sequence of events or full context of something from beginning to end.
s: When you need to understand the whole story of how a conflict started and developed. When explaining a project to someone and wanting them to know the complete background and progression of events.

m: To be overly suspicious and fearful, seeing danger or threats where none actually exist.
s: When someone is so paranoid that they interpret every innocent comment as a personal attack. When a person constantly worries that others are plotting against them despite having no real evidence.

l: a cup of water for a cart of firewood
m: An insignificant amount of help that is utterly insufficient to solve a major problem.
s: When you try to help someone in serious financial trouble with a small donation. When a company faces bankruptcy and receives a tiny government subsidy that won't make a real difference.

l: cups and plates in chaotic disorder
m: A scene of complete disorder and mess, typically after a meal or gathering where things have been left in disarray.
s: When you walk into a room after a wild party and find dishes, cups, and food scattered everywhere. When describing how messy your dining table looks after a large family dinner that nobody has cleaned up yet.

m: Someone or something has disappeared completely without any trace or news, never to be seen or heard from again.
s: When a friend suddenly moves away without saying goodbye and you never hear from them again. When someone borrows money and then completely disappears, leaving no contact information or way to reach them.

l: distant and without sound or message
m: Someone has disappeared or gone missing with no news or communication from them for a long time.
s: When a friend suddenly stops responding to calls and messages and you haven't heard from them in months. When someone goes traveling abroad and completely stops contacting their family, leaving everyone worried about their whereabouts.

m: To expend effort, thought, or scheming on something that ultimately proves futile or pointless.
s: When you spend hours planning a surprise party but the person finds out anyway. When someone devises an elaborate excuse to avoid work but gets caught anyway. When you stay up late crafting the perfect argument but the other person won't listen no matter what you say.

l: pillow spear and wait for dawn
m: to remain vigilant and prepared for battle, ready to respond to danger at any moment without rest.
s: When soldiers are stationed at a border and must stay alert through the night in case of attack. When a security team remains on high alert during a critical situation, ready to act immediately if needed. When someone is anxious about an upcoming challenge and cannot relax, staying tense and prepared.

l: forest of spears and rain of bullets
m: An intense and dangerous situation with heavy gunfire or overwhelming attacks coming from all directions.
s: When soldiers are caught in intense enemy fire during battle. When someone faces multiple aggressive criticisms or attacks at the same time from different people. When describing any chaotic and dangerous situation with constant threats coming from everywhere.

l: owl head displayed to the public
m: To execute a criminal by beheading and publicly displaying their head as a warning and punishment.
s: When a government makes an example of a serious criminal by executing them publicly. When someone faces severe public humiliation and punishment for their crimes as a deterrent to others.

m: A person or situation that seemed hopeless or finished experiences an unexpected revival or second chance at life.
s: When someone who was struggling or down on their luck suddenly gets a new opportunity and turns their life around. When a failing business gets new investment and becomes successful again. When an old relationship or friendship is rekindled after years of being apart.

m: To serve the state or public good selflessly despite personal hardship and deprivation.
s: When a civil servant works tirelessly for the people despite earning very little and struggling to feed their family. When someone sacrifices their own comfort and well-being to fulfill their public duties or serve a greater cause.

l: investigate and find no substantive evidence
m: There is no concrete evidence or factual basis to support a claim or accusation.
s: When police investigate a crime but cannot find any physical evidence to prove who did it. When someone accuses another person of something but cannot provide any proof or documentation to back up their claim.

l: mark the new and establish the different
m: To deliberately adopt novel or unconventional ideas and practices in order to stand out from the crowd.
s: When a designer creates a fashion line that looks nothing like current trends and deliberately chooses shocking colors and cuts. When a student refuses to follow the standard essay format and invents their own structure just to be unique. When a company markets itself as completely different from all competitors, even if their actual product quality is the same.

l: combing the wind and bathing in the rain
m: To endure hardship and adversity through persistent effort and determination over a long period of time.
s: When someone has worked hard outdoors in difficult weather conditions for years to build their business. When describing a person who has struggled through many challenges and obstacles to achieve their goals.

l: the tree falls and the monkeys scatter
m: When a powerful leader or organization collapses, those who depended on it for support quickly abandon it and go their separate ways.
s: When a company goes bankrupt and all the employees who were only there for the paycheck immediately look for new jobs elsewhere. When a politician loses power and their staff and supporters quickly distance themselves and find new positions.

l: A tall tree invites the wind
m: When someone becomes too prominent, successful, or powerful, they attract criticism, envy, and trouble from others.
s: When a successful business owner starts facing lawsuits and scandals after becoming too famous and wealthy. When a high-achieving student gets bullied by classmates out of jealousy. When a celebrity tries to stay humble to avoid attracting negative attention and controversy.

p: shù yù jìng ér fēng bù zhǐ
l: The tree desires stillness but the wind does not cease
m: One cannot control external circumstances even when one wishes for peace or stability; sometimes misfortune strikes regardless of one's desires.
s: When someone is trying to live a quiet life but keeps getting pulled into drama or conflict. When you want to focus on your work but keep getting interrupted by unexpected problems or demands from others.

l: erect a monument and compose a biography
m: To be remembered for great deeds and have one's accomplishments recorded for posterity.
s: When someone does something so impressive and meaningful that people want to commemorate them forever. When discussing how historical figures are honored and remembered through monuments and written records of their lives.

p: shù gāo qiān zhàng ， yè luò guī gēn
l: A tree a thousand cubits high, its leaves fall and return to the root
m: No matter how far one travels or how successful one becomes, one will ultimately return to one's hometown or origin.
s: When someone who has achieved great success in a distant city decides to move back to their hometown. When an immigrant who has lived abroad for decades decides to return to their native country to retire. When a person reflects on how important it is to reconnect with family roots despite having built a life elsewhere.

m: Something is depicted or described so realistically and vividly that it appears to be alive or authentic.
s: When you see a painting so detailed that the subject looks like it might move at any moment. When a writer describes a character so well that you feel like you know them personally. When a sculptor creates a statue that looks so realistic it's almost eerie.

m: Something is so deeply established or ingrained that it is extremely difficult to change or remove.
s: When a person has held the same belief their entire life and refuses to consider other perspectives. When a company has a corporate culture that has been in place for decades and resists any reform. When prejudices or bad habits have become so integrated into someone's behavior that they seem impossible to break.

m: To kill or punish someone without mercy or consideration, treating them as an enemy that must be eliminated.
s: When a military commander orders troops to show no mercy to invaders and kill them on sight. When someone is deemed such a threat that there is no room for negotiation or mercy in dealing with them.

l: squares and circles do not fit together
m: Things that are fundamentally incompatible or unable to harmonize with each other.
s: When a quiet, introverted person joins a group of loud, extroverted party-goers and just doesn't mesh with the crowd. When someone with traditional values tries to fit into a modern, progressive workplace but constantly clashes with the culture. When a formal, strict teacher's rigid style conflicts with a school's relaxed, creative learning environment.

l: The tyrannical dog barks at the sage
m: Petty people with no virtue attack and criticize those who are virtuous and worthy, unable to recognize true merit.
s: When someone criticizes a respected leader or good person out of jealousy or malice. When mediocre people attack excellent ones simply because they cannot appreciate their superiority.

m: A person who is stubborn, rebellious, and refuses to be controlled or disciplined by others.
s: When a teenager constantly defies their parents' authority and ignores all rules. When a wild horse refuses to be tamed no matter what methods you try. When an employee openly challenges their boss and refuses to follow company policies.

l: peach and plum blossoms fill the world
m: A teacher or mentor has cultivated many successful students and disciples who are spread throughout society.
s: When describing a respected professor who has taught thousands of students now working in important positions across the country. When honoring a mentor whose former students have become leaders in their fields and are recognized everywhere.

m: A euphemistic or ironic way to refer to a thief or burglar who hides in the rafters or roof of a house.
s: When someone steals from you and you want to describe them indirectly or humorously. When discussing a burglary that occurred in someone's home, using old-fashioned or coded language.

l: dream and sleep in pursuit of
m: To desire something so intensely that you think about it constantly, even in your dreams.
s: When someone has wanted something for years and finally gets it, like a musician who dreamed of performing at a big concert. When a student works hard for a goal they've been hoping for since childhood, such as getting into their dream university.

m: All things in life are transient and illusory, lacking substance or permanence, like dreams that fade upon waking.
s: When reflecting on how quickly youth passes and seems unreal in retrospect. When someone realizes their past ambitions were hollow and meaningless. When contemplating the impermanence of wealth, status, or relationships that once seemed so important.

l: comb hair and apply makeup to dress up
m: To carefully groom oneself and dress up in fine clothes to look attractive and presentable.
s: When a woman spends time doing her hair and makeup before going out for an important event. When someone wants to make a good impression and takes care to look their best for a special occasion.

m: Two evenly matched competitors or adversaries who are of equal skill and ability.
s: When two athletes compete and they're both equally talented, neither one has a clear advantage. When you finally meet someone who challenges you intellectually in a debate or discussion because they're just as smart as you are.

l: the forest of all forms and phenomena
m: All things in the universe and the infinite variety of natural phenomena and creation.
s: When describing the vast diversity of nature and everything that exists in the world. When marveling at how many different forms of life and matter fill our universe. When trying to express the idea that all things in existence, from the smallest to the largest, are interconnected and part of one grand whole.

m: No one can escape or be exempted from something that applies universally to all.
s: When describing a rule or fate that applies to absolutely everyone without exception. When explaining that even important people must follow the same laws or face the same consequences as ordinary people.

m: To be deliberately ambiguous or noncommittal, leaving room for multiple interpretations.
s: When a politician gives a vague answer that could mean yes or no depending on how you interpret it. When someone refuses to take a clear stance on an issue and uses words that could be understood in different ways.

m: Things are scattered and disorganized in every direction without any order or pattern.
s: When you walk into a room and clothes are thrown all over the floor in messy piles. When books and papers are scattered randomly across a desk instead of being neatly arranged. When cars are parked haphazardly in a lot without following any line or organization.

m: To act recklessly and impetuously without regard for consequences or others in the way.
s: When someone rushes into a situation without thinking it through. When a person barges into a room without knocking or pushes through a crowd without consideration for others. When someone makes hasty decisions that create problems for everyone around them.

m: A government or authority uses harsh, excessive, and arbitrary taxation or levies to extract wealth from the people in a cruel and oppressive manner.
s: When a corrupt official imposes unreasonable taxes on farmers and merchants without justification. When a company aggressively squeezes customers with unfair fees and charges while showing no concern for their financial hardship.

m: to achieve overwhelming victory or success by defeating all opposition with great force and momentum.
s: When a sports team dominates their opponents so completely that they win by a huge margin. When a political candidate wins an election by an enormous landslide, defeating all rivals decisively.

m: Unexpected complications or obstacles suddenly arise to disrupt progress or plans.
s: When you're trying to complete a simple project but suddenly face unforeseen problems that delay everything. When a straightforward business deal suddenly encounters new issues that weren't anticipated before.

m: To act with complete disregard for rules or consequences, behaving arrogantly and without any sense of fear or accountability.
s: When a powerful person bullies others openly without worrying about getting punished. When a criminal gang operates openly in a neighborhood, stealing and threatening people without fear of the police. When someone uses their position of authority to do whatever they want, ignoring all rules and treating others poorly.

l: traverse arrogantly and bully the way
m: To act with arrogant dominance and bully others without restraint, treating oneself as above rules and consequences.
s: When a powerful person in a workplace intimidates colleagues and ignores policies because they think no one can stop them. When a wealthy individual throws their weight around in a community, demanding special treatment and dismissing others' concerns.

m: A large crowd is cheering loudly and enthusiastically, creating an overwhelming noise that fills the space.
s: When a sports team scores the winning goal and the stadium erupts in loud cheers from thousands of fans. When a popular singer finishes their final song at a concert and the audience roars with applause and excitement.

m: Extremely happy and joyful, with a sense of celebration and delight pervading everything.
s: When a couple gets married and the whole family is celebrating together with great happiness. When you finally get a job offer you've been waiting for and you're in an excellent mood all day. When a child gets their desired gift and runs around the house filled with excitement and joy.

l: joyful and excited, drums and dance
m: To feel great joy and excitement, often expressed through celebration or enthusiastic behavior.
s: When your team wins an important competition and everyone is cheering and celebrating together. When you get news of something wonderful you've been hoping for, like a job offer or acceptance to your dream school, and you can't contain your happiness.

m: To be overwhelmingly happy and excited, losing one's composure due to extreme joy.
s: When someone receives unexpectedly good news like winning a lottery or getting their dream job and they can barely contain their excitement. When a fan finally meets their favorite celebrity after years of waiting and they become completely overjoyed.

m: Something is developing vibrantly and showing signs of great success and growth.
s: When a new business is growing rapidly and doing very well. When you see a garden full of blooming flowers and lush green plants thriving in spring.

p: yù jiā zhī zuì ， hé huàn wú cí
l: If you want to add a crime, why fear lacking a pretext?
m: When someone is determined to punish or harm another person, they can always find or fabricate an excuse to justify their actions.
s: When a boss who dislikes an employee finds minor mistakes to fire them, inventing reasons that weren't previously concerns. When an authoritarian government wants to arrest a dissident and simply manufactures evidence or charges against them. When someone is already determined to end a relationship and will use any small flaw or misunderstanding as justification.

m: To obtain something you desire, you must first give or make concessions to others.
s: When you need to compromise or make sacrifices now in order to achieve your goals later. When someone realizes they need to be generous first before they can expect generosity in return, like a business owner investing in customer service to build loyalty that will eventually bring profits.

l: The abyss of desire is hard to fill
m: Greed and desire are insatiable; no matter how much one obtains, it is never enough.
s: When a wealthy person keeps wanting more money and possessions despite already having plenty. When someone's ambitions grow bigger with every success, never feeling satisfied with their achievements.

l: wanting to capture so deliberately releasing
m: To deliberately let something go in order to gain control over it later; a strategic retreat or pretense of indifference to achieve a larger goal.
s: When a negotiator deliberately makes concessions early on to build trust, then gains leverage later in the deal. When someone plays hard to get in a relationship to make themselves more attractive. When a general retreats strategically to draw the enemy into a trap.

l: wanting to cover makes it more apparent
m: Attempting to hide or conceal something only serves to draw more attention to it and make it more obvious.
s: When someone tries to cover up a mistake at work but their excuses make it even more suspicious. When a student tries to hide a bad test score from their parents but their secretive behavior makes the parents more curious and investigative.

l: wanting to stop but unable to
m: Unable to stop doing something despite wanting to, whether due to external constraint, addiction, or compulsion.
s: When someone keeps scrolling on their phone even though they know they should sleep. When a person wants to quit a bad habit but finds themselves unable to break free from it. When someone is forced to continue a task against their will because they have no choice.

m: Rushing to achieve something quickly often backfires and prevents you from reaching your goal.
s: When someone is trying to finish a project so fast that they make careless mistakes and end up taking longer. When a student rushes through studying and doesn't actually learn the material, doing worse on the exam as a result.

l: deceive the world and steal a name
m: To gain undeserved fame or reputation through deception and dishonest means.
s: When someone takes credit for work they didn't do to boost their reputation. When a person uses fake credentials or misleads others to appear more accomplished than they actually are. When a company makes false claims about their product to gain market recognition.

m: Dishonest or misleading speech intended to deceive others.
s: When a salesman makes exaggerated claims about a product that aren't true. When someone tells lies to manipulate you into doing something against your interest.

m: To treat others with such blatant disrespect and dishonesty that it becomes intolerable and crosses all moral boundaries.
s: When someone lies to your face repeatedly and doesn't even try to hide it anymore. When a boss makes unreasonable demands and acts like employees should just accept being mistreated without question.

l: bully the soft and fear the hard
m: to act aggressively toward those weaker than oneself while showing cowardice or submission toward those who are stronger.
s: When someone is mean to their subordinates but acts very polite and obedient around their boss. When a student picks on classmates they can easily beat up but immediately backs down when confronted by someone tougher.

m: to excessively praise someone's achievements or qualities, often in a flattering or insincere manner.
s: When politicians or media outlets constantly glorify a leader's accomplishments without any criticism. When coworkers excessively flatter their boss to gain favor, regardless of whether the praise is deserved.

l: songs and dances ascending to peace
m: A state of superficial peace and prosperity characterized by excessive entertainment and revelry, often masking underlying social problems or instability.
s: When a government focuses on propaganda and entertainment to distract citizens from serious economic issues. When a company throws lavish parties and celebrates while ignoring warning signs of decline in its core business.

m: Something turns out exactly as you hoped or desired, perfectly matching your wishes.
s: When your friend suggests going to your favorite restaurant for dinner, exactly what you wanted. When a job opportunity comes up that offers precisely the role and salary you were looking for.

m: A person of high moral character, integrity, and virtue who conducts themselves with honesty and righteousness.
s: When describing someone who always does the right thing even when no one is watching. When praising a friend who stands up for their principles and refuses to compromise their values for personal gain.

l: Correct the root and purify the source
m: To solve a problem by addressing its fundamental cause rather than just treating the symptoms.
s: When a company keeps having quality issues, you need to fix the root cause in manufacturing rather than just handling complaints. When someone repeatedly fails exams, they should address their fundamental understanding of the subject instead of just studying harder the night before.

m: To sit in a formal, dignified, and respectful manner, often adopting a serious demeanor.
s: When someone suddenly becomes very formal and serious in front of an authority figure like a boss or teacher. When you need to present yourself professionally and composedly during an important meeting or interview.

m: To display a stern, serious, and dignified expression that shows disapproval or authority.
s: When a teacher looks at a misbehaving student with a stern face to show displeasure. When a parent gives their child a serious look to indicate they are upset about something they did. When someone addresses a group with a grave expression to emphasize the importance of what they're saying.

p: cǐ dì wú yín sān bǎi liǎng
l: This place has no silver three hundred taels
m: Attempting to deny or hide something only serves to draw attention to it and reveal the very thing you were trying to conceal.
s: When someone denies a rumor so loudly and repeatedly that everyone becomes convinced it's true. When a person tries to cover up a mistake but their excessive explanations make it obvious they're guilty.

m: Things occur in succession or alternation, with one thing rising or appearing as another falls or disappears, often describing continuous waves of activity or noise.
s: When multiple people are shouting or talking one after another in a meeting, creating continuous noise. When waves of applause come from different parts of an audience at a concert, with some people clapping while others stop.

l: tread in the dust behind others
m: To follow in someone else's footsteps or imitate what others have done instead of forging your own path.
s: When a student copies their classmate's essay instead of writing their own. When a company just imitates what successful competitors are doing rather than innovating.

m: Someone is having great difficulty walking or moving forward, whether due to physical exhaustion, injury, or being weighed down by burdens.
s: When an elderly person is struggling to walk due to age or illness. When someone is so tired after a long journey that they can barely move forward. When a person is carrying such heavy loads that they can only shuffle along slowly.

l: advance with measured steps and establish camp at each step
m: To advance cautiously and methodically, consolidating one's position at each stage rather than rushing forward recklessly.
s: When a company carefully expands into new markets one region at a time, ensuring success before moving to the next. When someone builds their skills gradually through deliberate practice, mastering each level before advancing to harder challenges.

m: To move or act together in perfect coordination and agreement with others.
s: When a team works together smoothly toward the same goal without any disagreement. When two countries align their policies and strategies to work as partners. When dancers or marching soldiers move perfectly synchronized together.

m: Corrupt, immoral, or perverse influences and practices that spread through society or an organization.
s: When a workplace develops a toxic culture where unethical behavior becomes normalized and accepted. When a community is plagued by criminal gangs and antisocial behavior that corrupts the local atmosphere.

m: to die with deep regret, resentment, or unfinished business, unable to rest in peace.
s: When someone passes away feeling they were treated unjustly and never got closure. When a person dies before achieving an important goal they spent their whole life pursuing. When someone leaves this world with unresolved conflicts or betrayals still weighing heavily on them.

m: to die in an unexpected, violent, or unnatural way rather than from old age or natural causes.
s: When someone dies in a car accident instead of living a long healthy life. When a young person passes away suddenly from an accident or violence. When discussing someone who met a tragic or premature death.

m: To experience an extreme oscillation between states of near-death and recovery, or to undergo intense fear and relief in rapid succession.
s: When someone is so terrified they feel like they might faint, then suddenly feel relief and come back to themselves. When a patient is in critical condition and the doctors manage to revive them at the last moment, bringing them back from the brink of death.

m: to die in a way that is worthy, honorable, or meaningful, having fulfilled one's purpose or duty.
s: When someone sacrifices their life for a noble cause and people want to acknowledge their death was meaningful. When describing a soldier or hero who died protecting others and their death is considered honorable and appropriate.

m: To be completely devoted or committed to something without any hesitation or doubt.
s: When someone is absolutely determined to marry their partner no matter what obstacles arise. When an employee is completely loyal to their company and willing to work there for the rest of their life. When a fan is devoted to a celebrity or sports team through thick and thin.

m: When someone is dead, there is no way to verify their account or contradict claims made about them, making it impossible to establish the truth.
s: When someone blames a deceased person for something that can't be proven or disproven. When a person makes accusations about what a dead person supposedly did or said, knowing no one can refute them because that person is no longer alive to defend themselves.

m: A person's crimes are so severe that death alone is insufficient punishment for the wrongs they have committed.
s: When someone has committed such heinous acts that execution seems too lenient. When describing a criminal whose atrocities are so grave that even the ultimate penalty doesn't feel like adequate justice.

m: An atmosphere or environment that is completely devoid of life, energy, or vitality, creating a gloomy and oppressive feeling.
s: When you walk into a room where everyone is silent and depressed with no one talking or smiling. When a once-lively workplace becomes dull and lifeless after layoffs or bad news. When a party or gathering has such a negative mood that all the energy and fun has drained away.

m: Something that was thought to be completely finished or ended suddenly comes back to life or resumes activity.
s: When an old conflict between two people suddenly flares up again after years of peace. When a failed business that everyone thought was done suddenly reopens and becomes active again. When someone's old bad habits that seemed cured suddenly return with force.

m: To shamelessly and persistently pester or importune someone despite rejection or disapproval.
s: When someone keeps asking you for money even after you've said no multiple times. When a person won't stop begging for a favor despite being turned down repeatedly and shows no embarrassment about their behavior.

m: To memorize something mechanically without understanding its meaning or reasoning.
s: When a student memorizes facts for a test without actually comprehending the concepts. When someone repeats information they've heard but can't explain it or apply it to new situations.

m: To narrowly escape from a life-threatening situation or survive against all odds.
s: When someone survives a serious car accident that could have killed them. When a person recovers from a severe illness that doctors thought was fatal. When someone narrowly avoids danger in an emergency situation.

p: sǐ mǎ dāng huó mǎ yī
l: treat a dead horse as a living horse doctor
m: To try any desperate remedy or attempt anything possible when facing a hopeless situation, even if the effort is futile.
s: When a company is failing and the owner tries every possible strategy to save it, even unrealistic ones. When someone is seriously ill and the family tries experimental treatments as a last resort, regardless of the low chance of success.

m: A person feels profound worry, compassion, or concern for someone or something, showing deep emotional investment and care.
s: When a parent loses sleep worrying about their child's health or future. When an old friend hears that someone they care about is going through a difficult time and feels genuine, deep sorrow for them.

l: Different paths lead to the same destination
m: Although people may use different methods or take different routes, they can ultimately arrive at the same result or conclusion.
s: When multiple colleagues approach a project differently but all produce equally good results. When friends have different opinions or strategies but end up agreeing on the final decision. When various scientific theories or mathematical approaches all prove the same underlying truth.

m: A disorganized group of survivors left after a major defeat or failure, typically lacking strength or cohesion.
s: When a team has lost most of its key players due to injury or departure and is struggling to compete. When a company has gone through massive layoffs and the remaining employees are demoralized and scattered across different locations.

m: A landscape devastated by war or disaster, with only fragments of its former natural beauty remaining.
s: When describing a war-torn region that has been heavily damaged and depleted. When discussing environmental destruction or urban decay where nature has been ravaged and little remains intact.

l: leftover cups and cold meat scraps
m: Something that is discarded, unwanted, or treated as unimportant; the remnants or leftovers that nobody wants.
s: When someone treats you like you're not worth their time or attention, as if you're just leftovers. When a company gets rid of old employees or products that are no longer profitable, leaving them as forgotten remnants.

m: The remaining members of a defeated enemy faction or evil force who continue to cause trouble or refuse to surrender.
s: When describing the last surviving members of a criminal organization still operating after their leaders are caught. When referring to the remaining supporters of a fallen regime or movement who persist in their opposition.
