m: Something is broken, defective, or missing essential parts, making it no longer whole or functional.
s: When you receive a product with missing pieces or broken parts. When a book has pages torn out or a collection is missing key items. When important information is lost or a project is left unfinished.

l: The mirror of the past is not far away
m: Recent history provides a clear cautionary example that is close at hand and should serve as a warning for present decisions.
s: When a company is about to make the same mistake that bankrupted a competitor just last year. When someone is about to repeat a failed approach that didn't work for their friend a few months ago, and you want to remind them that the example is right there in front of them.

m: Something that took a long time to build or achieve is completely destroyed or lost in a very short time.
s: When a company's reputation is destroyed overnight by a scandal after years of building trust. When someone loses their life savings in a bad investment after decades of saving.

m: To act with firm determination and unwavering resolve, without hesitation or doubt.
s: When someone makes a difficult decision and commits to it completely without looking back. When a person leaves their job to pursue their dream despite the risks. When someone stands up for their principles even when facing opposition.

m: Things continue to get progressively worse over time without any sign of improvement.
s: When a student's grades keep dropping semester after semester despite having the ability to do better. When a company's financial situation deteriorates month after month as it loses customers and revenue. When someone's health condition keeps getting worse even though they're receiving treatment.

p: měi féng jiā jié bèi sī qīn
l: Every time a festive occasion arrives, one thinks of relatives even more
m: On holidays and special occasions, one's longing for distant family members becomes especially acute and poignant.
s: When you're spending a holiday alone far away from home and miss your family more than usual. When someone receives a family video call during a major festival and realizes how much they miss being together in person.

p: bǐ shàng bù zú ， bǐ xià yǒu yú
l: Compared to those above, insufficient; compared to those below, excessive
m: One's circumstances are mediocre—not as good as those better off, but better than those worse off.
s: When describing someone who is content with a middle-class lifestyle, not striving to be wealthy but grateful they're not poor. When a student gets a B grade and feels satisfied because it's better than failing, even if it's not an A. When someone has a modest job that pays decently and they feel fortunate, even though their colleagues in senior positions earn much more.

m: Something is extremely common and can be found or seen almost everywhere.
s: When you notice that many people in your office are working from home these days. When a particular style of clothing suddenly becomes popular and you see it on almost everyone at the mall.

l: shoulders side by side, heels touching
m: A large crowd of people standing so close together that they are touching shoulder to shoulder and heel to heel.
s: When you're in a packed subway during rush hour and everyone is squeezed tightly together. When you're at a crowded concert or festival where people are standing so close that you can barely move.

p: bì qí gōng yú yī yì
l: Complete all one's achievements in a single undertaking
m: To attempt to accomplish everything or reach a final goal all at once through one decisive action or effort.
s: When a student crams all their studying into one night before an exam hoping to pass. When a struggling business puts all their resources into one final marketing campaign to save the company. When someone tries to solve all their problems through one big decision or action.

m: Acting in a careless, hasty, or clumsy manner without proper attention to detail.
s: When someone rushes through their work and makes mistakes because they're not being careful. When a person is constantly knocking things over or breaking things because they're too rough or thoughtless in their movements.

m: To volunteer oneself for a task or position without being asked, showing initiative and confidence in one's own abilities.
s: When someone sees a challenging project and steps forward to take it on without waiting to be asked. When a new employee offers to lead a meeting or presentation because they believe they can do a good job. When someone puts themselves forward for an opportunity they really want instead of waiting for an invitation.

l: hair and bones shudder with dread
m: To feel an intense, overwhelming sense of fear or horror that makes one's entire body tremble involuntarily.
s: When you watch a scary movie and get so frightened that you feel chills run down your spine. When someone tells you a horrifying ghost story late at night and you can't stop shaking.

m: To be completely indifferent or unconcerned about something, showing no regard whatsoever.
s: When someone dismisses your concerns and acts like they don't care at all what you think. When a person continues doing something despite repeated complaints from others around them.

l: not off by a hair's breadth
m: To be perfectly accurate or precise with no deviation whatsoever from the target or expected result.
s: When a skilled archer hits the exact center of a target every single time. When an accountant's ledger balances perfectly without any discrepancy. When someone's prediction turns out to be completely correct down to every detail.

m: Two or more things are completely identical or indistinguishable from each other.
s: When two products look and function exactly the same way. When two people's opinions or arguments are completely the same. When comparing two situations that turn out to be no different at all.

c: 民不畏死，奈何以死惧之
p: mín bù wèi sǐ ， nài hé yǐ sǐ jù zhī
l: If the people do not fear death, how can you threaten them with death?
m: When people are desperate or have nothing left to lose, threats of death become ineffective as a means of control or coercion.
s: When a government tries to intimidate protesters who are already facing severe hardship and have nothing to lose. When someone attempts to threaten another person who is already willing to sacrifice everything for their cause or beliefs.

l: the common people have no way to live
m: The people are suffering so severely from hardship, oppression, or disaster that they can barely survive or have no hope for their lives.
s: When a country experiences severe economic collapse and people cannot afford basic necessities like food or shelter. When a government's policies are so oppressive that ordinary citizens lose all hope and cannot sustain themselves.

l: The people regard food as heaven
m: Food is the most essential and important thing in people's lives, more fundamental than anything else.
s: When discussing why a country invests heavily in agriculture and food production. When explaining why someone prioritizes earning money for meals over other activities. When a government faces criticism for not ensuring food security for its citizens.

l: the people's resentment boils and seethes
m: The masses are extremely angry and their discontent has reached a fever pitch.
s: When a government policy causes widespread anger among citizens. When a company's unfair treatment of workers sparks public outrage and protests. When repeated injustices finally ignite massive public dissatisfaction.

m: The common people's living conditions have deteriorated severely, resulting in widespread poverty and suffering.
s: When a country experiences economic collapse and ordinary citizens can no longer afford food or shelter. When a government's poor policies lead to mass unemployment and decline in the quality of life for ordinary families.

l: the people impoverished and wealth exhausted
m: A state where both the common people and the government have become extremely poor, with all resources completely depleted.
s: When a country has spent so much on wars or corruption that ordinary citizens are starving and the government has no money left. When years of mismanagement have left both the treasury empty and the population destitute.

l: the fat and marrow of the people
m: The wealth and resources of the common people, especially when extracted or exploited by those in power.
s: When a government imposes heavy taxes on ordinary citizens to fund lavish projects. When corrupt officials embezzle public funds that were meant for social welfare programs.

m: To approach or confront someone in a threatening, aggressive, or intimidating manner with obvious hostile intent.
s: When someone storms into a room looking angry and ready to pick a fight. When a group of people marches toward you with clear hostile intentions and an intimidating presence.

l: momentum and spirit magnanimous and expansive
m: Something has an impressively grand, powerful, and commanding presence or scale.
s: When describing a massive mountain range that overwhelms you with its size and majesty. When a musical performance or artistic work is so bold and sweeping that it captivates the entire audience. When a leader or speaker commands attention through their sheer confidence and powerful demeanor.

m: To possess such grand ambition, courage, or momentum that one seems capable of conquering the entire world.
s: When a young entrepreneur presents their startup vision with such confidence and passion that they seem unstoppable. When a military leader or revolutionary figure displays such overwhelming power and determination that they appear to dominate an entire nation.

m: People who share the same interests, values, or temperament naturally get along well and form close connections.
s: When two friends discover they both love the same obscure band and immediately become inseparable. When you meet someone at a party who has the exact same sense of humor as you do and you just click instantly. When colleagues who both prefer working late at night and have similar work styles become best friends in the office.

l: spirit grand as mountains and rivers
m: Someone possesses such tremendous courage, ambition, or moral character that it seems to rival the grandeur of nature itself.
s: When a leader inspires their followers with such bold vision and confidence that everyone feels invincible. When someone stands up against injustice with such conviction and strength that they seem almost superhuman. When a hero's unwavering determination and noble spirit make them seem larger than life.

l: angry and frustrated to the point of ruin
m: To become extremely angry and lose one's composure, acting irrationally or badly due to intense rage.
s: When someone gets so mad during an argument that they start yelling insults or throwing things. When a person loses their temper completely and does something they'll regret, like storming out or saying hurtful things they don't mean.

m: On the verge of death or collapse; barely alive with only a faint breath remaining.
s: When an elderly person is gravely ill and may not survive the night. When an old business is barely operating and about to shut down. When someone is exhausted to the point of being barely conscious.

m: To display extreme arrogance and aggression, behaving in a domineering and menacing manner without regard for others.
s: When a bully intimidates others and acts like they can do whatever they want without consequences. When a powerful person throws their weight around and disrespects everyone beneath them. When someone becomes increasingly reckless and bold after getting away with bad behavior.

m: A scene or landscape displays magnificent and varied beauty with countless impressive features and constantly changing splendor.
s: When you stand on a high mountain and see the vast landscape with changing weather, clouds, and light creating a spectacular view. When describing a grand natural scene like a canyon or seascape where the scenery is dramatically beautiful and seems to shift with every angle you observe it from.

m: An extremely powerful and imposing presence or spirit that seems to reach toward the heavens with great force and grandeur.
s: When describing a leader or warrior with an overwhelming commanding presence that inspires awe in those around them. When someone displays such fierce determination and strength that they seem almost superhuman or larger than life.

l: fish for the moon in the water
m: To pursue something that is impossible to obtain or an illusion with no basis in reality.
s: When someone is chasing an unrealistic dream that has no chance of happening. When a person wastes time and effort trying to achieve something that is fundamentally impossible, like trying to become famous overnight without any talent or work.

m: Two things or people are so closely integrated and harmonious that they become inseparable, like water and milk mixing perfectly.
s: When two countries have such close diplomatic relations that their cultures and economies are deeply intertwined. When a married couple work together so seamlessly in their business that you can't distinguish one person's contribution from the other's.

l: when water arrives, the channel is formed
m: When conditions are right and sufficient effort has been made, success comes naturally without forcing it.
s: When a student has studied hard all semester and finally passes the exam easily. When a business gradually builds its customer base and suddenly becomes profitable without any special marketing push. When two people have spent years getting to know each other and their relationship naturally progresses to the next level.

m: so densely packed or crowded that nothing can pass through, not even water; completely blocked or impenetrable.
s: When you're at a packed concert or festival and there are so many people you literally cannot move in any direction. When a highway is so congested during rush hour that traffic is completely stopped and nothing can advance.

m: When external conditions improve, all related parties benefit proportionally, or one's circumstances improve as the overall situation gets better.
s: When the economy booms and everyone's business grows together. When a company's profits increase and all employees get bonuses as a result. When a student's test scores improve because the entire class's academic level rises due to a better teacher.

m: People are suffering from extreme hardship and misery, as if caught between dangerous forces on all sides.
s: When describing a country experiencing both natural disasters and war at the same time. When talking about a community facing multiple severe crises simultaneously, like economic collapse combined with disease outbreak.

m: Persistent effort over time can accomplish seemingly impossible tasks, no matter how small each individual action may be.
s: When someone keeps working toward a goal day after day without giving up, even though progress seems slow. When you're encouraging a friend not to lose faith in their long-term project because small, consistent steps will eventually lead to success.

l: water and fire are not compatible
m: Two things are fundamentally opposed to each other and cannot coexist peacefully.
s: When two people have completely opposite personalities and constantly argue with each other. When two competing businesses have irreconcilable differences and will never work together.

l: water and fire have no feeling
m: Natural disasters like floods and fires are indiscriminate and merciless, destroying everything in their path regardless of who or what is affected.
s: When describing how a wildfire spreads through a neighborhood destroying homes without distinction. When explaining why people need insurance against unpredictable natural disasters that spare no one.

p: shuǐ zhì qīng zé wú yú
l: When water becomes too clear, there are no fish
m: Excessive strictness or perfectionism can be counterproductive and may drive away people or opportunities, just as overly pure water cannot support fish life.
s: When a manager is so demanding and critical that employees quit or avoid the company. When someone has such high standards in relationships that they push away potential partners. When a boss insists on absolute perfection in every detail and creates such a tense environment that no one wants to work there.

m: The truth becomes clear and obvious once obscuring factors are removed or circumstances change.
s: When a mysterious situation is finally resolved and everyone understands what really happened. When someone's true character or intentions are eventually revealed after being hidden for a while. When an investigation concludes and all the facts come to light.

l: eternally hang down and not decay
m: To be remembered and honored forever; to achieve lasting fame or legacy that will never be forgotten.
s: When talking about a historical figure whose contributions changed the world and will never be forgotten. When celebrating someone who made such a great impact that their memory will live on for all generations to come.

m: To remember something forever and never allow it to be forgotten, often referring to honoring someone's memory or an important historical event.
s: When you want to commemorate a loved one who has passed away and keep their memory alive. When a nation honors the sacrifices made by soldiers or heroes from the past. When someone makes a solemn vow to always remember an important lesson or experience.

l: seek it but cannot obtain it
m: Something that is greatly desired but difficult or impossible to achieve.
s: When you've been wanting something for a long time but can't seem to get it, like finding the perfect job or meeting someone special. When someone desperately wishes for an opportunity that seems out of reach.

m: to demand absolute perfection and find fault with minor imperfections in others or their work.
s: When a manager criticizes an employee's excellent work because it has one small typo. When a parent is never satisfied with their child's straight-A report card because they didn't get into the top university they wanted.

m: Find common ground with others while respecting and tolerating your differences of opinion or perspective.
s: When a team with different viewpoints works together on a project by focusing on shared goals. When countries with opposing ideologies negotiate trade agreements by emphasizing mutual benefits. When family members with conflicting beliefs learn to coexist peacefully by accepting each other's views.

p: qiú dà tóng ， cún xiǎo yì
l: seek great commonality, preserve small differences
m: Focus on finding common ground and shared goals while tolerating minor disagreements and differences of opinion.
s: When a team needs to work together on a project despite having different ideas about some details. When family members want to stay united even though they don't agree on everything.

l: sweat flows and soaks the back
m: To be drenched in sweat due to hard work, intense fear, or extreme physical exertion.
s: When someone has been working in the hot sun all day and their shirt is completely wet with sweat. When a student is so nervous before an important exam that they are sweating profusely. When an athlete finishes an intense training session and is covered in sweat from head to toe.

l: sweat oxen and fill the halls
m: There is such an enormous amount of books or written material that it would be exhausting even for oxen to transport them and they would overflow from the buildings.
s: When describing a massive library collection that seems to have endless shelves of books. When someone has accumulated so much written work or research material over their lifetime that it's almost unmanageable in quantity.

m: Hard work and dedicated service that produces significant achievements or contributions.
s: When someone has worked tirelessly for years to build a successful company from the ground up. When a military general has fought in many difficult campaigns that led to important victories for the nation.

p: jiāng shān yì gǎi ， běn xìng nán yí
l: Rivers and mountains are easy to change, but one's nature is hard to change
m: It is far easier to change the physical landscape than it is to change a person's fundamental character or inherent nature.
s: When someone has tried many times to break a bad habit but keeps reverting to old behavior. When you realize that despite all your efforts to improve yourself, you keep falling back into the same patterns you've always had.

l: patching a leak in the middle of the river
m: Attempting to fix a serious problem only when it has already become critical or dangerous, rather than addressing it preventively.
s: When a company waits until their system completely fails before fixing security vulnerabilities. When someone ignores warning signs of a health issue and only seeks treatment when they're in the hospital. When a student doesn't study until the night before an important exam.

l: Rivers and streams decline day by day
m: Things are progressively getting worse or deteriorating with each passing day.
s: When a company's business keeps getting worse month after month. When someone's health condition continues to decline despite treatment. When a relationship keeps getting more strained and distant over time.

m: A bold, notorious criminal or bandit who operates on a large scale and is known for major crimes.
s: When describing a famous criminal who has committed many serious crimes across a wide area. When talking about someone known for their daring and large-scale illegal activities.

m: A corrupt, degrading, or morally reprehensible environment or situation that contaminates those who enter it.
s: When someone gets involved with a criminal organization or corrupt business dealings. When a person is trapped in a toxic workplace or abusive relationship that drags them down. When describing a society plagued by pervasive corruption and moral decay.

m: Describes something that is rising with great intensity, momentum, and power, often used for emotions, movements, or situations that are overwhelming and turbulent.
s: When a crowd's energy builds up during a concert or protest and becomes increasingly intense. When someone's anger or passion suddenly erupts and overwhelms them. When a wave of change or social movement sweeps through society with unstoppable force.

l: seep into the heart and spleen
m: Something deeply refreshing, pleasant, or comforting that touches one's innermost being.
s: When you smell a beautiful fragrance that instantly lifts your mood. When you taste something delicious that makes you feel completely satisfied and content. When you hear a piece of music that feels so soothing it calms your entire being.

l: fertile plains stretching a thousand miles
m: An extensive area of rich, productive land that is abundantly capable of supporting agriculture and prosperity.
s: When describing a region known for its agricultural wealth and natural resources. When praising the natural abundance and economic potential of a large area of countryside or farmland.

l: putrid vapor and noxious air become one
m: When corrupt or unscrupulous people band together in collusion to act immorally or illegally.
s: When two dishonest officials work together to cover up a scandal. When corrupt business partners scheme together to defraud customers and split the profits.

m: A serious wrong or injustice remains unresolved and the victim has no way to prove their innocence or get vindication.
s: When someone is falsely accused of a crime but has no evidence to clear their name. When a person has been wronged by others but nobody believes their side of the story and they cannot get justice. When historical wrongs are ignored and victims are never acknowledged or compensated.

m: Someone who speaks very little and prefers to remain quiet rather than engage in conversation.
s: When describing a coworker who rarely speaks up in meetings and keeps to themselves. When you notice someone is naturally introverted and doesn't talk much at social gatherings.

m: To search for something valuable or worthwhile among a large amount of worthless material through careful selection and effort.
s: When you're reading through many articles to find a few really useful ones. When a recruiter reviews hundreds of resumes to find the few qualified candidates. When you're shopping at a thrift store, digging through piles of clothes to find a few gems.

l: Never forget until teeth fall out
m: To remember something gratefully and never forget it for as long as one lives.
s: When someone has done you a tremendous favor that you will always be grateful for. When you want to express that you will remember someone's kindness or sacrifice forever, no matter how much time passes.

l: a single grain of millet in the vast sea
m: Something so insignificantly small in comparison to the vastness of the universe or world that it is almost negligible.
s: When you realize how tiny your problems are compared to the whole world. When someone feels humbled by the immensity of nature or the cosmos and realizes how small they really are.

l: the azure sea becomes mulberry fields
m: Everything in the world is subject to constant change and transformation over time.
s: When you revisit a place from your childhood and it's completely unrecognizable due to development. When you reflect on how drastically your life has changed over the years, or how a once-thriving business or community has been transformed by time and circumstance.

m: The world is in turmoil and chaos, with turbulent times causing upheaval and uncertainty everywhere.
s: When a country experiences major political or social upheaval that affects everyone's daily life. When global events like wars, economic crises, or pandemics create widespread chaos and instability. When someone reflects on living through a particularly tumultuous historical period.

l: rivers run clear and seas are calm
m: The world is at peace and in perfect order, with everything functioning harmoniously and without conflict.
s: When a country experiences a period of stability and prosperity with no wars or social unrest. When describing an ideal government that brings about widespread peace and good governance.

l: waiting for the river to run clear
m: waiting for an impossible or extremely unlikely event to happen; hoping for something that may never occur.
s: When someone keeps waiting for unrealistic conditions to improve before taking action. When a person postpones their plans indefinitely, waiting for circumstances that are unlikely to ever change. When someone says they'll start their business once the economy becomes perfect, which might never happen.

m: To be slick-talking and deceitful, using smooth words to manipulate or deceive others.
s: When a salesman uses clever words to trick you into buying something you don't need. When someone keeps making excuses with smooth talk to get out of trouble instead of being honest.

m: Someone who is slick, cunning, and good at manipulating others through smooth talk and deceptive behavior.
s: When you meet someone who is always flattering people and saying the right things to get what they want. When a salesman uses clever manipulation and charm to pressure you into buying something you don't need.

m: Speaking in a glib, insincere, and overly smooth manner designed to charm or deceive others.
s: When a salesman uses smooth, flattering words to try to sell you something you don't need. When someone talks their way out of trouble by being charming and slick rather than being honest about what they did.

l: treating silk threads only entangles them further
m: attempting to fix a complicated problem through clumsy intervention only makes it worse
s: When someone tries to help resolve a conflict between two friends but ends up making the situation more tense. When a manager tries to fix a workplace misunderstanding by getting involved but creates more confusion instead.

l: govern the country and bring peace to the people
m: To rule a state effectively by establishing good governance and ensuring the welfare and stability of its citizens.
s: When discussing a leader's primary responsibilities and what makes them successful. When evaluating whether a government is fulfilling its fundamental duties to its population. When praising a period of history when a nation was well-managed and people lived in harmony.

m: to help others by correcting their mistakes or faults with good intentions, similar to how a doctor treats illness to save lives.
s: When a manager gives critical feedback to an employee to help them improve their work performance. When a friend confronts you about a bad habit because they care about your wellbeing. When a teacher corrects a student's mistakes not to punish them, but to help them learn and succeed.

l: purchase a name and fish for praise
m: To seek fame and reputation through insincere or dishonest means rather than genuine accomplishment.
s: When someone does charitable work only to post about it on social media for attention. When a politician makes grand promises they have no intention of keeping just to win votes. When a colleague takes credit for others' work to look good in front of the boss.

l: touch and touch oneself with joy
m: To be excessively pleased with oneself and show arrogant satisfaction over minor achievements or qualities.
s: When someone wins a small competition and won't stop bragging about it for weeks. When a coworker makes one successful project and suddenly acts like they're the best employee in the company.

l: follow the wave and seek the source
m: To trace something back to its origin or root cause by following the visible path or evidence.
s: When you investigate a problem by looking at the symptoms and working backward to find what caused it. When a detective follows clues in a case to discover where the crime really started. When you trace a rumor back to see who actually started spreading it.

m: To beg for charity by going from door to door, or to live in poverty and depend on others' generosity for survival.
s: When someone has lost all their wealth and must rely on begging to survive. When describing someone who has fallen into extreme poverty and must ask for help from everyone they encounter.

m: A shallow, casual relationship with someone that lacks depth or genuine connection.
s: When you know someone but only see them occasionally and don't really know much about them. When two people are friendly at work but never talk outside of the office. When you have a large number of contacts but few of them are actually close friends.

m: Something has become so excessive or widespread that it causes serious harm or problems.
s: When fake news spreads so widely on social media that it causes real confusion and panic in society. When counterfeit products become so common in the market that they damage the reputation of legitimate brands and hurt consumers.

l: waves and billows majestic and expansive
m: Something is characterized by grand scale, magnificent momentum, and dramatic intensity.
s: When describing an epic historical event or period with significant upheaval and grandeur. When talking about a sweeping narrative, movie, or novel that has dramatic twists and impressive scope. When someone's life journey has been full of turbulent but remarkable experiences.

m: To cry so intensely that one cannot speak or articulate words due to overwhelming emotion.

When someone's plans fall apart catastrophically and they are left looking utterly pathetic and undignified.

l: wolf and hyena act as villains together
m: Two or more wicked or despicable people collude and work together for evil purposes.
s: When two corrupt officials team up to embezzle public funds. When a dishonest merchant and a fake inspector work together to defraud customers. When two bullies gang up on someone weaker to cause harm.

l: a cat weeping over a mouse
m: False or insincere sympathy shown by someone who is actually responsible for or benefits from the other person's misfortune.
s: When a boss pretends to sympathize with an employee they just fired while actually being glad to cut costs. When someone expresses sadness about a friend's breakup but was the one who encouraged the breakup in the first place.

m: To voluntarily provide advice, suggestions, or strategic ideas to help someone solve a problem or make a decision.
s: When someone eagerly steps forward to help a friend plan a business venture. When a colleague contributes creative solutions during a team meeting without being asked. When someone willingly shares their expertise to help resolve a difficult situation.

m: A person with a base, cunning, or contemptible appearance that reflects their dishonest or untrustworthy nature.
s: When you meet someone whose shifty facial features and nervous demeanor immediately make you suspicious of their intentions. When describing a criminal or swindler whose appearance matches their deceitful character.

m: Something that is extremely mysterious, profound, and difficult to understand or explain.
s: When someone tries to explain a complex philosophical concept but it just makes you more confused. When you read an abstract art description and have no idea what it actually means.

m: To follow established customs, traditions, or precedents without questioning or making changes.
s: When a company continues to use outdated procedures simply because that's how they've always done things. When someone refuses to try new methods and insists on sticking with traditional ways even when better options are available.

p: yù bù zuó ， bù chéng qì
l: Jade that is not carved cannot become a vessel
m: Without proper training, education, or refinement, a person cannot reach their full potential or become truly valuable.
s: When encouraging someone to study hard and develop their skills. When explaining why children need good education and discipline to succeed in life. When motivating a talented but lazy person to work on improving themselves.

m: Both the innocent and the guilty are destroyed together without distinction, resulting in mutual ruin for all involved.
s: When a company goes bankrupt and everyone loses their job, including both hardworking employees and lazy ones. When a family feud escalates so badly that all members suffer equally, regardless of who was actually at fault.

l: play with the world without reverence
m: To adopt a cynical, irreverent attitude toward life and society, treating serious matters with contempt and mockery.
s: When someone constantly makes jokes about everything and refuses to take anything seriously, even when it matters. When a person dismisses all social norms and moral values with a scornful attitude, acting like nothing deserves respect.

l: playing with fire and burning oneself
m: When you engage in dangerous or reckless behavior, you will ultimately harm yourself rather than others.
s: When someone keeps cheating people and eventually gets caught and punished. When a person spreads lies and rumors that eventually damage their own reputation instead of their target's.

m: Indulging in trivial pursuits and distractions causes one to lose sight of important goals and noble aspirations.
s: When someone spends all their time on video games and social media instead of studying or working toward their dreams. When a talented person wastes their potential by constantly engaging in frivolous activities rather than developing their skills.

l: appear in person to explain the method
m: To teach or convince others by demonstrating through one's own personal example and experience rather than just words.
s: When a reformed criminal visits schools to tell students about the dangers of crime based on his own mistakes. When someone who quit smoking shares their personal journey to inspire others to quit. When a successful entrepreneur shares their business failures and how they overcame them to teach aspiring business owners.

m: Someone's speech or writing is eloquent, polished, and beautiful in expression, flowing smoothly and flawlessly.
s: When listening to a skilled public speaker whose words seem perfectly chosen and flow beautifully. When reading someone's well-written article or poem that sounds lovely and polished to the ear.

l: pearls linked and jade discs combined
m: Two outstanding people or things come together in perfect harmony and complement each other beautifully.
s: When two talented musicians perform together and create amazing music that's better than either could make alone. When a company hires two experts whose skills perfectly match what the business needs, creating an ideal team.

l: brandish an axe before the gate of Lu Ban
m: to presumptuously display one's inferior skills or knowledge before an expert, thereby inviting ridicule or criticism.
s: When you try to give cooking advice to a professional chef. When someone attempts to teach a master musician about music theory despite having no training themselves.

m: Unable to argue further because one's logic is flawed and one has run out of convincing points to make.
s: When someone is losing a debate and can no longer defend their position with valid arguments. When a person realizes they are wrong and has nothing left to say in their defense.

l: reason is so it should be thus
m: Something is justified, expected, or should naturally follow based on logic or circumstances.
s: When a student who studies hard gets good grades, it seems like a matter of course. When a company that invests in research naturally produces better products. When someone who works hard deserves to be promoted.

l: reason is straight, energy is bold
m: When you have a just cause and solid justification, you can speak and act with complete confidence and strength.
s: When someone stands up for themselves after being treated unfairly and they speak with complete certainty because they know they're in the right. When a person defends their position in an argument confidently because the facts and logic are entirely on their side.

l: jade and glass fill the eye
m: A dazzling variety of beautiful or valuable things are displayed in abundance.
s: When you walk into a luxury shopping mall and see countless high-end stores with glittering displays. When you visit a museum with rooms full of precious artifacts and rare collections arranged beautifully.

m: A beautiful, magnificent, or ethereal place that seems otherworldly or impossibly perfect, often used to describe luxurious or dreamlike structures.
s: When describing a stunning, impossibly beautiful building or palace that takes your breath away. When someone describes a fancy hotel or resort as if it were a magical, heavenly place. When talking about architecture or design that seems too perfect and elegant to be real.

l: A flaw does not conceal the jade
m: Minor flaws or shortcomings cannot diminish the value or excellence of something or someone's overall merit and virtue.
s: When evaluating a job candidate who is highly qualified but made one small mistake in their presentation. When a great artist's work has a tiny imperfection but is still considered a masterpiece. When assessing a friend's character, you recognize they have one bad habit but their many good qualities far outweigh it.

m: Everyone or everything has both strengths and weaknesses; both good and bad qualities coexist.
s: When evaluating a person's overall character, you might acknowledge that they have admirable qualities but also some notable flaws. When reviewing a book or movie that has both brilliant scenes and disappointing parts. When assessing an employee who does excellent work in some areas but struggles in others.

l: Auspicious snow foretells a bountiful year
m: Timely snowfall in winter is a good sign that the coming harvest will be abundant and prosperous.
s: When winter snow arrives at just the right time and farmers are optimistic about the next year's crops. When people see favorable weather conditions and believe it will lead to good fortune and plenty in the future. When natural signs seem to indicate that good times and abundance are coming.

m: Natural talent or potential that has not yet been refined or developed through education and experience.
s: When describing a young person who shows great promise but still needs training and guidance to reach their potential. When someone has raw ability but lacks the polish and skill that comes from practice and learning.

l: When the melon is ripe, the stem falls off
m: When conditions are right and development is complete, things naturally reach their conclusion or resolution without forcing.
s: When a student has studied hard all semester and finally passes the exam naturally. When a business project has been carefully developed and is ready to launch on its own. When two people have built a strong relationship over time and naturally decide to get married.

m: A situation where one's actions or presence, though innocent, may easily be misunderstood or suspected by others due to compromising circumstances.
s: When a manager is alone with a subordinate behind closed doors and people start spreading rumors about favoritism. m: mediocre or talentless people making loud noise and attracting attention, often drowning out truly talented individuals.
s: When a talentless musician gets famous while skilled artists go unnoticed. When someone with no real expertise becomes a celebrity and dominates public discourse, overshadowing genuinely knowledgeable people.

m: Someone who is trapped in a confined space with no way to escape, or a situation where victory is certain because the target has no means of escape.
s: When a criminal is cornered by police with no exit routes. When someone is caught in a situation where they cannot possibly win or get away no matter what they do.

l: catching a soft-shelled turtle in a jar
m: A task that is extremely easy to accomplish because the target is trapped with no possibility of escape.
s: When you have a clear advantage in a competition and victory is guaranteed. When someone is cornered and has no way out of a difficult situation. When a task is so simple that success is absolutely certain.

l: sweet as if it were maltose candy
m: To willingly endure hardship or difficulty because one finds it meaningful, worthwhile, or even enjoyable.
s: When someone works extremely hard on a challenging project and doesn't mind the stress because they love what they do. When a parent sacrifices comfort and rest for their children's wellbeing and considers it a joy rather than a burden.

l: willingly bow to the lower wind
m: To willingly concede that someone else is superior and acknowledge their greater ability or achievement.

m: Rumors, accusations, or public outcry are spreading widely and intensely, reaching a peak of intensity.

m: Insincere flattery or deceptive compliments used to manipulate or deceive someone.
s: When a salesman showers you with praise and compliments just to get you to buy something expensive. When someone suddenly becomes very nice and says all the right things because they want a favor from you.

p: shēng yú yōu huàn ， sǐ yú ān lè
l: Born from worry and hardship, die from comfort and leisure

s: When a successful company becomes complacent after years of growth and eventually fails because they stopped innovating. When a person raised in poverty works hard and achieves success, but their children raised in comfort become lazy and directionless.

m: To mechanically imitate or copy something without understanding its true meaning or essence.
s: When a student memorizes an essay word-for-word without comprehending what it means. When someone copies a technique or style from another person but lacks the skill or understanding to do it properly. When someone adopts foreign ideas or methods without adapting them to their own context or understanding them deeply.

m: To use forced, strained, or far-fetched reasoning to make a weak connection between unrelated things.
s: When someone tries to blame their bad exam performance on the weather that happened weeks ago. When a speaker keeps making ridiculous connections between random topics to support their argument.

m: To mechanically apply rules or methods without considering specific circumstances or adapting to the actual situation.
s: When a manager tries to use the exact same business strategy from one company at a completely different company without adjusting for their unique needs. When a teacher applies the same teaching method to all students despite their different learning styles and abilities.

m: The absolute power to decide whether someone lives or dies, or more broadly, complete control over someone's fate.
s: When a dictator has total authority over their citizens and can imprison or execute anyone at will. When a manager has complete power to hire, fire, or promote employees without oversight. When someone in a powerful position can make decisions that entirely determine another person's future.

l: life and death existence and destruction
m: A critical moment where survival or extinction hangs in the balance, representing the most crucial and dangerous situation possible.
s: When a company is facing bankruptcy and needs to make one final decision to survive. When a patient is in critical condition and the next few hours will determine whether they live or die. When a country is under invasion and fighting for its very existence.

l: life and death are closely related
m: A matter of critical importance where the outcome determines survival or complete failure.
s: When a company faces a decision that will either save it from bankruptcy or cause it to collapse. When a patient needs an urgent surgery because their survival depends on it. When a student's final exam score will determine whether they pass or fail the course.

m: Full of vitality, energy, and liveliness; displaying strong life force and vigor.
s: When you see a young child running around excitedly and full of energy. When describing a thriving business that is growing rapidly and doing very well. When someone recovers from illness and returns to their normal active, energetic self.

m: Widespread suffering and death of the common people caused by war, disaster, or tyranny.
s: When a country experiences devastating war that destroys countless lives. When a natural disaster or famine causes mass casualties among the population. When a tyrant's rule leads to the suffering and death of millions of ordinary people.

m: The profound sorrow of being separated from loved ones, whether through life circumstances or death itself.
s: When family members move far away and you don't know when you'll see them again. When elderly grandparents pass away and you realize you'll never have another conversation with them. When close friends drift apart due to life changes and lose touch forever.

p: shēng mǐ zhǔ chéng shú fàn
l: raw rice cooked into cooked rice
m: What is done is done and cannot be undone; a fait accompli that cannot be reversed.
s: When someone has already made an irreversible decision and there's no point in arguing about it anymore. When a couple gets married and people realize they can't change the outcome no matter what they say. When a business deal is finalized and signed, so complaining about the terms now won't help.

m: Exceptional literary or artistic talent that produces vivid, graceful, and imaginative work.
s: When describing a writer who creates beautiful, lively prose that captivates readers. When praising an artist or author whose work is particularly creative and eloquent.

m: Full of vitality, energy, and vigor; describing someone or something that is vibrant and full of life.
s: When a child is running around the playground with endless energy and enthusiasm. When an elderly person stays active and healthy despite their age, surprising everyone with their vigor.

m: To command military forces with such skill and strategic brilliance that it seems almost supernatural or divinely inspired.
s: When a military general executes a flawless battle strategy that catches the enemy completely off guard. When a sports coach makes brilliant tactical decisions that lead to an improbable comeback victory. When a leader demonstrates such exceptional decision-making ability that their success seems almost magical.

m: A society has fallen into such moral decay and desperation that men resort to theft and women to prostitution.
s: When describing a community that has deteriorated due to poverty and lack of opportunity, where people have abandoned their morals out of desperation. When discussing the breakdown of social order and values during times of extreme hardship or corruption.

l: draw a boundary and make it a prison
m: to voluntarily limit oneself within narrow confines, creating self-imposed restrictions that prevent growth or freedom.
s: When someone is afraid to try new things and stays within their comfort zone. When a person has the ability to succeed but holds themselves back with unnecessary self-doubt and limitations.

c: 画虎画皮难画骨，知人知面不知心
p: huà hǔ huà pí nán huà gǔ ， zhī rén zhī miàn bù zhī xīn

m: It is easy to understand someone's outward appearance or surface qualities, but difficult or impossible to truly know their inner thoughts, character, and intentions.
s: When you meet someone who seems friendly and trustworthy on the surface, but later you discover they had hidden motives the whole time. When you've known a colleague for years but realize you never really understood what they were truly thinking or feeling beneath their professional demeanor.

l: painting a tiger but resembling a dog
m: to attempt something ambitious but end up with a result that is far inferior or ridiculous, failing to achieve one's intended goal.

l: draw a snake and add feet
m: To ruin something good by making unnecessary additions or improvements.
s: When someone adds extra details to a simple solution and makes it worse. When a designer keeps adding unnecessary features to a product that was already perfect. When someone tries to improve on something that didn't need improving.

l: paint a cake to satisfy hunger
m: to console oneself with false hopes or empty promises that provide no real benefit or sustenance.
s: When a company keeps promising bonuses that never materialize, employees are just painting cakes to satisfy their hunger for better pay. When someone talks endlessly about their future plans to get rich but takes no real action, they're just feeding themselves with painted cakes. When a politician makes grand promises during campaigns but never delivers on them, voters realize they were given nothing but painted cakes.

m: To add a crucial final touch or detail that brings something to life or completes it perfectly.
s: When a presentation is good but needs one key insight to make it great. When an artist adds a final detail that suddenly makes their painting come alive. When someone makes a comment that suddenly clarifies an entire discussion or problem.

l: speak freely what one wishes to say
m: To express one's thoughts and opinions openly and without restraint or fear of consequences.
s: When a boss creates a safe environment where employees feel comfortable sharing ideas without worry. When a close friend tells you exactly what they think about your situation, holding nothing back.

l: fear and shrink back without advancing
m: To hesitate and retreat out of fear, lacking the courage to move forward or face challenges.
s: When someone is too scared to take a necessary step forward, like being afraid to speak up in an important meeting. When a person lets fear prevent them from pursuing an opportunity or confronting a difficult situation.

l: fear the head fear the tail
m: To be overly cautious and hesitant about taking action, worrying excessively about potential problems at every step.
s: When someone is afraid to start a project because they keep worrying about what could go wrong. When a person hesitates to make a decision because they're anxious about both the beginning and the end result of their choice.

c: 留得青山在，不怕没柴烧

m: As long as you preserve the foundation or core resources, you will always have the means to recover and survive future difficulties.
s: When someone loses money but still has their health and skills, so they can earn it back later. When a business faces temporary setbacks but still has its core team and reputation intact, so it can rebuild. When someone decides to retreat strategically from a bad situation to protect what matters most.

m: To intentionally hold back or not go to extremes, keeping some room for flexibility, retreat, or future adjustment.

m: To have a slight edge or marginal advantage over someone or something else.

m: To catch a glimpse of only a small part or aspect of something much larger, giving a limited understanding of the whole.

l: distance does not separate the close

m: A confusing situation or mystery remains unexplained and unclear, leaving people puzzled and uncertain.

l: suspicion gives birth to hidden ghosts

s: When someone is constantly worried that their partner is cheating despite no evidence, and they keep interpreting innocent actions as proof of infidelity. m: To be excessively suspicious and distrustful of everything and everyone around you, imagining problems that don't actually exist.

l: sores and scars fill the eye

m: to strongly despise wrongdoing and evil with intense moral disapproval, as if it were a personal enemy.

m: To speak harshly and sternly with an intimidating or angry demeanor.

m: Only through severe hardship or testing can one's true character and strength be revealed.

m: To be extremely distressed, anxious, or angry, showing one's displeasure through facial expressions and bodily gestures.
s: When someone is deeply troubled by bad news and can't hide their worry on their face. When a person is so frustrated with a situation that they furrow their brow and show obvious signs of distress.

m: Sickness and disease often result from what we eat or drink, emphasizing the importance of being careful about food hygiene and diet.
s: When someone gets food poisoning from eating contaminated food. When a parent warns a child not to eat unwashed fruits or street food. When someone falls ill after eating at a questionable restaurant.

l: sickness has entered the vital organs
m: A disease or problem has become so severe that it is beyond cure or remedy.

l: When ill in desperation, randomly seek medical treatment
m: When facing a critical problem or crisis, people act desperately and irrationally, accepting any solution without careful consideration or verification.

m: To cry bitterly and uncontrollably with an overwhelming outpouring of tears.

l: After the pain subsides, reflect on the pain
m: After suffering a setback or loss, one calmly reflects on what went wrong in order to prevent similar mistakes in the future.
s: When a business fails and the owner takes time to analyze what mistakes led to the collapse. When someone goes through a difficult breakup and later thinks carefully about what they could have done differently in the relationship.

m: To feel intense pain, anger, and anguish about something that has caused deep distress or injustice.

l: pain the heart and disease the head

s: When a parent sees their child make a terrible life choice and feels both heartbroken and deeply concerned. When a coach watches their team repeatedly lose because of preventable mistakes, feeling both disappointed and pained.

m: To genuinely repent and completely reform oneself from past mistakes and wrongdoings.

When someone transitions from being a beginner in their field to becoming an accomplished expert.

m: To reach the highest possible level of excellence or perfection in something.

m: Something or someone is perfect and flawless, without any defects or faults.

m: A person who is scholarly and intellectual but lacks practical experience, physical strength, or worldly wisdom.

l: a white horse passes through a crevice

m: To comply with everything someone asks and obey their every command without question.

m: Something is severely damaged, deteriorated, or in extremely poor condition with countless defects and problems.

When a company that's already market leader continues investing in innovation rather than maintaining the status quo.

m: In attempting to correct a fault or problem, one goes to the opposite extreme and overcorrects, creating a new problem.
