When someone tries so hard to be frugal after overspending that they refuse to buy even necessary items. When a company overcorrects after a scandal by implementing rules so harsh that it damages employee morale.

m: A direct, intense, and close-range confrontation or conflict between opposing forces.
s: When two competitors face off directly in a final showdown. When a company must directly compete with a rival in the same market. When two arguments come down to a heated face-to-face debate.

m: Something that is brief in length but powerful and effective in impact or quality.
s: When a short speech or article delivers a strong message without wasting words. When a small team accomplishes great things through skill and determination. When someone gives a concise explanation that perfectly captures the essential point.

l: a stone sinks into the vast sea
m: Something disappears without a trace or produces no response, as if it vanished completely.
s: When you send an important message or email and never hear back, it's like your words sank into the vast sea. When you make a suggestion at work but nobody acknowledges it or acts on it, your idea has disappeared like a stone into the vast sea.

m: An event or statement is so shocking, dramatic, or earth-shattering that it astonishes everyone and changes the situation fundamentally.
s: When a major scandal suddenly becomes public and shocks the entire nation. When someone makes an unexpected announcement that completely transforms how people think about a situation. When a breakthrough discovery or invention surprises the world and changes everything.

l: break open mouth and curse greatly
m: To suddenly burst into a torrent of angry, abusive cursing and insults.
s: When someone loses their temper and starts yelling obscenities and insults at another person without holding back. When a person is so furious they can no longer contain their anger and begin cursing loudly and harshly.

l: break the old and establish the new
m: To discard outdated systems, ideas, or practices and replace them with modern, progressive ones.
s: When a company abandons its legacy technology platform to adopt cloud-based systems. When a government reforms old regulations that no longer serve society's needs. When someone leaves behind traditional ways of thinking to embrace contemporary methods.

m: to suddenly shift from sadness or crying to happiness and laughter.
s: When a child stops crying and suddenly starts laughing after being comforted. When someone receives good news that immediately lifts their sad mood. When a sad moment is interrupted by something funny that makes everyone laugh instead.

m: Something is so poorly made or executed that it has numerous obvious defects and mistakes.
s: When someone tells a lie but makes so many contradictions that it's immediately obvious they're not being truthful. When a student submits homework that's clearly rushed and has errors throughout, making it obvious they didn't put in effort.

l: break the cauldrons and sink the boats
m: to commit fully to a course of action by eliminating the possibility of retreat or failure.
s: When someone quits their job to start a risky business with no backup plan. When a student decides to pursue an extremely competitive goal and turns down all safer alternatives.

m: A separated couple reunites and restores their relationship, or any estranged parties reconcile after a period of separation.
s: When a couple breaks up but later gets back together and decides to give their relationship another try. When two friends who had a big fight finally make peace and become close again after months of not talking.

m: To reject superstitious beliefs and embrace rational, scientific thinking instead of relying on supernatural explanations.
s: When a family stops believing in fortune telling and feng shui, instead making decisions based on logic and evidence. When a community abandons traditional superstitious practices in favor of modern medicine and education.

m: Something is extraordinarily large and unmatched in its magnitude or scale.
s: When describing something impressively huge that stands out from everything else, like a massive building that dwarfs all others around it. When someone is astounded by the sheer size of an object or structure that has no equal in their experience.

m: A rare and precious survivor or achievement that stands alone after others have disappeared or failed.
s: When a historic building is the last one of its kind still standing in a city. When someone is the last member of their family or generation still alive. When a company is one of the few remaining competitors in an industry that once had many players.

m: Something that is absolutely proven, undeniable, and impossible to change or dispute.
s: When you have solid evidence that proves someone guilty beyond any doubt. When a scientific fact has been established so thoroughly that no one can argue against it anymore.

m: Living an unremarkable, ordinary life without making any meaningful achievements or contributions.
s: When someone goes through life without pursuing any goals or dreams. When a person has talent but chooses to live a mundane, purposeless existence without striving for anything better.

l: obstruct the hands and obstruct the feet
m: To be in the way and hinder someone's work or progress.
s: When a colleague keeps interrupting you while you're trying to focus on an important task. When someone is standing in your way while you're trying to clean or move furniture around the house. When a younger sibling keeps following you around and getting in the way of what you're trying to do.

l: grinding a pestle into a needle
m: persistent effort and patience can accomplish seemingly impossible tasks, or turn something rough and unsuitable into something fine and useful.
s: When someone achieves success through years of dedicated practice and hard work. When a student gradually improves their grades through consistent studying, even though progress seemed impossible at first. When someone transforms their life situation through relentless determination and patience.

m: It is a courtesy and social norm to reciprocate when someone shows you kindness or gives you a gift.
s: When your friend gives you a birthday present, you feel obligated to give them one too. When someone invites you to dinner, you naturally want to invite them back another time to maintain the friendship.

p: shén bù zhī ， guǐ bù jué
l: The gods do not know, the ghosts do not perceive
m: To do something in complete secrecy without anyone noticing or discovering it.
s: When someone sneaks out of the house without telling their parents. When a student copies homework without the teacher finding out. When someone makes a small change to something and hopes nobody will notice.

m: Something is so extraordinary, mysterious, or skillfully done that it seems to transcend normal human understanding and ability.
s: When a magician performs an illusion so convincingly that you can't figure out how it's possible. When someone's cooking skills are so exceptional that their dishes taste almost supernatural. When a hacker's abilities seem almost magical in how they can solve impossible technical problems.

m: To appear and disappear mysteriously and unpredictably, moving with such speed or stealth that one seems almost supernatural.
s: When a talented player in sports seems to vanish from one part of the field and suddenly appears elsewhere to make a crucial play. When a skilled thief manages to break in and out of a place without anyone knowing how they did it. When someone is always hard to pin down or locate because they move around so unpredictably.

m: Something is so mysterious, profound, or marvelous that it cannot be understood or predicted, defying ordinary comprehension.
s: When you watch a magician perform an impossible trick and can't figure out how they did it. When someone explains a complex scientific concept so elegantly that it seems almost magical and you can't fully grasp the depths of how it works.

m: Craftsmanship so skillful and intricate that it seems to transcend human ability and appear as if created by supernatural forces.
s: When you see an incredibly detailed sculpture or painting and you can't believe a human actually made it. When someone builds or creates something so perfectly that it seems almost impossibly well-crafted, like it must have been made by higher powers rather than human hands.

m: One's mind is wandering, distracted, or in a dazed state where one cannot focus or think clearly.
s: When someone is so worried about bad news that they can't concentrate on their work and keep zoning out. When you're so tired after a long night that you're going through the day in a fog, barely aware of what's happening around you.

m: Possessing brilliant foresight and strategic wisdom that seems almost supernatural in its accuracy and cleverness.
s: When someone predicts exactly what will happen in a situation before it occurs. When a general or strategist makes a military decision that turns out to be perfectly calculated and succeeds beyond expectations. When a person demonstrates such keen insight and planning that their success seems almost magical or impossible to have anticipated.

m: To display an extremely arrogant, conceited, or self-important demeanor with excessive pride and confidence.
s: When someone acts extremely full of themselves after winning a competition or getting promoted. When a person struts around acting superior to everyone else because of their wealth or status.

m: To remain calm and composed, showing no change in facial expression or emotion despite difficult or surprising circumstances.
s: When someone receives bad news but doesn't show any reaction on their face. When a student gets called on in class unexpectedly but answers confidently without looking nervous or embarrassed.

m: Someone has extraordinary abilities, influence, or resourcefulness that allows them to accomplish seemingly impossible things.
s: When someone seems to be able to solve any problem or get anything done no matter how difficult. When a well-connected person can pull strings to make things happen that others thought were impossible.

m: Looking energetic, vibrant, and full of life with a bright and lively demeanor.
s: When someone walks into a room looking refreshed and confident after a good night's sleep. When an elderly person is active and full of energy, surprising everyone with their vitality. When a student aces their exam and comes to class beaming with pride and enthusiasm.

l: spirit and soul turned upside down
m: To be so captivated, enchanted, or infatuated that one loses composure and rational thinking.
s: When someone is so deeply in love that they can't think straight or stop talking about their crush. When a person becomes completely mesmerized by a beautiful performance or artwork and seems lost in a trance. When someone is so obsessed with a new hobby or interest that they neglect everything else around them.

m: When one bad thing happens, it is often followed by other misfortunes in quick succession.
s: When someone loses their job and then their car breaks down the next week. When a person gets sick and then their pet gets injured at the same time. When bad news keeps arriving one after another during a difficult period.

l: bring calamity to the state and disaster to the people
m: To cause ruin to the nation and suffering to its citizens through destructive actions or policies.
s: When a corrupt leader's decisions lead to economic collapse and widespread poverty. When a government official's incompetence or greed results in famine, war, or national decline that harms millions of ordinary people.

m: Good fortune rarely comes in multiples; when one blessing occurs, do not expect another to follow immediately.
s: When someone wins the lottery and then expects to win again soon. When a person gets promoted at work and immediately expects a bonus as well, forgetting that good things don't usually stack up like that.

l: leave home and abandon the well
m: to leave one's hometown and live far away from one's native place and family.
s: When someone moves to a distant city for work and hasn't been home in years. When a person immigrates to another country and is separated from their family and birthplace.

m: People's hearts have grown distant and their loyalty has wavered, causing unity and trust to break down.
s: When team members stop cooperating and start working against each other's interests. When a group that was once close-knit begins to split apart as people lose faith in the shared mission or leader.

l: depart from the classics and rebel against the way
m: To reject orthodox teachings or established conventions and pursue unorthodox or rebellious ideas.
s: When someone completely abandons traditional beliefs to follow an unconventional philosophy. When an artist rejects all established artistic rules to create something radically different. When a student refuses to follow conventional wisdom and takes a completely different approach to solving a problem.

l: leave the group and seek solitary dwelling
m: to withdraw from society and live in isolation or solitude.
s: When someone deliberately avoids social interactions and prefers to live alone away from others. When a person becomes a hermit or recluse, rejecting community and social life. When someone isolates themselves from friends and family to live a solitary existence.

l: wander ten thousand miles from the topic
m: To deviate so far from the original subject that one's discussion or argument has almost nothing to do with the point being made.
s: When someone starts talking about their vacation in the middle of a serious work meeting discussion. When a student's essay answer goes completely off-topic and discusses something entirely unrelated to the question asked.

m: Something that appears impressive or attractive on the surface but lacks real substance, value, or genuine content.
s: When a product has fancy packaging but poor quality inside. When someone gives an elaborate presentation that sounds good but has no real data or evidence to back it up. When a company makes grand promises but fails to deliver actual results.

m: Selfish desires and distracting thoughts that cloud one's judgment or prevent one from acting with pure intentions.
s: When someone makes a decision based on what benefits them personally rather than what is best for the group. When a person is supposed to be impartial but their own interests keep getting in the way of fair judgment.

m: Secret or unauthorized exchange of goods, money, or favors between two parties, typically implying impropriety or violation of rules.
s: When officials are caught exchanging bribes under the table. When two people make a secret deal that bypasses proper channels or regulations. When employees privately trade favors without their employer's knowledge or approval.

l: not harming even an autumn hair
m: to maintain perfect discipline and conduct without committing even the slightest offense or transgression
s: When describing an army that marches through a region without looting or harming civilians. When praising someone's impeccable moral character and integrity despite having the opportunity to do wrong.

m: A period of unusually hot and humid weather that occurs in early autumn after a brief cool spell, resembling a tiger's fierce attack.
s: When you experience an unexpected heat wave in September after a few cool days in late August. When the weather suddenly becomes unbearably hot and sticky again just when you thought summer was finally over.

m: An irresistible force easily destroys something weak and fragile, or a powerful entity effortlessly eliminates insignificant opposition.
s: When a strong army quickly defeats a much weaker opponent. When a large corporation easily crushes a small startup competitor. When someone with authority quickly dismisses objections from people with no power.

l: the autumn wind passes the ear
m: To ignore or disregard something completely, as if it went in one ear and out the other without making any impression.
s: When someone gives you advice but you completely ignore it and don't take it seriously. When a teacher explains something important in class but a student doesn't pay attention at all and forgets it immediately.

p: zhòng guā dé guā ， zhòng dòu dé dòu
l: Plant melons and harvest melons, plant beans and harvest beans
m: You will inevitably get the results that correspond to your actions or efforts, whether good or bad.
s: When someone works hard on a project and it turns out great, showing that their effort paid off. When a student who never studies fails an exam and realizes they brought it upon themselves. When a person is reaping the consequences of their past decisions, whether positive or negative.

m: To keep something completely secret and refuse to disclose it to others.
s: When a company doesn't reveal details about an upcoming product launch. When someone refuses to share the details of a surprise party they're planning. When a person keeps their salary or financial situation private and won't tell anyone about it.

m: A long-standing mutual dislike or incompatibility between two people that has built up over time.
s: When two coworkers have never gotten along and their tension keeps growing. When family members have had disagreements for years and can't seem to reconcile. When former friends have developed such deep resentment that they refuse to be in the same room.

m: Working excessively hard over a long period of time eventually damages your health and causes you to become ill.
s: When someone works so hard for so long without rest that they finally get sick. When a dedicated employee pushes themselves to the breaking point and their body gives out.

m: Small amounts or efforts accumulated over time will eventually grow into something substantial and significant.
s: When someone saves a small amount of money regularly and builds up substantial savings over years. When a student studies a little bit every day and eventually becomes very knowledgeable. When a company reinvests small profits consistently and grows into a large business.

m: A long period of time passing gradually through the accumulation of days, months, and years.
s: When someone has been doing the same job for many years and has built up a lot of experience. When a relationship has grown stronger over many years of being together. When dust or dirt builds up in a place that hasn't been cleaned for a very long time.

m: Repeated small criticisms and attacks can eventually destroy even the strongest person, just as accumulated corrosion can wear away solid material.
s: When someone constantly receives negative comments or gossip about them until their reputation or spirit is completely broken. When a person endures relentless minor setbacks or insults that gradually wear down their confidence and well-being over time.

m: small, seemingly insignificant problems or mistakes can accumulate over time and eventually lead to serious consequences or failure.
s: When a company ignores minor customer complaints and they keep adding up until customers leave in droves. When someone procrastinates on small tasks until the workload becomes overwhelming and unmanageable. When a relationship deteriorates not because of one big argument, but because of countless small resentments building up over time.

m: One should save and prepare resources during times of plenty to guard against future hardship and scarcity.
s: When someone sets aside money from their salary each month for emergencies and unexpected expenses. When a family stocks up on supplies before a natural disaster season hits their region.

l: accumulated weight is difficult to return
m: A deeply rooted problem or bad habit that has developed over a long time is very hard to correct or reverse.
s: When a company has had poor management practices for years and needs major organizational reform. When someone has been living unhealthily for decades and struggles to change their lifestyle despite health warnings.

l: accumulate grain by grain and inch by inch
m: Small amounts accumulated over time eventually become significant through persistent effort and patience.
s: When someone saves a little money each month and eventually has enough for a down payment on a house. When a student studies consistently day after day and gradually improves their grades significantly. When a writer collects small ideas and observations that eventually become a complete book.

l: call each other brother and address as younger brother
m: To become sworn brothers or to treat each other as close friends with deep bonds of brotherhood and loyalty.
s: When two men become extremely close friends and pledge lifelong loyalty to each other. When friends from different backgrounds form a deep bond and treat each other like family members. When people in a group become so tight-knit that they act like brothers despite not being related by blood.

l: call oneself solitary and speak of being widowed
m: To act with arrogant self-importance and lonely pride, as if one is a superior ruler standing alone above others.
s: When a leader isolates themselves and acts superior to everyone around them, refusing to listen to others' input. When someone adopts an air of grandiose self-importance, treating themselves as uniquely special or above the rest of the group.

m: Everything turns out exactly as you hoped, bringing complete satisfaction and contentment.
s: When you finally find the perfect apartment after months of searching. When a gift someone gives you is exactly what you wanted and needed. When a vacation goes perfectly according to plan with no unexpected problems.

l: proclaim oneself king and proclaim oneself hegemon
m: To seize power and establish absolute dominance over a territory or domain.
s: When a local gang leader takes over a neighborhood and controls everything that happens there. When a company aggressively buys out competitors and becomes the monopoly in their industry. When someone tries to dominate a group or organization and make all the decisions themselves.

m: To possess enormous power or determination capable of accomplishing seemingly impossible feats through sheer force or will.
s: When describing someone who has achieved something that seemed completely impossible through sheer determination and effort. When talking about a leader or organization that has transformed an entire industry or society through their immense power and influence.

m: To cunningly substitute or replace something with something else, often by deception or sleight of hand.
s: When someone swaps out a genuine product with a fake one and tries to pass it off as real. When a person takes credit for someone else's work or ideas by presenting them as their own. When a scammer replaces valuable items with worthless counterfeits in a deceptive exchange.

m: To transform the prevailing customs and social practices of a society or community.
s: When a government implements new policies to reduce wasteful spending on weddings and funerals. When a school successfully changes student behavior from cheating to honest studying through education and role modeling.

m: Something is very unusual, bizarre, or eccentric in a way that is hard to understand or explain.
s: When you see someone wearing really odd clothing combinations that don't match at all. When a friend has a collection of very unusual hobbies or interests that seem weird to everyone else. When you encounter a product design that looks completely unconventional or outlandish.

m: Things are thinly distributed, appearing in small quantities spread far apart with noticeable gaps between them.
s: When you look at a sparsely populated neighborhood with houses far apart from each other. When attendance at an event is poor and there are many empty seats. When rain falls lightly with long gaps between drops.

l: slightly settle do not be impatient
m: Stay calm and patient; do not become anxious or agitated when facing difficulties or waiting for results.
s: When someone is worried about test results and keeps checking their phone every minute, you might tell them to relax and wait. When a friend is panicking about a job interview outcome before hearing back from the company, you could advise them to be patient and composed.

l: Slight neglect and it immediately vanishes
m: Opportunities pass by extremely quickly and are easily lost if you are not vigilant or do not act promptly.
s: When a good job opportunity comes up but you hesitate and someone else takes it. When you see a sale item you want but wait too long and it sells out before you can buy it.

l: minor official histories and rustic tales
m: Unofficial or unverified accounts, rumors, and folk stories that circulate among common people rather than authoritative historical records.
s: When someone is sharing gossip or hearsay they heard from friends instead of facts from reliable sources. When you're reading entertaining but unverified stories about celebrities or historical figures on social media rather than in official biographies. When someone dismisses what you're saying as just common rumors and not serious documented history.

m: A very large gathering of many people in a crowded public place.
s: When you're trying to have a private conversation but there are too many people around listening. When something embarrassing happens to you in front of a huge crowd at a public event.

m: To proceed methodically and carefully with a solid foundation, taking reliable steps without rushing toward success.
s: When a student studies consistently every day rather than cramming before exams. When a business grows gradually through careful planning instead of taking risky shortcuts. When someone learns a skill step by step, mastering the basics before moving to advanced techniques.

m: To have victory or success securely in one's grasp with certainty, leaving no doubt about the outcome.
s: When a sports team is playing so well that winning the championship seems guaranteed. When a student has studied thoroughly and feels completely confident about passing an important exam. When a company has such a strong competitive advantage that they are certain to dominate the market.

l: dwell in caves and live in the wilderness
m: to live a primitive, isolated life far removed from civilization and society.
s: When describing how ancient people survived before cities were built. When someone chooses to live completely off-grid, away from modern society in remote areas. When talking about hermits or monks who retreat to isolated natural settings to live in solitude.

m: A remote, underdeveloped, and isolated rural area far from civilization and modern amenities.
s: When describing a village that is far away from the city with limited infrastructure and few opportunities. When someone moves to a place that feels cut off from the rest of the world with very few modern conveniences.

l: exhaust troops and waste military resources
m: A government or leader continuously wages unnecessary wars, squandering the nation's military strength and resources in endless conflict.
s: When a country keeps starting wars it can't afford and drains its treasury on military campaigns. When a leader is obsessed with conquest and keeps sending soldiers to fight in pointless battles, weakening the nation overall.

l: poor and fierce to the extreme
m: Describing someone who is extremely violent, vicious, and has committed the most heinous crimes without any moral restraint.
s: When describing a serial killer or mass murderer who has committed brutal acts. When talking about a criminal gang that has committed numerous violent offenses and shows no mercy or humanity. When referring to a dictator or warlord known for extreme cruelty and atrocities.

m: When facing difficult circumstances or lack of resources, one is forced to think creatively and adapt by trying new approaches.
s: When a struggling business owner decides to completely overhaul their strategy because their current methods aren't working. When someone in financial hardship learns new skills or takes a different career path out of necessity rather than choice.

l: poor in resources yet extravagant in desires
m: pursuing excessive luxury and indulgence despite lacking the means to afford it, leading to financial ruin.
s: When someone spends money they don't have on expensive luxuries and goes into debt. When a person lives a lavish lifestyle way beyond their actual income or wealth.

m: A desolate and inhospitable place with barren mountains and treacherous waters that is difficult to survive in.
s: When describing a remote, underdeveloped region with harsh natural conditions. When someone talks about moving to or visiting a place known for its extreme poverty and dangerous terrain.

m: To work hard and persistently over a long period of time, often with hardship or exhaustion.
s: When someone has been studying or working on a project for years without rest. When describing how an artist spent many years perfecting their craft through continuous effort.

m: To be in a state of extreme boredom and tedium with nothing meaningful to do or think about.
s: When you're stuck at home with nothing to do and feel like time is moving impossibly slowly. When someone has exhausted all entertainment options and is desperately bored out of their mind. When you're waiting for something important but have hours of empty time with no way to occupy yourself.

m: In a desperate situation with no way out and no hope of escape.
s: When a company is bankrupt and facing closure with no way to save itself. When someone is trapped in a bad situation and has exhausted all possible options to escape it.

l: a tower pavilion in the air
m: Something that is imaginary, unrealistic, or impossible to achieve because it lacks a solid foundation.
s: When someone makes grand plans without any practical steps to achieve them. When a business idea sounds good in theory but has no realistic way to succeed. When a friend keeps talking about their dreams but never does anything concrete to make them happen.

m: Something has never happened or existed before in history; completely unprecedented.
s: When a company achieves sales figures that have never been reached before in their entire history. When a natural disaster occurs that is more severe than anything recorded in the past century. When an athlete breaks a world record that stood for decades.

l: unprecedented and never to be matched again
m: Something so extraordinary and exceptional that nothing like it has ever existed before and nothing like it will ever exist again.
s: When describing a once-in-a-lifetime achievement that no one else will ever be able to replicate. When someone accomplishes something so remarkable and unique that it stands completely alone in history.

m: Making promises or claims without any evidence, action, or intention to back them up; talking without substance.
s: When someone keeps promising to help you but never actually does anything. When a politician makes grand claims about what they'll accomplish but provides no concrete plans or evidence.

m: A promise or commitment that has no real substance or intention to be fulfilled.
s: When a politician promises to fix all problems but takes no action. When your boss keeps saying they'll give you a raise but never follows through. When someone makes grand promises they have no ability or intention to keep.

m: Something that appears impressive on the surface but lacks real content, value, or meaning underneath.
s: When someone gives a long speech that sounds fancy but doesn't actually say anything meaningful. When a product is heavily marketed but offers no real benefits or quality.

l: Wind comes through an empty hole
m: Rumors and gossip typically have some basis in fact, even if exaggerated or distorted.
s: When your coworker tells you a story about the boss that seems unlikely, but you suspect there's a kernel of truth to it. When people are spreading rumors about someone and you wonder if there's any truth behind the talk.

m: completely empty or utterly barren with nothing of value or substance remaining.
s: When you open your wallet and find no money inside. When someone promises great ideas but delivers nothing but empty words. When you visit a restaurant during off-hours and find it completely devoid of customers or atmosphere.

l: pierce and force together, attach and connect
m: To artificially connect unrelated things or force a far-fetched interpretation by manipulating facts and logic.
s: When someone tries to prove their point by cherry-picking random facts and twisting them to fit their argument. When a person insists on finding hidden meanings or connections between completely unrelated events just to support their theory.

l: thread the needle and guide the thread
m: To act as an intermediary or mediator who skillfully brings together different parties or resolves conflicts between them.
s: When a friend helps broker peace between two people who are arguing. When someone in management connects different departments that need to work together. When a diplomat negotiates between two countries to find common ground.

m: To disappear suddenly and without warning, leaving no trace or explanation of one's whereabouts.
s: When someone leaves town without telling anyone where they're going. When a friend suddenly stops responding to messages and nobody knows what happened to them. When a person abandons their responsibilities and vanishes without a word.

m: Something happens unexpectedly and without warning.
s: When a storm hits without any forecast warning. When your boss suddenly calls you into their office for an unscheduled meeting. When a friend shows up at your door without telling you they were coming.

m: To make rapid and dramatic progress or improvement in a short period of time.
s: When a student's grades suddenly improve dramatically after they start studying harder. When a startup company experiences explosive growth and success in just a few months.

m: engaging in illicit or secret romantic and sexual affairs, typically referring to extramarital or improper relationships.
s: When someone is caught having a secret affair behind their spouse's back. When a person is sneaking around with someone they shouldn't be involved with romantically.

m: To speak in hushed, secretive tones, often implying gossip or conspiracy.
s: When you notice a group of people huddled together talking quietly and you suspect they're gossiping about someone. When coworkers are whispering in the corner of the office and stop talking when you walk by.

m: A space is extremely clean, orderly, and well-maintained, reflecting care and attention to detail.
s: When you walk into someone's home and everything is spotless and well-organized. When a classroom or office has been thoroughly cleaned and arranged perfectly.

p: kuī cè fāng xiàng ， yǐ qiú yī chěng
l: spy on the direction to seek a moment of advantage
m: To carefully observe circumstances and wait for an opportune moment to achieve one's selfish or ambitious goals.
s: When a coworker watches for signs of weakness in the company to make a power grab. When someone waits patiently for their rival to make a mistake so they can take them down. When a politician observes shifts in public opinion to exploit them for personal political gain.

p: lì yú bù bài zhī dì
l: stand in a place of no defeat
m: to position oneself in a situation where victory is assured or failure is impossible.
s: When a company dominates its market so completely that competitors cannot catch up. When a student studies so thoroughly before an exam that they feel completely prepared and confident. When a team has such a strong lead in a game that the other side has virtually no chance of winning.

l: establish merit to atone for guilt
m: To redeem oneself or make amends for past wrongdoings by performing good deeds or accomplishing worthy acts.
s: When someone who made a serious mistake wants to prove they've changed by doing something good and meaningful. When a person in trouble tries to regain trust by performing acts of service or making positive contributions to others.

l: stand a pole and see its shadow
m: An action produces immediate and visible results.
s: When you clean your room and it immediately looks so much better. When a medicine works right away and you feel better almost instantly. When a company makes one small change to their website and sales jump up immediately.

l: a place to stand and gain footing
m: A stable position or secure foundation from which to operate or develop.
s: When someone newly immigrated needs to find stable employment and housing to build their life in a new country. When a startup needs initial funding and customers to establish itself as a viable business. When a person needs to get their finances in order before they can pursue their larger goals.

l: establish oneself and conduct oneself in the world
m: To conduct oneself with proper principles and ethics while navigating social relationships and life circumstances.
s: When someone has good character and knows how to behave appropriately in different social situations. When you want to describe someone who maintains their integrity while dealing with the complexities of society and relationships.

l: a place to stand an awl
m: An extremely small amount of space or territory, so minimal that it barely provides room to exist.
s: When someone is so crowded or squeezed that they have no personal space. When a poor person has nowhere to call their own, not even a tiny piece of land. When describing someone who is completely without resources or a foothold in society.

m: Mountains or hills that are completely barren and denuded of all vegetation, typically due to deforestation or environmental degradation.
s: When you see a hillside that has been completely stripped of trees and forests, leaving only bare rock and soil. When describing an area that has been over-logged or cleared of all its trees, leaving nothing but a wasteland.

m: To make the greatest possible effort using all of one's abilities and resources to accomplish something.

s: When a new car is great but has one minor mechanical issue. When a beautiful house is perfect except for one small structural problem. When a job offer is ideal but the salary is slightly lower than expected.

l: ashamed to be grouped together with
m: to feel shame or disgust at being associated with someone or a group of people.
s: When someone's behavior is so bad that their friends don't want to be seen with them anymore. When a company distances itself from a partner because of a scandal.

m: A state of extreme shyness or embarrassment where someone appears flustered and tongue-tied.
s: When a shy person is suddenly put on the spot and doesn't know what to say. When someone is caught doing something embarrassing and their face turns red while they stammer trying to explain.

m: When people unite together, their combined strength and bravery becomes much greater than any individual could achieve alone.
s: When a group of coworkers stands together to ask the boss for better conditions, they feel braver than if one person complained alone. When a team of volunteers bands together to tackle a difficult community project, they accomplish far more than they would separately.

m: When many people pool their wisdom and efforts together, they can accomplish great things.
s: When a team works together on a project and everyone contributes their ideas and effort. When a community comes together to solve a problem that no single person could handle alone.

l: the crowd rises together to attack it
m: A large group of people unite to criticize, oppose, or attack someone or something together.
s: When a celebrity says something offensive and suddenly everyone on social media is criticizing them at the same time. When a company makes an unpopular decision and customers band together to boycott or complain about it loudly.

m: A chaotic situation where many evil or destructive forces act wildly together, creating complete disorder and pandemonium.
s: When a company falls into complete disarray with multiple departments working against each other and no clear leadership. When a protest turns into a riot with groups clashing and looting happening everywhere at once.

l: A group of dragons without a head
m: An organization or group that lacks leadership and cannot function effectively or make unified decisions.
s: When a team's manager suddenly quits and no one takes charge, leaving everyone confused about what to do. When a group project has no designated leader and everyone is doing their own thing without coordination.

m: Someone has become strong, mature, or self-sufficient and no longer needs support or protection from others.
s: When a young adult moves out and becomes independent from their parents. When a junior employee at work gains enough experience and skills to work without constant supervision.

m: Someone or something is not yet mature, experienced, or fully developed enough to stand alone or succeed independently.
s: When a young company is still finding its footing in the market and isn't ready for major challenges. When a new employee hasn't gained enough skills or confidence to work without constant supervision.

m: To be extremely fickle and unpredictable in one's behavior, attitudes, or allegiances, changing from one extreme to another without consistency or principle.
s: When a politician who loudly championed a cause suddenly opposes it when it becomes unpopular. When a friend who was your closest confidant suddenly treats you coldly without explanation and then acts friendly again. When a business partner constantly changes their mind about deals and commitments based on what benefits them most at the moment.

l: overturning the sky and covering the earth
m: A dramatic and fundamental transformation that completely changes the nature of something or the world itself.
s: When a country undergoes a major revolution that completely reshapes society. When new technology fundamentally changes how people live and work in ways nobody expected.

l: climb over mountains and cross ridges
m: To overcome great obstacles and difficulties through persistent effort and determination.
s: When someone travels a long difficult journey to achieve their goal. When a person perseveres through many hardships to reach their destination or accomplish something important.

m: To repeatedly turn something over or to move restlessly back and forth without settling down.
s: When you can't sleep at night and keep tossing and turning in bed. When someone keeps changing their mind about a decision, going back and forth between options. When you're anxiously pacing around, unable to stay still or calm down.

l: overturn the river and pour out the sea
m: To cause massive upheaval, destruction, or chaos of tremendous scale.
s: When a major scandal rocks a company and disrupts everything about how it operates. When an unexpected announcement causes massive changes that affect many people's lives. When someone's arrival or actions create enormous turmoil and disorder in a previously stable situation.

m: to search through something thoroughly and messily, leaving things in disarray in the process.
s: When someone rummages through drawers and shelves looking for something, leaving everything scattered behind. When a parent searches their child's room for a lost item and makes a big mess in the process.

l: overturning and returning with no constancy
m: Fortune and circumstances are unpredictable and subject to constant change, with no stability or reliability.
s: When someone's financial situation keeps dramatically improving and then collapsing unexpectedly. When a company's market position swings wildly between success and failure due to unpredictable external factors. When describing how a person's luck seems to completely reverse without warning.

l: flaunt military might and display power
m: To ostentatiously display one's strength, authority, or superiority in an arrogant and aggressive manner.
s: When a bully intimidates others by showing off their physical strength or connections. When a wealthy person constantly brags about their money and status to make others feel inferior. When a powerful company aggressively dominates a market and boasts about their dominance.

m: Someone who is extremely cunning and deceitful, having accumulated wiles and scheming skills over a long time.
s: When a seasoned criminal uses clever tricks to evade justice. When a manipulative coworker has spent years perfecting their deceptive tactics and is hard to catch or expose.

m: An elderly person remains strong, energetic, and capable, refusing to be diminished by age.
s: When a grandparent still runs marathons or works as hard as someone half their age. When you see an older colleague outperform younger workers and show no signs of slowing down.

m: describing someone who is very old and decrepit, moving slowly and unsteadily with the physical signs of advanced age
s: When you see an elderly person shuffling slowly down the street with a hunched back and shaky movements. When describing a grandparent who has become frail and can barely walk without assistance.

m: To be mature, prudent, and composed in manner, showing the wisdom and reliability that comes with experience.
s: When describing someone who is calm and thoughtful in their decisions, never rushing or acting rashly. When you want to praise a young person who acts with unusual wisdom and stability beyond their years. When someone handles a difficult situation with careful consideration and good judgment instead of panic.

m: Someone who acts in an outdated, pretentious manner or adopts an overly serious, old-fashioned demeanor that is inappropriate for their age or situation.
s: When a young person dresses and acts like someone much older, with serious mannerisms and outdated tastes. When someone your age tries to sound wise and sophisticated but comes across as pompous and stiff instead of natural.

m: A repeatedly mentioned topic or idea that is no longer fresh or interesting because it has been discussed so many times before.
s: When someone brings up the same advice about healthy eating and exercise that everyone already knows. When a teacher repeats the same warning about studying hard that students have heard countless times before.

m: When someone is embarrassed or ashamed, they become angry and lash out instead of accepting the criticism or situation.

m: To be shrewd, cunning, and carefully calculating with long-term plans and hidden intentions.

l: an old horse knows the way
m: An experienced person can find their way or solve problems because of their familiarity with similar situations in the past.
s: When an experienced employee finishes a difficult task quickly because they've handled similar projects before. When a veteran chef can prepare a complex dish without consulting a recipe because of years of practice. When an older team member navigates a tricky business negotiation smoothly due to their extensive experience.

p: lǎo jì fú lì ， zhì zài qiān lǐ
l: An old steed in the stable still aspires to travel a thousand miles
m: Even in old age, one can maintain ambition and determination to achieve great things.
s: When an elderly person starts a new business or learns a new skill with passion and energy. When someone in their later years refuses to give up on their dreams and continues to pursue meaningful goals with vigor.

p: lǎo shǔ guò jiē ， rén rén hǎn dǎ
l: a rat crossing the street, everyone shouts to hit it

m: Something that is interesting, thought-provoking, or subtle enough to reward careful consideration and repeated reflection.

m: To give someone serious, earnest advice or instruction directly and repeatedly, with sincere care and concern for their wellbeing.

m: To be gradually influenced and shaped by one's environment and surroundings through constant exposure over time.

l: ears familiar can explain in detail

m: To have a completely fresh and renewed perspective or experience, feeling invigorated by something novel and unexpected.

m: Having acute hearing and sharp vision, or more broadly, being perceptive, alert, and well-informed about one's surroundings.

p: ěr wén bù rú mù jiàn
l: Hearing with ears is not as good as seeing with eyes
m: Direct personal experience and observation are more reliable and convincing than hearing about something secondhand.
s: When someone describes a beautiful place to you, but you need to visit it yourself to truly appreciate it. When a friend tells you about a product, but you want to see it in person before deciding whether to buy it. When someone explains how to do something, but you need to try it yourself to really understand it.

m: to personally witness or experience something firsthand rather than learning about it secondhand.
s: When you've actually been present at an event and can describe it accurately because you saw and heard it yourself. When someone tries to argue with you about something you were directly present for and know the truth about.

l: talk taken in through the ear

m: To exaggerate or spread alarming claims in order to shock and frighten people.
s: When a news outlet publishes sensational headlines that turn out to be misleading or greatly exaggerated. When a company makes dramatic claims about a competitor's product to scare customers away.

m: Extremely tall or high, reaching toward the heavens; something so grand or magnificent that it seems to touch the sky itself.

m: To pass time in a casual or superficial way in order to get through a difficult period or the remaining days.

m: To find some small comfort or solace in something when facing disappointment or hardship.

m: Something small or mediocre is still better than having nothing at all.

m: Many people or things arrive in quick succession or in great numbers, one after another.

m: Small accumulated amounts eventually grow into something large and significant; persistent effort and accumulation lead to great results.
s: When someone saves small amounts of money regularly and eventually accumulates a large sum. When a student studies a little bit each day and gradually becomes very knowledgeable. When a company starts small but grows into something major through consistent effort.

m: To focus one's complete attention and mental energy on a single task or activity with undivided concentration.
s: When a student is studying hard for an important exam and completely shuts out all distractions. When someone is deeply engaged in a hobby like painting or playing a musical instrument and loses track of time.

p: cōng míng yī shì ， hú tú yī shí
l: Clever for a lifetime, confused for a moment

s: When a usually reliable and intelligent person makes an uncharacteristic stupid decision that surprises everyone. When someone who has always been sensible suddenly does something foolish out of character. When you want to comfort a normally wise person who is embarrassed about a rare moment of bad judgment.

p: cōng míng fǎn bèi cōng míng wù

m: One's own intelligence or cunning backfires and causes them to suffer the consequences they were trying to avoid.

m: Exceptional intelligence, quick wit, and intellectual ability combined together.
s: When describing someone who is naturally smart and picks things up quickly. When praising a person for their clever problem-solving skills and sharp mind. When acknowledging someone's intellectual gifts and mental sharpness.

m: To suddenly feel deep respect and reverence for someone or something upon witnessing their character, accomplishment, or dignity.
s: When you learn about a person's selfless sacrifice and suddenly feel profound admiration for them. When you witness someone's unwavering principles or moral integrity and are moved to respect them deeply.

m: Acting without any fear of consequences or concern for rules, morality, or others' feelings.
s: When someone publicly insults their boss without worrying about getting fired. When a person spreads rumors about others without caring about the damage they cause. When a student cheats on every exam without any fear of being caught or punished.

l: liver and gallbladder smeared on the ground
m: To give one's all, sacrifice everything completely, or die in service to a cause or person.
s: When someone is willing to do anything for their country or leader, even sacrifice their life. When a person shows absolute loyalty and dedication to a cause, no matter the personal cost.

m: Two people show complete honesty and trust with each other, revealing their innermost feelings and thoughts without reservation.
s: When two friends have such a deep bond that they can tell each other anything without fear of judgment. When colleagues work together so closely that they understand each other's intentions and motivations perfectly, trusting each other completely.

m: An extremely crowded place where people and vehicles are packed so tightly together that they are constantly touching and colliding.

l: words from the lungs and heart
m: Sincere and heartfelt words spoken from the deepest part of one's heart.
s: When someone finally opens up and tells you their true feelings after keeping quiet for a long time. When a person speaks with complete honesty and vulnerability, sharing something deeply personal that they've been holding inside.

m: To display obsequious and servile behavior through physical gestures and false smiles in order to please someone.
s: When someone acts excessively submissive and ingratiating around their boss or someone in authority. When a person puts on a fake cheerful demeanor while clearly uncomfortable or degrading themselves to gain favor from another person.

m: To have such extreme boldness or audacity that one fears nothing, not even heaven itself; showing reckless disregard for rules, authority, or consequences.
s: When someone commits a serious crime in broad daylight without any concern about getting caught. When a employee openly insults their boss to their face without fear of being fired. When a teenager completely ignores their parents' strict rules and does whatever they want.

m: Acting with extreme audacity and recklessness, disregarding consequences or rules without proper justification or restraint.
s: When someone makes dangerous decisions without thinking about the risks or how their actions might hurt others. When a person ignores all warnings and does something illegal or harmful just because they think they're above the rules.

l: bold of heart and fine of mind
m: To be courageous and decisive while simultaneously being careful, thoughtful, and attentive to details.
s: When a surgeon needs to make quick, confident decisions during an operation while still being extremely precise and careful with every movement. When a business leader takes bold risks but also pays close attention to the fine details that could make or break the deal. When someone shows courage in facing challenges but remains cautious and observant about potential pitfalls.

m: To be extremely fearful and lacking in courage, easily frightened by minor things.
s: When someone is afraid to speak up in a meeting or confront someone about a problem. When a person is too scared to try something new or take even small risks.

m: To be extremely frightened or terrified, experiencing intense fear and anxiety.
s: When you're walking alone at night and hear strange noises behind you. When you're about to give a presentation in front of a large audience and feel your heart pounding with nervousness. When you accidentally break something valuable belonging to someone else and are waiting for their reaction.

m: To act treacherously by breaking promises and abandoning moral principles that one was bound to uphold.
s: When a business partner takes your money and disappears without fulfilling their obligations. When a friend reveals your secrets to others after you confided in them. When a spouse leaves their partner for someone else after years of promising lifelong commitment.

l: with back to the city, borrow one last gamble
m: to make a final desperate stand or all-or-nothing effort when facing certain defeat, with no retreat possible.
s: When a team is losing badly in the final minutes of a game and decides to throw all their remaining players forward in one last desperate offensive push. When a company on the brink of bankruptcy bets everything on a single high-risk product launch with no backup plan.

l: fight with one's back to the water
m: To fight a desperate battle with no possibility of retreat, forcing oneself to go all-in with complete commitment and determination.
s: When a company is on the verge of bankruptcy and makes one last bold move to save itself. When a student who has been procrastinating finally buckles down and studies intensively right before a critical exam, knowing failure is not an option.

l: carry the way and run in opposite directions
m: To move in completely opposite directions or to work against each other in fundamental ways.
s: When two people have completely opposite goals and their actions contradict each other. When a company's stated values don't match what it actually does in practice. When someone says they want to save money but then spends recklessly.

p: shèng bù jiāo ， bài bù něi
l: Victory does not make one arrogant, defeat does not make one discouraged
m: Maintain a humble and resilient attitude regardless of whether you succeed or fail.
s: When someone wins a competition but stays modest and keeps working hard. When a student fails a test but doesn't give up and studies even harder for the next one. When a sports team loses a game but remains confident and focused on improvement.

m: To be fully capable of handling a task and to do so with genuine pleasure and satisfaction.
s: When someone is well-suited for a job and approaches it with enthusiasm and joy. When a person has both the skills and the positive attitude to excel at their responsibilities without complaint.

p: shèng bài nǎi bīng jiā zhī cháng
l: victory and defeat are the common occurrences of military affairs
m: In competition or conflict, winning and losing are both natural and inevitable outcomes that everyone must accept.
s: When a sports team loses a game and the coach reminds players that every team experiences wins and losses. When a business fails and the entrepreneur reflects that success and failure are both part of doing business. When someone is discouraged after a setback and needs to be reminded that ups and downs are a normal part of life.

m: To act lawlessly and without regard for rules, morality, or consequences.
s: When someone ignores all the rules and does whatever they want without caring about the impact on others. When a person in power abuses their authority and acts completely irresponsibly. When a teenager acts out recklessly and refuses to follow any guidelines or restrictions.

m: To let one's mind wander aimlessly with unfounded worries and wild imaginings, often creating problems that don't actually exist.
s: When someone keeps worrying about things that haven't happened yet and may never happen. When a person stays up at night thinking about unlikely scenarios and scaring themselves with imagined problems. When someone overthinks a casual comment from a friend and invents an entire conflict in their head.

m: To speak irresponsibly or incoherently, talking nonsense without regard for truth or sense.
s: When someone is drunk and rambling incoherently about things that don't make sense. When a person spreads rumors or makes wild accusations without any evidence. When someone is confused or delirious and says things that are completely illogical.

m: To talk nonsense or say absurd, completely unreliable things without any basis in fact.
s: When someone makes up wild accusations without any evidence. When a person tells outrageous lies or exaggerates stories ridiculously. When you catch a friend making completely false claims to impress others.

m: To lack knowledge, understanding, or a clear plan; to be ignorant or unprepared.
s: When someone is asked a direct question but has no idea how to answer it. When a person tries to make a decision without any information or preparation beforehand.

m: To have a clear understanding or firm grasp of a situation; to know exactly what you are doing or what will happen.

m: To be open-hearted and honest, showing genuine sincerity without pretense or hidden motives.
s: When someone tells you their true feelings and deepest thoughts without holding back or being defensive. When a person admits their mistakes openly and doesn't try to hide their real intentions or beliefs.

m: To be straightforward, honest, and free from cunning or deceit, without hidden thoughts or schemes.
s: When someone is completely honest and transparent about their feelings, always saying what they think without any hidden agenda. When a person lacks the ability to play politics or manipulate situations, instead just being genuine and open with everyone around them.

m: To have a mind free from resentment, grudges, or lingering negative thoughts; to let go of grievances and maintain a clear conscience.
s: When someone forgives a friend quickly after an argument and doesn't hold a grudge. When a person naturally lets go of past offenses without dwelling on them or seeking revenge.

When someone tackles a difficult project confidently because they've already thought through all the steps.
