m: A persistent negative influence or haunting memory that continues to trouble someone and cannot be easily shaken off.
s: When an embarrassing moment from years ago keeps coming back to bother you. When a past failure or mistake continues to affect your confidence and decisions. When someone cannot stop thinking about a traumatic experience despite trying to move forward.

m: To flatter and please others excessively by agreeing with everything they say, especially for personal gain or advantage.
s: When a coworker constantly praises the boss's ideas even when they're obviously bad, just to get a promotion. When someone agrees with everything a rich person says, laughing at unfunny jokes and complimenting their terrible decisions, because they want money or favors.

m: Something that is useless, burdensome, and should be removed because it serves no purpose and only causes trouble.
s: When a company has outdated departments that no longer contribute to the business. When someone keeps a bad habit or relationship that only drags them down and offers nothing of value.

m: Outdated customs and inferior practices that persist from the past and should be abandoned.
s: When a company refuses to modernize its old bureaucratic processes that slow everything down. When traditional practices in a community are clearly harmful but people continue them anyway just because they've always done it that way.

m: Overused, trite phrases or clichéd ideas that lack originality or freshness.
s: When a politician gives a speech full of the same tired lines everyone has heard a thousand times before. When someone tries to comfort you with the same hackneyed sayings that don't actually help. When a book or movie relies on predictable plot devices and tired dialogue instead of bringing anything new to the table.

l: The old repeatedly causes the old
m: To mechanically follow outdated practices and customs without any innovation or critical thinking.
s: When a company keeps using the same old business methods that no longer work in the modern market. When someone does things a certain way just because 'that's how it's always been done' without questioning if there's a better approach.

m: to lower one's standards or compromise one's principles in order to achieve a goal or gain acceptance.
s: When a company reduces product quality to cut costs and increase profits. When someone accepts a job well below their qualifications just to get employed quickly.

l: subdue the dragon and suppress the tiger
m: to overcome powerful and dangerous enemies or obstacles through superior skill and courage.
s: When someone manages to defeat a formidable opponent that everyone thought was unbeatable. When a leader successfully handles multiple serious crises or threats at the same time.

l: eliminate evil and must be thorough
m: When eliminating evil or corruption, one must do so completely and leave no remnants or opportunities for it to return.
s: When a company discovers fraud and needs to investigate all involved parties, not just the obvious culprits. When a government cracks down on organized crime and pursues every member of the organization, not just the leaders. When dealing with a persistent problem, you need to address all its causes and sources, not just the surface issues.

l: remove the old and display the new
m: to discard outdated practices, ideas, or systems and replace them with fresh, modern ones.
s: When a company completely redesigns its website and branding to feel more contemporary. When a government implements major reforms to replace corrupt or inefficient old policies. When someone decides to leave their past behind and reinvent themselves with a new lifestyle and mindset.

l: eliminate the violent and protect the good
m: To overthrow tyranny and oppression while protecting and helping the common people who are suffering under it.
s: When a leader takes action to remove a corrupt official who has been abusing power and terrorizing the community. When a strong person intervenes to stop a bully from harassing the weak and defenseless.

m: To be imprisoned or trapped in a dire situation from which escape seems impossible.
s: When someone gets arrested and locked up in jail. When a person becomes trapped in a difficult circumstance like debt or a bad relationship that feels inescapable.

l: follow the sound and attach agreement
m: To agree with others without independent thought, simply echoing what others say.
s: When someone always agrees with whatever their boss says in meetings without offering their own opinion. When a friend just nods along to everything the group decides without expressing what they actually think.

m: To do whatever one wants without restraint or consideration for others or consequences.
s: When someone acts completely selfishly without caring about rules or other people's feelings. When a child throws a tantrum and does whatever they want without listening to their parents.

l: follow circumstances and respond to changes
m: To adapt flexibly to changing circumstances and respond appropriately to new situations rather than rigidly following a fixed plan.
s: When a project plan needs to be adjusted because unexpected problems come up. When someone quickly changes their approach during a negotiation because the other person's attitude shifts. When a teacher modifies the lesson plan mid-class because students don't understand the original material.

l: follow the waves and pursue the current
m: to passively go along with the crowd or circumstances without independent thought or conviction.
s: When someone just agrees with whatever everyone else is doing instead of forming their own opinion. When a person doesn't stand up for what they believe in and just does whatever is popular or trendy.

m: To adapt to whatever situation you find yourself in and remain content rather than resisting or complaining.
s: When you get assigned to a project you didn't want but decide to make the best of it anyway. When someone moves to a new city and quickly adjusts to the local lifestyle instead of constantly wishing they were elsewhere. When life doesn't go according to plan but you stay calm and accept what comes.

l: shift the rudder with the wind
m: To change one's position or tactics opportunistically in response to changing circumstances, often implying a lack of principle or consistency.
s: When a politician changes their stance based on which way public opinion is leaning. When a company suddenly shifts its business strategy just because a competitor is doing well. When someone abandons their stated values the moment it becomes inconvenient or unpopular.

m: To hide one's true identity and live in obscurity under an assumed name or without recognition.
s: When a celebrity goes undercover to live a normal life without being recognized. When someone flees their past and starts over with a completely new identity in a different place. When a witness in a legal case needs to be protected and given a new identity for safety reasons.

l: conceal the bad and promote the good
m: To hide people's faults while publicly praising their virtues, showing kindness and discretion in how you speak about others.
s: When you choose not to tell everyone about your friend's embarrassing mistake, but instead highlight all the great things they do. When a manager decides to keep an employee's minor error private while celebrating their accomplishments with the team.

m: Something that is obscure, mysterious, or deliberately complicated and hard to understand or follow.
s: When someone explains something in a confusing way with lots of hidden meanings. When a piece of writing is intentionally obscure and hard to interpret, like classical poetry or a cryptic message.

m: To speak in a deliberately vague, ambiguous, or evasive way that obscures the true meaning or intent.
s: When someone avoids giving you a straight answer and keeps speaking in unclear terms. When a politician uses complicated language to dodge a difficult question without actually committing to anything.

m: Private conversations may be overheard by others, so one should be cautious about what is said in any location.
s: When you're about to share a secret but realize someone nearby might hear you. When warning a friend not to discuss confidential matters in a public place where others could be listening.

l: watch the fire from the opposite shore
m: to observe a dangerous or difficult situation from a safe distance without getting involved or offering help.
s: When your coworkers are having a conflict but you choose not to take sides and just watch what happens. When a country observes a war happening in another country without intervening. When you see a friend making bad decisions but decide it's not your problem to fix.

l: scratching the boot to relieve an itch
m: Addressing a problem in an ineffective or superficial way that fails to tackle the root cause.
s: When a company only gives employees a small raise instead of addressing the real workplace issues causing them to leave. When someone tries to fix a broken relationship by going on a nice date instead of actually talking about the underlying problems.

m: Something is so depleted or exhausted that it becomes nearly impossible to sustain or maintain.
s: When a company's funds are running so low that they can barely pay their employees next month. When someone is so physically exhausted during a long journey that they can hardly take another step.

m: People who share the same hardship or misfortune and thus have a strong bond of mutual sympathy and understanding.
s: When two friends go through a difficult breakup at the same time and support each other. When coworkers are both struggling with the same demanding boss and commiserate together about their shared challenges.

l: difficult to achieve and therefore precious
m: Something that is rare and valuable precisely because it is hard to accomplish or find.
s: When someone shows exceptional honesty in a situation where it would be easy to lie. When a friend makes a genuine effort to improve themselves despite their struggles. When you find a product or service that is both high quality and affordable.

l: difficult to give up, difficult to part
m: Two people or things are so closely connected or emotionally attached that it is extremely hard for them to separate from each other.
s: When a long-married couple faces being apart due to work or circumstances and they struggle greatly with the separation. When two close friends who have done everything together for years have to move to different cities for their careers.

l: difficult to untangle and difficult to separate
m: Two things are so deeply intertwined or intermingled that they cannot be easily distinguished or separated from each other.
s: When two people are so close that you can't imagine them apart. When business partners have mixed their finances so thoroughly that it's impossible to divide their assets cleanly. When a personal relationship and professional relationship have become so blended that separating them seems impossible.

l: a difficulty that is hard to speak about
m: A secret worry, pain, or concern that someone is reluctant or ashamed to discuss openly with others.
s: When someone has been acting withdrawn and sad but won't tell you what's bothering them. When a person carries emotional baggage from their past but feels too embarrassed or hurt to talk about it with anyone.

m: A powerful and noble ambition to achieve great things.
s: When a young person dreams of becoming a successful entrepreneur and is willing to work hard to build their business from scratch. When someone declares their determination to make a significant contribution to society despite their humble background.

m: A person possesses exceptional intelligence, outstanding ability, and far-reaching vision to accomplish great things.
s: When describing a leader or military commander who has both brilliant tactical skills and an ambitious long-term vision. When someone demonstrates remarkable ability to see the bigger picture and execute ambitious plans effectively.

m: Something that appeals to both refined and common tastes; work that is enjoyed by people of all levels of education and sophistication.
s: A movie that both critics and general audiences love equally. A song that appeals to both classical musicians and casual listeners. A restaurant dish that food experts praise while everyday customers also find it delicious.

m: By bringing together ideas and wisdom from many people, you can achieve better solutions and greater success than working alone.
s: When a team brainstorms together to solve a difficult problem and comes up with a creative solution nobody would have thought of individually. When a company asks employees from different departments for input before making a major decision, resulting in a much better plan.

l: gathering small furs into a large coat
m: Small accumulations over time can combine to create something substantial and valuable.
s: When you save small amounts of money regularly and eventually have enough for a major purchase. When a student studies a little bit every day and gradually becomes very knowledgeable about a subject. When a company collects feedback from many small customer suggestions and uses them to make significant improvements.

m: A minor or insignificant skill that is not worth taking seriously or boasting about.
s: When someone is proud of a small accomplishment that doesn't really matter much. When a person tries to impress others with a trivial talent or ability that has no real value or importance.

m: Something appears or develops suddenly and in large quantities, growing very rapidly.
s: When new businesses or startups suddenly appear in your city. When social media posts about a trending topic suddenly multiply and spread everywhere. When new housing developments suddenly pop up in previously quiet neighborhoods.

m: After a difficult period, things improve and become better again.
s: When someone goes through a tough breakup but eventually feels happy again. When a company faces financial troubles but then recovers and becomes profitable.

l: frost added on top of snow
m: A new misfortune or difficulty arriving when someone is already suffering or in a bad situation.
s: When someone loses their job right after a major medical expense. When bad news keeps coming one after another during an already difficult time, making the situation worse and worse.

m: Providing timely help or support to someone in dire need or difficult circumstances.
s: When a friend lends you money right when you're struggling financially and can't pay rent. When a colleague helps you meet an urgent deadline when you're overwhelmed with work and at your breaking point.

m: Working on something intermittently and in small, disconnected pieces rather than in one sustained effort.
s: When you only have time to work on a project in brief intervals between other tasks. When someone makes progress slowly by doing a little bit here and there instead of dedicating focused time to finish something.

m: To act with extreme speed, efficiency, and decisive force, without hesitation or delay.
s: When a manager immediately implements a new policy and gets the entire team working on it right away. When a company quickly responds to a crisis with decisive action and rapid execution. When someone tackles a problem head-on without procrastinating or wasting any time.

p: léi shēng dà ， yǔ diǎn xiǎo
m: Making a big fuss or promising much but delivering little in actual results or action.
s: When a company announces a major product launch with huge advertising but the actual product is underwhelming. When someone talks a big game about what they're going to accomplish but then does very little. When a politician makes grand campaign promises but takes minimal action once elected.

l: thunder and lightning with ten thousand jun of force
m: An overwhelming, irresistible force or power that cannot be stopped or resisted.
s: When a superior officer makes a decision that everyone must follow immediately without question. When a natural disaster or sudden crisis strikes with such intensity that people are helpless against it. When someone acts with such decisive authority that no one dares to oppose them.

l: shake the ancient and melt the present
m: To possess such outstanding talent or achievement that one surpasses all great figures of the past and present.
s: When describing a genius artist or scientist whose work is considered greater than any predecessor. When someone has made such a groundbreaking contribution that they've exceeded every historical figure in their field.

l: shake and strike the human heart
m: To profoundly move or deeply impress someone emotionally or spiritually.
s: When a powerful movie or speech leaves you feeling deeply moved and emotional. When a tragic event or inspiring story affects everyone around you so strongly that people can't stop talking about it.

l: shake the ears and nearly deafen
m: An extremely loud noise that is so intense it feels like it might rupture one's eardrums.
s: When a rock concert is so loud that you can barely hear yourself think. When construction noise outside your window is absolutely unbearable and overwhelming.

m: To accidentally expose one's true intentions, mistakes, or deceptions that had been hidden.
s: When someone tries to hide their involvement in something but accidentally gives themselves away. When a dishonest person makes a slip-up that reveals they were lying all along.

l: ascend the blue clouds directly upward
m: To achieve rapid promotion or success and quickly rise to a position of power, wealth, or prominence.
s: When someone gets promoted multiple times in quick succession and their career takes off dramatically. When a person suddenly becomes famous or successful after years of obscurity. When a friend lands a dream job that launches them into a much higher social or professional status.

p: qīng chū yú lán ， ér shèng yú lán
l: The blue comes from the indigo, yet surpasses the indigo
m: A student or successor becomes superior to their teacher or predecessor through learning and development.
s: When a talented student eventually becomes more skilled than their mentor. When a child grows up to achieve greater success than their parents. When a company founded by someone's protégé becomes more successful than the original company.

m: A ferocious, demonic, or frightening appearance, often used to describe something evil or monstrous.
s: When describing a villain or monster in a story with a terrifying appearance. When someone is so angry their face looks distorted and menacing. When talking about the scary makeup or costumes of demons in traditional Chinese opera.

l: the green and yellow are not connected
m: A period of scarcity or difficulty that occurs when old resources are exhausted but new ones are not yet available.
s: When a company runs out of inventory before the new shipment arrives. When a student finishes their savings before their next paycheck comes in. When a farmer's stored grain runs out just before the new crop is harvested.

m: Someone who has no family relation or prior connection to you; a complete stranger.
s: When you need help moving but don't want to bother family or close friends, so you hire someone from a moving company who is neither relative nor acquaintance. When a new coworker joins your team and you realize they know nothing about your company's history or relationships.

l: not the same as small matters
m: Something is of great importance or serious consequence, not a trivial matter.
s: When your company is being investigated by authorities and you need to stress how serious the situation is. When a friend tells you they're quitting their stable job to start a business and you want to emphasize this is a major decision, not something to take lightly.

m: Something that is a confusing mixture of different things and doesn't fit clearly into any single category.
s: When you see a piece of furniture that's awkwardly designed and doesn't function well as either a chair or a table. When someone creates artwork that blends styles so poorly it doesn't work as any recognizable form. When a restaurant tries to serve both fancy cuisine and fast food, doing neither well.

p: kào shān chī shān ， kào shuǐ chī shuǐ
l: relying on mountains eat from mountains, relying on water eat from water
m: People should make use of the resources and advantages available in their immediate environment to survive and prosper.
s: When a coastal town's economy depends on fishing, the locals naturally rely on the sea for their livelihood. When a village is surrounded by forests, the people there depend on logging and forestry products. When someone uses their family connections to get ahead in their career because they were born into a well-connected family.

m: Decadent or morally corrupting music that leads people toward indulgence and away from virtue.
s: When someone listens to music that seems to encourage lazy or immoral behavior. When a parent worries that their child's favorite songs are a bad influence that makes them lose discipline and focus.

m: To remain calm and composed without showing any emotional reaction or fear in the face of difficulty or shock.
s: When someone receives bad news but doesn't show any facial reaction or emotion. When a person stays completely composed during a tense or embarrassing moment that would make most people blush or look worried.

m: Someone's face becomes very pale or ashen, typically from extreme fear, shock, or illness.
s: When someone receives terrible news and their face goes completely white. When a person is so frightened that all the color drains from their face. When someone is gravely ill and looks ghostly pale.

l: face to face impart opportune counsel
m: To give someone secret advice or instructions in person and in private, typically for strategic or tactical advantage.
s: When a coach pulls a player aside during a game to give them specific instructions that shouldn't be overheard by the opposing team. When a leader meets privately with a trusted advisor to discuss sensitive plans before announcing them publicly.

m: Someone's face becomes extremely pale, usually due to fear, shock, or severe illness.
s: When you see someone's face turn white after receiving bad news. When a person looks so frightened or sick that they seem to have lost all color from their face.

m: Someone or something has changed so dramatically in appearance or character that they are almost unrecognizable from before.
s: When a friend gets a major makeover and looks completely different. When a run-down building is renovated and transformed into something beautiful. When a company redesigns its entire image and brand identity.

m: Something has changed so drastically that it is completely unrecognizable compared to its original state or appearance.
s: When a city you grew up in has been so heavily developed that you can barely recognize any old landmarks. When someone returns after many years away and their personality or values have changed so much that they seem like a completely different person.

p: miàn mù kě zēng ， yǔ yán wú wèi
l: visage loathsome and speech without flavor
m: Someone is both physically repugnant and tediously boring or unpleasant in conversation.
s: When describing someone who is unattractive and also has nothing interesting to say. When a person is disliked both for their appearance and their dull or unpleasant manner of speaking.

m: To be extremely embarrassed, ashamed, or angry, as evidenced by one's flushed face and reddened ears.
s: When someone gets caught in a lie and their face turns bright red. When a person is so angry during an argument that their ears start turning crimson. When you say something inappropriate at a meeting and feel your entire face flush with embarrassment.

m: To attend to every aspect or detail comprehensively, ensuring nothing is overlooked.
s: When a teacher designs a lesson plan that addresses the needs of all different types of learners in the classroom. When a project manager creates a plan that considers every possible risk and contingency. When someone tries to please everyone by considering all perspectives and concerns in a decision.

l: face facing face gazing at each other
m: A group of people look at each other in silence, typically due to shock, embarrassment, awkwardness, or not knowing what to do.
s: When a teacher asks a difficult question and all the students just stare at each other blankly without raising their hands. When something awkward happens at a dinner table and everyone goes quiet, just exchanging glances without speaking.

m: Looking sickly, malnourished, or extremely exhausted with a pale complexion and emaciated body.
s: When someone has been very ill for a long time and lost a lot of weight. When a person is overworked and visibly unhealthy due to stress and lack of rest. When describing someone who is starving or severely malnourished.

l: cast off the old and establish the new
m: To discard outdated practices, beliefs, or systems and replace them with modern, improved alternatives.
s: When a company completely redesigns its outdated business model to compete in the modern market. When a government implements major reforms to replace inefficient old policies with new, progressive ones. When someone abandons traditional methods in favor of innovative approaches.

p: jū gōng jìn cuì ， sǐ ér hòu yǐ
l: bow and exhaust oneself, only stop after death
m: To serve with complete devotion and dedication until the very end of one's life, never ceasing in one's efforts or commitment.
s: When describing a selfless public servant who worked tirelessly for their country throughout their entire career until they passed away. When praising someone who dedicated their whole life to a cause or mission they believed in, never retiring or giving up despite hardship.

m: To analyze or criticize something with keen insight that penetrates to the very heart of the matter.
s: When a teacher explains a difficult concept so clearly that students finally understand it completely. When a film critic writes a review that perfectly captures what makes a movie truly great or terrible.

l: the whip is long but cannot reach
m: One's power, influence, or ability is limited and cannot extend to distant or difficult situations.
s: When a parent cannot control their adult child who lives far away. When a company's policies cannot effectively manage what happens in distant branch offices. When a government struggles to enforce rules in remote regions.

m: To hide one's talents and abilities while building strength, waiting for the right opportunity to act.
s: When a talented person keeps a low profile at work instead of showing off, waiting for the right moment to demonstrate their skills. When a company quietly develops new technology in secret before launching it to surprise competitors.

l: reach the sky and stand on the earth
m: To stand tall and firm with integrity, dignity, and an upright character that commands respect.
s: When describing someone who has strong moral principles and isn't afraid to stand up for what's right. When you want to praise someone for being courageous and principled in their actions despite pressure or difficulties.

m: To show extreme respect, admiration, or devotion to someone or something, often in an excessive or servile manner.
s: When someone treats a celebrity or authority figure with blind reverence and follows their every word without question. When a fan idolizes a famous person so much that they imitate everything they do and hang on their every word.

p: xiàng zhuāng wǔ jiàn ， yì zài pèi gōng
l: Xiang Zhuang dances with his sword, but his intention is toward the Duke of Pei
m: Someone appears to have one purpose on the surface, but their true hidden intention is something entirely different and often harmful.
s: When a coworker suggests a business meeting that seems routine, but you suspect they're actually planning to undermine you or steal your clients. When a competitor offers partnership while secretly trying to sabotage your company or take over your market share.

m: People are so numerous and closely packed together that they stand shoulder to shoulder, or things are so abundant that they are everywhere in sight.
s: When you're in a crowded marketplace where people are packed so tightly together that you can barely move. When describing a city street during rush hour where pedestrians fill every space from one end to the other.

p: shùn zhī zhě chāng ， nì zhī zhě wáng
l: Those who follow it prosper, those who oppose it perish.
m: Success comes to those who align with prevailing trends and natural order, while failure befalls those who resist or go against them.
s: When a company adapts to new market demands and thrives while competitors cling to outdated practices and fail. When someone accepts a major life change and moves forward successfully, while someone else fights against it and struggles. When a business adopts new technology and grows prosperous, but a rival refuses to change and eventually goes out of business.

m: to take something that isn't yours while appearing to do so casually or incidentally, taking advantage of an opportunity to steal without drawing attention.
s: When someone sneaks a candy from a store shelf while pretending to shop normally. When a coworker grabs office supplies without asking, making it look accidental. When a guest pockets a small item from someone's house during a casual visit.

m: A favor or kindness that is easy to provide because it requires little effort or cost on your part.
s: When you help a coworker by forwarding an email to someone you were already emailing anyway. When you recommend a friend to a job opening at your company simply by mentioning their name in conversation, without going out of your way.

l: push a boat along with the current
m: Take advantage of favorable circumstances to achieve your goals with minimal effort.
s: When someone uses an opportunity that naturally comes their way to succeed. When a manager assigns a task to an employee who is already heading in that direction anyway. When you take advantage of existing momentum or trends to reach your objective more easily.

l: Following the principle, the chapter is completed
m: When things proceed naturally and logically according to their inherent principles, the result follows inevitably and smoothly.
s: When a student studies hard all semester and naturally gets good grades as a result. When a company invests in quality products and customer service, and as a result their business grows without any extra effort needed.

l: Follow the vine to find the melon
m: By following a clue or lead, you can gradually uncover the truth or find the root cause of a problem.
s: When a detective traces clues from a crime scene to identify the criminal. When you start investigating a small problem at work and it leads you to discover a much larger issue in the company's operations.

m: To persuade someone who is extremely stubborn or seemingly immovable through persistent effort or compelling argument.
s: When a salesman finally convinces a resistant customer to make a purchase after much persuasion. When a parent's repeated explanations finally get through to a rebellious teenager who refuses to listen.

m: To prioritize the collective interest or overall situation over personal gain or individual concerns.
s: When someone gives up a promotion to stay with their team during a difficult project. When a player makes a sacrifice play for the benefit of the whole team rather than trying to score themselves.

l: mind the front and not the back
m: To focus only on immediate concerns while neglecting future consequences or broader implications.
s: When someone rushes to finish a project quickly without checking for errors that will cause problems later. When a business prioritizes short-term profits and ignores the long-term damage to their reputation or environment.

l: consider the name and think about its meaning
m: the meaning of something can be understood directly from its name without further explanation.
s: When a product is called 'waterproof phone case' and you immediately understand what it does. When someone introduces themselves as a 'Life Coach' and you get the basic idea of their job right away.

l: regard one's shadow and feel pity for oneself
m: to feel lonely and sad about one's own circumstances, often indulging in self-pity and melancholy.
s: When someone sits alone at home feeling sorry for themselves instead of reaching out to others. When a person dwells on their misfortunes and feels like no one understands or cares about them.

l: care for this but lose that
m: When you focus on one thing, you inevitably neglect another, resulting in a loss overall.
s: When a student spends so much time on one subject that their other grades suffer. When a business owner focuses only on sales and ignores customer service, causing clients to leave. When someone tries to fix one problem at work but accidentally creates another one in the process.

m: To look around proudly and feel superior to others, displaying arrogance and self-importance.
s: When someone walks into a room acting like they're better than everyone else, looking around with contempt. When a person who just got a promotion or achievement struts around acting superior to their peers.

m: Being weighed down by many worries, doubts, or fears that prevent someone from taking action or moving forward.
s: When someone wants to start a business but is held back by fears about money, failure, and competition. When a student hesitates to apply to their dream school because they worry about whether they'll be accepted, afford tuition, or fit in.

m: To suddenly gain understanding or have an epiphany after being confused or ignorant.
s: When you finally understand a difficult math concept after your teacher explains it a certain way. When someone realizes the solution to a problem they've been stuck on for weeks. When you suddenly comprehend why your friend was upset with you all along.

l: praise the ancients and criticize the present
m: To excessively admire the past while disparaging the present day, refusing to acknowledge progress or merit in modern times.
s: When someone constantly complains that everything was better in the old days and dismisses all modern innovations as inferior. When an elderly relative refuses to adopt new technology because they insist the old ways were superior and nothing has improved since then.

l: command with a nod and direct with a gesture
m: To act in an arrogant and domineering manner, treating others as subordinates and expecting them to obey without question.
s: When a boss treats employees like servants, expecting them to jump at every gesture without saying please. When a wealthy person acts superior to service workers and treats them with contempt and disrespect. When someone uses only body language and curt gestures to boss others around instead of treating them with basic courtesy.

m: To be disorganized, confused, or to speak in a muddled and incoherent way.
s: When someone tells a story that jumps around with no clear order or logic. When a person's thoughts are so scattered that nothing they say makes sense. When describing a workplace or situation that is chaotic and nothing is in its proper place.

m: To deliberately misrepresent facts and present false information as truth, or to confuse what is morally right with what is wrong.
s: When a politician distorts the facts about their opponent's record to mislead voters. When someone twists the story of a conflict to make themselves look innocent and blame an innocent person. When a dishonest salesman misrepresents the quality of a product to deceive customers.

m: to deliberately distort the truth by presenting false information as fact and facts as lies.
s: When a politician twists the facts to make their opponent look bad during a debate. When someone lies about what happened in an argument to make themselves look innocent and blame the other person entirely.

l: toppled and struck but not broken
m: Something is so solid and true that it cannot be refuted or destroyed no matter how much it is attacked or challenged.
s: When a scientific theory has been proven so thoroughly that no evidence can disprove it. When someone presents an argument so logically sound that no counterargument can shake it. When a friendship is so strong that conflict or misunderstanding cannot damage it.

l: toppled and displaced, flowing and scattered
m: To be forced to wander from place to place due to hardship, war, or poverty, living an unstable and miserable life without a permanent home.
s: When a family loses everything in a disaster and has to move between shelters and relatives' homes. When refugees are forced to flee their country and live in temporary camps or unfamiliar cities. When someone experiences a series of job losses and has to constantly relocate for work, never settling down.

m: A prominent and influential figure who commands widespread attention and respect in society.
s: When talking about a celebrity or business leader who is everywhere in the news and seems to shape current events. When describing someone who has become so famous and powerful that everyone knows who they are and what they're doing.

m: Circumstances change rapidly and unpredictably, like shifting weather patterns.
s: When market conditions change suddenly and businesses must adapt quickly. When political situations shift dramatically in unexpected ways. When someone's fortune or circumstances transform completely within a short time.

m: A sudden and dramatic shift in circumstances or fortune, often referring to unexpected political or social upheaval.
s: When a company's stable situation suddenly becomes chaotic due to management changes. When a peaceful community suddenly faces conflict or crisis without warning. When someone's good luck abruptly turns to misfortune.

m: To do something with overwhelming speed and force, leaving nothing behind; to move or act with unstoppable momentum.

m: When in desperate circumstances, one will accept help from any source without being choosy or particular about it.
s: When someone is in a dire situation and accepts assistance from unlikely or undesirable sources just to survive. When a person facing ruin accepts any opportunity or ally, even those they would normally reject, because they have no other options.

l: into whose hand the deer falls
m: It is unclear who will ultimately win or emerge victorious in a competition or struggle.
s: When multiple companies are competing for a major contract and it's hard to predict who will win. When several political candidates are running for office and the outcome is still uncertain.

m: To become emotionally insensitive and indifferent to the suffering of others or to one's surroundings.
s: When someone has witnessed so much hardship that they no longer react emotionally to problems around them. When a person becomes so desensitized by repeated bad news that they stop caring about things that should matter to them. When someone ignores their friend's pain because they've heard complaints too many times before.

m: A state of complacency and inattentiveness that causes one to overlook dangers or problems.
s: When a driver becomes overconfident on a familiar route and stops paying attention to the road. When a company ignores warning signs of trouble because things have been going well for so long.

p: má què suī xiǎo ， wǔ zàng jù quán
l: Though the sparrow is small, it has all five internal organs
m: Something may be small or seemingly insignificant, but it is complete and fully functional in all essential aspects.
s: When describing a small business that has all the departments and functions of a larger company. When someone lives in a tiny apartment but it has everything they need - bedroom, kitchen, bathroom, living room. When a startup is small but has all the core teams necessary to operate as a full company.

m: A fleeting dream or illusion that seems real but dissolves upon waking, symbolizing how life's ambitions and pleasures are transient and ultimately meaningless.
s: When someone pursues an elaborate plan or fantasy only to have it fall apart suddenly. When you wake up from a vivid dream where you were successful or wealthy, only to realize it was just a dream and your actual life remains unchanged.

p: hēi yún yā chéng chéng yù cuī
l: Black clouds press down on the city as if to destroy it
m: An ominous or threatening situation that feels overwhelming and on the verge of collapse, or a tense atmosphere before a major crisis or conflict.
s: When political tensions between two countries escalate to a breaking point and war seems imminent. When a company is facing multiple serious problems at once and bankruptcy appears inevitable. When a dark, heavy mood descends on a group or community before some catastrophic event.

m: A situation where right and wrong, or good and bad, are obvious and easy to tell apart with no ambiguity.
s: When a legal case has clear evidence that proves one person is guilty and the other innocent. When judging a competition and one contestant clearly performed much better than the others.

m: Someone has exhausted all their skills or resources and has nothing left to offer or no way forward.
s: When a magician has performed all their tricks and has nothing impressive left to show. When a company that once innovated keeps releasing the same tired products because they've run out of new ideas.

m: To work or live in obscurity without receiving recognition or attention from others.
s: When someone does good work behind the scenes but nobody knows about it. When a hardworking employee never gets credit for their contributions. When an artist creates beautiful works but remains completely unknown to the public.

m: To become dull, unremarkable, or inferior when compared to something else.
s: When a new restaurant opens and all the old popular places suddenly seem less appealing by comparison. When a talented newcomer joins a team and makes the existing members' achievements seem less impressive.

m: A situation where three forces or powers are balanced equally against each other, with none dominant over the others.
s: When three competing companies have equal market share and none can gain an advantage over the others. When three countries maintain a delicate balance of power where each is strong enough to prevent the others from dominating.

m: To muster all one's courage, determination, and effort to tackle a task or challenge with maximum vigor and enthusiasm.
s: When a team is preparing for a big competition and the coach tells them to gdrum up all their energy and give their best effort. When someone is facing a difficult exam and decides to stop procrastinating, gather all their willpower, and study with complete dedication.

m: Having an extremely narrow vision and lack of foresight; being unable to see beyond immediate, petty concerns.
s: When someone makes a decision based only on short-term gain without considering long-term consequences. When a person refuses to think strategically and only focuses on trivial matters right in front of them.

m: Petty theft and sneaky, dishonorable behavior, often referring to small-scale criminal activity or underhanded tactics.
s: When someone resorts to cheating or cutting corners in small ways to get ahead. When a company uses deceptive marketing tactics or hides unfavorable terms in the fine print to trick customers.

m: Multiple people or things making progress at the same pace or rate simultaneously.
s: When two companies are growing at similar rates and gaining market share equally. When students in a class are all learning at the same speed and progressing together through the curriculum.

m: When people work together with complete agreement and combined strength toward a common goal.
s: When a team successfully completes a difficult project by having everyone contribute their best effort. When a group of friends bands together to help someone in need, each person doing their part without conflict.

l: dragons and tigers fighting for dominance
m: An intense and evenly matched struggle between powerful opponents or forces.
s: When two talented athletes compete fiercely in a championship match. When rival companies engage in aggressive business competition for market share. When two skilled teams play an incredibly competitive game where either side could win.

m: An extremely dangerous place full of powerful and ruthless people or forces that one must enter at great risk.
s: When someone has to go into a very dangerous situation to accomplish something important, like entering a criminal organization to gather evidence. When you need to negotiate with hostile people in their own territory where you have no control or safety.

m: A state of vigorous, dynamic activity and energetic progress characterized by powerful momentum and vitality.
s: When a company experiences rapid growth and expansion with lots of exciting new projects launching. When a sports team is playing with incredible energy and winning decisively. When a country's economy is booming and developing at an impressive pace.

m: A place of strategic importance or natural defensive strength, typically referring to a location with commanding geographical features.
s: When describing a fortress city nestled in mountains that would be very difficult to attack. When talking about a region that has natural barriers like rivers and hills making it easy to defend. When historians discuss why an ancient capital was built in a particular valley or mountain pass.

m: Vigorous, lively, and graceful movement or expression that is bold and magnificent in style.
s: When someone writes with beautiful, flowing calligraphy that looks energetic and artistic. When a dancer performs with impressive, sweeping movements that captivate the audience. When describing flamboyant or dramatic gestures that command attention.
